body:
## Summary

Fixes #5860

When using AgentOS with a custom FastAPI `base_app`, `resync()` called `_reprovision_routers()`, which wiped all routes except docs/mcp paths. That deleted caller-defined routes (e.g. `GET /status` → 404 after resync).

This tracks the concrete route objects AgentOS itself adds (by identity via `id()`), and on resync only removes those — leaving FastAPI docs, the `/mcp` mount, and any `base_app` routes in place.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Checklist

- [x] Code complies with style guidelines
- [ ] Ran format/validation scripts (`./scripts/format.sh` and `./scripts/validate.sh`)
- [x] Self-review completed
- [x] Documentation updated (comments, docstrings)
- [ ] Examples and guides: Relevant cookbook examples have been included or updated (if applicable)
- [x] Tested in clean environment
- [x] Tests added/updated (if applicable)

### Duplicate and AI-Generated PR Check

- [x] I have searched existing [open pull requests](../../pulls) and confirmed that no other PR already addresses this issue
- [x] If a similar PR exists, I have explained below why this PR is a better approach
- [x] Check if this PR was entirely AI-generated (by Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor, etc.)

Prior attempt [#6269](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/pull/6269) (closed) tracked managed routes by path allowlist. This PR tracks by route object identity so conflict-skipped routes are not recorded as AgentOS-owned, and `/mcp` (mounted outside `_add_router`) is preserved without a hardcoded path list.

I reviewed the change, understand the route-ownership model, and verified `pytest libs/agno/tests/integration/os/test_custom_fastapi_app.py` — 20 passed including the new `test_custom_app_endpoints_preserved_after_resync`.

author: n-a-monterocarvajal
body:
Dos correcciones al `LICENSE` declarado en el PR anterior. Ambas nacen de una objeción certera: la página del artículo desapareció, y nunca se comprobó que el código heredado sea el suyo.

## 1. Alcance de la atribución

La sección 1 afirmaba que la capa heredada **es** la obra de Antoine Aubry bajo CPOL, como hecho establecido. No lo es: nunca se comparó el código con el del artículo, porque CodeProject dejó de operar y el artículo ya no está disponible.

Lo que realmente sostiene la atribución es testimonio concordante de terceros —gmcouto, mnivet y agabor— más un `Copyright ©  2007` sin titular en el `AssemblyInfo.cs` importado. Es evidencia razonable, no verificación.

El documento lo declara ahora como atribución, explicita que **se desconoce si el código heredado coincide con el del artículo**, y mantiene la postura conservadora de tratar CPOL 1.02 como vinculante en lugar de asumir que no aplica. La incertidumbre se suma a la sección «Lo que se desconoce».

## 2. La línea de procedencia era falsa

Se presentaba como `agabor → gmcouto → mnivet`. Comprobado:

- `gmcouto/RightKeyboard` no es fork de GitHub de ningún repositorio (`fork: false`, sin padre).
- Su código difiere del de agabor: comparando el volcado de 2020 con los archivos de agabor, `Layout.cs` y `LayoutSelectionDialog.cs` tienen tamaños muy distintos, aunque `Program.cs` coincide.

Son derivaciones **hermanas** de un ancestro común, no una sucesión:

```text
Artículo núm. 20994 (2007)
  ├─► agabor (2015) — rama independiente, no antecesora
  └─► gmcouto (2020) ─► mnivet (fork) ─► este repositorio
```

agabor pasa a citarse solo como **testimonio independiente**: un tercero sin relación de fork que atribuye su propio código al mismo artículo. No debilita la atribución, la refuerza, pero no forma parte de la línea.

Solo documentación.

author: alexberardi
body:
## Summary

Four consecutive voice requests were **silently dropped on the node** and never reached command-center. Each transcribed perfectly:

```
"Can you make an appointment at Total Patient Care for me one day this week?"
"Make an appointment at Total Patient Care one day this week."
"Can you call and make an appointment at Total Patient Care for this week?"
```

Cause: **signal 4** (whisper segment shape). More than 8 words plus a single segment ≥4 s was treated as ambient narration — but a deliberate 14-word request spoken *without pausing* is exactly one long segment. The rule punished fluency, and since phone-call commands are inherently that long ("make an appointment at X for me this week"), it made the feature unusable by voice.

The fix keys on the distinction the logs actually show. Signal 4 is skipped when the transcript looks like a deliberate utterance:

- capitalised first word **and** terminal punctuation (whisper reliably supplies both for a complete sentence), **and**
- `hit_max_duration` is False — the listener stopped because the *speaker* stopped.

Overheard speech is a fragment: it starts mid-thought or trails off. Narration keeps going and runs into the cap. Both are still caught, and signals 1–3 are untouched.

Deployed to `jarvis-dev.local` and verified against the exact dropped utterance (now passes); the four originals are pinned as regression tests.

Related: this heuristic is arguably in tension with the standing design rule that the "is this for me?" verdict belongs in CC's LLM, which can see the toolset. This PR keeps the node-side filter but stops it eating well-formed commands; a broader rethink is a separate conversation.

## Test plan

6 new tests: the four real dropped utterances, a fluent gap-less multi-segment command, and two guards proving fragments and at-the-cap narration are still caught. Full false-wake suite: **46 passed**, including the pre-existing narration corpus unchanged.

body:
## Problem

- The structured parse path in `src/parse_logs.py` put an **unbounded** number of lines into `actual_error` (and `step_context`/`github_error`), so a long log could blow up the LLM prompt (cost, context-limit errors).
- The `DEFAULT_LOG_LENGTH` env var was unreachable: `action.yml` never set it, so users had no way to control log size.

## Fix

- New `_tail()` helper in `parse_logs.py`; every section is now capped at `max_lines`, keeping the **tail** since errors cluster at the end. The no-marker fallback path uses the same helper.
- New `log_lines` action input (default `1000`), passed as `INPUT_LOG_LINES` and parsed with `_parse_log_lines()` in `config.py`, which falls back to 1000 on missing/invalid/non-positive values.
- Config key renamed `default_log_length` → `log_lines` to match the input end-to-end; `DEFAULT_LOG_LENGTH` removed.
- README inputs table updated.

Verified with a quick script: structured sections are capped to the tail, fallback path capped, invalid values fall back to 1000.

Checklist item 2 (Session 1).

author: dionismuzenitov
body:
Implements **SLS-60** — visible engine plumes (previously the landing burn was invisible).

## What
A single `<EnginePlumes />` `InstancedMesh` of additive cones (one draw call, ≤33 engines) hung off the nozzles and driven each frame from the live `world.engineStates`:
- **Throttle → flame**: length + width scale with throttle; zero plume when the engine is off. A low coast burn (the policy uses one) still shows a small flame.
- **Gimbal**: each cone tilts with its engine's gimbal (same `Euler(pitch,0,yaw)` the nozzle nodes use in `BoosterModelGLB`).
- **Altitude regime**: sea-level → vacuum interpolation widens/lengthens/dims the plume with altitude (grounded: confined bright banded plume low, free-expansion faint fan high).
- **Bloom**: additive core exceeds luminance 1 so it glows through `<PostFX>`.

## How
- Pure curves in `enginePlumeMath.ts` (throttle→intensity, altitude→regime, dims, flicker) — unit-tested (+13 tests).
- The R3F component reads the store imperatively in `useFrame` (zero React re-render, matching `CollisionDebug` / camera rigs). No per-particle CPU.
- Vehicle (booster 33 / ship 6) picked by engine count like `BoosterFlight`; unused instances collapse to a point.
- Anchored at `rigidBody.position` (the engine plane) with body attitude; mounts scaled by `MODEL_SCALE` to match the scaled GLB.

## Perf
Single instanced draw call, no CPU particle system — negligible cost (well inside the eventual SLS-61 budget). Owner to eyeball frame-rate in the live scene during review.

## Verification
typecheck clean · 412/412 unit tests · build green. The existing camera-controls + smoke e2e load the scene (now including plumes) and assert no console errors.

author: siddharthag09
body:
## What

`sat_add` zero-extends the weight with a replication count of `SCORE_WIDTH - WEIGHT_WIDTH + 1`, which goes negative when the weight is wider than the score. The ISA (section 6) lists `SCORE_WIDTH = 6` and `WEIGHT_WIDTH = 8` as validated ranges, but that combination failed to elaborate:

```
token_importance_unit.sv:116: error: Concatenation repeat may not be negative (-1)
```

Even if it had elaborated, the `SCORE_WIDTH+1`-bit sum register can't hold `score + weight` in that regime, so the single-carry-bit saturation check would silently wrap instead of saturating.

## Fix

Compute the sum one bit wider than the wider of the two operands, and saturate on a reduction-OR of the overflow bits — which reduces to the original single carry-bit check when `WEIGHT_WIDTH <= SCORE_WIDTH`. The openlane `src/` copy is kept byte-identical per repo convention.

## Verification

- Directed TB: 29/29 · Real-data replay: 40/40
- All 15 ISA-validated width combos now elaborate (6/8 failed before)
- Functional saturation test at 6/8: weight 200 saturates the 6-bit score at 63; 6×10 accumulates exactly to 60, then saturates at 63
- Yosys formal equivalence (SAT + induction, 106/106 points proven) of new vs. old RTL at the default parameters — the signed-off config is provably unchanged, and synthesized FF/cell counts are identical

author: ebubeb683-ship-it
body:
Closes #76 
This PR introduces a lightweight, custom VirtualList component and integrates it into the two transaction‑display components that previously rendered the entire transaction array at once.

What was changed
File  Change
components/ui/virtual-list.tsx  New reusable virtualization component (absolute‑positioned, scroll‑based windowing).
components/app/transaction-list.tsx  Refactored to use VirtualList; item height fixed at 64 px, container height adapts to number of items (max 320 px).
components/app/transaction-history-view.tsx  Refactored to use VirtualList; item height fixed at 80 px, container height caps at 320 px.
Imports  Added VirtualList import to the two components.
Why this matters
Performance: Rendering thousands of rows without virtualization caused UI jank. The new list only renders items visible in the viewport plus a small buffer, dramatically reducing DOM size and improving scroll smoothness.
Scalability: The underlying API already supports pagination; this change makes the UI ready for real‑world transaction volumes.
Accessibility: The component preserves role="list" and role="listitem" semantics, and all existing ARIA attributes remain intact.
No external deps: A custom implementation avoids pulling in heavy third‑party libraries that could clash with existing peer dependencies.
Verification
The changes compile successfully (npm run build works in the repo).
Manual testing in the browser confirms smooth scrolling with 5 000+ dummy transactions (the mock data can be enlarged to verify behavior).
Existing unit tests for TransactionList still pass (they target the data-testid attributes which are preserved).
How to review / test locally
Checkout the branch

bash


git fetch origin
git checkout virtualization
Install dependencies (if not already installed)

bash


npm ci
Run the test suite

bash


npm test
(All existing Jest tests should pass; the new virtualization logic does not affect component contracts.)

Run the app and verify scrolling performance in the Transaction List and Transaction History pages.

Upstream / Branch tracking – The local virtualization branch is already set to track origin/virtualization, and the PR is ready to be merged.

author: marcioecom
body:
## Summary

This PR adds optional Tailscale support for administrative access to hetzner-k3s clusters.

When enabled, hetzner-k3s installs Tailscale on each node during provisioning, joins the nodes to the tailnet, uses Tailscale hostnames for SSH operations, and generates kubeconfig files that target the Kubernetes API over Tailscale.

This allows operators to keep SSH and Kubernetes API access on the tailnet instead of depending on public allowlists.

This is intentionally scoped to administrative access. It does not attempt to cover the broader IPv6-only / 464XLAT work discussed in #768.

## Changes

- add `networking.tailscale` configuration with `enabled`, `hostname_suffix`, and `auth_key`
- install and join Tailscale during cloud-init
- route hetzner-k3s SSH operations through Tailscale hostnames when enabled
- add Tailscale hostnames to the API server TLS SANs
- generate kubeconfig files that use the master's Tailscale hostname
- skip current-IP validation for `allowed_networks` when Tailscale is enabled
- document setup and cleanup requirements

## Notes

- existing behavior is unchanged when Tailscale is disabled
- cluster deletion does not remove machines from the tailnet; stale machines should be removed manually to avoid hostname suffix changes when recreating a cluster

author: sammyjdev
body:
Closes #83. Follow-up to #76 / PR #82, addressing the three residual SSRF gaps the Codex cross-review of #82 surfaced.

## Changes
- **DNS-rebinding TOCTOU (HIGH):** `check_url_safety` now returns a vetted resolved IP; `PinnedHTTPHandler`/`PinnedHTTPSHandler` connect to that pinned IP (original `Host` header preserved), so urllib does not re-resolve the hostname to a different (internal) address at connect time.
- **Cross-origin auth-header leak (HIGH):** transport strips the entire `source.headers` block when an article URL's origin differs from the source endpoint's origin (allowlist-by-origin, not a sensitive-name denylist); redirects keep only a safe header allowlist.
- **192.0.0.0/24 special-use (MEDIUM):** explicit denylist for ranges Python 3.11's `is_global` reports as public.

## Validation
`tests/expansion` 62 passed / 0 failed (7 pre-existing xfails); 3 new test files (pinning, origin-header-scoping, special-use) 14 passed; ruff clean (S ruleset enforced). No existing test files modified.

## ⚠️ Review status - needs a careful look before merge

author: strangeleet
body:
## Summary

Describe the user-visible behavior and save-format impact.

Pals created through the editor (`/api/create` → `storage.create`) inherit the cosmetic skin of the clone source, so in-game the created Pals are all rendered with the source Pal's appearance regardless of their real `CharacterID`.

**Root cause:** `create()` uses the first populated Pal as a clone source and then calls `_reset_created_entry()` to reset identity fields (`CharacterID`, gender, level, IVs, passives, etc.). It does **not** reset `SkinName` or `SkinAppliedCharacterId`. If the clone source has a cosmetic skin applied, every created Pal keeps that skin, and the game renders a Pal from its applied skin when present — so a batch of created Pals with different `CharacterID`s all appear as the source Pal.

Real-world repro: the clone source was a Chillet Ignis with `WeaselDragon_Fire_Skin003` applied; six freshly created Pals (Direhowl, Azurobe Cryst, Galeclaw, Chillet, Lyleen Noct, Xenolord) all showed up — Palbox icon and deployed model — as Chillet Ignis, while their detail panels (name/stats/passives) were correct. A Pal captured normally in-game (`SkinName = None`) was unaffected, which pinpointed the skin fields.

**Save-format impact:** in `_reset_created_entry`, `SkinName` is reset to the `NameProperty` value `None` and `SkinAppliedCharacterId` is reset to the empty-GUID `StructProperty`, matching the values Palworld writes for an unskinned Pal. No other fields or slot structure change.

## Validation

- [x] `python -m py_compile app/*.py convert_globalpalbox.py`
- [x] `git diff --check`
- [x] Container build completed
- [x] Load, export, and reload behavior checked when save logic changed

## Save Safety

- [x] Generated files, SAV files, backups, `.env`, and `runtime/` are not included.
- [x] The change preserves valid Global Palbox slot structure.

body:
## Summary

Closes #207.

The faceted-diamond mark's hairline girdle read as illegible micro-text at masthead size. This adopts the owl of Athena (from the tetradrachm-inspired artwork picked in the design exploration) as the site mark, traced to SVG so it is crisp at every size:

- **`Mark.tsx`** (inline wordmark glyph) and **`icon.svg`** (favicon): the owl-only crop, dark ink `#063f1d`. The full composition has too much detail to survive 16px.
- **`icon.svg`** additionally swaps its fill to paper `#fbfaf6` via a `prefers-color-scheme: dark` media query, since the dark ink is near-invisible on dark tab strips (~1.7:1 contrast on black). Safari ignores SVG favicons and falls back to the touch icon.
- **`apple-icon.tsx`** (180px touch icon): the full composition (owl, olive sprig, rounded frame) on the opaque warm-paper tile, where the dark ink is always legible.

## Design process

Three ideation rounds (~70 candidates across abstract owls, refined claim-node marks, graph-structure marks, Greek typographic marks, and tetradrachm abstractions) reviewed on an untracked `/logo-preview` page, with per-candidate geometry critique and small-size misread checks (cat/skull/fox/robot). The final artwork was supplied as a bitmap, un-matted to alpha, component-separated (owl vs. sprig vs. frame), and potrace-vectorized into a `0 0 24 24` viewBox matching the previous mark's conventions.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` passes.
- Verified in the running app: masthead glyph next to the wordmark, `/icon.svg` serving, and small-size legibility (14/16/24/48px) plus dark-background behavior on the preview page.

body:
💡 **What:** Improved the accessibility of the `DateSelectorStrip` component by explicitly defining TalkBack semantics and full date names.

🎯 **Why:** Previously, screen readers read abbreviated text ("MON") without explicitly announcing the selected state since they do not inherently pick up on visual UI changes (like color or font weight) denoting a selected item. Adding the explicit `selected` property ensures users using TalkBack understand which date is currently active. Using full text (e.g. "Monday") provides a clearer experience.

📸 **Before/After:**
*Before:* TalkBack reads "MON, 20"
*After:* TalkBack reads "Monday, July 20. Selected." (when selected)

♿ **Accessibility:** Added `.clearAndSetSemantics` to override the default text reading. Explicitly supplied `contentDescription` with full names (via `TextStyle.FULL`) and provided the `selected = isSelected` semantic property, positioned after `.clickable` to avoid overriding the click action.

PR Description
## Summary

- Harden Reef’s durable command and event path before raising the verified 10k commands/sec ceiling.
- Preserve transactional correctness, deterministic ownership, replay integrity, and idempotent materialization.
- Document the evidence, remaining bottlenecks, promotion gates, and restart plan for 20k–50k tuning.

## What Changed

- Add transactional Kafka command consumption and venue-event publishing.
- Add shard ownership leases, deterministic recovery checksums, and terminal-state retention controls.
- Make canonical venue-event batch persistence atomic and idempotent.
- Add database integrity constraints and migration coverage.
- Improve materializer batching, accounting, and failure handling.
- Add configurable simulator price ticks to avoid pathological one-level-per-order workloads.
- Add repeatable materializer scaling gates and benchmark validation.
- Record the architecture audit, measured 10k results, storage amplification, fault lines, and phased scaling plan.

body:
## 目的

Home サイドバーで新規 session を作成したとき、**daemon 作成完了までの間に出るはずの 2 行 loading skeleton（activity glyph + 名前の低速 wave）が表示されない**回帰を修正する。ユーザー報告「作成の時の waving が消えている（削除の時は出ている）」に対応。

## 調査結果（root cause）

- 削除中の wave（`✂` + Danger shimmer）は既存の `removing` 実装があり**正常**。壊れていたのは**作成側**。
- 作成 skeleton は「まだ存在しない session」の**合成行**が必要だが、本番 controller/legacy shell 経路に投影・描画がどこにも無かった（shell の `ui.creating_session` は failure reflux 用の token を持つだけで、`removing_session` と違い描画に使われていなかった）。
- 仕様 `document/03-tui.md:139-151` は「作成中は `+ new session` の直前に session と同じ 2 行の skeleton を低速 wave で描く」と既に規定しており、実装欠落＝ **doc drift**。inline 作成（#361）→ CreateSession modal（#315/#1055）→ inline revert（#1089）の変遷で作成 skeleton 描画が落ちたのが原因。

## 変更内容

- shell `ui.creating_session` を `PendingCreate { token, name }` に拡張し、in-flight 作成の名前を保持。dispatch でセット、`drain_session_completions` の完了 take でクリア（daemon 行が着地するフレームで atomic に skeleton→実 row へ置換）。
- `render_controller_frame` から `HomeProjection.create_pending` へ名前を thread。`home_left_pane` が `+ new session` の直前に 2 行 skeleton を描画（`create_skeleton_lines`、`widgets::Shimmer` の低速 sweep）。viewport は skeleton 分を予約し `+ new session` をスクロールで隠さない。skeleton は非選択・current 対象外。
- 削除 wave（`removing`）は無改変。

## テスト・確認方法

- 追加した regression tests:
  - `create_skeleton_draws_two_padded_lines_that_wave_with_the_tick`（純関数: 幅一定・tick でフレーム変化＝静的点滅でない）
  - `home_pending_create_waves_a_skeleton_above_new_session`（`render_home`: `+ new session` 直前に skeleton／pending 無しでは skeleton も "creating" も出ない）
  - `render_controller_frame_draws_a_waving_pending_create_skeleton`（本番 frame 経路の表示 + tick アニメーション）
- `cargo fmt` / `cargo test -p usagi-tui`（634 pass）/ `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` green。
- coverage 100% は PR CI に委譲（規約どおりローカルでは重い full gate を回さない）。新規の coverage 対象コード（`create_skeleton_lines` / `with_create_pending` / `home_left_pane` 分岐 / `render_controller_frame`）は上記 3 test で網羅。shell 側追加（`PendingCreate`・dispatch・drain・loop 呼び出し）は既存どおり `#[coverage(off)]`。
- 未実行 gate: ローカル coverage（instrumented daemon test が極端に遅く timeout。CI で確認）。docs は既に仕様を記載済みのため変更なし（drift 解消）。

## 経緯（この PR の履歴）

triage session として起票 → 症状が「作成側 wave」と判明し issue #384 を作成 wave 回帰へ改題・再定義 → 実装 → issue を done。

## Summary

Un-quarantines `s55_nested_decompose`, quarantined under #9925 as 'born-racy' (~80% red 2026-07-18).

**The issue's original diagnosis was wrong.** It attributed the flake to a decompose→review escalation race. Investigation (full dossier on #9925) disproved that: there is no HITL-worker race, decompose-before-HITL is already solid, and the numbering/ledger-reset hypotheses were ruled out with hard evidence.

**Actual root cause:** the #9796 `DiscoverRunner`/`ShapeRunner` **air-gapped-sandbox wedge**. s55's children start at `hydraflow-find` and pass through discover/shape with no discover/shape script seeded, so those runners spawned a real `claude` and ran to `agent_timeout`, freezing the discover/shape phase loop. The child never reached review→escalate→decompose and the epic stalled at 50% — the exact symptom, timing-sensitive (worse on slow CI runners → ~80% red, 'victim varies per run').

**#9919 already fixed it** (sentinel-guard the discover dispatch + drop `ShapePhase._runner` in `sandbox_main`; shipped `test_issue_9796_discover_sandbox_bypass.py`). It landed **28 minutes after** the quarantine, so it fixed s55 too — but nobody noticed because s55 was already out of collective runs.

## Evidence

**31/31 consecutive green docker runs**, far exceeding #9925's 10-consecutive-green bar:
- Local: plain 6/6, host-CPU-stress @load-84 8/8, container `cpus:0.35` 5/5 (19/19)
- **GitHub CI runners: 12/12** (via a temporary diagnostic workflow, since reverted — the environment where it actually reproduced)

## Changes
- Drop `QUARANTINED='#9925'` from the scenario → restores it to collective runs
- Restore s55 to ci.yml's PR→staging fast subset (+ fix the stale step name)
- Update the quarantine contract pins (hidden set is now empty)

The re-enabled s55 in this PR's own `sandbox-fast` CI run is the e2e regression; `test_issue_9796_discover_sandbox_bypass.py` (from #9919) is the unit regression.

Closes #9925.

## Summary

- guides owners from business context into evidence-aware AI provider selection
- distinguishes connection availability from approval for company data, with conservative runtime activation defaults
- records account type, no-training terms, and enabled processing regions using the existing provider-connection substrate
- gives clear use-now, review-first, and blocked workload guidance, including local-model caveats
- lets the owner ask the COO for an explanation; the COO delegates regulation and sovereignty questions to AGT-902 through the governed coworker interface
- adds source-backed compliance corpus, prompts, user documentation, design documentation, and regression tests

## Why

Non-technical owners should be able to configure providers confidently without mistaking a personal login or successful connection for a business-safe data-processing decision. This is especially important for EMEA, regulated sectors, and sovereignty-sensitive workloads.

## Verification

- governed merged-code pregate passed at 54e6b3970: full web test suite, TypeScript typecheck, production build, Prisma generate, and all 414 migrations checked
- focused provider suitability and COO handoff tests passed
- authenticated UX walkthrough passed on desktop and 390x844 mobile for provider guidance, account evidence, and the COO handoff
- new UI fits with guardrails; a pre-existing provider status-row mobile overflow was observed outside this diff

## Safety posture

Guidance is evidence-aware and fail-closed. Provider-published facts are kept distinct from evidence about the connected account, unknowns are stated, factual compliance claims require references, and the coworker does not present this as legal advice.

## Design grounding

- Existing specs/plans reviewed: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-03-21-coo-led-onboarding-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-19-estate-sovereignty-governance-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-28-activity-level-ai-routing-harness-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-28-ai-readiness-console-design.md`, and the AIPS-003 inputs reflected in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-19-governed-llm-provider-onboarding.md`.
- Current code substrate reviewed: `apps/web/lib/govern/activate-provider.ts`, `apps/web/lib/actions/ai-providers.ts`, `apps/web/lib/tak/agent-routing.ts`, setup progress/actions, provider pages, coworker prompts, and the existing `AiProviderConnection` evidence fields.
- Source of truth: existing provider connection evidence plus canonical business context; no parallel provider-policy table was introduced.
- Decision: compile business context and account evidence into conservative workload guidance, keep the COO as owner-facing persona, and delegate specialist compliance questions to AGT-902.

UX-Fit-Decision: fits-with-guardrails — plain-language progressive disclosure, safe defaults, an explicit unsure option, and one owner-facing COO action; detailed evidence remains on the provider detail page.

Seed-Fit-Decision: global-default

author: dequanlin520
body:
Closes #47

## Protocol version and capabilities

- Raises Bridge XPC protocol to `1.2` with compatible minor-version semantics.
- Adds `authorizedRootManagement` and `fileEventObservation` capabilities.
- Compositions without file integration return typed `unsupportedCapability` responses.

## Root-management operations

- Adds typed operations for list, register, refresh, deactivate, reactivate, remove, and status.
- Registration and refresh accept bounded bookmark `Data` only; there is no path-string alternative.
- Authorized-root summaries expose safe metadata only and omit resolved paths and bookmark data.

## Event-subscription model

- Adds a Bridge-owned file-integration coordinator and bounded polling subscription broker.
- Supports create, poll, acknowledge, cancel, and monitor-status operations.
- Subscriptions use generated IDs, selected active authorized root IDs, bounded root count, bounded queues, bounded poll timeout, inactivity expiry, idempotent cancellation, and shutdown cleanup.

## Cursor and backpressure semantics

- Tracks observed, delivered, and acknowledged cursors separately.
- Acknowledged cursor advances only on explicit acknowledgement.
- Duplicate acknowledgements are idempotent; acknowledgements beyond delivered cursor are rejected.
- Slow consumers overflow to bounded `rescanRequired` batches with safe dropped-event reasons.
- Replay, history-done, rescan-required, and dropped-event states are explicit.

## Integration result

`Scripts/integration/m5-002-file-events-xpc.zsh` completed with:

```text
ROOT_XPC_REGISTRATION_PASSED=yes
ROOT_SUMMARY_REDACTED=yes
SUBSCRIPTION_CREATED=yes
EVENT_BATCH_RECEIVED=yes
EVENT_PATHS_RELATIVE=yes
CURSOR_ACKNOWLEDGED=yes
SUBSCRIPTION_CANCELLED=yes
RESCAN_PROPAGATION_VALIDATED=yes
FILE_CONTENT_EXPOSED=no
ABSOLUTE_PATH_EXPOSED=no
RESIDUAL_MONITOR_PROCESS=no
M5_002_RESULT=PASS
```

## Privacy boundary

- No file contents, absolute resolved paths, raw bookmark data, prompts, tokens, volume-private identifiers, generic filesystem access, generic event bus, arbitrary path parameters, or generic streaming method are exposed.
- File-event payloads contain root IDs and root-relative paths only.
- File-integration errors are redacted typed codes.

## Tests

Validation run:

- `swift format --in-place --recursive Package.swift Sources Tests`
- `swift build`
- `swift test`
- `swift test --filter HermesBridgeFileIntegrationXPCTests`
- `zsh -n Scripts/integration/m5-002-file-events-xpc.zsh`
- `Scripts/integration/m5-002-file-events-xpc.zsh`
- `git diff --check`
- absolute-path/file-content/token/prompt scan
- residual monitor/service-process check

Test list count: 293.

## Remaining security-scoped authorization work

The next issue should add the trusted app `NSOpenPanel` user-selection flow and security-scoped bookmark validation with the appropriate signed, sandboxed app entitlements. M5-002 intentionally does not add NSOpenPanel UI.

author: beardthelion
body:
An arbitrary-equality (`===`) version accepts commas, but `SpecifierSet` treats a comma as the separator between specifiers, so the two disagree:

- `SpecifierSet("===hello,")` and `SpecifierSet([Specifier("===hello,")])` produce different results.
- `Specifier("===moo,<=0.1")` silently swallows the second specifier.

This excludes commas from the arbitrary-equality character class in the specifier regex, so `Specifier` and `SpecifierSet` agree and a comma consistently separates specifiers.

Added `tests/test_issue_1000.py`, which fails on the current tree and passes with the change; `tests/test_specifiers.py` still passes in full.

Closes #1000

This makes the plumbing **deliver** the model's genders, never override them. ## The three fixes **F1 — `frontend/src/orwell_cast_identity.py` `_extract_json` (the P0).** The identity model emitted its JSON object twice (`{obj}{obj}`); the old first-`{`→last-`}` slice yielded invalid JSON → `None` → `{}` → `recordCastIdentity` never called → the engine's #1140 gender re-cohere never ran → stale floor gender shipped. New `_first_json_object` scans from the first `{` with `json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode` (decode-and-stop) and returns the first complete object. A normal single object is byte-identical (no regression). **F2 — `src/adapters/engine/GameSessionAdapter.ts` `recordCastGenesis`.** Added `cohereGenesisNames(cast)` right after the model's names commit: for any warmed NPC whose given name reads *unambiguously as the opposite binary gender* of the pinned `genderPresentation`, re-pick a same-gender name via the existing `pickGivenNameFor` (#1140 machinery), keeping the surname, off a dedicated `:genesis-gender-cohere` sub-stream (calibration-neutral). author: 24x7
body:
PR5 of the shape-purity program — the R2/R4 pivot (spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-19-…-design.html; plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-19-shape-purity-tranche-4.md).

## What
The capability broker moves from each `__wasm-host` child into the daemon, making R2's three structural promises true.

- **Daemon-side broker service** (`src/broker/{server,wire,client}.rs`): one supervised UDS accept loop (SAFETY rule 2) behind a **0700 dir + 0600 socket** — the directory perm is a kernel-enforced same-uid check on both Linux and macOS, subsuming `SO_PEERCRED` without platform syscalls. Each granted function gets a random **32-byte token** minted at spawn; a token authorizes exactly one function's grant table, so a compromised worker can never reach another function's grants. Grantless functions get no socket → `denied` locally, zero IPC. Connection budget bounded (reject-not-queue).
- **BCP wire codec** (`wire.rs`): length-prefixed frames + CALL payload, bounded decode (4 MiB cap), property-style tests (roundtrip, truncated, oversize, unknown type).
- **Sync child client** (`client.rs`): the `__wasm-host` child **drops its tokio runtime and `block_on` entirely** for a `std::os::unix::net::UnixStream` with read/write timeouts = `call_timeout + slack`; lazy connect, reconnect-on-error → `timeout` envelope, never a hung guest. `--broker-grants` argv and `RIZ_BROKER_RESOURCES` env are deleted; `ProcessManager` mints `RIZ_BROKER_{SOCK,TOKEN,TIMEOUT_MS}` per granted wasm worker.
- **Shared pool** (`pg.rs`): one **`deadpool-postgres` pool per resource** (`max_connections`/`acquire_timeout_ms`) — pools the *proven* tokio-postgres backend rather than sqlx, preserving the verified decode matrix, text-param convention, read-only tx, rustls TLS, and the wire mock byte-for-byte (the highest-risk surface stays unchanged; sqlx was the spec's first pick, deadpool its pre-agreed alternative). **DSNs resolve at daemon startup** (fail-fast). Verb dispatch (`Broker::dispatch`) moves daemon-side.
- **Merge-blocking tests**: `wasm_broker_pg` green end-to-end through the socket (granted→200, denied→502, stalled→timeout); `broker_limits` tombstone (concurrency 4 vs max_inflight 1 → exactly 1 admitted, 3 throttled, peak backend concurrency 1); `broker_pg` (7 wire-mock tests) unchanged.
- **orders-wasm capstone**: best-effort persist through the `db` grant — denied/error degrades to `persisted:false` so the order still prices; commented grant block in riz.all.toml shows the wiring.

## Gates
fmt ✅ · clippy -D warnings ✅ · safety-check --gate ✅ · nextest workspace 1272/1272 ✅ · e2e_smoke_all ✅ · template_smoke_all 6/6 ✅

author: synaptsea
body:
Fixes #154199

`Python/getversion.c` formats the compiler identification with `"%.80s"`. The banner
that `PC/pyconfig.h` emits for clang-cl builds is
`"[Clang " __clang_version__ "] 64 bit (AMD64) with MSC v.<n> CRT]"`, and official LLVM
Windows binaries have an 86-character `__clang_version__` (version + repo URL + full
commit hash), so the tail carrying the `"MSC v."` marker is always cut off.

`ctypes.util._get_build_version()` looks for that marker and, not finding it, fell back
to `return 6` — "assume the compiler is MSVC 6". `find_msvcrt()` then maps version 6 to
`msvcrt.dll` and `find_library('c')` returns it. That CRT does not share its `errno` with
the ucrt that `_ctypes` is linked against, so `ctypes.get_errno()` silently returns stale
values after a failing call. No exception is raised — the caller just gets wrong data.

This reports the build version as unknown instead, so `find_msvcrt()` and
`find_library('c')` return `None` exactly as they already do on modern MSVC builds
(where `_get_build_version()` returns 14.x and the "CRT is no longer directly loadable"
branch from bpo-23606 applies). `find_msvcrt()` already had a `version is None` guard, so
this simply routes truncated banners into the existing safe path.

While fixing that I found a second manifestation of the same truncation: when the cut
lands *inside* the version digits, the marker is present but the number is not, and
`s, rest = sys.version[i:].split(" ", 1)` raises
`ValueError: not enough values to unpack` out of `find_library('c')` — worse than a wrong
return value. `partition()` handles both cases. Happy to split that into its own PR if
you would rather keep this one to the single change.

The documented contract is unchanged: `Doc/library/ctypes.rst` already says `find_msvcrt()`
returns `None` "if the name of the library cannot be determined", and that `find_library("c")`
fails on Windows. Only the undocumented MSVC-6 fallback is removed.

## Testing

Added `FindLibraryWindows` to `Lib/test/test_ctypes/test_find.py`. It patches `sys.version`
with `unittest.mock`, so it exercises the fix on any Windows build — a clang-cl build is not
needed to run it. It covers a truncated clang banner, a truncation inside the marker, and a
real MSVC banner (asserting 14.4 / `None`, so the MSVC path is pinned against regression).

On a local clang-cl free-threaded build, `python -m test test_ctypes`:

- before: `run=674 failures=1` (`test_errno.Test.test_open`: `AssertionError: 0 != 2`) — FAILURE
- after: `run=678 skipped=40` — SUCCESS

`test_open` now skips with `'Unable to find C library'`, identical to an MSVC build. Three
tests move from run to skipped (`test_errno.test_open`, `test_loading.test_find`,
`test_callbacks.test_issue_8959_a`); all three already skip on MSVC builds, so this converges
clang-cl onto the reference platform rather than reducing coverage. Verified no MSVC
regression by mocking real banners: `MSC v.1944` -> 14.4, `MSC v.1600` -> `msvcr100.dll`,
`MSC v.1200` -> `msvcrt.dll` (a genuine MSVC 6 build is unaffected).

The root cause is arguably the `"%.80s"` precision in `Python/getversion.c` — `sys.version`
also ends mid-hash without its closing bracket on these builds, and it broke
`sysconfig.get_platform()` the same way in gh-145410. I have not touched it here since that
would change `sys.version` content for every consumer, but it may be worth a separate issue.

author: mjmelon
body:
## Problem
Customer's portal shows **Available Points: 1,532** but the checkout Points section shows **Balance: 0 pts** with the Redeem button greyed out. Two pages, two different numbers, same customer.

## Root cause
The customer portal (`src/pages/shop/main.js` in the account view) reads the `salesweb_customer_points_balance` view AND, when that returns 0, falls back to summing `orders.points_issued` and subtracting redeemed rows from the ledger. That's why the portal displays 1,532: the ledger view is coming back empty (probably `issuePoints` never inserted an Earned ledger row for those historical orders, but `points_issued` on the order rows themselves is populated) and the fallback recovers.

Checkout's `loadPointsBalance` had no such fallback — it just trusted the view read, and defaulted to 0.

## Fix
`public/payment.html` `loadPointsBalance()` now mirrors the portal's computation exactly:
1. Try the balance view (with `pending_redeemed` fallback for older schemas — from PR #219).
2. If the view returns `balance <= 0`, sum `SUM(salesweb_customer_orders.points_issued)` for the user.
3. Subtract `SUM(|change|)` of negative rows in `salesweb_points_ledger`.
4. Subtract `pointsPendingHold`.
5. Use that derived value if positive.

No SQL needed — client-side change only.

## Test plan
- [ ] Hard-refresh the checkout page for the same customer whose portal shows 1,532 pts.
- [ ] Points section now shows **Balance: 1,532 pts**, Redeem button enabled.
- [ ] Typing a value into the input still live-previews the balance drop (from PR #218).
- [ ] Clicking Redeem still applies the discount and drops the balance display accordingly.

author: brainsyeth
body:
## Why

Adding a few specific videos to the clip library required running the **full 38-channel scan**, which heatmap-scrapes every Tier-2 candidate (a `yt-dlp -J` per video). With `VIDEOS_PER_CHANNEL` bumped for supply, that became minutes-per-channel and the *productive* new channels sit at the end of the list — so a refill could grind for hours before reaching them. The scan is the wrong tool for "add these videos."

## What this adds

Two scan-free modes in `clipengine-local/run-local.sh`:

- **`--urls-file <file>`** — batch-add a hand-picked list. One YouTube URL per line, optional trailing river slug (`<url> current`); `#` comments and blank lines ignored. **Each URL is pre-deduped against `clip_library` before any `yt-dlp` download**, so already-clipped URLs cost one REST call, not a full scrape+extract. `--category high_water` tags the whole batch.
- **`--channel <url>`** — scan just ONE channel instead of all of `channels.json` (onboarding a newly-added source without re-walking the other 37).

Implementation: adds small shared helpers (`video_id_of`, `dedup_status`, `add_one_url`); the channel-scan body is **unchanged** — only its producer is wrapped so `--channel` emits a single entry. `--url`/`--peak` behavior is untouched (single `--url` still respects `--peak` for a specific window, so it is intentionally *not* pre-deduped).

## Honest note on the "skip the heavy -J" idea

I explored replacing the `-J` with a light duration fetch for known-river adds. There isn't one: yt-dlp always does a full single-video extraction (`--print duration` ≈ `-J`), and channel flat-playlist listings don't return duration. So the real efficiency win is **not scanning 38 channels** + **skipping already-clipped videos before the download** — which is where the time actually went. Documented as such in `clipengine-ops.md`.

## Verification

- `bash -n` clean.
- Batch-add of an already-clipped video (`_eRGIZ4KgAQ`) via `--urls-file`: parsed the file (comment + blank line skipped, URL + river parsed), pre-deduped, and **skipped with no download** → `Batch add complete: 0 dispatched of 1 URL(s)`.
- Full end-to-end (actual dispatch) not run here to avoid YouTube load; the produce/handoff path is the same `process_video` the scan already uses.

`docs/clipengine-ops.md` updated (behavior change) with the new modes under "Diagnosing a dry backlog → Refill on demand".

author: jdfalk
body:
## Summary

Adopts the **TODO.md fragment system** — the TODO-file counterpart of the
`changelog.d/` + `scriv` system this repo already uses — so parallel PRs stop
colliding on `TODO.md`.

New tasks are added by dropping a uniquely-named Markdown fragment in `todo.d/`
instead of editing `TODO.md` directly. `scripts/assemble_todo.py` folds them in
below the `<!-- todo-insert-here -->` marker and `git rm`s the fragments it
consumed, so the insertion and removals land in one commit.

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `todo.d/todo.ini` | Config. **Its presence is what opts this repo in.** |
| `todo.d/README.md` | Contributor guide. |
| `todo.d/templates/new_fragment.md` | Fragment scaffold. |
| `scripts/assemble_todo.py` | The assembler (`--dry-run`, `--check`, `--keep`). |
| `.github/workflows/todo-collect.yml` | Daily + `workflow_dispatch` collector. |

- **Add-only** — fragments add tasks; checking one off or promoting it out of the
  Inbox is a normal direct edit of `TODO.md`.
- **No PR check** (unlike changelog fragments) — adding a task is optional and
  shouldn't gate code PRs.
- **Opt-in by presence** of `todo.d/todo.ini`; the workflow self-skips without it.

Added the `## 📥 Inbox` section and marker to the existing `TODO.md`; no curated section was touched.

Built and validated in falkcorp/github-common#328 (round-trip verified there:
a fragment folds into the Inbox and is deleted, and an all-comments fragment is
dropped as an intentional no-op).

body:
## O gap (fraqueza `orq-anti-goodhart`, grade de réguas nota **5,0**)

> *"Sem anti-Goodhart no layer de agente"* — evidência do ledger: **gate-selftest cobre gates; ledger-check C10 NÃO CALIBRADO; camada C não-implementada**. Degrau literal: **"fixture artefato-plantado no refuter"**.

O `gate-selftest` prova que as **catracas (scripts determinísticos)** mordem com fixture boa+ruim. Mas o **LAYER DE AGENTE** (o REFUTER LLM dos workflows adversariais) não tinha negative control: nada provava que o refuter *refuta de verdade* e não só carimba (**One Token to Fool** — juiz enganado por pista superficial). O `ledger-check C10` (calibração do juiz) foi desenhado pra isso mas precisa de **rótulo humano às cegas** e está com **0 rodadas**. Este chip é o negative control **automático** complementar.

## O que faz

Injeta um **artefato PLANTADO** — uma claim de superioridade **absurdamente falsa** (ex.: *"nenhum ERP usa git, só o oimpresso"*) — no **mesmo refuter**, com o **mesmo prompt/schema**. O refuter **TEM que derrubá-lo** (`REFUTADO`). Se ele **APROVA** o plantado (`ACIMA_CONFIRMADO`), está carimbando → **Goodhart**. É o análogo do gate-selftest, aplicado ao layer de agente.

## Dois braços (idêntico à relação gate-selftest ↔ gates reais)

| Braço | Onde | Prova |
|---|---|---|
| **VIVO** | `.claude/workflows/reguas-do-sistema.js` (fase Refutar) — canário injetado no refuter LLM real, fora do cap/placar/ledger, disclosure na grade (regra 17) | que o **braço negativo do adversário DISPARA** — espelha o disclosure `REFUTADO_TB=0 em 81` (nunca disparou → não se sabia se PODE) |
| **DETERMINÍSTICO** | catraca `refuter-canary` do `gate-selftest` + fixtures `{good,bad}` + `refuter-canary-check.test.mjs` | que a **DETECÇÃO** de Goodhart morde, sem LLM/rede (hermético, segundos) |

**Residual honesto (declarado nos comentários):** o selftest prova que o *alarme dispara* sob aprovação; o refuter LLM em si só é exercitado pelo braço VIVO. Mesma relação do gate-selftest com os gates reais.

## Aderência às ressalvas §5

- **(a) extensão do gate-selftest CONSOLIDADO, não motor novo:** +1 catraca no `gate-selftest.mjs` + `.test.mjs` espelhando o precedente do C10 (`ledger-check-juiz.test.mjs`).
- **(b) fixture-que-MORDE, não presence-gate:** o caso *bad* (refuter aprovou o plantado) **TEM que avermelhar** (exit 1) — verificado.
- **(c) relaciona-se com `REFUTADO_TB=0/81`:** o plantado é a prova **controlada** de que o braço negativo PODE disparar.

## Arquivos

- `scripts/governance/refuter-canary-check.mjs` — corpus + `avaliarVerdict`/`avaliarLote` + CLI `--check`/`--list` (deconflito vs C10/pr-critic no header).
- `scripts/governance/gate-selftest.mjs` — catraca `refuter-canary`.
- `tests/governance-fixtures/refuter-canary/{good,bad}/refutacao.json` + README.
- `scripts/governance/refuter-canary-check.test.mjs` — 17 vetores bite/release (wired advisory em `governance-script-tests.yml`).
- `.claude/workflows/reguas-do-sistema.js` — canário vivo no refuter (prompt compartilhado `promptRefuterFull`, byte-idêntico ao real).
- `.claude/skills/reguas-do-sistema/SKILL.md` — nota de descoberta (regra 3, body-only).

## Verificação local (Node-puro — fora da regra CT100 de Pest/PHPStan)

- `gate-selftest.mjs`: **68/68** catracas mordem (boa passa, ruim falha pelo motivo certo).
- `refuter-canary-check.test.mjs`: **17/17**.
- `selftest-registry-check`: 0 órfãos (novo test reconhecido como wired).
- `skills-index --check`: em dia.

**PARA NO PR** (R10 — merge é decisão [W]). Ledger `memory/reguas/` **intocado** de propósito (re-grade é a fase Persistir do workflow; "nota nunca é alvo" — errata 0159). O modo delta re-verifica `orq-anti-goodhart` no próximo run (commit em `.claude/workflows/` está nos paths de `orquestracao-adversarial`).

author: degueba
body:
## What happened (prod incident)
The studio's deployed preview shows **'Onda render error · Invalid props for KineticText: received "slice", invalid_enum_value'** for the *Slice*, *Squeeze* and *Flip* templates and every composition built from them.

**Root cause — release gap, not a code bug:** `0.6.0` was published at 17:56 UTC on 2026-06-25; the kinetic-type-pack (PR #39, adding `squeeze`/`slice`/`flip` to KineticText) merged to main **86 minutes later** and was never released. The studio backend validates against its *vendored* bundle (which has the presets), so seeding/vetting/export all pass — only the browser preview, running published `onda-engine@0.6.0`, rejects the enum. Release-Please is path-scoped to `packages/umbrella` and never proposed a release for components-only commits (the documented manual-bump case).

## This PR
One line: umbrella `0.6.0 → 0.6.1`. Everything else ships from main as-is (tag→main diff is additive only: kinetic presets, magic-resize/responsive additions, `flattenResponsive` export).

**0.6.1 (not 0.7.0)** so the studio frontend's `^0.6.0` pin picks it up with zero code change — just a redeploy.

## After merging
Run the manual publish (Release-Please won't fire for this): **Actions → Release (npm) → Run workflow**, or:
```
gh workflow run release-npm.yml --repo onda-engine/onda-engine
```
Then redeploy the studio frontend (any push to its main) and hard-refresh.

## 内容要点

- **破题**：用「楼下咖啡馆借条」把「当老板（股东）」与「当债主（债券）」并排对照——债主吃「固定」、股东吃「剩余」。
- **四个零件**：面值、票息率、期限、发行方（信用），以及「一排固定小票 ＋ 末尾还本」的现金流结构。
- **皇冠章节**：从第一性原理讲透「**债价与市场利率反向**」这条第一铁律（票息被锁死→只能改价格追平新利率），含现值公式与久期直觉，并解释 2022 年「猛烈加息→全球债券也大跌」。
- **两个交互 widget**：① 债券现金流拆解器；② 债价 vs 利率跷跷板（拖动利率看价格反向跳、长债更敏感）。均为自包含 IIFE、含空值守卫，套用站点 `.widget` 样式。
- **三重风险**：利率风险、信用/违约风险（含评级与「高收益=垃圾债」警示，呼应 Topic 20/25）、通胀风险。
- **组合定位**：债券是「压舱石」而非「发动机」，为后续资产配置模块埋种子。
- **🇸🇬 新加坡视角**：SGS、SSB、T-bills、公司债/债券基金与 CPF 的「类债券」逻辑，强调 SGS（有价格风险）vs SSB（保本）的性格差异。
- **章末自测**：5 题，`answer` 分布 [1,2,0,2,1]，JSON 校验通过；覆盖债权本质、反向铁律、久期、高息风险、压舱石定位。

author: gghatano
body:
## 概要

Issue #1「回収した結果をまとめたい」への対応です。単にスキルを回収するだけでなく、各スキルが**どういう目的のものか**を横断的に把握できるよう、目的（カテゴリ）別の整理を同期パイプラインと GitHub Pages の両方に組み込みました。

91 スキル（50 ユニーク名）を 9 カテゴリに分類しています。

## 変更内容

### 新規

- **`catalog/categories.json`** — スキル名 → 目的カテゴリのタクソノミー定義。複数リポジトリで共通利用される同名スキル（`report-review`、`experiment-plan` 等）はスキル名単位で 1 回定義すれば全リポジトリに反映されます。
- **`docs/skill-purpose-catalog.md`** — 出典リポジトリ順ではなく**目的別**に整理した新カタログ（自動生成）。

### 変更

- **`scripts/sync_skills.py`**
  - タクソノミーの読み込み・検証（ID/スキル名の重複を拒否）
  - 各スキルへのカテゴリ付与と、未分類スキルの警告出力
  - 目的別カタログのレンダリング
  - `manifest.json` / `index.html` の各エントリへ `category` を付与
  - `--from-manifest`: GitHub にアクセスせず既存マニフェストからカタログ類を再生成するオフラインモード
  - `--from-manifest` 実行時に `categories.json` が欠損している場合は再生成を拒否（既存カテゴリの黙示的消失を防ぐガード）
  - 生成物はすべて `skills/` を置換する前にレンダリング・検証し、途中失敗で部分状態が残らないよう担保
- **`web/index.template.html`（GitHub Pages）** — 目的別ブラウズに対応
  - ツールバーに目的カテゴリのフィルタ（件数付き・タクソノミー順）を追加
  - 各行にスキルの目的タグを表示
  - 検索対象にカテゴリ名を追加し、カテゴリ × 検索 × リポジトリ × 移植性の複合フィルタに対応
- **`catalog/manifest.json`** — 各エントリに `category` を付与
- **`README.md`** — 目的別整理の仕組みと生成物を追記
- **`tests/test_sync_skills.py`** — 分類ロジック・目的別カタログ生成・マニフェスト往復・欠損ガードのテストを追加

## カテゴリ内訳

| カテゴリ | スキル数 |
| --- | --- |
| 研究レポート作成ライフサイクル | 49 |
| 開発ワークフロー（Git / Issue / PR） | 13 |
| 合成データ生成パイプライン | 11 |
| 品質・整合レビュー | 7 |
| 文章・UI/UX ライティング | 3 |
| プライバシー事例カタログ | 3 |
| シミュレーション・数値検証 | 3 |
| 配布・パッケージング | 1 |
| ドメイン固有ツール | 1 |

## 検証

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` — 15 件すべて成功
- `python3 scripts/sync_skills.py --from-manifest` を複数回実行しても生成物に差分が出ない（冪等）ことを確認
- 全 91 スキルが分類済みで、未分類の警告なし
- **敵対的検証**を実施し、`--from-manifest` でタクソノミー欠損時にカテゴリが黙って失われる footgun を発見・修正
- **GitHub Pages を実機 Chromium で検証** — カテゴリ選択で件数一致（例: 品質・整合レビュー → 7 件）、カテゴリ×検索の複合フィルタ動作、JS 例外なしを確認

新しいスキルが未分類のまま同期されると `未分類` カテゴリにまとめられ、同期時に警告が出ます。分類を追加・変更するときは `catalog/categories.json` を編集して再生成してください。

### 既知の制約

- 分類はスキル**名**単位のため、将来「同名で別目的」のスキルが現れると同一カテゴリに併合されます（現状の 10 件の同名スキルはすべて同一目的であることを確認済み）。

## Why this PR exists

#420 was stacked on this branch (`phillram/fix/introvideo-tab-layout`, itself #419's branch) while #419 was still open. When #420 was merged, GitHub merged it into its base — this branch — not into `main`. No follow-up PR landed those commits on `main`, so this branch has been sitting six commits ahead of `main` with real, already-reviewed work on it. This PR closes that gap.

## What's in it (already shipped as #419 and #420, just not on `main` yet)

- **Register selected** button — registers an already on-disk, unregistered video without re-browsing to it via a file picker.

author: bluebugs
body:
## What
Adds a sim-only (translate_off) assertion + documentation to the single-clock (CACHE_SAME_CLOCK) dcache data RAM, recording whether a single-port SRAM could serve it.

## Result
Across **1019** directed dcache scoreboard tests (`sim/cache_sim.sh sc`, hit-under-miss included) plus the `dc` control, the collision assertion — port0 read (`r_en`) and port1 write (`w_en and w_wr`) in the same cycle — fires **0 times**. The blocking FSM only ever allows a concurrent read/write on *different* indices, never the same-cycle single-resource conflict. So a **single-port SRAM (e.g. GF180 `gf180mcu_fd_ip_sram`) is a transparent drop-in** for this RAM (read/write mux, no stall). Documented in `dcache_ram.vhd`; the assertion stays in as a permanent regression guard (fires if a future FSM change breaks the invariant).

Motivation: the jcore-soc GF180 ASIC target maps the cache data RAM onto vendor single-port SRAM; this spike de-risked that (no cache-side stall needed).

Note: `icache_ram.vhd` has no sc/dc split and no unit scoreboard, so its analogous fetch-read/refill-write case is documented structurally only — but the icache is strictly simpler (no CPU store, same blocking FSM), so the same no-collision reasoning applies.

No behavioral RTL change (assertion is translate_off; the rest is comments).

## What

A live-data prototype of the **VoteNow money-in-politics** product, plus a companion research audit. Added under `prototypes/votenow-money-map/`.

**The app** (Vite + React, `react-simple-maps` + real `us-atlas` geometry):
- Landing = **"The Number"**: the de-duplicated federal total, computed by *exact netting* of the FEC bulk committee-summary files (gross receipts − committee-to-committee transfers). Shows the gross decomposition (candidates / parties / PACs) and a comparable cross-cycle trend.
- **US money map** shaded **per registered voter** → drill **nation → state → district → race** → the **source → vehicle → race** money chain, ending at the **dark-money wall** (super PAC ← its top donors, dark-conduit flagged).
- **`scripts/fec-ingest.mjs`** — real OpenFEC ingest (candidate receipts + Schedule E independent expenditures + a donor hop), run with a free `FEC_API_KEY`.

**The research** — `PAE-campaign-finance-audit.md` (+ PDF): a Harvard-PAE-style audit of the sector (the total and its measurement problem, concentration, the dark gap, plus a deep-research section on scandals/prosecutions, uncounted third-party money, and loopholes), each tied to a policy fix.

## Placement / safety
- Lives in `prototypes/` **on purpose** — outside the pnpm workspace globs (`apps/*`, `packages/*`), so it is **not** part of the root `pnpm install` or turbo build and cannot break them.
- Self-contained: own `package.json` + lockfile. Verified: `npm install` + `npm run build` pass (498 modules).
- No changes anywhere else in the repo.

## Production path
Port from this Vite spike to **`apps/votenow-web` (Next.js)** when it graduates (`react-simple-maps` + `us-atlas` work under Next with a `'use client'` map component).

## Run
```bash
cd prototypes/votenow-money-map && npm install && npm run dev
```

## Summary
Adds two notes to `CLAUDE.md` based on friction hit while verifying the project boots on a fresh nightly install:
- A fresh toolchain needs `rustup target add x86_64-unknown-uefi` in addition to `rust-src` — missing it produces a `can't find crate for `core`` error for the loader that's easy to misattribute.
- `rust-toolchain` pins bare `nightly` with no date, so unexpected compile errors (trait-impl mismatches, target-spec fields rejected) may be nightly API drift rather than a code regression — worth checking a crate bump/renamed target-spec value before assuming something broke here.

## Why
Both gotchas were hit for real this session getting a fresh checkout to build (see the two toolchain-compat fixes merged in #6). Writing them down so the next fresh-environment build (agent or human) doesn't have to rediscover them.

## Reviewer notes
Docs-only change, no code/build-script changes. Related: #7 (separate tooling gap, not addressed here).

author: robobun
body:
## Repro

Under `BUN_JSC_validateExceptionChecks=1` on a debug build:

```js
const { expect } = require('bun:test');
expect(new Proxy({}, {})).toEqual(expect.any(Array));
// or:
expect(new Proxy([], {})).toMatchObject([]);
// or:
expect({ a: 1 }).toHaveProperty(new Proxy(new Set(['a']), {}));
```

```
ERROR: Unchecked JS exception:
    This scope can throw a JS exception: isArraySlowInline @ JavaScriptCore/runtime/ArrayConstructor.cpp:128
    But the exception was unchecked as of this scope: hasInstance @ JavaScriptCore/runtime/JSObject.cpp:2678
ASSERTION FAILED: exception check validation failed
```

## Cause

`JSC::isArray()` declares a throw scope on its Proxy path (`isArraySlowInline`, for the revoked-Proxy case). Three call sites in `src/jsc/bindings/bindings.cpp` used it inside an `if` condition and then either entered another throw-scope-declaring call, or returned with the scope's `m_needExceptionCheck` still set:

- `matchAsymmetricMatcherAndGetFlags` (`AsymmetricMatcherConstructorType::Array`): `isArray()` then falls through to `constructorObject->hasInstance()`.
- `Bun__deepMatch`: `isArray(globalObject, objValue) && isArray(globalObject, subsetValue)` chains two throw-scope calls, then `getPropertyNames()`.
- `JSC__JSValue__getIfPropertyExistsFromPath` (the `toHaveProperty` path lookup): when `isArray()` returns false for a Proxy over an iterable non-array (Set, Map, generator), the body is skipped and the function returns `{}` with the outer `ThrowScope` still unsatisfied.

The `Bun__deepEquals` sites (`v1Array`/`v2Array`) already had the check.

## Fix

Hoist each `isArray()` result out of the condition and `RETURN_IF_EXCEPTION` immediately after it. Same pattern as #34747 for the `NodeVM.cpp` instances.

Release behavior is effectively unchanged for `expect.any(Array)` and `toHaveProperty` (the `isArray` revocation error already reached the caller via a later check). For `toMatchObject` with a revoked-Proxy receiver, the thrown `TypeError` message changes from the generic revocation message to `Array.isArray cannot be called on a Proxy that has been revoked`, matching the operation that actually failed.

## Verification

New subprocess test in `test/js/bun/test/expect.test.js` spawns with `BUN_JSC_validateExceptionChecks=1` and runs every affected matcher shape with transparent and revoked Proxies. On builds without exception-scope verification the option is a no-op and the child exits 0 either way.

```
# fail-before (src/ stashed, bun bd):
(fail) expect.any(Array)/toMatchObject/toHaveProperty check the isArray() exception for Proxy values
  exitCode: 134, signalCode: SIGABRT
  ERROR: Unchecked JS exception: isArraySlowInline ... hasInstance

# pass-after (bun bd):
(pass) expect.any(Array)/toMatchObject/toHaveProperty check the isArray() exception for Proxy values
```

`expect.test.js` (408 pass), `jest-extended.test.js` (57 pass), `test/js/node/assert/deep-equal.test.ts` (260 pass) all pass.

## Related

#32948 applies the same `Bun__deepMatch` split as part of a larger Proxy-transparency change and composes with this one; it does not touch the `expect.any(Array)` or `toHaveProperty` sites.

author: gumorming
body:
## What

This PR enhances container creation through quickstart menu option 6:

- Use `VLLM_ENGINE_CONTAINER_NAME` as the canonical container-name variable.
- Keep `VLLM_ENGINE_CONTAINER` as a deprecated compatibility alias.
- Prompt users to enter a custom container name or press Enter to use an automatically generated default.
- Generate the default name from the image basename/tag and current login username.
- Validate container names against Docker naming rules.
- Preserve the username suffix when generated names reach Docker's length limit.
- Clone `ascend-runtime-manager` on demand when quickstart option 6 is used without an initialized workspace.
- Update README, environment templates, profiles, and onboarding documentation.

Example prompt:
```text
Press Enter to use the default [vllm-ascend-v0.17.0rc1-<username>], or input a container name:
```

## Why

Previously, quickstart reused a fixed container name, making it difficult for multiple users or parallel workloads to maintain independent Docker instances.

The documented `VLLM_ENGINE_CONTAINER` variable also differed from the requested `VLLM_ENGINE_CONTAINER_NAME` interface. This PR establishes one canonical variable while retaining backward compatibility.

Additionally, quickstart option 6 previously failed with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'hust_ascend_manager'` when `ascend-runtime-manager` had not already been cloned. The option can now bootstrap this dependency on demand.


Fixes: #18

Signed-off-by: GuMorming <gumorming@163.com>

body:
The **"Add an item"** row read as slightly separated from the list rather than as the next row.

## Two mismatches

1. **Top gap (both breakpoints).** `.folder__add` used `padding-top: --space-3` (12px) where item rows use `--space-2` (8px), so the button landed 4px lower below its divider than an item name does — the content gap before "Add an item" was 21px vs the 17px between items.
2. **Mobile button height.** On mobile an item's name field drops to a compact box (`min-height:0`, tighter padding + leading), but the add button kept its full 36px `min-height`, floating its text lower than the compact names above it.

- `.folder__add` top padding → `--space-2`, so the divider-to-text gap matches the item-to-item gap.
- The add buttons (`.folder__addbtn` and the nested group's `.item-nest__add`) take the item name field's compact mobile metrics below `$bp-stack`, so their text sits at the same rhythm as the rows above.

author: thehalfmoon
body:
## Ratified policy summary

This PR adds the P01-04A Specification and Policy Ratification Package to `specs/mesc-pilot-01/p01-04/`.

**Exact 700/150/150 target** for the 1,000-example PubMedQA dataset (no plus/minus tolerance for the current version).

**No holdout** in P01-04 version 1. Holdout requires separately ratified policy amendment.

**Source-document grouping** with `source_document_id` as the canonical indivisible grouping unit. The current registry contains 1,000 examples, 1,000 source documents, zero multi-example groups. Grouping is currently structurally vacuous but remains the correct forward-compatible invariant. P01-04 does not claim this grouping alone rules out question-level or context-level leakage.

**Deterministic SHA-256 ranking contract** for group allocation: groups ranked by ascending SHA-256 digest of canonical UTF-8 payload using seed `mesc-pilot-01-split-v1` and algorithm version `mesc-pilot-01-split-algorithm/1`. No pseudorandom generator. No raw lexicographic ordering.

**Stratification and apportionment**: decision field stratified on yes/no/maybe. Integer constrained apportionment minimizes squared deviation from ideal 70/15/15 label proportions, with lexicographic tie-breaking (label order: yes, no, maybe; partition order: train, validation, test).

**Leakage taxonomy**: exact example identity, source-document identity, exact raw-question equality, NFKC-normalized question equality, token-set Jaccard greater-than-or-equal-to 0.90 near-duplicate detection, context equality, semantic similarity (deferred). All unresolved candidates must be explicitly classified. Suppression is a stop condition.

**Runtime and promotable evidence separation**: stable identifiers only in public registries. External evidence (command logs, generation workspaces, process access) must remain outside the repository.

**Incident-prevention contract**: isolated paths, independent Generation A/B, byte-equality gate, anti-writeback controls, no in-place repair after freeze, invalidated candidates preserved.

## P01-03G dependency

P01-04 depends on P01-03G promotion (PR #36 merged). The ordered example registry and source-document registry are authoritative inputs and must not be modified.

## Execution boundary

- No source code changes in this PR
- No Python file changes in this PR
- No test changes in this PR
- No real split membership calculated or disclosed
- No leakage audit executed on real data
- No real split artifacts created in this PR
- P01-04B and later: NOT AUTHORIZED
- P01-04 execution: NOT AUTHORIZED
- P01-05: NOT AUTHORIZED

author: ismailgok33
body:
## Why

Flipping the switcher to FR translated only the *chrome* — titles stayed English and the screen read as half-localized. That was the documented ADR-0012 stance (titles are server-localized **content**, not client string tables), but the demo experience argued for demonstrating the server side too. Since the bundled fixture *is* our server (ADR-0004), this PR models production content localization end-to-end: **the data layer serves a per-language payload** — the Accept-Language analog.

## What

- **`achievements-fr.json`** — a structurally identical French document (generic titles translated; **brand Ekiden race names verbatim**, as real localization would). Parity is contract, not convention: ids, types, statuses, values, asset keys are test-pinned equal, so a language switch can never change *what* is shown, only *how it reads*. A canonical-content pin covers the FR copy the same way the EN one is covered.
- **`BundledAchievementsDataSource`** selects the variant via a pure, tested rule (`fr*` → FR document, anything else → base); **`DefaultAchievementsRepository`** takes a `@Sendable` `languageCode` provider read **per call**. The composition root passes the same AppStorage + system-default resolution the switcher UI uses (`AppLanguage` goes public for exactly that consumer), so chrome and content can never disagree.
- **On switch the feature re-fetches** (`refreshContent()`): in-place replace, no loading flip, failure keeps the current content — the client half of re-requesting on an Accept-Language change.
- **Tests:** MedalData 23/23 (7 new), Feature 21/21 (3 new), app suite green; the switcher UI test now asserts the FR *content* end-to-end (`Records personnels`, `Course la plus longue`) plus the fully-French combined header label.
- Visual golden `grid-french` re-specified for FR content + brand-verbatim intent and re-judged **0.975** over the refreshed fully-French capture.

## The review round-trip (read this first)

The adversarial `/ios-review` **FAILED the branch** with a finding that matters beyond this PR: my `.onChange(of: appLanguage)` hook sat **inside** the `.id(appLanguage)` identity boundary — so the language switch replaced the subtree wholesale, `.onChange` never fired, `.task` re-ran a full `load()`, and `refreshContent()` was **dead code in the composed app** (loading flip + error-on-failure, the exact behaviors the spec said don't happen). The reviewer *proved it with its own SwiftUI probe* — my UI test couldn't distinguish the mechanisms because FR content arrives either way. Fixed by reordering (now documented as ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING), re-verified independently — the reviewer re-ran the switcher UI test itself on the simulator before issuing **PASS**.

Second empirical correction from the same round: accessibility labels **follow the app's effective language** (the probe disproved the spec's earlier device-language model — labels render through `Text` under `\.locale`). `accessibility.md`, ADR-0013, the feature spec's Known corner, and two code comments were rewritten to observed behavior, with the switcher UI test as the standing empirical pin.

Both rounds — FAIL, fixes, independent re-verify — are in `telemetry/runs.jsonl`.

## Verification

MedalData 23/23 · AchievementsFeature 21/21 · app suite 6 snapshot/integration + 3 UI green on iPhone 17 · `swiftformat --lint` + `swiftlint --strict` clean · visual suite 6 graded cases 0.975 all-pass, calibration case failing at 0.425 by design · fully-French screenshot in `docs/media/04-fr.png`.

## Summary
Two related nav fixes in one PR (both surface as \"nothing happens when I switch views\"):

1. **/admin/public-page and /admin/fan-page had no dashboard shell.** They were wrapped in a raw \`UniversalLayout\` — public marketing header, no sidebar, no way back to Command Center. Swapped to the same \`UniversalLayout showHeader={false}\` + \`DashboardShell\` pattern the other tenant-admin routes already use (Messenger, Workspace Settings, Analytics, LTI, …). Editors keep their body; they just gain the sidebar + topbar around them.
2. **Platform owner couldn't preview roles.** \`useEffectivePreviewRole\` gated the \"Preview my sidebar as\" toggle strictly to tenant super-admins (either spelling). A platform owner (\`gw_profiles.is_super_admin\`) impersonating a tenant subdomain doesn't have \`gw_tenant_members.role='super_admin'\` there, so the pill highlighted but the sidebar never changed. Broaden the gate to accept the platform-owner flag too.

## Security note
\`applyPreviewRole\` in \`navCatalog.ts\` can only ever **remove** capabilities relative to a real super-admin (see the header comment there — module access is deliberately not overridden). The gate change lets an already-trusted platform owner see less, not more; there's no escalation path.

## What this is

Replaces the shipped plain-CSS/JSX Workbench (`frontend/`) with a **React 18 + TypeScript + Vite + Tailwind + shadcn/Radix** single-page app, wired to the real OpenKB REST API, with an Apple-design material/motion pass, light-default / dark-auto theming, and 中文 / English i18n. Adds the backend endpoints and runtime-config plumbing the new UI needs.

86 commits · 170 files · +21k / −4k. **Squash-merge intended.**

## Frontend

- **Chat-first IA** — Home launcher (recent sessions + grounded chat input with KB scope + slash-command generators `/deck` `/skill` `/visualize`), KB list with a real **create-KB** flow, KB detail (card-nav Overview: Index / Concepts / Entities / Summaries / Reports / Documents; opens `index.md` like a real wiki), per-KB settings gear.
- **Docked artifact panel** — deck / graph / conversationally-generated `output/**.html` open in a sandboxed-iframe side panel (blob URL + bearer, never a token in a URL); chat shows compact "open" cards.
- **Interleaved chat trace** — streamed narration + tool reads render as an ordered step trace (each read a click-through ✅ line) followed by the answer — live **and on restore** (the trace is persisted per turn, read-tool-only; sessions saved before this fall back to the flat text).
- **MarkdownView** — fenced code, lazy Mermaid diagrams, `[[wikilink|alias]]`, LaTeX math via KaTeX (bundled / self-contained), and `---` rules.
- **Apple design** — glass materials, critically-damped springs (`motion`), `prefers-reduced-motion` / `-transparency`, size-specific typography; a11y (Radix modal semantics for the settings sheet, labeled complementary region for the panel).
- **Settings** — global-config editor (model / PageIndex threshold / wiki output language via a UN-official-languages combobox / global default credentials), an About tab, and theme + language toggles in the top-right chrome.
- **i18n** — react-i18next, 8 lazily-loaded namespaces, 中文 default + English, plus a build guard (`check-i18n.mjs`) that fails on leftover UI CJK or zh/en key-set drift.
- New deps pinned **exactly** (motion, mermaid, the i18next stack, katex).

## Backend

- `entities` added to `GET /api/v1/list` (+ `get_kb_list`).
- New routers — `GET /api/v1/graph/html` (self-contained graph), `GET /api/v1/output` (path-guarded, `output/`-only HTML sink), `GET`/`PATCH /api/v1/config` (global defaults + credentials).
- **Runtime config unification** — `resolve_effective_config(kb_dir)` layers defaults → `~/.config/openkb/global.yaml` → KB `.openkb/config.yaml` for the global scalars, migrated across the `load_config` call-sites; RFC-7386 merge-patch with null-removal that preserves inheritance.
- **Chat** — write-capable agent (emits an `artifact` SSE event on a `write_file` of `output/**.html`); per-turn trace persistence (`ChatSession.assistant_traces`), recording only read-tool calls so large generated file contents never hit the session JSON or the restore wire.
- **Global default credentials** written to `~/.config/openkb/.env` (0o600, atomic, under the global-config lock; the API key value is never returned by GET nor logged).

## Testing

- Backend — `uv run pytest -q` → **1175 passed**; `ruff check` / `ruff format` clean.
- Frontend — `npm run build` (tsc + vite) + the `i18n:check` guard green.
- Manual browser verification across light/dark, both locales, and each surface (create-KB dialog, chat trace live + restore, KaTeX math + `---` rules, settings credentials, artifact panel).
- Each sub-project passed an opus whole-branch code review; findings were fixed and re-reviewed.

## Notes

- Configuration lives in files (`global.yaml` / per-KB `config.yaml` / `.env`), not startup input.
- The local API is unauthenticated by default (opt-in bearer via `OPENKB_API_TOKEN`) — intended for local use.
- Dependencies are pinned exactly (supply-chain caution).

author: bobmatnyc
body:
## Summary

- Fixes #3403 — the `app.picker` modal (opened by `/model` and `/provider`) silently swallowed any keystroke that wasn't Up/Down/Enter/Esc. `handle_key` routed **every** key to `handle_picker_key` whenever `app.picker.is_some()`, and `handle_picker_key`'s `_ => {}` catch-all discarded printable chars, Backspace, Tab, etc. with zero feedback.
- This is the `app.picker` sibling of the #3325 (PR #3344) / #3346 (PR #3350) `app.choices` swallow bug — those fixes only ever touched the OTHER overlay state (the LLM-list / `/switch` picker). `app.picker` was never touched.
- Reported live over SSH: user opens `/model` or `/provider`, starts typing, keystrokes vanish.

## UX chosen: type-to-dismiss

Mirrors the #3325 resolution. `handle_key` now only routes `Up`/`Down`/`Enter`/`Esc` into `handle_picker_key`. Any other key:
1. Dismisses the picker (`app.picker = None`)
2. Falls through to the normal input-editing path in the rest of `handle_key`

So a printable character lands in `input_buf` exactly as if no picker were open — never silently discarded. Backspace, Left/Right, Ctrl combos, etc. all fall through the same way.

I considered type-to-filter (narrowing the list as you type) but rejected it for this PR: it changes the picker's interaction model non-trivially (would need a query buffer, re-filtering, cursor-reset semantics) for a bug whose non-negotiable requirement is simply "no silent vanish." Type-to-dismiss is the minimal, consistent-with-precedent fix; a filter UX can be a separate follow-up if wanted.

The picker's footer hint (`↑↓ navigate  Enter select  Esc cancel`, `crates/trusty-agents/src/repl/tui/pickers.rs:244-248`) already existed and needed no change — it correctly describes the now-accurate nav-key-only capture surface.

## Change

`crates/trusty-agents/src/repl/tui/keys.rs` — `handle_key`'s picker-modal gate:

```rust
if app.picker.is_some() {
    match key.code {
        KeyCode::Up | KeyCode::Down | KeyCode::Enter | KeyCode::Esc => {
            return handle_picker_key(app, key);
        }
        _ => {
            app.picker = None;
            // Fall through to normal input handling below.
        }
    }
}
```

Plus updated doc comments in `keys.rs` and `types.rs` (`ReplApp::picker`) reflecting the narrowed capture surface.

## Tests

New, in `crates/trusty-agents/src/repl/tui/tests_render.rs`:

body:
## What

Actually validates the four video-mined `day_intra` prospects against **cached FX 5m history (2015→2025, ~750k bars/pair)** instead of leaving them as unverified specs. Adds `scripts/backtest_prospects.py` and records the results into each candidate's notes + a consolidated `research/video_library/PROSPECT_BACKTEST.md`, so they sync to your **Assess panels** on `git pull`.

The harness reuses the shared `simulate_trades`/`summarize_trades` scorer (single-position, intra-bar stop/TP), splits IS<2022≤OOS, adds a **with-trend control** to beat and a **`--cost-pips` spread model**.

## Results — OOS, pooled AUD/GBP/EUR (PASS bar: PF ≥ 1.3)

| Strategy | Video | N | WR% | PF gross | PF net (0.7pip) | Verdict |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|---|
| orb_retest | 7teij9jI7mg | 1,885 | 42.8 | **1.11** | 1.00 | ⏸ pending |
| three_line_strike | RyTlRkMujuk | 9,887 | 38.1 | 1.01 | 0.89 | ❌ reject |
| amd_session_reversal | Bdgev1or-7M | 1,533 | 37.5 | 0.95 | 0.87 | ❌ reject |
| ema_reclaim_pullback | 7Ds9djcEKB4 | 10,260 | 34.1 | 0.95 | 0.86 | ❌ reject |
| _control_ (with-trend 2:1) | — | 11,543 | 39.3 | 0.97 | 0.85 | baseline |

## Verdict

**None clears PF ≥ 1.3.** With a *tight* 0.7-pip round-turn cost, all four go net breakeven-to-losing:

- **three_line_strike** — the creator's ~70–75% WR claim did not survive; mechanical WR is 38% at a fixed 2:1 (the coin-flip a 2:1 payoff implies). Net-negative → **reject**.
- **ema_reclaim_pullback / amd_session_reversal** — net losers, worse than the naive control → **reject**.
- **orb_retest** — the lone survivor at breakeven-net (EURUSD OOS PF 1.23 gross). But it's SPY/QQQ/ES-native and we have **no cached 5m equity data**, so this FX stand-in isn't faithful → kept **pending** for a proper RTH-equity re-run.

Each detector is a **mechanical interpretation** of the extracted spec (50-EMA for trend, session ranges for AMD, opening-range levels for ORB). This is consistent with the whole intraday pass and the **UFjajYgJBHg** cost-adjusted ORB study: sub-1.3 opening-range/EMA/session scalps don't survive honest transaction costs.

## Reproduce
```bash
python -m scripts.backtest_prospects --since 2015-01-01 --oos 2022-01-01 --pairs AUDUSD,GBPUSD,EURUSD
python -m scripts.backtest_prospects --cost-pips 0.7   # net of a tight retail spread
```

## Follow-ups
- Cache 5m SPY/QQQ/ES bars (Alpaca `/data-fetch`) and re-run `orb_retest` with a 09:30 ET open anchor — the only prospect worth further work.
- Small ORB param sweep (range TF, R:R < 2:1, cutoff) per the UFjajYgJBHg finding.

author: fachriza19
body:
Two related defects, one root cause: "today" is per-user and timezone-dependent, but only the write path knew it.

Habit logs are written with the browser's local date (use-habits.ts), while todayCount and streak were computed with getLocalToday() on the SERVER (habit.service.ts). Whenever the two sit on different calendar days the read misses the row the write created. The Docker image runs UTC with no TZ set, so for a UTC+7 user this broke habit tracking every day from midnight to 7am: progress showed 0/N and streaks appeared broken while the log rows existed all along.

Reproduced against the standalone build with TZ=Pacific/Midway (server 2026-07-19, client 2026-07-20): logging count=5 then reading back returned todayCount=0. With the client's date supplied it returns 5.

Second defect, same cause: nothing invalidated the habits cache at midnight, so a page left open overnight kept yesterday's todayCount — and the +1 control submits an ABSOLUTE count derived from it, so the first tap after midnight wrote an inflated value against the new date.

Fix:
- useLocalToday() exposes the browser's local date and updates it across the day boundary.
- The habits list and detail queries send that date and include it in their cache key, so the day flipping refetches instead of serving stale progress. Verified by shifting the page clock 24h: the list refetched and the count reset from 2/3 to 0/3 on its own.
- listHabits/getHabit take today as a parameter; the route handlers read it from the query string and validate the format, falling back to the server date only for callers with no browser context.

Cache keys are now ["habits", date], so exact-match getQueryData/ setQueryData calls in the mutation hooks were updated. Prefix invalidation on ["habits"] still reaches every dated entry.
