### Summary of Changes
This pull request resolves issue #1: **🎯 Fix: Request Body Exhaustion on HTTP Retries When Using `io.Reader`**.

#### Technical Details
- **Resolved Body Handling for Retries**: Implemented proper buffering or regeneration of the `io.Reader` body for each retry attempt in the HTTP client. This ensures that the request body is correctly managed, especially when the original body is not seekable or rewindable.

- **Enhanced `http.Request` Creation**: Modified the `NewRequest` function to check if the request body is seekable. If not, it buffers the body using a `bytes.Buffer` and updates the `GetBody` function to return a new `io.ReadCloser` for each retry, ensuring consistent behavior across multiple attempts.

*Submitted cleanly via verified engineering workflow.*

author: ryankiley
body:
## The bug

A parent row's weight column shows the **group total** and is `readonly`, so a row that already had a weight lost it the moment anything nested under it — still counted in every total, printed on no row, editable in no field.

Repro on `main`:
1. Add "Zpacks Duplex" → 505 g. Edits fine.
2. Click **Add a nested item**, add "Stakes" at 60 g.
3. The Duplex row now reads 565 g and is locked. 565 − 60 = 505 g that exists, counts, and appears nowhere.

That weight is real data, not a derived value — `groupLineMg` is `own + children` ([weights.ts:135](../blob/main/shared/weights.ts#L135), asserted in `weights.test.ts:357`). The only way back was to un-nest every child, fix it, and re-nest.

## The fix

A group is a container, not a product. Nesting into a row that **carries a weight** now wraps it: a new group takes the row's slot and the product slides underneath as its first child, name/weight/catalog link intact.

```
tent                 550 g   ← group (read-only total)
   └ Zpacks Duplex   490 g   ← editable again
   └ Stakes           60 g
```

A **weightless** row is already a container and still takes children directly, so a hand-built "Cook kit" group behaves exactly as before. All three entry points route through one helper (`containerFor`): the button, the indent action, and drag-to-nest.

The group takes the product's common name ("Tent") and the child gives it up, so the label isn't printed twice; with none to take, the group starts empty with its name field focused. Pulling the last child back out discards an untouched group via `discardEmpty`, which already refuses to remove a row that has children or a name.

**One subtlety worth review:** clearing the child's common name has to set `commonNameOverridden: true`. The child keeps its catalog link, and `hydrateCatalogNames` refills an un-overridden common name from the catalog on the very next snapshot — the label came straight back until I set it.

## Also: "common name" → "gear type"

The user-facing term was botanical jargon. Renamed to **gear type**, which is what the code has called it all along (`shared/gearTypes.ts`: *"the loose-canonical set of 'what it is' labels"*). The placeholder drops the concept noun entirely and shows examples only — it sits directly under the product name, so the contrast is what explains it.

The examples are now the three most common types in the catalog (`backpack` 237 rows, `tent` 118, `quilt` 107). The old **"Shoes" was not a gear type at all** — zero of 2,339 rows carry it, footwear is `trail runners` or `hiking shoes` — so the field was advertising a value it would never fill in.

A group offers no gear type of its own, since its name already is one; a value it acquired before becoming a group still shows, so nothing is stranded. CSV column becomes `Gear Type`, and the importer still accepts the old `Common Name` header so existing exports round-trip.

## Verification

Driven in the browser, not just reasoned about: weight edits on the wrapped product (505 → 490, total tracks to 550) and survives a reload; weightless-container nesting unchanged; indent path produces an empty group with focus in its name; packing mode renders an unnamed group as a dimmed "Group"; un-nesting the last child leaves no litter. 345 tests pass, `typecheck` clean.

## Known gaps

- **No test coverage for this logic.** `containerFor` lives in a client composable and there's no harness for `app/composables/` — every existing test targets `shared/`.
- **Deleting** the last child of a group still leaves the group behind. That path offers undo, and tearing down the group would complicate what undo restores.

author: eseidel
body:
## Summary

Drop `Equatable` from `RenderSchema` and make its duplicate-instance
dedup an explicit pointer key at the collectors (#187).

`RenderSchema` extended `Equatable` only to back the `Set<RenderSchema>`
dedup that collapses the duplicate instances `toRenderSchema` builds per
`$ref` site, so a definition reached many ways writes one file. That cost
two things: every schema-field PR paid a tax threading the new field into
a `props` list (this PR removes eleven such overrides, and #352 had just
added another), and the resulting `==` compared **neither identity nor
value** — it meant "same `[snakeName, pointer]`", a surprising equality
for a node in the render graph.

Now `RenderSchema` uses the default identity `==`, and the two collect
sites key on `pointer` directly:

- `_ModelCollector` / `collectAllSchemas` → `Map<JsonPointer, RenderSchema>`.
- `_NamedSchemaCollector` keys `imported` / `inline` on `pointer`;
  `NamedSchemas.imported` / `inline` become deduped lists.

A schema's location is its identity, and pointer is exactly what the rest
of the pipeline already keys on — the resolver's recursion stack
(`Set<JsonPointer>`) and the naming pass (`Map<JsonPointer, String>`, so a
schema's name is itself a function of its pointer, which is why `snakeName`
would be redundant in the key).

## Verification

- **Byte-identical regen** across github, discord, petstore,
  spacetraders, backstage.
- The obsolete `RenderSchema equality (load-bearing)` unit group (which
  only passed via `const` canonicalization once `==` was identity) is
  replaced by a test exercising the real invariant where it now lives:
  two distinct instances that share a pointer collapse to a single import
  (`tree_visitor_test.dart`).
- Full suite green.

## Not addressed here

Two documents both defining `#/components/schemas/Foo` collide (pointers
from an external components-library are document-relative, not globally
unique). This is pre-existing — the pipeline keys on `pointer` everywhere
and already warns — and unchanged in behavior on every tracked spec. Filed
as #358; the fix belongs in `assemble.dart` (namespace those pointers by
document, as split-spec targets already are).

## Scope

Render layer only. Parser has no `Equatable`. The resolver's
`ResolvedSchema` `Equatable` **stays** — it genuinely value-compares via
`_CollectionStructure`, the `_collectionCache` key that shares identical
`oneOf` / `anyOf` collections.

author: manjunathshiva
body:
A fresh `pip install tabfm[pytorch]` cannot load the released checkpoint. On tabfm 1.0.1 (`cb6ba46`), Python 3.13, torch 2.13.0:

```python
from tabfm.src.pytorch import tabfm_v1_0_0
model = tabfm_v1_0_0.load(model_type="classification")
```

```
File ".../huggingface_hub/hub_mixin.py", line 813, in _load_as_safetensor
    if packaging.version.parse(safetensors.__version__) < packaging.version.parse("0.4.3"):
NameError: name 'safetensors' is not defined
```

**Cause**: `huggingface_hub` declares `safetensors` as an optional dependency and imports it lazily, but the PyTorch loader always goes through `PyTorchModelHubMixin`, and since 1.0.1 the Hugging Face checkpoint ships only `model.safetensors` (#33 / the 1.0.1 weight-loading fix dropped the `pytorch_model.bin` path). So `safetensors` is a hard runtime dependency of the `pytorch` extra — and `torch` does not pull it in transitively. Anyone installing per the README's PyTorch instructions hits the `NameError` on their first `load()`.

It likely went unnoticed because CI's `pip install -e .[dev,jax,pytorch]` never loads the released checkpoint (tests build small models directly), and any environment that has ever installed `transformers`/`accelerate` already has `safetensors` present.

**Change**: add `safetensors` to the `pytorch` extra in `pyproject.toml`, and a matching pinned entry (`safetensors==0.8.0`, current release) to the `requirements.txt` lock in pip-compile format/ordering. The JAX path is unaffected — its weights restore via orbax.

**Verified** in a clean venv: `pip install -e .[pytorch]` on this branch pulls `safetensors` and `tabfm_v1_0_0.load(model_type="classification")` succeeds; on `main` the same steps reproduce the `NameError` above.

**Note on overlap with #49**: the MLX backend PR bundles this same dependency fix (both the `safetensors` line in the `pytorch` extra and the `safetensors==0.8.0` pin in `requirements.txt`). author: slepp
body:
A fresh aggregate constructor that embeds a whole by-value `string` parameter and is stored copy-in into a Vec (e.g. `v.push(Slot{ value: Some(param) })`) made an owned clone whose release nobody scheduled, leaking one heap allocation per store. This is the last-known residual of the copy-in element-store leak class (the move-in routing lanes correctly could not cover it, since the constructor embeds a borrowed parameter and moving it would double-free the caller's value).

This mints a scope-exit release for that copy-in temp's own clone. The borrowed parameter's caller ownership is preserved (never released here); non-string and mixed/projection-owned parameter embeds are handled fail-closed, since minting there would release storage the caller still owns.

## Verification
- Leak closed: the standalone Arena insert/remove cycle drops from a linear per-cycle leak to a flat 0 slope; a permanent parameter-embed ownership oracle (9 cases) pins release-count-one, caller-parameter-not-double-freed, mixed-projection-not-double-freed, and non-string rejection under the poisoned allocator.
- ll-diff, checked-mir-verify, funcupdate baselines, corpus coverage, and the compiled-.hew ratchet all green; no golden movement.

## Out of scope
- Arbitrary deep-owned (non-string) parameter embeds — minting there is not statically sound and stays fail-closed.

Closes #7

## Summary

This PR implements the end-to-end Contributor Portfolio system. It establishes a comprehensive backend reporting framework (including dashboards, a 6-stage Kanban tracking pipeline, milestone definitions, 90-day skill growth metrics, and earnings projections) and hooks it up directly to a responsive frontend UI complete with dynamic per-contributor views and PDF exporting capabilities.

---

author: steipete
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Control UI users running the Codex harness could see commentary/preamble narration while a turn was active, but it disappeared when the turn completed and could not be restored from history after reload.

## Why This Change Was Made

Codex commentary is mirrored into the durable transcript as keyed, unphased assistant fallback messages, ordered with tool activity through a shared monotonic transcript clock. The Control UI persists commentary by default and renders it separately from the final answer. The existing explicit `chatPersistCommentary: false` contract remains a retention opt-out: commentary stays visible during an active run, including reconnect/history reconciliation, but is removed at completion and omitted from new Codex durable transcript mirrors. Messaging-channel delivery behavior is unchanged.

## User Impact

Control UI users now keep the model's preambles and progress narration after a Codex turn completes and after history reloads by default. Existing operators who explicitly disabled commentary retention keep that behavior. Commentary remains visually separate from the final answer.

## Evidence

- Focused Control UI regression suite: 6 files, 333 tests passed.
- Added Codex projector coverage for durable keyed commentary, explicit-false durable omission, and commentary/tool ordering when `Date.now()` values collide.
- Added active-run history coverage proving explicit-false commentary remains live across reload and tool-result reconciliation until terminal completion.
- `git diff --check` and focused `oxlint` passed for the scoped patches.
- Final Codex autoreviews completed cleanly with no accepted/actionable findings, including the compatibility correction.
- Exact-head CI was green before the compatibility correction, including `openclaw/ci-gate`, UI, production/test types, lint, Codex extension package boundaries, and prompt snapshots. A new exact-head run is pending for the final commit.
- Direct upstream contract inspection confirmed Codex app-server commentary phases and preamble requirements in `codex-rs/protocol/src/prompts/base_instructions/default.md`, `codex-rs/protocol/src/models.rs`, and `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs`.

body:
#622 후속 — 실기기 피드백 4건 수정.

## 수정
1. **탭 페이저 스와이프 충돌**: 차트 위 가로 드래그가 탭 전환으로 새던 것 → 차트 컨테이너에 `data-no-swipe` 부착(App.vue `isSwipeBlockedTarget` closest 계약). 드래그가 스크럽으로 동작, 세로 스크롤은 페이지에 양보(`touch-action: pan-y`)
2. **X축 라벨 간격**: `% 12`(0·12시 2개만) → `% 6`(오전 12·6시, 오후 12·6시). 마지막 지점은 축 끝에 잘려 붙어 제외(경계 라벨 미표시)
3. **구간 햅틱**: 스크럽 인덱스(시간)가 실제로 바뀔 때만 `triggerSelectionHaptic` — 드래그가 새 시간 칸에 진입함을 손끝으로 알림
4. **Y축 우측**: 눈금 라벨 `position: right` — 온도 곡선 시작점이 좌측 축에 가리지 않게

## 검증
- dev 라우트: X축 4개 라벨(6h 그리드)·끝 라벨 제외·Y축 우측 렌더 스크린샷 확인
- mousemove 스윕: 스크럽 패널 갱신 + `navigator.vibrate` 구간 전환마다 호출(20스텝→20회) 확인
- vue-tsc 통과
- ⚠️ 탭 페이저 차단은 실기기 터치 최종 확인 대상(dev 페이지엔 페이저 없음)

author: copilot
body:
The `Build (debian/trixie)` Actions job was failing after a successful package build because the workflow uploaded artifacts from a stale directory layout. This updates the workflow to use the actual `make debian-sbuild` output path.

- **Workflow artifact path**
  - Change `actions/upload-artifact` to read from `build/<package>/<distro>-<dist>-sbuild/`, which is the Makefile-defined output directory for sbuild artifacts.
  - Keep the existing exclusion for `*.build` logs aligned with the corrected directory.

- **Why this matters**
  - The package build completed successfully, but the upload step looked under `build/<package>/debs/...`, so the job failed with `No files were found with the provided path`.

```yaml
path: |
  build/${{ env.OOS_PACKAGE }}/${{ matrix.distro }}-${{ matrix.dist }}-sbuild/*
  !build/${{ env.OOS_PACKAGE }}/${{ matrix.distro }}-${{ matrix.dist }}-sbuild/*.build
```

author: vmalafa
body:
Second workstream of #109: single auth verification per request + home-truth parallelization + shared guard consolidation.

## What changed

- **`src/lib/auth/request-user.ts`** — a request-scoped guard (`React.cache()`): `getRequestUser` resolves the Supabase user at most once per request; `getRequestUserId` is the common convenience shape. A single Home render used to verify the same session ~8 times.
- **Ten guard copies + twelve inline `getUser` blocks collapse into it** across the action modules, the three server pages (spending/timeline/calendar), and `getActiveProfileId` — which is now itself request-cached (auth + profile lookup once per request, not once per action call). The bank-data guard reuses the request user but keeps its per-call MFA assurance check (ADR-0002 semantics unchanged).
- **`getHomeTruth`'s three independent detections** (Money Date raise, Milestones, bonus glance) run concurrently. Pool settings unchanged — excess queries queue.
- **`BonusMomentSection` drops its `router.refresh()`** on decide: the action's `revalidatePath("/dashboard")` already returns the refreshed render in its own response; the extra refresh just queued a second full Home read (and flaked bonus-smoke under suite load).
- **e2e**: milestone-prompt click gains the pre-hydration gate (same class as WS1's dial fill); home-smoke's assignment reload-poll gains the drain-the-write gate (a suite-wide audit confirmed it was the last ungated site); the Money Date opening-card timeout — the tightest in the suite — widens 20s→40s.

## Verification

`npm run check` fully green: lint, 317 unit tests, build, 28/28 e2e with seeded fixture. Suite wall-clock improved (11.3m vs 13.1–13.6m before WS2).

#109 continues with workstream 3 (next/font).

author: juanjobarroeta
body:
## Qué es

Segunda iteración del módulo PURIFICADORA (#435): digitaliza el flujo real del negocio — el **talón diario del chofer** y el **Excel de cortes** (hojas mensuales por semana/día, matriz NEGOCIOS, hojas por cliente con sucursales, y RESUMEN anual). El frontend correspondiente ya está en el repo [`purificadora`](https://github.com/juanjobarroeta/purificadora).

## Cambios

**Schema + migración** (`20260720_purificadora_cortes`, drift check verde)
- `PurifRuta` (repartidores: Brayan, Angélica, Ventanilla…), `PurifSucursal` (puntos de entrega por cliente: FCA Reforma, Serdán…), `PurifClienteConfig` (precio de garrafón pactado por cliente).
- `PurifCorte` + líneas (`PurifCorteRuta`/`PurifCorteEmpresa`/`PurifCorteGasto`) con cortesías y estado `BORRADOR → CONFIRMADO`; `@@unique(companyId, fecha)` (un corte por día).
- `PurifVenta.corteId`, `PurifVentaItem.sucursalId`; claves SAT en `PurifConfig` (claveProdServ/claveUnidad/descripcionFactura) para facturar el consumo mensual.

**Corte del día** (`/api/purificadora/cortes*`)
- CRUD del borrador (editable, sin efecto contable) + `POST /[id]/confirmar` que en una sola transacción genera: ventas de casas por ruta (EFECTIVO y/o TRANSFERENCIA con garrafones prorrateados por importe), una venta a CRÉDITO por empresa con partida por sucursal al precio del cliente, los gastos con su asiento, folios consecutivos con reintento ante carrera de unicidad.

**Catálogos**: `rutas`, `sucursales`, `clientes/config` (GET/POST/PATCH/PUT con `requireWriter` + `requireModule`).

**Reportes** (`/api/purificadora/reportes/*`)
- `matriz`: garrafones por día — empresa × día del mes, o sucursal × día de un cliente (la hoja NEGOCIOS / hojas por cliente).
- `estado-cuenta`: consumo mensual por sucursal + saldo pendiente + datos para timbrar el CFDI del consumo (el satélite llama `POST /api/facturas` con `Idempotency-Key purif-consumo-<cliente>-<año>-<mes>` y vincula las ventas al CFDI).
- `resumen`: ingresos/garrafones por cliente por mes + gastos por mes (la hoja RESUMEN).

## Verificación

- `tsc --noEmit` ✅ · `vitest run` 109 archivos / 1149 tests ✅
- `prisma migrate diff --exit-code` (el check `drift` de CI) verificado en verde localmente contra un shadow Postgres con pgvector.

### Issue for this PR

Closes #

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

At Plan exit, OpenCode estimates how much of the configured Code-mode model context the current session has used. The existing follow-up question now shows that estimate when the user chooses to continue in the current session.

When the estimate reaches the existing automatic-compaction threshold, the option to start a new session is marked as recommended. The new session path preserves the planned work by seeding the child session with the finalized plan.

The change also adds the optional `recommended` question option field and renders it consistently in the CLI, TUI, and app.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Added tests for model resolution, provider-default fallback, token aggregation, percentage calculation, unknown context limits, and compaction-threshold recommendations.

author: htlin222
body:
實作 `docs/plans/2026-07-20-per-question-timing.md`:讓每次作答都留下「這題花了多久」,並據此產出配速報告。

## (a) 做了什麼

**資料層**
- `migrations/0023_attempts.sql` — 新增 append-only 的 `attempts` 事件表(8 欄 + 3 個 index),成為作答的唯一真相。`review_progress` 降級為 derived cache(仍永久雙寫,因為它同時扛 `bookmarked` / `bookmark_folder_id`),`exam_answers` 仍是模擬考的當前作答狀態。
- `worker/lib/attempts.ts` — `clampElapsedMs()`(不信任 client:非有限數字 → `null`,其餘夾進 `[0, 30分鐘]`)+ `insertAttemptOp()`。

**寫入路徑**
- `POST /api/review/answer` 接受 optional `elapsed_ms` / `source`,聚合與事件合併成一次 `DB.batch()`(單一交易,不會出現「times_seen 加了但 attempts 沒寫」)。
- `POST /api/review/anki/review` 同樣接受 `elapsed_ms`;**只在有 `chosen` 時**才 append(純 rating 不是一次 MCQ 作答)。
- `POST /api/exam/:sid/answer` 接受 `elapsed_ms`,`UPDATE exam_answers` 與 attempt append 併成 batch。
- `POST /api/exam/:sid/finish` 用 `correct_answer_at_finish` 快照回填該場 attempts 的 `is_correct`,交卷後不留 NULL(日後 challenge 升級答案不會回頭改寫歷史)。

**讀取路徑**
- `worker/lib/pacing.ts` — `percentile`(線性插值)/ `median` / `pacingSplit`(前後半段,奇數題中間題歸前段)/ `MIN_COHORT = 5`。
- `GET /api/questions/:id/stats` — 舊欄位全保留,新增 `my_elapsed_ms` / `median_elapsed_ms` / `p90_elapsed_ms` / `timed_responders`。每人只取最快一次(避免重刷灌樣本),排除 >10 分鐘的 outlier,`timed_responders < 5` 時中位數/p90 回 `null`(20 人的群體裡 3 人的「中位數」等於點名)。
- `GET /api/exam/:sid` 的 answers 左接 attempts 聚合,新增 `elapsed_ms`(用 `SUM` 而非 `MAX` — 改答案會有多筆 attempt,總和才是這題真正花掉的時間)。
- `GET /api/exam/:sid/pacing`(新)— 前後半段平均、`delta_pct`、中位數、最慢五題。有 owner check(403)。無計時資料的舊 session 回 `n: 0` 而非 500。
- `GET /api/review/pacing?days=90`(新)— 每日題數/答對數/平均耗時,學習曲線的資料基礎。**依計畫不做對應前端圖表**。

**前端**
- `frontend/src/lib/questionTimer.ts` — 純函式狀態機(不註冊 listener、不讀 `Date.now()`,時間由呼叫端傳入)。`visibilitychange` 期間不累加(「離開分頁去查資料」不算思考時間)、單題上限 10 分鐘、hide/show 冪等(瀏覽器會重放事件)。
- `QuestionCard` — 換題重啟計時、掛 `visibilitychange`,`submit()` 帶上 `elapsed_ms`;揭曉後多顯示「你 74 秒 · 全體中位數 52 秒」(人數不足只顯示自己的秒數)。
- `Exam.tsx` — 換題(`activeIdx`)重啟計時,題級 timer 跟隨 session 的 pause/resume;`choose()` 的 debounce flush 帶 `elapsed_ms`。**`submit()` 的重送迴圈刻意不帶** `elapsed_ms`(那是補寫不是新作答,附耗時等於灌假資料)。
- `ExamResult.tsx` — 每題 meta 加「· 用時 1:14」(`null` 顯示「—」),分數 banner 下加配速卡(`delta_pct > 25` 標 rose、`< -25` 標 emerald)+ 最慢五題連結。無資料時整張卡改成一行灰字。純文字 + 既有 Tailwind class,**沒有引入任何圖表函式庫**。

## (b) 與計畫的偏離

1. **實作順序調整**(非行為差異):計畫是 2.2 → 3.2,但 Task 2.2 的 UI 要顯示 Task 3.2 才新增的 `median_elapsed_ms`。改成先做 3.1/3.2(server),再做 2.2(UI),讓每個 commit 都是可運作狀態。commit 訊息仍照計畫給的文字。
2. **計畫 Task 1.4 的程式碼片段有筆誤** — `c.env.DB.batch([, /* 既有的 UPDATE */ insertAttemptOp(...)])` 開頭有個多餘逗號(elision,會塞進一個 `undefined`)。照真實程式碼寫成正常的兩元素陣列。
3. **`pacingSplit` 多加一個測試**:`firstHalfAvg === 0` 時 `deltaPct` 回 `null`。計畫的實作說明有提到這個 case,但測試清單沒涵蓋,補上以免除以零回傳 `Infinity`。
4. **Task 4.1 Step 3 說「先問使用者要哪種」** — 依交辦指示採預設的簡單版(直接切換到 `attempts`),不做「舊資料走 review_progress」的混合 UNION。
5. **`fmtSeconds` / `fmtMs` 是新加的小 helper**(計畫說「沿用該檔既有的 mins/secs 風格」,但那是 inline 算式、不是可重用函式,無從沿用)。

## (c) 過程中發現/修復的既有 bug

**`GET /api/review/heatmap` 嚴重低估每日作答數。**第一個 UNION 分支讀 `review_progress.last_seen_at` —— 那是「每題一列、會被後續作答覆寫」的聚合列,所以**一天做 10 題只會算 1 次**(只有 10 題各自的最後時間戳,而且同一題重複作答完全不留痕)。已改成數 `attempts` 的列。

同時**移除了 `exam_answers` 那條 UNION 分支** —— 模擬考作答現在也進 `attempts`,留著會重複計數。

`fsrs_review_logs` 分支保留:純 rating(無 `chosen`)不會進 `attempts`,移除會漏記;帶 `chosen` 的 Anki 複習兩邊都算,是刻意接受的重疊(已寫進 SQL 註解)。

本地驗證:同一天 8 筆作答(5 review + 3 exam),修復後 heatmap 回 `n: 8`。

## ⚠️ 預期的破壞性行為:heatmap 舊日期會變空白

`attempts` 從 0023 才開始寫,**依計畫刻意不回填歷史** —— 舊資料只有聚合值,把 `times_seen=5` 展開成 5 個捏造的時間戳等於汙染唯一真相並讓中位數失真。代價是 heatmap 在 0023 套用日之前的格子會變空、舊 session 的配速欄一律顯示「—」。**這是預期行為,不是 bug。**

若日後決定在意,可改成「`created_at >= <0023 套用時間>` 用 attempts,更早用 review_progress」的混合 UNION;本 PR 不做。

## (d) 給整合者:本分支動到的共用檔案

有多個平行分支在改同一個 repo,以下是可能衝突的點:

**`worker/routes/*.ts`**
- `worker/routes/review.ts` — 4 處:① import 區加一行;② `/answer` 的 body type + `answerProgressOp` 從 `.run()` 改成 `DB.batch([...])`;③ `/heatmap` 的 SQL 與 `.bind()` 參數(**衝突風險最高,SQL 整段重寫**);④ `/anki/review` 的 body type + `ops.push()`;⑤ 新增 `GET /pacing` 端點(插在 `/heatmap` 與 `/anki/decks` 之間)。
- `worker/routes/exam.ts` — import 區加一行;`/:sid/answer` 改成 batch;`/:sid/finish` 加一段回填 UPDATE;`GET /:sid` 的 answers SQL 加 LEFT JOIN 與第二個 bind 參數;新增 `GET /:sid/pacing`(插在 `GET /:sid` 與 `DELETE /:sid` 之間)。
- `worker/routes/questions.ts` — import 區加一行;`/:id/stats` 的 `return c.json(...)` 前插入 timing 查詢並擴充回傳物件(舊欄位一字未動)。

**`frontend/src/**`**
- `frontend/src/components/QuestionCard.tsx` — import 一行;檔案頂層新增 `fmtSeconds()`;元件內新增 timer ref + effect;`StatsPayload` type 擴 4 欄;`submit()` 的 POST body;揭曉後的 meta 列多一個 `<span>`。
- `frontend/src/routes/Exam.tsx` — import 一段;`ExamInProgress` 加 `timer` ref 與一個 effect;`choose()` 的 POST body;`pause()` / `resume()` 各加一行;`submit()` 只加註解。
- `frontend/src/routes/ExamResult.tsx` — `Result['answers']` type 加 `elapsed_ms`;新增 `Pacing` type + `fmtMs()`;新增 `pacing` state 與 fetch;score banner 與 filter tabs 之間插入配速卡;每題 meta 列多一個 `<span>`。
- `frontend/src/lib/questionTimer.ts` / `.test.ts` — **全新檔案,不會衝突**。

**其他**
- `migrations/0023_attempts.sql` — 全新。若有平行分支也用了 0023,重新編號時只要改檔名即可(內容不依賴編號)。
- `worker/lib/attempts.ts` / `pacing.ts` + 測試 — 全新檔案。
- `CLAUDE.md` — 在「Images: R2 via Worker proxy」小節**之前**插入一個新小節,未動既有內容。

## 驗證

```
pnpm test                                                  102 pass / 0 fail
node --test --experimental-strip-types 'frontend/src/lib/*.test.ts'   34 pass / 0 fail
pnpm exec tsc --noEmit                                     clean
(cd frontend && pnpm build)                                ✓ built
```

只跑了 local migration(`pnpm db:migrate:local`),**沒有** `--remote`,**沒有**部署。

實機驗證(本地 wrangler dev + local D1):
- `elapsed_ms: 74000` → 存 74000;不帶 → `NULL`;`-1` → `0`;`1e12` → `1800000`;`"abc"` → `NULL`
- 開一場考答 3 題 → 交卷後 3 筆 attempts 的 `is_correct` 皆非 NULL
- `/api/exam/:sid/pacing` → `n:3, first_half_avg_ms:30000, second_half_avg_ms:60000, delta_pct:100`;換人存取回 403

body:
Adds syntax highlighting for fenced code blocks — the first of the two road-to-1.0 items (SEO is the other).

## Approach: build-time, not JS
kramdown + Rouge already emit token `<span>`s at build time (`<figure class="highlight">`), so highlighting is **pure CSS — zero JS**. A no-JS visitor gets the *fully-coloured* code, identical to everyone else (strictly better than a JS-with-fallback approach).

## Theme
- **gruvbox**, a deliberate **code-block-only exception** to the monochrome palette (documented in DESIGN.md §1/§5).
- Mapped to theme-aware `--hl-*` tokens that flip with the light/dark toggle (same `:has(#theme-toggle:checked)` / `[data-theme]` triggers as the rest of the theme).
- **Every token AA-verified** on `--color-code-bg` in both modes; four light-mode hues (comment/string/type/class) darkened from stock gruvbox-light to clear 4.5:1.
- **Inline `code`** has no language → left as plain text on the code surface (no regression).

## Enhancements (progressive, `_includes/code-enhance.html`)
- **Copy button** (Clipboard API; absent if unavailable).
- **Line-number gutter** — sticky (stays put while code scrolls), `aria-hidden`, non-selectable so copy/readers get only the code.
- With JS off, neither exists — you still get the highlighted block.

## Files
- `_tailwind/highlight.css` — token colours + enhancement chrome; imported by `app.css`.
- `_includes/code-enhance.html` + `default.html` — the JS enhancement.
- `DESIGN.md` — §1/§2 exception, §5 the setup + AA, §8 how to swap themes.

Verified in both themes on a real post (see the linked screenshots in the conversation). Ships as `feat:` → release-please will propose `0.10.0`; `1.0.0` follows once SEO lands.

## Wat

De opdrachtgever zag op `/kandidaten` al of hij een reagerende ZZP'er kende — het **"eerder samengewerkt"**-signaal (`candidate-history.ts` → `CandidateHistoryBadge`). Het **symmetrische spiegelbeeld** voor de ZZP'er ontbrak: een ZZP'er die een opdracht bekeek zag nergens dat hij al eerder een samenwerking met déze opdrachtgever had afgerond. Dat is een sterk, laag-risico vertrouwenssignaal bij de reageer-beslissing ("een bekende opdrachtgever die je bevalt is sneller en zekerder"). Benchmark: Malt/Upwork tonen "worked together before" **bidirectioneel** — wij deden het maar één kant op.

## Fix

Een compact blok op de opdracht-detailpagina (`/opdrachten/[id]`, alleen niet-eigenaar FREELANCER, naast de bestaande client-signaal-blokken): **"Eerder samengewerkt"** / "N× eerder samengewerkt" met *"Je hebt al eerder voor {bedrijf} gewerkt · laatst afgerond in {maand jaar}"*.

- **`src/lib/freelancer-client-history.ts`** (+`.test.ts`, 6 tests) — pure `summarizeFreelancerClientHistory` (telt afgeronde samenwerkingen, meest recente `completedAt ?? createdAt` wint, `null` zonder historie → niets gerenderd) + `freelancerClientHistoryLabel`.
- **`src/lib/data/freelancer-client-history.ts`** — fetcher `getFreelancerClientHistory(userId, companyId)`: één gescoopte **COMPLETED**-query op het (ZZP'er, opdrachtgever)-paar (cap 500). Bewust alleen COMPLETED — de eenduidige "eerder samengewerkt"-claim; PROPOSED/ACTIVE tellen niet mee.
- **`src/components/jobs/client-history-block.tsx`** — blok, spiegelt de stijl van de andere client-signaal-blokken.
- **`src/app/(protected)/opdrachten/[id]/page.tsx`** — fetch in de bestaande `showClientSignals`-`Promise.all` (geen extra serieel rondje), render vóór de reputatie-blokken.

## Grens/scope

Read-only afleiding, alleen geaggregeerd (telling + laatste afronddatum) — nooit tarief- of andere partij-gegevens; per (ZZP'er, opdrachtgever)-paar gescoopt. Geen schemawijziging, geen nieuw mutatie/auth-oppervlak, geen woordenboek-wijziging (nieuwe `t()`-strings vallen terug op de NL-brontekst).

`npm run typecheck` · `npm run lint` · `npm run test` (**4603 passed** — één testbestand faalde op een Prisma-generate-race in de worker, slaagt los: 16/16) · `npm run build` · `npx prettier --write .` — allemaal groen.

author: akromicc
body:
El lado escritura del 42703 que #212 arregló para lectura. `applyMutation` ponía `organization_id` en la lista de columnas del INSERT sin guarda, así que crear en una tabla hija (líneas de un documento) moría con **42703**. Bloquea `purchases.create_purchase_order`, cuyas líneas van a `purchase_order_items`.

El precedente del patrón estaba a diez líneas: `created_by_id` sí consultaba `tableHasColumn`.

## Por qué NO es la simetría de #212

En **lectura**, tirar el predicado expone filas ajenas. En **escritura** el riesgo es el inverso y no lo cubre omitir la columna: el guest puede **colgar una fila del árbol de otra organización**. Nada en `{"purchase_order_id": "<ajeno>"}` es inválido, y una vez escrita la línea es hija real de un documento que el invocador nunca pudo tocar. Peor que una lectura: persiste, y aparece en los totales del documento ajeno.

Así que el fix son las dos cosas que anticipaste:

1. **Omitir `organization_id`** cuando la columna no existe (destraba el 42703).
2. **Verificar el link al padre** antes del INSERT, reusando `orgScopedForeignKeys` de #212 — no dupliqué la lógica de descubrimiento de FK.

Reglas en el camino org-less (`verifyChildCreateTenancy`):

- ninguna FK a un padre org-scopeado → **rechazo**;
- una FK que califica viene en `data` pero apunta a un padre inexistente o de otra org → **rechazo** (el intento cross-tenant);
- ninguna FK que califica viene en `data` → **rechazo**: una fila con todos los links en default no es atribuible, e insertarla crearía una fila que ninguna lectura org-scopeada puede devolver.

Padre ausente y padre ajeno dan la misma respuesta a propósito: el guest aprende "no es tuyo", nunca si el id existe en otro lado.

## Garantía de aislamiento

| Caso | Garantía |
|---|---|
| Tabla con `organization_id` | **Idéntica a antes.** El camino nuevo ni se toca. |
| Hija, FK verificada en la org del invocador | La fila sólo puede colgar de un padre de su propia organización. |
| Hija, FK a padre ajeno o inexistente | **Rechazo**, sin INSERT y sin evento canónico. |
| Hija sin FK verificable | **Rechazo.** |

Como sólo el camino org-less es nuevo, esto **no puede regresionar ningún create que hoy funcione**: hoy, por definición, todos van por tablas con `organization_id` — los otros ni llegaban al INSERT, morían con 42703.

Nota de alcance: la verificación de FK se aplica sólo a la rama org-less. Una tabla CON `organization_id` puede seguir apuntando una FK a un padre de otra org — es el comportamiento actual, y cambiarlo sería un endurecimiento aparte con riesgo de romper addons existentes. Lo dejo señalado, no lo cambio acá.

## Queda pendiente: update y delete tienen el mismo bug

`applyMutation` usa `WHERE id = $1 AND organization_id = $2` sin guarda en update (líneas 343, 370) y en delete (386, 404, 415). Sobre una tabla hija revientan con el mismo 42703. **No lo arreglé en este PR** porque es una decisión distinta: el predicado tendría que ser el `EXISTS` al padre, y hay que definir si un update sobre una fila hija de otra org devuelve `not_found` (consistente con hoy) o `forbidden`. Prefiero no meterlo de contrabando en un PR de create. Si querés, lo hago a continuación — o abrí un issue y lo tomo con el resto del slice de `purchases`.

## Tests

`runtime/wasm/datamutate_orgscope_test.go`, incluido el que pediste:

- el create en tabla hija omite `organization_id` y verifica el padre (regresión del 42703);
- **crear una línea colgando de un padre de OTRA organización se rechaza** — sin INSERT, sin evento canónico, `forbidden`;
- fila sin link verificable → rechazo;
- tabla org-less sin FK que califique → rechazo.

`go build ./...` y `go test ./...` verdes en todo el repo.

Fixtures: los tests de create ahora ven un probe de columnas que antes sólo corría cuando había actor. Hoisteé el probe (una sola consulta alimenta la decisión de `organization_id` y la de `created_by_id`, que probeaba por su cuenta), así que en el caso con actor hay **una** consulta menos que antes, y en el caso sin actor una más. Ajusté las expectativas de sqlmock; ninguna aserción de SQL cambió.

## Bonus, no es del kernel

La acción `create_purchase_order` postea `product_id` mientras la columna es `product_variant_id`. Es del addon `purchases`, no del kernel — lo dejo acá para que lo derives, no lo toqué.

author: starseeker
body:
Git-format patches defer destination writes until all files have been processed, allowing the changes to be applied atomically. Unlike the immediate-write path, the deferred writer reopened destination files without retaining the selected output mode.

On Windows this loses binary mode for explicit newline strategies such as --newline-output=preserve. The C runtime consequently translates newlines a second time, turning CRLF into CRCRLF and preventing subsequent patches from matching the resulting files.

The fix is to store the selected open mode with each deferred write and use it when finalizing the destination file.

(debugged using codex+gpt5.6)

author: sharonemathew
body:
**Issue**
[QA-503](https://linear.app/jesus-film-project/issue/QA-503/select-fonts-modal-cancel-button-misplaced-label-style-inconsistent) — On the Select Fonts modal, the Cancel button is pinned to the far-left while Confirm sits far-right (unusually wide gap), and the "Hint text" in the preview is indented so it doesn't line up with the "Label" or the input field.

The ticket's third item — "Label" text rendering in an inconsistent style in the preview — is **not addressed by this PR** and is left for a follow-up.

**Fix**
- **Footer buttons:** changed the action Stack from `justifyContent="space-between"` to `flex-end` with `gap={2}` (matching sibling dialogs), so Cancel and Confirm are grouped together at the bottom-right.
- **Hint text:** added `mx: 0` to the TextResponse `formHelperText` slot to remove MUI's default horizontal margin, so the hint aligns flush-left with the label and field. Note: `TextResponse` lives in the shared `libs/journeys/ui`, so this alignment change applies everywhere a text response hint renders (editor canvas and live journey player), not just the modal preview.
- **Close-while-saving guard:** Cancel and the title close button are disabled while the fonts mutation is in flight, and all close paths (backdrop click, Escape) route through a guard that no-ops mid-save — previously cancelling mid-save closed the dialog but the write still landed, firing a "Fonts updated" snackbar over a dismissed dialog.

**Test plan**
- Unit: `ThemeBuilderDialog.spec.tsx` asserts the action buttons share one flex row justified `flex-end` with Cancel preceding Confirm, and covers the close-while-saving guard (11 tests pass). The exact 16px gap is left to Chromatic since jsdom doesn't evaluate the sibling combinator.
- Unit: `TextResponse.spec.tsx` asserts the hint's computed horizontal margins equal the label's (verified red without the `mx: 0` fix, green with it).
- Manual: opened a Journey → text block → edit theme → Select Fonts; confirmed Cancel/Confirm grouped bottom-right and "Hint text" flush-left with "Label" and the input field (screenshot verified).

author: bensigo
body:
## What

The OpenRouter model-catalog substrate for #1338/#1339 (tiered routing + Jace chat routing), plus gateway-first cost pricing.

**PR① — catalog snapshot + slug validation:** a committed snapshot of OpenRouter's `/api/v1/models` (332 live models: id + per-MTok prices + context + provider), served from the committed file — no network on the hot path, stale-served when OpenRouter is down. AC3: a CI test validates every model slug in shipped config against the snapshot, so an invalid/retired slug fails CI loudly (catches the historical invalid-critic-slug class of bug).

**PR② — gateway-first pricing:** cost estimation + run-cost metering read the gateway snapshot first, PRICE_TABLE second, and record which tier resolved (`gateway` | `price_table` | `fallback`) so ledgers are auditable (AC1). Wired in both the console estimate lib and Python `_resolve_rates`.

## Review + fix round

Adversarial review (verdict: FIX-FIRST) found two silent gaps, both fixed in `245dd21`:

- **[Critical] the snapshot wasn't in the runner image.** `deploy/runner/Dockerfile` copies only `agentrail/` + pyproject, never `apps/console/`, so `pricing.py`'s snapshot path (under apps/console) was absent in the deployed hosted-fleet image → gateway-only models would silently price at **$0**, undercutting the fleet budget guardrail. Fixed with a byte-identical package-local copy at `agentrail/context/openrouter-catalog.snapshot.json` (added to `pyproject.toml` package-data so it ships in the non-editable `pip install`), `pricing.py` repointed to the package-relative path, the refresh script writes both copies, and a parity test fails CI on drift. Proven: wheel-built + installed into an isolated prefix with no `apps/console` → all 332 rates load, sonnet prices via `gateway`.
- **[High] `price_source` was computed but never persisted.** It reached neither the local JSONL ledger nor the server cost-events sink (only correctly filtered from Langfuse). Now threaded end-to-end into `build_cost_record` / `push_cost_event` → ingest route → a new `cost_events.price_source` ClickHouse column, with the pipeline→cost_push seam tests whose absence hid the gap. (Computation moved after the budget-leash block, so the spend guardrail is provably untouched.)

## Tests

Console 1540/1540 + ingest-route tests; `tsc` / `eslint` / `next build` clean. Python parity/seam/pricing/tracer/pipeline/budget 246/246. Controller independently re-verified: 103 targeted tests pass against the branch + a live snapshot-load proof (332 rates, package-relative).

Closes #1337.

author: shayanras
body:
## What
`_ensure_browser` guarded only on `self._ctx is None`, so when Chrome died **externally** (crash, Chrome self-update relaunch, off-screen window closed, or a 2nd daemon stealing the profile lock) the stale-but-non-None context was reused. Every submit tick then raised at `new_page()` on the closed context, and 3 consecutive raises tripped the `SUBMIT_RAISE_PAUSE_THRESHOLD` auto-pause — wedging the daemon until a **manual restart** (`--resume` alone can't clear an in-memory stale handle).

## Fix
- `_ensure_browser` now checks `self._ctx.is_closed()` and rebuilds from scratch when the context is dead → the daemon self-heals from any browser death.
- Launch extracted to `_launch_ctx()` so the self-heal decision is unit-testable without driving a real browser.
- Two regression tests added.

## Verification
- `pytest -k "not live"` → **124 passed, 0 regressions**.
- Live: restarted the wedged prod daemon on this code; it resumed submitting (170 → 185+) with no re-pause.

## Notes
Root cause corrects the earlier "two daemons fighting the profile lock" theory — that's only *one* trigger; the real defect was the missing liveness check that turned **any** browser death into a hard pause.

author: joryirving
body:
## What

Make `verifierAgentRef` optional in the issue-batch decomposition: when unset, each issue's pipeline is `code → review` (no deterministic verify gate), across the base round, the #946 review-fix iterations, and the coder-escalation tier.

## Why

Fixes #1151

The shortcut required `VerifierAgentRef` and always emitted a verify step, so every repo needed a `GateProfile` with a real image + command set — the sole remaining per-repo configuration cost in our loop. For operators whose deterministic signal is the repo's own CI on the opened PR (with the coder already self-verifying inside the issue-fix loop, per its task contract), the pre-PR gate is redundant: unmapped repos fall to the imageless `generic` profile and GATE-ERROR, and maintaining per-repo gate commands duplicates what the repo's CI already declares.

Opt-in and fully backward compatible: with `verifierAgentRef` set, the shape is byte-identical to today (`code → verify → review` everywhere), pinned by regression tests.

## How

- `chooseSteps`: the issue-batch case requires only `CoderAgentRef`; the no-coder error message updated accordingly.
- `synthesizeIssueBatch`: emits the verify step only when a verifier is set; reviews `dependsOn` the verify step, or the code step when gateless.
- `reviewIterationSteps` (#946) and `coderEscalationSteps`: previously **disabled themselves entirely** on a nil verifier; now they emit gateless iterations/escalations (`code-rK → review-rK`, `code-esc → review-esc`) so a gateless Workload keeps fix iterations and coder escalation.
- `#548` cascade: no change needed — it keys off declared dependencies, so reviews still cascade-fail when their code dependency fails; there's simply no gate verdict in between. Rollup likewise classifies by phase+verdict generically.
- API doc + CRD description regenerated (`make manifests && make chart-crds`).

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added/updated — `workload_gateless_test.go`: gateless batch shape + review wiring, verifier-set regression pin, `chooseSteps` acceptance, gateless coder-escalation, gateless review-iteration
- [x] `make test` passes locally (controller suite 82.7% coverage)
- [x] `make lint` passes locally (0 issues)
- [x] Conventional commits
- [x] Signed off (DCO)
- [x] AI assistance disclosed — authored with Claude Code
- [x] Documentation updated — API field doc + generated CRD description

author: taisei2324
body:
## Problem

The hero reel served phones the full **1920×1080 landscape frames (15.8 MB)** and cropped out a ~500px-wide center slice at draw time — **~74% of every downloaded pixel was never shown**. iOS Safari has no Network Information API, so iPhones always got the heaviest tier regardless of connection, which is why the hero loaded painfully slowly on anything under 5G. (The old `frames-m/` folder was a landscape downscale that nothing referenced.)

## Fix — adaptive tier on the same page

- **`frames-p/`** — 608×1080 portrait 9:16 center-crops of the 1080p reel, **5.65 MB**. The *exact* pixels cover-fit already displays on a portrait phone, pre-cut so the rest never leaves the server → iPhones download **2.8× less** with zero visible quality change.
- **`frames-p-720/`** — 406×720 portrait, **3.28 MB** → slow connections (data-saver / 2g / 3g / weak 4g) download **4.8× less**.
- **`scrubber.js`** — tier selection gains a SHAPE axis: phone-sized portrait viewports load the portrait tiers; runtime fallback sheds low → portrait → landscape if a dir 404s; memory bounding now also covers landscape-phone viewports (small in *either* dimension); the cheaper portrait frames buy a ~3× wider decoded-frame window, so fast flings hit fewer re-decode stutters.
- **`frames.js`** — portrait tier dirs + exact per-tier byte totals in the manifest.
- **`index.html`** — media-scoped `<link rel="preload">` so the correct first frame per shape is in flight before any JS runs.

No redirects, no UA sniffing, `mobile.html` untouched — one URL adapts.

## Verification (headless Chromium)

| Scenario | Downloads | Result |
|---|---|---|
| iPhone viewport, fast net | only `frames-p/` | ✅ |
| iPhone viewport, slow net | only `frames-p-720/` | ✅ |
| Desktop, fast net | only `frames/` | ✅ |
| Desktop, slow net | only `frames-720/` | ✅ |

Scrub renders correctly at start / underwater middle / Greek end card on a 393×852 @3x viewport; no console errors in any run.

author: tylerleonhardt
body:
> **Stacked on #326552** (C4) → #326270 (C9) → #326256 (C1). Review the stack in order; this PR's diff is one commit.

## What

**C8 — one teardown path, explicitly idempotent.** The pipeline had two teardown spellings that both async-disposed the `WarmQuery`, and their safety-under-double-call rested on the SDK's `close()` cleanup *happening* to be memoized (report 02, H1/H2). C8 collapses them into one private `_teardown()` guarded by a `_torndown` flag:

- **`shutdownAndWait()`** is the *awaited* face — used where we must not spawn a fresh subprocess reusing the same `--session-id` until the old one has released `<id>.jsonl` (yield-restart / rebuild resume).
- **`dispose()`** fires the *same* `_teardown()` and forgets. The abort + `WarmQuery.asyncDispose` run synchronously before `dispose()` returns, so the subprocess is still signalled to stop promptly.
- Both run `abort → WarmQuery.asyncDispose → Query.return` in one place, **at most once**, regardless of which caller wins.
- Replaces the two dispose-chain `toDisposable`s (separate abort + async-dispose) with one.

C9 already deleted the third spelling (`_rebindQuery`'s manual `asyncDispose`), so this closes out the set.

## Why it's safe

- Idempotency is now a property of *our* code (`_torndown`), not an SDK implementation detail. A `shutdownAndWait` followed by `dispose` (the rebuild path) is a guarded no-op instead of a redundant double-dispose.
- No behavior change to the await-vs-fire-and-forget distinction — `shutdownAndWait` still awaits actual process exit; `dispose` still fires-and-forgets.

## Validation

- New pipeline test pins the idempotency: *shutdownAndWait then dispose async-disposes the WarmQuery exactly once*.
- Suites green: `claudeSdkPipeline` **13**, `claudePromptQueue` **12**, `claudeAgent` **197**.
- `typecheck-client` / `eslint` / `valid-layers-check` clean.
- **Live smoke suite 19/19** (`test/agent-host-e2e/`): materialize / warm reuse / recover-rebuild / abort-churn with subprocess reaping — the scenarios that exercise teardown end-to-end against a real subprocess.

author: pmrv
body:
## Summary

One factual error found by tracing `docs/digests/digest_equivalence.rst` through `src/fleche/digest.py`:

**Wrong universal claim about type-name salting** — the opening paragraph stated that the digest function "salts the running hash with `type(value).__name__` for type discrimination" as an invariant. This is wrong for `Number` types (`int`, `float`, `complex`, subclasses).

For a `float`, the code does:
```python
m = hashlib.sha256()
m.update(b"float")       # added to m …
match value:
    case Number():
        value = hash(value)     # hash(1.0) == 1
        return _digest_bytes(value)  # … but m is abandoned; new SHA256 from hash()
```

The `m` that received `b"float"` is silently discarded. The final bytes come from a fresh `_digest_bytes(hash(1.0))` which uses `"int"` as the type name (because `hash(1.0)` returns `1`, an `int`). The type name `"float"` never appears in the final digest.

This is exactly why `digest(1) == digest(1.0) == digest(1+0j)`: Python's numeric hash protocol guarantees `hash(1) == hash(1.0)`, and no type-name salt survives to distinguish them. The previous text implied the type name always ends up in the hash, which contradicted the numeric equivalences shown immediately after without explaining why.

The paragraph now:
- states the general rule (type-name salting)
- explicitly identifies Number types as the exception and explains the mechanism
- resolves the apparent contradiction between "type discrimination" and `digest(1) == digest(1.0)`

## What

Restores Cosign **key-based** verification for offline, key-signed images that
carry no transparency-log entry and no RFC3161 timestamp (e.g.
`cosign sign --tlog-upload=false --key ...`) — the Ratify side of #2712.

Previously the v2 cosign verifier forced `IgnoreTLog=false` on the key-based
path, so `verify.Verifier` always required an observer timestamp and such

- Bump `github.com/notaryproject/ratify-verifier-go/cosign` to the version that
  adds `IgnoreObserverTimestamps` (upstream notaryproject/ratify-verifier-go#77).
- Add `ScopedOptions.IgnoreObserverTimestamps`. The key-based path now honors
  the caller's `IgnoreTLog` and `IgnoreObserverTimestamps` instead of
  hard-coding `IgnoreTLog=false`. Keyless behavior is unchanged.
- Expose `cosign.ignoreObserverTimestamps` in the `ratify-gatekeeper-provider`
  chart (values, executor template, README).
- Un-skip the base `cosign test` (kind e2e) and set

## Test

  `IgnoreObserverTimestamps` / `IgnoreTLog` wiring; existing tests pass.

Fixes #2712

author: bcrisp4
body:
Closes #6 (milestone M1).

Wires discover → chunk → embed → store as a one-shot `bsearch index` command — no daemon, no conversion, no summaries. All building blocks (discovery, chunker, embedder, sqlite store) already existed; this PR is the composition layer.

## What's new

- **`internal/pipeline`** — the orchestrator. Per document: read → `chunker.Normalize` → `chunker.Chunk` → `UpsertDocument(state=chunked)` (short tx, before any network call) → `EmbedPassages` → `UpsertVectors` → `UpdateDocumentState(indexed)`. M1 state machine subset: `discovered → chunked → indexed`.
- **`bsearch index [--config] [--db]`** — stdlib `flag.FlagSet` dispatch (ADR 0006, Proposed); scan summary, per-file progress, TCC path errors surfaced, final counts. Errors early with an actionable message when `inference.embedding_model` is unset.
- **Store additions** — `ListIndexable`, `UpdateDocumentState`, `MarkFailed`. The state-flip method exists because `UpsertDocument` replaces chunks and deletes vectors wholesale — using it after embedding would orphan the just-written vectors.
- **`EmbeddingSpec.Fingerprint()`** — recorded in `StageVersions` as `{chunker, embedding}`; re-runs diff it against current config, so a chunker/model/template/ceiling change re-processes automatically (DESIGN.md: the M1 one-shot is the manual re-embed path).

## Behaviour

- **Idempotent**: unchanged files skipped by discovery; up-to-date documents skipped by fingerprint — a fully-indexed re-run makes zero network calls (probe included).
- **Fail-fast probe**: one `EmbedQuery` before touching any document proves the endpoint is up and gives vec0 its dimension count.
- **Failure policy** (DESIGN.md health-gate philosophy): transient embed errors (`openai.Transient`) abort the run — nothing marked failed, aborted doc resumes from `chunked`. Unreadable/undecodable files and permanent embed errors mark that doc `failed` with reason and the run continues. SIGINT/SIGTERM abort cleanly with durable partial progress.
- **Hexagonal**: pipeline depends only on domain ports; the transient-vs-permanent classifier is injected (`openai.Transient` wired in cmd).

## Tests

Pipeline: happy path, idempotent re-run (asserts zero embedder calls), crash resume from `chunked`, model-change re-embed into new vec generation, undecodable file, transient abort, permanent failure, empty file, vanished file. Store: `ListIndexable` filtering/ordering, state flip preserves chunks+vectors, `MarkFailed` + clear-on-re-upsert. Cmd: flag errors, missing-model message, end-to-end run against an httptest embeddings server (the M1 demo in test form).

`make all` green.

## Summary

Phase 1 of the [catalog representation gaps plan](docs/plans/2026-07-19-catalog-representation-gaps.md) (plan doc included in this PR): one repository can now yield **multiple** catalog entities, so monorepos like `drewpayment/sprinklergoose` (Next.js UI + FastAPI executor in one repo) scan as two services instead of one flattened proposal.

### Go scan worker (shared GitHub + ADO)

- Composite fetch priority `class*10 + min(depth, 9)` — shallower files win within a class; `maxFilesPerRepo` 40 → 80

### TS detectors
- **Anti-noise gate:** non-root directories need ≥2 signal classes (build manifest / container / k8s) to propose a service — a pnpm/turbo monorepo's 30 workspace packages no longer flood `/discovery`

`payload-types.ts` regen also syncs pre-existing `invitedAt` drift from PR #87.

Implemented TDD (all new tests watched red first), adversarially reviewed (depth-clamp, compose sync-invariant, and noise-gate findings applied; deep-compose-under-k8s-dir confirmed inert and declined), and live-QA'd end-to-end.

This commit automates repository sanitation and de-inflation by identifying tests that cost more to maintain (tokens + churn) than the value they provide (unique coverage + regression safety). It implements the following logic:
- Maps the import graph using `pydeps` to identify associated source code.
- Calculates unique coverage per test using isolated `pytest-cov` runs.
- Identifies "Rot Patterns" such as Brittle Mocking, Context Bloat, and Tautologies.
- Modifies the AST via `ast.NodeTransformer` to externalize massive snapshots (Bloat Reducer).
- Automatically deletes tests with brittle logic and zero unique coverage.
- Quarantines highly churning test files.
- Enforces strict guardrails (Coverage Cliff, Vibe Check, Critical Path Immunity).

author: qr-madness
body:
The Ambassador's **close-out slice** — the last two deferred items worth building, both riding the v3 proposal machinery, before the project pivots to foundation work. Doctrine intact: **reads auto-run, writes confirm** (ADR-3 / amended INV-2 — the belt never *executes* a write).

## What she can do now

### `read_conversation_results` — "what did that conversation actually produce?"
- New SELECT-only belt read over the persisted synthetic `present_exhibit` tool turns (`conversation_history.load_exhibit_calls` — exhibits have no store of their own; those rows ARE the record).
- `_render_results` parses via `exhibit_from_present_call`, keeps the **latest revision per exhibit id** (re-present = revise-in-place), renders tables/images/diagrams as titled mentions and **citation sources as label + URL** — outcomes, not dialogue. Warm empty state; never raises.

### Confirm-first dispatch orchestration — `dispatch_task`
- `dispatch_task` joins `CONFIRMED_WRITE_TOOLS`: "have the Researcher dig into X" files a **proposal you confirm** — the loop stamping, `ambassador_tool_proposal` SSE, and voice parsing all key off the set, so the integration came free.
- `proposal_for` resolves the worker in one place (`_resolve_worker`: `agent_id` else exact case-insensitive name, **agents-only**) into `{action: dispatch, agent_id, agent_name, task, conversation_id?}`; an unresolvable worker returns a readable check-`list_agents` note.
- `POST /agent/ambassador/dispatch` gains optional `conversation_id` — dispatch **into an existing conversation** (unknown id → `404`, the relay guard). The confirmed dispatch still lands as *your* user turn (INV-2).
- **Instant task echo** (client): `openDispatchedTab` replaces the open-on-ready poll — the task shows as your user bubble at once (open-tab append / seeded `restoreConversation` / fresh seeded tab bound to the minted id, the `useResumeRun` fallback pattern). Confirm strips + the VoiceBar strip read **Dispatch**; the voice persona covers "have/get \<agent\> to…".

### Hygiene: conversation DELETE strands nothing
- Clears the sidecar families — structured state, rolling summary, and the ambassador's Inquiry thread — each best-effort; the response's `deleted.sidecars` reports what cleared.

## Parked on purpose (the close-out's non-goals)
Fully-unconfirmed autonomous dispatch (breaches writes-confirm — a future per-user policy setting), `AlloyExecutor.delegate` start/steer from the ambassador, Inquiry-thread durability + Deck scope (still-open design questions in phase-16), Factory UI.

## Tests
Pinned write-surface grows the documented `confirmed_dispatch_writes` class; dispatch proposal shapes (by id / by name / passthrough / unresolvable); never-executes tripwire on `enqueue_background_chat`; a full dispatch-proposal loop round (SSE + sidecar-clean, INV-2); endpoint `conversation_id` reuse + 404; grouped-exhibit render (latest-per-id, sources payoff) + warm-empty + degrade; DELETE sidecar cleanup; voice persona/parse. **66 tests green** in the Ambassador family; `task test:quick`, pyright 0, ruff clean, client tsc + 386 vitest green.

## Live-verified
Against the real DB stack: dispatch → **task bubble visible instantly** in its new tab → the worker actually ran it headless → DELETE removed turns + reported `sidecars: [state, summary, ambassador_thread]`; dispatch into an unknown conversation → `404`. (Also surfaced that the local dev DB needed `task db:migrate` for the v3 `conversation_meta` table — applied.)

## Docs
`OpenApi.yaml` (+ spec lint), docs-site `endpoints.md`, `Development-Notes.md` (close-out paragraph + endpoint table), `CLAUDE.md` one-liner, phase-16 checkboxes (+ parked non-goals noted), `Release-Notes.md` + `versions.yaml` → **0.21.235** (`task versions:sync`, `task docs:check` green).

author: noisemaker111
body:
## What & why

A `PAPERCUTS.md` sweep (per the `improve` skill): research each logged friction, fix the easy still-live ones directly, and delete entries whose root cause already landed on `main`. No tracked issue — this is backlog sanding.

Closes #

### Fixes

- **`shoot --url http://localhost:…` now works.** Bun/Node `fetch` (which backs `isUp`) resolves `localhost` to IPv6 `::1` first, so a dev server bound to IPv4 `127.0.0.1` read as *"nothing is listening"*, and the capture allowlist only accepted `127.0.0.1`. A new `normalizeLoopbackUrl` helper rewrites the host at the CLI entry point so `localhost` and `127.0.0.1` behave identically. (`scripts/browser-lib.ts`, `scripts/shoot-dev.ts`)
- **Windows `tar` drive-letter failure in `tarballInstall.test.ts`.** Extraction now runs `tar` from the work dir with colon-free relative paths instead of an absolute `C:\…\pkg.tgz` archive path, which GNU tar misreads as a remote host (*"Cannot connect to C: resolve failed"*). Extracts identically on GNU tar, bsdtar, and Linux — no platform branch. (`scripts/tarballInstall.test.ts`)
- **`drive --shot` now accepts an absolute path**, written verbatim like `shoot --out` (no size suffix); bare names still map to `shots/<game>-<name>.png` and relative paths are still rejected (clearer message). Closes the disagreement where the two capture entrypoints named output files differently. (`scripts/drive-dev.ts`)
- **`api-adoption` owner is now grep-discoverable.** `scripts/apiAdoption.ts` gains a header comment carrying the literal `api-adoption` string and the ownership map (generator / routing / baseline), and states plainly that there is no `scripts/api-adoption.json` — adoption is computed live. (`scripts/apiAdoption.ts`)

### Cleared from `PAPERCUTS.md` (verified fixed on `main`)

- The `check-game-shape` / `Games/vice-isle/src/editorKinds.ts` cluster (6 entries) — `EDITOR_MODULE_RE` in `packages/jgengine/src/gameShape.ts` already allows `editor<Name>.ts` + `.test.ts`.
- `export-manifest` drift surfacing on later branches (2 entries) — now gated on PRs (#1293/#1492).
- `gifenc` / `fflate` missing (2 entries) — both now installed.
- `bun --cwd` space-form docs (1 entry) — docs use the `=` form.
- `check-content-gate` stale baseline (2 entries) — verified clean (`check-content-gate: clean`).
- The two frictions fixed here (shoot localhost, drive/shoot output path) plus the api-adoption miss.

13 fixed entries removed; still-live frictions (feature gaps, sandbox/timeout issues, harness quirks, unfixed seams) kept.

### Root cause

The two capture/tar bugs shared a shape: tooling treated one representation as canonical (`127.0.0.1` for capture, an absolute drive-letter path for tar) and the other form silently fell through. Both are fixed by normalizing at the single entry point (URL parse / tar cwd) so the wrong representation is unreachable, rather than adding a special case. Blast radius is confined to dev tooling scripts; no package/runtime surface changes.

### Considered but not shipped

An export-manifest *stale-dist warning* (the generator warning when a new `src/foo.ts` predates a build): a src→dist inverse check false-positives on packages whose sources aren't built 1:1 to `dist/*.js` (`editor` `mcp/*`, `jgengine` `recipes/snippets/*`), so a noisy advisory would be net negative — and the drift is already gated on PRs. Papercut left open.

## Changelog

No published-SDK source (`packages/*/src`) changed — this is tooling, tests, and docs only. `check-changelog` passes with no `[Unreleased]` entry required.

## Verification

- `bun test scripts/browser-lib.test.ts` — 12 pass (5 new `normalizeLoopbackUrl` cases).
- `bun test scripts/tarballInstall.test.ts` — 15 pass (Linux; the relative-path change is cross-platform).
- `bun test scripts/apiAdoption.test.ts` — 6 pass (comment-only change).
- `drive --shot sub/name` rejects fast with the new message; `--help` shows `--shot <name|path>`; absolute-path capture path is code-verified (`step.out ?? default`).
- `bun run check-export-manifest` — up to date; `bun run check-content-gate` — clean.

No rendered surface changes (dev-tooling scripts, tests, docs), so no screenshots apply.

author: dakotaradigan
body:
Batch 1 of 2 from a full security + code review of the app. Focused, low-risk hardening fixes; no behavior change for legitimate users.

## Cost / availability (the review's main theme)
- **Release the daily budget unit on starter-cache hits** (`/api/chat` and `/api/chat/stream`). A cache hit makes no model call, so it must not consume the global `daily_conversation_limit`; otherwise free responses could drain it and return `503 BUSY` to every visitor for the rest of the day.
- **Only cache genuine successful generations.** `_persist_chat` now takes `cacheable`; the empty-response fallback string is no longer latched into the process-global starter cache on a transient first-click blip.
- **Prune day-keyed in-memory counters** (`_scoped_counts`, `_daily_conversation_count`) in `cleanup_expired` so the no-Redis path doesn't grow unbounded.

## Info disclosure / auth
- **Gate `/health/models` behind `X-Admin-Token`.** It fires live upstream Anthropic calls and reflects provider error detail, so it's an operator diagnostic, not a public amplification/recon surface.
- **Stop echoing `str(exc)` to clients** — `/api/resume` and the non-stream chat 500s now return a generic detail and keep the path in server logs only.
- **Anonymize the session id** in the invalid-Redis-history warning, matching every other id-logging site.

## Hardening
- Add `Strict-Transport-Security` (production only).
- Run the container as a **non-root user**.
- **Warn at startup** when `ENVIRONMENT` is neither `development` nor `production` — the exact string `production` gates the cookie `Secure` flag, CORS credentials, and the admin loopback fallback.

## Correctness / quality
- `get_history` returns a copy in the in-memory path, matching the Redis path.
- Replace deprecated `datetime.utcnow()` with a timezone-aware timestamp.
- Add upper bounds to the LLM/web SDK deps so an unreviewed breaking major can't ship on the next rebuild.
- Drop the stale whole-file `ruff` `F841`/`F401` ignores and the unused `exc` bindings they masked.

## Tests
- New regression test: cached starter hits do not consume the daily budget.
- `/health/models` test now asserts unauthenticated callers are rejected and authenticates with the admin token.
- Full suite: **95 passing** (4 integration tests skipped), `ruff` clean.

Deferred to batch 2 / follow-up: the per-visitor chat-quota refund on upstream failure, the forgeable JD "brief" sentinel gate, and larger design changes (per-IP daily sub-limit, HMAC-signed visitor cookie, proxy/`X-Forwarded-For` IP resolution) that need a decision on Railway's proxy behavior before changing.

## Why

Noon data has been migrated to XDG directories and canonical compressed v3 session logs. Keeping fallback readers and startup config migrations made session discovery fragile, including ordering sessions by migration-time filesystem mtimes instead of persisted update times.

## What changed

- Require canonical `{id}.jsonl` zstd-compressed v3 session logs and remove legacy JSON, plain JSONL, v2, alternate-ID, and dual-file handling.
- Read session list timestamps, titles, cwd, and model from persisted compressed records.
- Use XDG directories exclusively and remove the completed migration command and legacy Lua path API.
- Reject removed config fields and `[tools]` tables instead of migrating them at startup.
- Make the memory plugin use XDG state only.
- Update generated configuration and Lua API documentation.
- Restore early object-root validation for task output schemas and align task policy coverage with bounded retries and plain-task behavior.
- Align message selection/search tests with the current rendered role-prefix width and move global instruction coverage to XDG config.

author: bangddong
body:
Fixes #1086.

Date bounds materialized from a rolling window (`window_days`) were saved into the `session-filters` localStorage entry and restored verbatim on the next launch. Once yoked dates could no longer overwrite them — e.g. after the v1 storage migration disabled them — the range stayed pinned to the day it was saved and newer sessions silently disappeared from the sidebar and analytics.

The sessions store now tracks the provenance of its date bounds as `dateFiltersWindowDays`: bounds applied from a rolling panel state (`App.svelte`, `AnalyticsPage.svelte`) or a `window_days` deep link (`initFromParams`, validated with the route layer's shared `parseWindowDaysParam`) carry their rolling intent, while explicitly chosen fixed ranges carry `null`. Persistence stores the intent rather than the materialized dates: the saved entry keeps `windowDays` and blank bounds, and `loadSavedFilters` rematerializes the bounds against the current date, so a rolling filter survives restarts and keeps rolling forward instead of pinning or vanishing. `applyPanelDateFilters` persists immediately, so a provenance flip between fixed and rolling with identical materialized bounds — which does not register as a filter change and may never trigger a `load()` — still updates the saved entry. Wholesale filter resets clear the intent, and the store is now the sole writer of session date bounds (`clearSessionDateFilters` removed as dead code).

Already-poisoned installs are also repaired: saved entries are stamped with a storage version, and unversioned (pre-provenance) entries have their date bounds dropped once on load and are rewritten in the new format, mirroring the yoked-dates v1 migration. The check is deliberately `!==` rather than `<` so a downgraded newer format is also not trusted; dropping bounds is the fail-safe direction in both. Other persisted filter fields are preserved.

Reviewers should look at `saveFilters`/`loadSavedFilters`/`applyPanelDateFilters` in `sessions.svelte.ts` and the two call sites. Known cosmetic note: a persisted one-day rolling window rematerializes as `date_from`/`date_to` rather than the single `date` param; both filter identically.

author: plusmobileapps
body:
## What & why

Moves macOS desktop distribution from a notarized **Developer-ID DMG on GitHub Releases** to the **Mac App Store** (`.pkg` uploaded to App Store Connect), and disables the in-app self-updater on macOS as a consequence — the Store forbids self-updating and sandboxes the install. The DMG is retired; the in-app `DesktopUpdater` now runs on **Linux only** (Windows already deferred to the Microsoft Store).

macOS ships under the **same bundle id as iOS** (`com.plusmobileapps.chefmate.ChefMate`), so it lands in the single "Chef Mate" App Store record via **Universal Purchase** rather than a separate listing (App Store names are globally unique, so a second "Chef Mate" record wasn't possible anyway).

## Changes

- **Updater** — `DesktopUpdater.isSupported` is now `platformKey() == "linux"`; macOS joins Windows in deferring to its store.
- **Packaging** (`composeApp/build.gradle.kts`) — macOS target `Dmg` → `Pkg`, `appStore = true`, `appCategory`, App Sandbox entitlements + provisioning-profile env vars, and `bundleID` set to the iOS app id `com.plusmobileapps.chefmate.ChefMate` (was the Android-style `com.plusmobileapps.chefmate`). New `packaging/macos/entitlements.plist` (app) and `runtime-entitlements.plist` (nested JRE).
- **CI / Fastlane** — new `mac release` lane (match fetches Apple Distribution + Mac Installer Distribution certs + MAS profile, builds the signed `.pkg`, uploads to App Store Connect); `mac certificates` lane runs match only (the App ID already exists from iOS — no `produce`). `desktop-release.yml` gains a tag-only `macos` job and drops macOS from the GitHub Release artifacts and `latest.json` feed.
- **Docs** — new "macOS: Mac App Store" section, revised update-strategy table + feed shape, `packageReleasePkg` task references.

## Verification done

- `./gradlew :client:composeApp:packageReleasePkg --dry-run` resolves; `compileKotlinJvm` passes.
- Workflow YAML and Fastfile Ruby both parse.
- Not run: the actual signed `.pkg` build + App Store upload (needs the Apple-side setup below).

## Reviewer notes — required Apple-side setup before this can ship

Neither can be done from CI/code; they gate the first upload:

1. **Enable the macOS platform on the existing "Chef Mate" App Store Connect record** (Universal Purchase). No new App ID or app record — both already exist from iOS. The App ID needs **no extra capabilities** (sandbox/network/file access come from the build entitlements, not the portal).
2. **Run `bundle exec fastlane mac certificates` once locally** to mint the macOS App Store provisioning profile + certs into the `certificates` match repo. CI then consumes them read-only.

## ⚠️ Risks to validate

- **Sandbox + bundled JRE:** App Sandbox is mandatory, but this is a bundled-JRE app with a JavaFX WebView (recipe browser) + native file dialogs. Sandboxed JVM/JavaFX apps — especially with `disable-library-validation` / `allow-unsigned-executable-memory` — are a real App Store **rejection risk**. Smoke-test the signed `.pkg` sandboxed (WebView loads, file dialogs, sign-in/sync, no Console.app sandbox denials) before submitting.
- **Shared App ID capabilities:** the iOS App ID's capabilities (App Groups, Associated Domains, share-extension/watch) carry into the macOS provisioning profile. Normally fine (superset profile), but confirm it builds cleanly on the first `mac certificates` run.
- The first CI run should also confirm the `sigh_*` profile-path env var name and jpackage's installer-cert derivation (flagged in code comments).

Minor: `.github/certs/DeveloperIDCA.pem` is now unused (retired Developer-ID flow); left in place. The internal `admin/` module still builds a DMG and was intentionally not touched.

author: wenxu0907-eng
body:
## COM-151 — run fail 后没有自动重启、ticket 卡在 in_review

### Root cause (forensics on the live instance, COM-45)
| time (UTC) | run | what happened |
|---|---|---|
| 05:50–06:03 | `f95e3b34` | succeeded, parked issue **in_review** (continuation: investigate `/clip assign`) |
| 06:04–06:06 | `64a950ed` | continuation run **died `process_lost`**; event = *"Process lost -- server may have restarted"* → both `processPid` **and** `processGroupId` were null → **no eager retry queued** |
| 06:06→06:17 | — | **~11 min gap**: no active run, issue in `in_review`, nothing surfaced. ← the reported symptom |
| 06:17–06:22 | `ded808c3` | next continuation wake re-executed & **succeeded** (COM-145 / #29 Fix 2 correctly treated the stale `waiting_on_review` park as re-executable) |

`reapOrphanedRuns()` gated the one-shot `process_lost` retry on `(processPid || processGroupId)`. A `tsx watch` host restart (the COM-144/COM-145 self-inflicted-restart family) kills the child **and** reaps the run with no durable pid, so `buildProcessLossMessage` falls through to *"server may have restarted"* and the retry was skipped — **exactly the recoverable case**. The issue was released and left in `in_review` until the next natural continuation wake (~11 min later), invisibly.

So COM-145 (#29) *did* eventually self-heal, but only on the next scheduled continuation wake. This PR closes the invisible window by retrying immediately.

### Fix
Drop the pid requirement from the retry guard in `reapOrphanedRuns`:
```
- tracksLocalChild && (!!run.processPid || !!run.processGroupId) && (run.processLossRetryCount ?? 0) < 1
+ tracksLocalChild && (run.processLossRetryCount ?? 0) < 1
```
A tracked local-child run that ended `process_lost` and has not yet been retried gets **exactly one** eager retry (`processLossRetryCount` cap preserved). This mirrors the graceful-shutdown drain path, which already retries unconditionally. `pid`/`pgid` remain used solely for liveness detection and descendant cleanup above.

### Tests (`heartbeat-process-recovery`)
- a no-pid `process_lost` run now queues one retry **and** hands off the issue execution lock (not stranded in `in_review`)
- the single-retry cap still holds when the pid is absent (no retry loop)
- all 82 existing recovery tests pass

### Scope note
Surfacing a *still-parked* `in_review` to the board after recovery (the visibility half of the complaint) is tracked separately in **COM-152**. This PR is the auto-restart half.

body:
## 배경
`wifi <iface> br route find/auto`가 유선 peer를 찾지 못하고 빈 결과를 내는 경우가 있다. 실장비(192.168.0.20)에서 재현: eth0가 `192.168.1.1/24`인데 유선 peer는 `192.168.0.220` — `br route find`가 아무것도 못 찾음(서브넷을 `192.168.0.0/24`로 명시해도 실패).

## 근본 원인
`wifi_eth_peer_find.sh`가 `arping`을 **`-s`(source) 없이** 호출 → eth0의 IP(`192.168.1.1`)를 sender로 사용. peer `192.168.0.220`은 **같은 서브넷(192.168.0.x) source에만 ARP 응답**(strict arp)하므로 무응답 → 발견 실패. 서브넷 인자는 **sweep 범위만** 바꾸고 source IP는 안 바꿔서 소용 없음.

증거(실측):
| arping source | 결과 |
|---|---|
| `192.168.1.1` (eth0 IP, 기존) | 0 응답 |
| `192.168.0.20` (peer 대역) | 3/3 응답 (peer MAC `00:04:9F:0A:DA:11`) |

## 변경 — `wifi_eth_peer_find.sh`
- `_arp_src_opt(network, mask)` 추가: eth0가 대상 대역 내 IP를 이미 가지면 기본 source, 아니면 **대역에 속한 우리 IP(mlanN)를 `-s`로 지정**. sweep 루프와 quick-path arping 양쪽에 적용.
- `WIFI_EPF_SOURCE_ONLY=1` source-only 가드: 테스트에서 함수만 로드(링크체크/스윕 미실행).

## 신규 — `wifi_eth_peer_find_test.sh`
모의 `ip` + source-only 로드로 비-root 실행. `_arp_src_opt` 4케이스(eth0 in/out × mlan in/out/empty) + IPv4 헬퍼. **8 PASS**.

## 검증
- 단위 테스트 8 PASS / `bash -n` OK
- **온타겟(192.168.0.20, peer 192.168.0.220), 비파괴(/tmp 실행)**:
  - 배포본 `find 192.168.0.0/24` → 빈 결과(exit 1)
  - 수정본 `find 192.168.0.0/24` 및 기본 폴백 → **`192.168.0.220` 발견(exit 0)**

author: p-alik
body:
## Summary

- `libtest::get_free_port()` copied `sin_port` from `getsockname()` straight into the returned port with no `ntohs()`, so the port it reserved/reported differed from the one every caller (gearmand's `--port=`, `gearman_client_add_server()`, etc.) actually binds/connects to. This made the port-reservation fix from #471 (`1973c2ea`) protect the wrong port, leaving the real one exposed to collisions with other concurrently-running test processes under `make test -j5`.
- `tests/libgearman-1.0/multi_client_test.cc` kills a gearmand server mid-test and later restarts a new process on the exact same previously-used port (its clients are already configured for that host:port). That restart path never goes through `get_free_port()`, so the port sat completely unprotected between `kill()` and rebind.

Fixes both: `ntohs()` the port in `get_free_port()`, and add `libtest::reserve_port()` (same bind-without-listen `SO_REUSEADDR` trick) used by `multi_client_test.cc` to hold each port from kill through restart.

Full writeup: gearman/gearmand#479 (comment)

## Test plan

- [x] `t/multi_client` passes individually
- [x] `t/multi_client` passes run 6-way concurrently (previously the scenario that could trigger the race)
- [x] `get_free_port()`'s own unit tests (`t/unittest`) pass
- [x] Full `make test` shows no new failures beyond a pre-existing NixOS-only environment issue (`/bin/echo` not present) unrelated to this change

Fixes #479

### Motivation
- Applying the recommended fulfilment persisted inventory but did not explicitly persist product confirmation, causing the shared completion rule to report `allProductMatchesConfirmed: false` and blocking automatic pricing resolution.
- The intent is to treat a user `Use recommended` click as explicit acceptance of the matched product and to synchronously resolve pricing when the canonical completion rule deems configuration complete.
- Preserve the existing four-card Intelligent Quote Workspace and keep Pricing Resolution as a subsection of Quote Configuration while making pricing and commercial facts deterministic and auditable.

### Description
- Update the server action `selectFulfillment` to validate quote/line/product, re-evaluate inventory, reject blocked or empty fulfilments, persist explicit `product_confirmation` and `product_confirmed`, persist `inventory_decision`, `selected_inventory_decision`, `selected_fulfillment` and `inventory_confirmed_at`, preserve other metadata, revalidate the workspace routes, and use the canonical `quote-configuration-completion` rule to decide whether to invoke pricing; the action is idempotent to prevent duplicate events. (`lib/actions/quote-actions.ts`)
- Extend the pricing resolution service to follow the required price precedence, validate prices, compute per-line calculations via the canonical calculation helper, persist full `price_application` metadata and line-level pricing fields, include tax in quote totals, and persist a comprehensive `commercial_calculation` payload on the quote. (`lib/services/quote-pricing-resolution-service.ts`)
- Add normalized view-model fields and a persisted commercial summary to the workspace query service using `normalizeProductMatchState()` as the single product-confirmation interpreter, exposing per-line gross/discount/net fields and pricing metadata. (`lib/services/quote-workspace-query-service.ts`)
- Update the Quote Configuration UI to surface matched-product state, match method and confidence, applied/applied states and an improved Pricing Resolution table and Quote Summary (Customer Quote and Internal Economics) while retaining the four primary cards. (`components/quotes/quote-configuration-workspace.tsx`)
- Update unit coverage to assert that clicking `Use recommended` persists explicit product confirmation and that an already-applied/priced line is handled idempotently. (`tests/unit/quote-actions.test.ts`)
