body:
Test-only follow-up to #2974. Its suite pins `marks`/`markDefs` routing on root-level text blocks; during review the container-nested case was verified by a throwaway probe, and the "does this hold for arrays that aren't `marks`?" question wasn't pinned at all. This promotes both into the repo.

Five new scenarios in `event.patches.sidecar-arrays.test.tsx`, all passing against the shipped implementation unchanged:

- `marks` insert on a container-nested span, and an annotation toggle (`marks` + `markDefs` inserts) on a container-nested block, the case where the "root block" the data patch applies on is the container itself and the block-relative path descends field-generically.
- `marks` unset two containers deep (`table > row > cell > block > span`).
- insert into a void block object's custom array (`image.tags[-1]`), a sidecar array that isn't `marks`/`markDefs`.
- unset of an element in a container-owned data array (`callout.tags[0]`) sitting *beside* the container's structural child field (`content`), pinning that the classifier distinguishes the two arrays on the same node.

Beyond documenting the shipped contract, these are the regression net for the planned replacement of the classifier/fallback machinery with field-generic handlers (tracked separately as a follow-up): tests that predate that refactor and pin today's observable behavior. No production code changes, no changeset.

body:
## Problem

`recommend_hook_mode` only checked `hook_mode_override` (explicit config) and ignored all other disable signals. This caused the hook path to inject `permissions.deny` into `~/.claude/settings.json` even when the user explicitly opted out via:

- `LEAN_CTX_DISABLED=1`
- `LEAN_CTX_SHADOW_MODE=false`
- `LEAN_CTX_HEAL=off`
- `shadow_mode = false` in config.toml

MCP-server starts honored `shadow_mode=false` but the hook path ignored it — the inconsistency noted in #1037.

## Fix

- Add `is_deny_suppressed()` check to `recommend_hook_mode` that inspects all disable signals
- Cap mode at `Hybrid` (never `Replace`) when any disable switch is active
- Add `cap_at_hybrid()` method to `HookMode`
- 3 regression tests covering all three env-var paths

## Validation

- `cargo test --lib hooks`: 160 passed (3 new)
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features`: zero warnings

Closes #1037

author: natori-hrj
body:
## Description

Deploying on a non-default port produced a working proxy that the surrounding
tooling reported as broken. Tracing the probe turned up a second defect
upstream of it: the container could not change its port via `HEADROOM_PORT`
at all.

`headroom proxy --port` is a click option with `envvar="HEADROOM_PORT"`, and an
explicit CLI argument beats the envvar. The Dockerfile baked `--port 8787` into
CMD, so `HEADROOM_PORT` was inert for a plain `docker run` — while
`docker-compose.yml` already passes `command: ["--host", "0.0.0.0"]` with no
port, which is the intended shape. The Dockerfile was the outlier.

The two halves have to move together. An earlier revision of this change fixed
only the HEALTHCHECK; that made the probe follow `HEADROOM_PORT` while the
listener stayed pinned to 8787, and the container went from misleadingly
healthy to genuinely unhealthy. Evidence in Real Behavior Proof below.

Closes #2432

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [ ] Code refactoring (no functional changes)

## Changes Made

- `Dockerfile`, both runtime stages: dropped the baked `--port` from CMD so
  `HEADROOM_PORT` stays authoritative. `docker run` with no env still binds
  8787 (click's default), so the published default is unchanged.
- `Dockerfile` (`runtime-slim-base`): shell-form HEALTHCHECK so
  `${HEADROOM_PORT:-8787}` expands at probe time.
- `Dockerfile` (`runtime-slim`): distroless, no shell — the port is resolved
  inside Python instead, keeping exec form.
- `headroom/cli/doctor.py`: added `resolve_probe_port()`. `--port` /
  `HEADROOM_PORT` wins, then an unambiguous deployment manifest (`default`
  profile, or a lone named profile), then 8787. `headroom deploy --port N`
  writes N into the deployment's environment, not into the shell `doctor` runs
  in, which is why the manifest tier is needed; with several named profiles and
  no explicit request there is no non-arbitrary pick, so it stays on the

author: sanohiro
body:
W2's public routing shape: a table of `Route` values dispatched by **(method, path)**, with **404 and 405 distinguished**.

## The framework side

**`pkg.web.types`** (new, public leaf): `Ctx` and `Route`. They live in a dependency-free module because the internal router needs `Route` to dispatch a table and the `pkg.web` root needs both to build one — either defining them would be an import cycle, and Align has no re-exports (D9). Consumers name them qualified, like any cross-module type.

**`pkg.web.internal.router`**: `dispatch_routes(routes, method, path)` walks the radix tree on the path, then picks the route on that path whose method matches (an **empty method answers any**, which is how a fallback is written) — so `GET /x` and `POST /x` coexist. `method_not_allowed` reports "path matched but no method did": the **405** case, distinct from a **404**.

## Two silent compiler bugs this exposed

1. **`store_array_elems` stored nothing for a non-literal struct element.** An array literal of structs wrote elements field by field **only when the element was a struct literal**. Any other struct-valued element — a call, i.e. exactly `[web.get(…), web.post(…)]` — stored **NOTHING**, leaving the element uninitialised: a zeroed scalar and a **garbage `str`/fn pointer**. It now lowers the element and stores it whole (and nulls a moved owned source).

   ```align
   calls := [mk(10), mk(20)]
   c0 := calls[0]
   print(c0.b)   // was 0, should be 10 — and c0.a was a garbage pointer
   ```

2. **`check_slice_init` did not coerce a struct array to `slice<Struct>`.** So a route **table** could not be passed to a dispatcher by borrow at all — only moved. It now coerces by the same `ArrayToSlice` borrow the scalar case already uses.

## Tests

`array_materialize` (+1) pins the struct-array-from-calls round-trip; `apps_web_router` (+1) pins GET/POST on one path plus 405-vs-404. Existing web tests gain the new `types` module.

Regression: sema 151, m4 26, m5 172, struct_index 28, array_materialize 6, owned_structs_arrays 10, fn_values 21, apps_web_serve 3, apps_web_router 7 — green.

author: leo-brgn
body:
## Problème

Le déploiement continu du modulith vers **recette (managed-min Cloud Run)** échoue au boot depuis la bascule modulith (07-19). Les jobs `deploy-dev.yml` (build/push) sont verts, mais l'orchestrateur `pivot-infra` échoue à chaque rollout : le conteneur `pivot-core` `exit(1)` pendant la migration Flyway du module **collaboratif**.

```
FlywayValidateException: checksum mismatch for migration version 1
  Applied to database : 468595471   (recette)
  Resolved locally    : -1212893638 (JAR de main)
  at ModuleFlywayMigrationConfig.collaboratifSchemaFlywayMigrationRunner (ligne 83)
```

Résultat : recette sert encore l'ancienne révision pré-modulith (`4680bbb`), et chaque déploiement `pivot-ui` échoue son smoke-test `/api/actuator/health/readiness` en cascade.

## Cause racine

Convention pré-BETA « fichier V1 unique » : le `V1__schema_init.sql` d'un module change à mesure que son schéma évolue. La base **recette a hérité du schéma `collaboratif` (et `agilite`) de l'époque service-standalone** → elle stocke un checksum V1 **plus ancien** que celui résolu par le build modulith → `validate` (implicite dans `migrate`) avorte tout le contexte. Une base fraîche ne rencontre jamais ça — d'où « l'image boote en local mais le rollout recette est rouge ».

Deux divergences distinctes ont été identifiées :
1. **(bloquant)** dérive de checksum du V1 collaboratif ci-dessus ;
2. **(latent)** le `V7__board_share_invite_notifications.sql` du repo standalone n'a pas été repris (fonctionnalité re-logée : notifications désormais dans le module `notification` du shell) → un `applied but not resolved locally` possible si recette a appliqué V7.

## Correctif

Rendre les migrations de schéma-module **auto-réparantes**, ce que la convention V1-mutable implique déjà pour toute base durable :

- **`ModuleFlywayMigrationConfig`** — `repair()` avant `migrate()` pour chaque schéma module (`selfHealAndMigrate`). `repair()` réaligne les checksums stockés (bookkeeping uniquement — ne rejoue ni ne supprime aucun SQL appliqué), puis `migrate()` passe. No-op quand l'historique est cohérent (bases fraîches, CI, tests) et une fois le schéma figé en BETA.
- **`ModuleFlywayConfigurer`** — `ignoreMigrationPatterns("*:missing")` pour tolérer une migration appliquée dont le script n'existe plus dans ce build (V7 droppé).

## Vérification

Reproduction fidèle avec l'**image réelle qui échoue** bootée contre un Postgres ensemencé pour reproduire la dérive recette (checksum V1 = 468595471 + un V7 appliqué sans script) :

| Image | Résultat contre la base dérivée |
|-------|--------------------------------|
| **avant** (`199f0ab`) | reproduit le `FlywayValidateException` recette **à l'identique**, `exit(1)` |
| **après** (ce fix) | `repair()` réaligne le checksum (`468595471` → `-1212893638`), tolère le V7 fantôme, migre `collaboratif` + `agilite`, **démarre proprement** |

Compilation `test-compile` OK (JDK 25). Test d'intégration Testcontainers ajouté (dérive de checksum réparée + tolérance applied-but-missing) — exécuté par la CI.

## Notes

- Écart assumé vs proposition initiale : le V7 droppé n'est **pas** ré-ajouté — le code modulith n'utilise pas `share_id`/`collaboratif.notification` (0 référence ; notifications re-logées dans le shell). Le ré-injecter créerait du schéma mort dans les envs frais ; `ignoreMigrationPatterns("*:missing")` couvre proprement le cas.
- `ModuleFlywayConfigurer` est dans le starter publié — changement additif et rétro-compatible.

## What changed

- publishes the standalone explorer at `/kolams-on-an-octahedron/`
- publishes the article embed at `/embed/kolams-on-an-octahedron/`
- presents the three exact-inventory representatives with arm lengths `(2,2,2)`, `(3,2,1)`, and `(4,1,1)`
- gives each representative its own connected octahedron net, with the nonzero kolam visible before folding
- uses the approved tangent-continuous triangular kolam curves and Math Nomad terracotta palette
- folds each net into a regular octahedron and supports drag rotation, zoom, a continuous fold slider, reset, tile labels, and the active-graph overlay

- uses the final description: “Compare the three graph theoretic representatives on connected octahedron nets and explore the completed solid.”
- preserves responsive layouts, keyboard controls, reduced-motion handling, live announcements, and mathematical startup validation

## Mathematical model

The implementation uses the intrinsic three-axis convention for octahedron faces. The three representatives are stored as exact face-to-tile assignments on the dual cube, so each flat net, folded solid, label, and graph overlay comes from one combinatorial source of truth.

## Validation

- the implementation validates that every representative uses all eight words exactly once
- every shared side is checked for matching binary data
- every representative is checked to have exactly six active dual-cube edges
- the Vite multipage configuration and static route tests cover the standalone and embed routes

## Publication

This pull request is the approved publication version of the sandbox used by the companion article “Kolams on Octahedron.”

author: davidiach
body:
## Summary

- add an exact marked-cofactor obstruction for finite samples on one closed half-branch of any nondegenerate polynomial cubic graph
- record the proof in the claims ledger and research index without changing the repository's official/global or local strongest status
- add a Sturm-certified globally strictly convex quartic negative control showing that a one-sided endpoint can already have four same-radius arc witnesses in degree four

## Key identity

After Euclidean normalization to `gamma(t)=(t,a*t^3+b*t)` on `t>=0`, four marked witness roots give

```text
P(t)=Q(t)*(t^2+e1*t+nu)
(mu^2+kappa)=nu*e2-e1*e3+e4
```

Evaluation at the outer center forces `nu<0`, while distinct nonnegative witnesses give `e2>0` and `e1*e3>e4`. The right side is therefore negative, contradicting `mu^2+kappa>0`.

## Scope

This is `LEMMA / FAILED_SEARCH_FAMILY` only. It does not cover cubic samples straddling the inflection, arbitrary parametric cubics, finite quartic branch closure, or general strictly convex polygons. It neither proves Erdős #97 nor supplies a counterexample.

## Validation

- text-clean, status-consistency, artifact-provenance, diff, and Ruff checks passed
- broad fast pytest run: 1,601 passed; three environment-sensitive checks initially failed because the isolated runner lacked `PYTHONPATH=src` and the release guard correctly saw the pre-commit dirty tree
- all three affected tests passed on the clean commit with `PYTHONPATH=src`
- the symbolic distance expansion, coefficient identity, convexity discriminant, and quartic Sturm counts were independently rederived twice

## Summary
- New `src/adapters/dns-adapter.js`: resolves `transport = "dns"` playlist entries via regular unicast DNS (e.g. `raspi3.home` -> `192.168.1.53`), a genuinely different mechanism from the mDNS adapter -- `.local` is reserved for multicast DNS, but a router's own DHCP+DNS-assigned domain (`.home`, `.lan`, whatever it picked) is answered by a one-to-one unicast query to whatever DNS server the OS is already configured to use, normally the router itself
- Zero new runtime dependencies -- Node's built-in `node:dns` module speaks this natively (`resolve4`/`resolve6`)
- Same A-preferred, AAAA-fallback shape as the mDNS adapter, for the same reason a router-assigned hostname can be IPv6-only too
- `dns-packet` (already present transitively via `multicast-dns`) promoted to an explicit `devDependency` since `test/dns-adapter.test.js` imports it directly to build a fake local DNS server
- Wired into `bin/meterkastd.js`; new README.md section "Extending to router-assigned local DNS names"

## Test plan

- [x] Real end-to-end verification, closing the exact gap the mDNS adapter (PR #19) hit: confirmed this machine's actual configured DNS server is the router itself (`Get-DnsClientServerAddress` -> `192.168.1.1`), a direct `dns.resolve4('raspi3.home')` against it returned a real answer (`192.168.1.53`), and the real daemon with a real `raspi3.transport = "dns"` playlist entry returned the same via `GET /devices/raspi3` -- alongside Dirigera/Ecowitt/Smartbridge still serving real data. author: milky2018
body:
## Background

Proton's macOS runtime had related lifecycle and desktop-integration failures rather than a single close-button bug. Closing the last window could leave the MoonBit process or child processes alive, while forced or incorrectly ordered teardown could crash inside CEF. The renderer bridge could also wait forever during startup, and normal cancelled navigations could be misreported as bootstrap failures.

The underlying issue was ownership and sequencing across AppKit, CEF, the native handle registry, and the MoonBit async runtime. This PR makes those boundaries explicit: CEF owns browser closure, AppKit window closure follows the CEF callback sequence, native callbacks publish state/events, and MoonBit owns the asynchronous wait policy.

## Changes

- stabilize the macOS CEF window-close and runtime-shutdown lifecycle, including child-process cleanup behavior
- add a focused child-process close regression example
- replace synchronous macOS dialogs with request-scoped asynchronous dialog operations and events
- add public macOS application-menu APIs and an example
- route macOS notification clicks through the notification extension
- split runtime state/configuration and macOS engine responsibilities into focused native modules
- centralize the renderer bridge bootstrap in generated native assets shared by the CEF backends
- report structured bridge lifecycle failures to the MoonBit facade
- treat CEF navigation cancellation as cancellation rather than bridge startup failure
- bound bridge startup waits with a configurable MoonBit-side deadline instead of native forced teardown
- isolate CLI doctor tests from ambient `PROTON_NATIVE_DIST` values
- synchronize the public ABI and shipped platform prebuilts

## Design Notes

The close path does not use a timeout to force browser destruction. A close request enters CEF's normal close lifecycle; browser and window state are invalidated only at the corresponding callbacks, and runtime shutdown starts after owned browser state has drained.

Bridge startup is similarly state-driven. Native code installs and reports the centralized bootstrap lifecycle, while the MoonBit facade waits asynchronously and applies the startup deadline. This keeps native callbacks non-blocking and prevents timer threads from destroying thread-owned CEF state.

Dialogs use explicit request ids and completion events so AppKit panels remain owner-window scoped without blocking MoonBit's async runtime.

## Platform Scope

The lifecycle, dialog, menu, and notification behavior in this PR is primarily implemented and manually exercised on macOS. Shared CEF bootstrap and ABI changes are present in all native backends, and the shipped platform artifacts are synchronized, but this PR does not claim equivalent Linux or Windows desktop-feature validation.

## Validation

- `PROTON_NATIVE_DIST=$PWD/native/build-engine moon -C proton check --target native --diagnostic-limit 80`
- full MoonBit test suite: 270/270 passed
- `cmake --build native/build-engine --config Debug`
- `ctest --test-dir native/build-engine -C Debug --output-on-failure`: 2/2 passed

The branch is rebased onto the current `main` (`b6b2d32`).

author: gotofritz
body:
## Summary

Finding #22 (EVOL) from `docs/plans/01-issues.md`.

The entire schema is a single v1 migration of `IF NOT EXISTS` statements, which masked three weaknesses in `RunMigrations` that would bite the moment a v2 migration lands:

1. **Swallowed check error** — the applied-version lookup used `_ = db.QueryRow(...).Scan(&exists)`, so a transient failure read as "not applied" and the migration re-ran. A future `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` re-applied fails hard or corrupts.
2. **Two-step, non-atomic apply** — the migration SQL and its `schema_migrations` record were separate `Exec` calls. A crash between them left the schema changed but unrecorded, so it re-applied on next start.
3. **No newer-DB guard** — an older `tbuk` opening a newer `~/.tbuk/tbuk.sqlite` silently read/wrote a schema it doesn't understand (realistic for a local-first tool with standalone binaries against one long-lived DB).

## Fix

- Propagate the version-check error instead of discarding it.
- Apply each migration's SQL **and** its version record inside a single transaction, rolling back on any failure.
- Reject a DB whose recorded max version exceeds the latest known migration, via a new sentinel `ErrSchemaTooNew` and an "upgrade tbuk" message.
- Split the loop into an unexported `runMigrations(db, migs)` so multi-migration and failure paths are testable with custom lists.

## Testing

- `TestMigrations_newerDBRejected`: a DB seeded with a future version returns `ErrSchemaTooNew`.
- `TestRunMigrations_secondMigrationApplies`: a v2 migration applies in its own tx, records version 2, and re-runs as a no-op.
- `TestRunMigrations_failedMigrationRollsBack` / `TestRunMigrations_recordInsertFailureRollsBack`: a failing SQL or a failing version-record insert rolls the transaction back — neither the schema change nor the version survives.
- `TestRunMigrations_bootstrapError`: a closed DB surfaces the bootstrap error.
- Existing `TestMigrations_idempotent` still green (transaction wrapping works with the FTS5 virtual table + triggers).
- `make check-ci` green: total coverage 88.1%, `internal/storage` 85.9%, all packages ≥ 85%.

Updated `docs/initial-context.md` (migrations section) and marked finding #22 `✅ DONE`.

author: yuxiangyun
body:
## Root cause

Dashboard chat projection keyed live events by bare message/tool IDs, discarded tool results that arrived before starts, and cleaned retries by adjacency/global activity. Durable history also regrouped text and tool parts, losing original order. Artifact cards trusted `kind` without binding the value to a known tool and domain schema. `RUN_ERROR` replaced message rows, hiding already received text and confirmation UI, while wildcard renderers could preempt local validation and lifecycle phases were not announced consistently.

## Changes

- Add a scoped event ledger keyed by `{threadId, runId, messageId, toolCallId, sequence}` with orphan-result buffering, idempotent replay, cross-run isolation, and run-scoped retry cleanup.
- Convert durable history in one pass so interleaved text/tool parts retain source order.
- Add a `{toolName, source, schema}` artifact provenance registry. Saved artifacts require canonical confirmation receipts; read artifacts require allowlisted DB tools and domain schemas. Unknown tools, forged kinds, and legacy schemas fail closed.
- Represent run failures as independent terminal items so received text and unresolved human confirmations stay visible and retryable; restore server-owned `runError` / `activeRunId` on cold load.
- Enforce renderer priority: exact → validated local artifact/suppression → wildcard → safe notice.
- Centralize live-region announcements for waiting-user, committing, stopped, and error states without duplicate status roles.
- Update GEB L2/L3 documentation alongside code.

## User impact

Out-of-order or replayed events no longer corrupt prior runs, durable conversations preserve the response's real part order, untrusted tool payloads cannot masquerade as PostgreSQL facts, and failed background runs remain understandable and retryable without hiding useful content or forms. Screen-reader users receive explicit lifecycle announcements.

## Verification

- `pnpm typecheck` — passed
- `pnpm lint` — passed
- `pnpm test:run` — 46 files / 258 tests passed
- Post-rebase focused Dashboard suite — 4 files / 66 tests passed
- Rebased against latest `origin/main` before push (already up to date)

## Known limitations

This PR intentionally does not modify `use-dashboard-agent-chat.ts`, `agent-ui-runtime.ts`, confirmation forms, or the Dashboard runtime transport. The ledger consumes durable event `sequence` when the transport supplies it; sequence-less live callbacks receive a local monotonic sequence until the parallel runtime work forwards persisted replay sequence metadata.

author: yerzhansa
body:
## Problem

On a brand-new install the daemon exited immediately with a not-configured readiness result: readiness requires `config/config.yaml` to exist and parse as a YAML map, but onboarding writes configuration through the `configureRuntime` RPC — which needs the daemon up. Nothing ever created the initial file, so a fresh machine could never reach onboarding without hand-seeding the config.

## Fix

The desktop main process now seeds a minimal pre-onboarding `config/config.yaml` before constructing the daemon supervisor, only when the file is absent:

- Resolves the same athlete home the daemon uses (`ENDURAGENT_HOME` override or `~/.enduragent`).
- Creates the directory chain with mode `0700` and the file with mode `0600`.
- Publishes atomically via a same-directory temp file + no-clobber hard link, so a concurrently created configuration is never overwritten (POSIX `rename` would replace it; `link` fails with `EEXIST` and preserves the competing bytes).
- Fills `session.timezone` from the host (`Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone`, `UTC` fallback); all credential fields seed empty for onboarding to fill.
- Seeding failure is reported on stderr and startup continues to the supervisor unchanged.

## Verification

- 10 new unit tests (seeding, existing-config no-op, concurrent-creator byte preservation, permissions, timezone fallback, home resolution).
- Full repo gate green (4592 passed) plus desktop build, runtime and security smokes.
- Packaged-app proof: launched the built app against a nonexistent home — `config.yaml` seeded with mode `600` and the daemon came up and published its connection files with no manual intervention.

author: yarivhashaicomet
body:
## Details

Client-side ingestion size safety for the **TypeScript SDK**, at parity with the Python SDK (OPIK-7335 / #7469). Prevents unbounded span/trace payloads from destabilising ingestion (the OOM class of incidents), while preserving large media as attachments instead of dropping it.

**What's in it:**

1. **Base64 → attachment extraction** (runs *before* truncation). Inline base64 media (≥ 256 KB, configurable) in `input`/`output`/`metadata` is MIME-sniffed, replaced with a compact `[…-attachment-…]` placeholder, and uploaded as an attachment (S3 multipart + local `BEMinIO` single-PUT). Node-only. Unrecognized/non-media base64 is left inline. Linear character scan (not regex) so multi-MB blobs don't overflow V8's regex stack.
2. **Per-object truncation** (spans **and** traces). Two-pass rule: (1) truncate any `input`/`output` field individually over the cap; (2) if `input`+`output` together are still over, truncate the rest. `metadata` is exempt and excluded from the whole-object measurement. Oversized fields become the shared marker `{opik_truncated: true, reason: "<omitted_due_to_size_NMB_error_code_413_400>"}`. Fail-safe: never throws / breaks entity creation.

Because `@track` mirrors the outermost call's payload onto **both** the trace and its root span, the trace path needs the same guard — hence truncation is wired into `TraceBatchQueue`, not just spans.

**Config (parity with Python):**

| Setting | Env | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `maxPayloadSizeMb` | `OPIK_MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE_MB` | 20 (`<= 0` disables) |
| `isAttachmentExtractionActive` | `OPIK_IS_ATTACHMENT_EXTRACTION_ACTIVE` | true |
| `minBase64EmbeddedAttachmentSize` | `OPIK_MIN_BASE64_EMBEDDED_ATTACHMENT_SIZE` | 256000 |

> Renamed `maxSpanPayloadSizeMb` → `maxPayloadSizeMb` (env `OPIK_MAX_SPAN_PAYLOAD_SIZE_MB` → `OPIK_MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE_MB`) now that the guard covers traces too. Unreleased — no back-compat cost.

## Change checklist

- [x] Feature covers spans **and** traces (create + update paths)
- [x] Attachment extraction runs before truncation so media is preserved, not truncated
- [x] `metadata` exempt from truncation and from the whole-object measurement
- [x] Fail-safe: truncation/extraction never throw and break entity creation
- [x] Config parity with the Python SDK (names, env vars, defaults)
- [x] Unit + e2e tests added/updated; verified local and against prod

## Issues

- OPIK-7349 (this change)
- Parent: OPIK-7312 (enforce Opik span/trace ingestion size limits)
- Python counterpart: OPIK-7335 (#7469)

## Testing

- `tsc --noEmit` clean; `eslint` clean on changed files.
- Unit suite green (only the repo's known pre-existing `PromptVersion` / lazy-loading failures remain — unrelated to this change).
- **e2e — 10/10 both local and prod** (`payloadTruncation.e2e` + `attachmentExtraction.e2e`): truncation (span, trace, hard per-object cap, disabled, configurable, update path, metadata-exempt) + attachment extraction (span, trace, round-trip on read).
- A separate throwaway 15-scenario matrix (mixed multi-span, data-URI, non-media, multiple images, config variations) was run against a local backend and prod to visually confirm markers/placeholders in the UI.

## Documentation

No user-facing doc changes in this PR. The customer-facing ingestion size-limits documentation is tracked separately under OPIK-7336 (#7468), which will be updated to state Python **and** TypeScript once this lands.

## Summary

Fixes the "I logged in but can't find Flow" problem found during go-live. Staff had to type `/flow` manually: sign-in always landed on the CMS dashboard, and `/admin` had no link onward.

- **CMS nav entry**: adds a **"Taskcover Flow"** item to the `/admin` sidebar (for admins and editors — Flow does its own capability checks on arrival). CMS ↔ Flow is now one click in both directions (Flow already linked back to Content CMS since FLOW-001).

author: bpowers
body:
Part 2 of Track A, the follow-on to #980 (now merged as `24759a7e`; this branch has been rebased
onto `main`). #980 deleted LTM's `AST -> text -> AST` round trip on the
*output* side (generated equations stored as typed ASTs) and killed the classify-twice contract
that produced silent-zero link scores. This deletes the round trip on the **input** side: the
ceteris-paribus wrap no longer parses the target equation's printed text.

Part of #965. Does **not** close it — see "What remains" below.

## The result worth leading with

`expr2_to_string` is literally `print_eqn(expr2_to_expr0(e))`. So every one of the eight
`Expr0::new` sites in `ltm_augment.rs` was parsing *our own printed output of a tree we already
held in that exact shape*. Deleting them is "pass the `Expr0` instead of the `String`".

The consequence is stronger than the parse count. `db::ltm_ir` computes every occurrence's
`SiteId` on the `Expr2` tree; the wrap addresses occurrences by the child-index path it tracks as
it descends. Feeding the wrap the direct lowering makes those two path spaces **the same tree by
construction**. Before, they coincided only because print-then-parse happened to round-trip — a
property the corpus alignment sweep could *sample* but never *establish*. Given that five of the
six defects #980's review found were silent zeros arising from exactly this class of
"coincides in practice" assumption, moving it to by-construction is the point of the change.

Parse-site tally: **5 deleted, 1 relocated to a legitimate source-format boundary, 2 remain**
(with reasons, below). `ltm_augment.rs`: 5921 -> 5644 lines.

## Commits

| | |
|---|---|
| `8c7b4892` | lower LTM target equations to Expr0 without a reparse |
| `455001c9` | pin LTM per-element rows inside the wrap, not after it |
| `d6aadf8e` | delete the LTM occurrence fields nothing reads |
| `17a3ab27` | prove the LTM test occurrence axes against the IR |
| `2ac7c986` | carry LTM reducer bodies as ASTs, not printed text |
| `92615225` | decline loudly when an LTM row pin has no occurrence |
| `c4478627` | correct the LTM augmentation map in CLAUDE.md |
| `8b5df6b2` | pin LTM table-argument rows structurally, not loudly |
| `fc6c6ae0` | descend expression indices in the LTM pin-only walk |
| `1ea4f0f7` | decline an LTM table-argument index that reads at runtime |
| `afd1b92b` | gate the LTM table-index refusal on the enclosing freeze |
| `b429d4d8` | enumerate the LTM table-index verdicts, not just the found cases |
| `872e8f37` | resolve LTM table indices by the shared derivation |
| `4b295f52` | row the fifth LTM table-index variant too |
| `1375dad6` | look inside a compound LTM table index |
| `13aff4a5` | break an LTM index name collision the compiler's way |

## The crux: row pinning moved inside the wrap

`455001c9` is the load-bearing commit. Deleting the last two production Expr0-side classifiers
required relocating `PerElement` row pinning, and the obvious approach — a shape-preserving
pre-pass on the original AST — is **wrong**, which we established from the corpus rather than by
argument.

Row pinning emits two spellings of the same site shape: the occurrence the wrap left **live**
gets the row with bare element names; every occurrence it **froze** gets the same row qualified
(`region·boston`), so the frozen read compiles to a direct `LoadPrev` instead of an ambiguous bare
element name. That live-vs-frozen fact exists only in the *wrapped* tree, and it is not derivable
from the occurrence — two occurrences with identical `axes` can land on opposite sides.
`per_element_index_nested_occurrence.txt` already pins both spellings inside one equation. On a
model whose element names are ambiguous across dimensions — C-LEARN's regions — the bare spelling
**fails to compile**, so a pre-pass's divergence would be a silent zero, not cosmetic.

So the pin runs *inside* the wrap, which is the one traversal that knows both the occurrence (by
path) and whether it is about to freeze. This **reverses a documented decision** made in #980
(the "drive LTM live-ref selection from the occurrence IR" commit, squashed into `24759a7e`),
whose rustdoc rejected wrap-time occurrence *tagging* — that needs a tag-only descent
or a `Loc`-keyed side map, i.e. a second representation with its own drift surface. A pin-only
descent writes no tag and carries no map; it reads the one IR by path and performs the actual
lowering. Different thing, admissible for that reason.

Pinned narrowly rather than incidentally: mutating `child_frozen = frozen || will_wrap` down to
`frozen` — the exact information loss a pre-pass suffers — fails **precisely one** golden, the one
named in advance. Ignoring live/frozen entirely fails eight.

## One classifier family, and the surviving mirror is gated

`classify_expr0_per_element_axes` and `expr0_iterated_axis_lines_up` are out of production. Per-axis
equivalence is exact, not approximate: the retired classifier consulted the same
`ltm_agg::classify_axis_access` the IR uses, gate for gate.

A `#[cfg(test)]` Expr0 mirror survives, moved beside its only consumer in
`ltm_augment_wrap_test_support.rs`. Full deletion is not achievable: three wrap unit tests cannot
be db-backed fixtures — two feed deliberately unparseable and empty text (they pin the loud
parse-failure contract), and the third is `SUM(w[from]) + from`, which the engine **rejects as a
model** (`ArrayReferenceNeedsExplicitSubscripts`) yet still needs an occurrence stream.

Per the plan's own rule — *mirrors are acceptable when drift is loudly gated; where one must stay,
the gate is the deliverable* — `17a3ab27` extends the corpus gate from comparing `shape` to
comparing **`axes`** as well, so it now proves every field of the reconstruction the production
wrap reads (`SiteId` path, `shape`, `axes`, `in_reducer`). An `IndexExpr0 -> IndexExpr2` lift was
rejected: it would add a mirror faithful only to the forms `classify_axis_access` happens to
inspect, in order to delete a mirror.

## `OccurrenceSite`: four fields deleted, one kept

`target_element`, `routing`, `reducer_keys`, `already_lagged` had no production reader. The
strongest case is `routing`, which was not merely unread but a **duplicated derivation**:
`model_ltm_reference_sites` held two copies of the #793 agg-narrowing rule, and deleting the field
deletes one of them. Duplicate logic inside the IR built to remove duplicate logic.

`in_reducer` stays — its reader is the corpus gate's reducer-context assertion, and deleting it
would silently narrow that gate. Its rustdoc says so explicitly, and records why it is **not**
consumed by the #779 bare-feeder decline: `reducer_collapses_to_scalar` includes `SIZE` and
excludes `RANK` while `builtin_routes_through_agg` does the opposite, so wiring it up would flip a
bare source inside `RANK(...)` from scored to loudly declined. Filed as **#982**.

Deleting `already_lagged` also removed a parameter still threaded through every recursive call of
`walk_all_in_expr` computing only itself — dead code the compiler cannot see, because it is
genuinely "used" at each hop.

## A regression introduced and fixed inside this branch

`455001c9` introduced a silent zero, and the story is disclosed rather than tidied because the way
it was found matters.

A `PerElement` source occurrence inside a `LOOKUP` **table argument** came out un-pinned:
`lookup(pop[region, young], ...)`. That dimension-name subscript cannot resolve in a scalar
fragment, so the fragment is dropped, the variable keeps a layout slot with no bytecode, and the
score reads a constant 0. The cause is a genuine tension: `db::ltm_ir` records no occurrence under
a table argument (*"static data, not a causal edge"*) and it is **right** — but the pin such a
reference needs is about **compilability, not attribution**. The pre-`455001c9` pass pinned it
anyway because it re-classified the wrapped tree and so needed no occurrence. The IR-driven
pinning correctly refused to guess, and then said nothing, which

author: jamesiit
body:
# feat(infra): Provision ECS Task Execution Role & SSM Security Policies

## 📌 Overview

This PR introduces the `ComputeStack` within our AWS CDK infrastructure and configures the foundational IAM permissions required by the ECS Fargate Agent (`taskExecutionRole`).

It establishes the security model allowing Fargate to pull container images from Amazon ECR, stream logs to Amazon CloudWatch, and securely fetch database credentials from AWS Systems Manager (SSM) Parameter Store at boot time.

---

## 🛠️ Key Changes

### 1. `ComputeStack` Setup

* Created and wired `ComputeStack` into the main CDK application entry point (`CdkApp`).

### 2. Execution Role & Core Managed Policies

* Instantiated the `taskExecutionRole` assumed by `ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com`.
* Attached the AWS-managed `AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy` to grant Fargate permission to:
* Authenticate and pull Docker images from Amazon ECR.
* Create and push container logs to CloudWatch Log Groups.



### 3. Least-Privilege SSM Parameter Access

* Referenced external SSM parameters for database credentials (`dbUsername` and `dbPassword`) using CDK's `IStringParameter` interface (`StringParameter.fromStringParameterName`).
* Granted explicit read permissions directly to the `taskExecutionRole` using `.grantRead()`, ensuring scoped least-privilege access without exposing plaintext secrets in CloudFormation templates.

---

## 🔒 Security & Architectural Highlights

* **Decoupled Application & Infra:** Secrets are injected at runtime into the container's environment variables by the ECS Agent, avoiding hardcoded values or `.env` files in git repositories.
* **Scoped Least Privilege:** Avoided blanket SSM read policies by explicitly granting `taskExecutionRole` access strictly to the required database parameter ARNs.

author: stan-breik
body:
The key-events label editor (v0.15.0) froze on "Loading" on instances with real GA4 data (reported on breik.cloud, console: state_unsafe_mutation).

`labelFor()` lazily created a missing `event_labels` entry during template render — a state mutation during render, which Svelte 5 rejects. The crash aborted the card's render exactly when the drill-down returned real rows. The demo data used to verify v0.15.0 returned "unavailable" (no live Google), so the table body never rendered and the bug stayed hidden; the label flows that were exercised (stored labels, add-by-name) create entries in event handlers, which is allowed.

Fix: `labelValue()` is a pure read for the template, `setLabel()` creates the entry on first keystroke (input event only).

Verified by reproducing first: stubbed the drill-down response with three GA4 rows against the running v0.15.0 build → same frozen Loading + state_unsafe_mutation as production. With the fix: rows render editable, a previously stored label appears in its fetched row, a typed label persists through saveLayout and a full reload, zero page errors. svelte-check 0 errors.

author: hunterh37
body:
Milestone 4 — durability & reliability (enterprise hardening). Makes the editor safe to trust with real work.

## Crash-safe command journal (EditingKit)

`CommandStack` wraps the document stage in a `JournalingStage` proxy that captures, for every `StageMutation` a command applies, both the forward mutation **and its inverse** — computed from the stage state immediately *before* the apply (`StageMutation.inverse(reading:)`).

This is what generalizes the existing mesh-edit session journal: no command needs per-command journaling code, because every command funnels through `stage.apply`.

- `FileCommandJournal` — the WAL. JSON Lines, `fsync` per append, torn trailing line discarded on read.
- `SessionStore` — session layout under Application Support, crash detection via a `session.live` sentinel that only survives when no clean shutdown ran.
- `CommandStack.recovered(stage:journal:records:)` — replays a plan against the reopened document, restoring stage content **and both the undo and redo stacks** to their exact pre-crash depths and labels, then keeps appending to the same WAL.

## Round-trip invariants as a blocking CI job

New `openusdz roundtrip` subcommand + `scripts/roundtrip-gate.sh`, wired into `ci.yml` as its own red-on-failure job:

| Invariant | Scope |
|---|---|
| Model idempotence — `open(F) == open(save(open(F)))` | whole corpus |
| Edit/undo neutrality — `open(F) == open(save(undoAll(edit(open(F)))))` | whole corpus |
| Strict flattened-text diff (`--strict`) | opt-in per file |

Each file's expected outcome lives in an `EXPECTATIONS` table, and **the gate is red when reality disagrees in either direction** — a declared-passing invariant that starts failing is a regression; a declared-failing one that starts passing means the table must be tightened. Same ratchet discipline as `coverage-gate.sh`. Verified red in both directions before landing.

A missing usd-core is a local skip but a hard CI failure (`ROUNDTRIP_REQUIRE_USD=1`) — a gate that passes when its dependency is absent isn't a gate.

## Bridge mini-corpus + USDBridge to its spec floor

Committed fixtures under `Packages/USDBridge/Tests/USDBridgeTests/Fixtures/Corpus` — cube/variants/skel/animated as `.usda`, cube+skel packaged as `.usdz`, plus malformed — with golden assertions against real usd-core, plus real `StageSaver` save-path round-trips.

**USDBridge graduates from its 90% ratchet to its 95% spec floor** (measures 100%).

## Exit harness

`EditingKitTests/CrashRecoveryTests` writes the WAL through the real command stack, `SIGKILL`s a real child process so no graceful shutdown or sentinel cleanup runs, and restores the exact command stack from the bytes on disk alone — including the case where the kill tears a record in half.

## Two pre-existing gaps, now enforced rather than silent

The round-trip gate surfaced two real data-loss paths. Both are pre-existing and squarely outside this milestone's scope, so they are **recorded in the gate's table** rather than fixed here:

- `USDASerializer` emits no `variantSet` blocks → variant sets dropped on save (Phase 12).
- Attributes the bridge surfaces as `.unsupported` (a purely time-sampled channel has no default-time value) are written as an "omitted" comment → their values dropped on save (Phase 10).

This is also why `strict` is `no` across the corpus today: re-serializing materializes computed attributes (`purpose`, `visibility`), so flattened text is not yet byte-equivalent. Closing either gap requires tightening `EXPECTATIONS`, which the gate enforces.

## Gates

`dependency-lint` · `module-governance` · `test-all --coverage` · `coverage-gate` (EditingKit + USDCore 100%, CLI 96.4%, USDBridge 100%) · `roundtrip-gate` — all green locally.

Specs updated in the same PR: `specs/testing.md`, `specs/editing-model.md`, `specs/mesh-editing.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `CLAUDE.md`.

author: rjwalters
body:
## Summary

Foundational Phase-2 piece for the Botho MetaMask Snap (`web/packages/snap`).
The Phase-1 MVP kept **no** persisted state — every `botho_getBalance` /
`botho_showBalance` re-scanned the chain from genesis (`getOutputs(0, tip)`),
O(chain height) per read and forgotten when the execution context ends. This PR
adds the Snap's first persisted surface via `snap_manageState` and makes
scanning **incremental + resumable**, so #1092 (history) and #1093 (contacts)
have a state store to build on.

## Changes

- **`src/state.ts` (new)** — encrypted, versioned, network-bound `{ version, scan }`
  schema, namespaced so #1092/#1093 extend it without a migration. Persists owned
  outputs with `blockHeight` + `txHash` (history needs no rescan) but **not** spent
  status (recomputed live via `chain_areKeyImagesSpent`). Includes network/version
  invalidation, a `REORG_BUFFER`, target-key dedupe, windowing helpers, and the
  `incrementalScanBalance` orchestrator (keeps `index.ts` thin).
- **`src/node.ts`** — `getOutputsWithMeta`: a meta-carrying windowed `chain_getOutputs`
  fetch preserving per-block height + per-output txHash (the flat `getOutputs` drops them).
- **`src/index.ts`** — rewired both balance reads to `read state → windowed scan →
  persist → live spent-filter for the sum`. Derivation and the wrong-network guard
  are unchanged.
- **`snap.manifest.json`** — added `snap_manageState` permission; build refreshed the shasum.
- **`test/mock-node.ts`** — the mock now honours the `chain_getOutputs` `[start,end]`
  window and can carry per-block `height` / per-output `txHash`.
- **`test/state.snap.ts` (new)** — pure-logic contract tests + behavioural
  incremental-scan tests driven off `node.calls`.
- **`README.md`** — documented the permission, schema, and incremental-scan model;
  moved windowed scanning from Deferred to Shipped.

## Acceptance Criteria Verification

| Criterion | Status | Verification |
|-----------|--------|--------------|
| Manifest gains `snap_manageState`; shasum refreshed | ✅ | `initialPermissions.snap_manageState: {}`; `build:snap` recomputed the shasum |
| Typed, versioned, network-bound blob read/written encrypted; namespaced `{ version, scan }` | ✅ | `readState`/`writeState` use `snap_manageState` `encrypted: true`; `usableScanState` unit test |
| Owned outputs persist `blockHeight`+`txHash`; spent status not persisted | ✅ | `toPersistedOwnedOutput` test asserts fields present and `spent`/`spentHeight` absent |
| Balance scanning windowed + incremental; 2nd call at same tip fetches no new windows beyond reorg buffer, same balance | ✅ | `state.snap.ts` "resumes from the checkpoint" asserts window ranges off `node.calls` |
| Stale/foreign state invalidated → full rescan from 0 | ✅ | `usableScanState` unit test + "invalidates persisted state from another network" behavioural test (start_height 0) |
| Existing behavior preserved (empty chain → 0, guards, send/address/dialogs) | ✅ | `balance.snap.ts` / `send.snap.ts` / `derivation.snap.ts` / `units.snap.ts` all green, unchanged |
| README documents permission, schema, incremental-scan model; Deferred updated | ✅ | new "Persisted state & incremental scanning" section; Deferred list updated |

## Test Plan

- `pnpm --filter @botho/wasm-signer build:wasm:bundler` (artifact for the SES bundle)
- `pnpm --filter @botho/snap typecheck` — clean
- `pnpm --filter @botho/snap build:snap` — bundle built, manifest shasum refreshed
- `pnpm --filter @botho/snap test:snap` — **5 suites / 26 tests pass** (new `state.snap.ts` + no regressions)

`@botho/wasm-signer` source was not modified (reference only), so its suite was not re-run.

Closes #1091

author: hua0424
body:
Implements aichatoverview#180

## What
REQ-014 思考内联化：前端需按「已加载消息页的 msgId」批量反查 thinking 元数据。本 PR = server 侧只读小端点 + 死端点清理。

### 新增 `POST /im/aiclaw/thinking/by-trigger`
- 入参 `{ roomId: Long, triggerMsgIds: Long[] }`；`triggerMsgIds` `@NotEmpty` + `@Size(max=100)`，空/超限按参数校验拒绝。
- 授权复用 `ThinkingService.checkCurrentUserMembership`（同 reviewThinking 的 IDOR 统一拒绝语义：非成员 → `BizException "思考记录不存在或无权查看"`，查询前置）。
- 查询 `WHERE room_id=? AND trigger_msg_id IN (...) AND is_del=0 ORDER BY id ASC`；`idx_trigger_msg` 已存在，**无 DDL**；metadata only（**不含 content**，全文仍走 `/thinking/{thinkingId}`）。
- 同一 triggerMsgId 多 aiclaw = 多行，按 id 升序。

### 删除旧游标列表死端点（全链）
- `AiclawController.listThinkingByRoom`（`GET /thinking/list`）
- `ThinkingService.listThinkingByRoom` + 死常量 `DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE`/`MAX_PAGE_SIZE` + 死 import
- `AiclawThinkingMapper.selectThinkingListByRoom`

唯一消费者是 frontend 归档抽屉（随同 Milestone 的 #181 一并废除）；codegraph 复核 server 内无其他调用方。⚠️ 合并→frontend 单合并前旧客户端归档抽屉短暂 404，已裁决接受。

## Response 契约（供 frontend #181）
`R<List<AiclawThinkingListItemResp>>`，字段：`id / aiclawUid / triggerMsgId / status / durationMs / hasResponse / createTime`（与旧列表项一致），id ASC。

## Tests (TDD)
`ThinkingServiceTest`：新增 `ListThinkingByTriggerMsgIds`（成员→映射行 + mapper 被调；非成员→统一 BizException + mapper `never()`；空结果；多 aiclaw 同触发多行 id-asc）+ DTO 上限/空/null 校验；旧 `ListThinkingByRoom` 用例删除。
`mvn -pl luohuo-im-biz test -Dtest=ThinkingServiceTest` → **Tests run: 24, Failures: 0**；controller `test-compile` BUILD SUCCESS。

## 红线
feature off dev，base=dev；不 bump umbrella 指针；不动 DDL；不动 ws-biz ThinkingProcessor / 内部 ThinkingController。

author: bobmatnyc
body:
## Summary

Issue #3408: the native file watcher (inotify/FSEvents) cannot observe writes
made by another host onto a shared EFS/NFS/SMB mount — an OS-level
limitation. Previously the watcher started successfully on such a mount, the
daemon reported healthy, and the watcher silently never fired for cross-host
changes. This PR fixes the silent failure and blesses the existing supported
path.

- **Part 2 (the bug):** `service::network_fs::classify_root` detects a
  network-mounted path via `statfs` (macOS `f_fstypename`; Linux `f_type`
  magic number + a `/proc/mounts` fallback for named network FUSE backends
  like `fuse.sshfs`), using the already-vendored `nix` crate's `fs` feature.
  Detection is conservative and **fails open to Local** on any error/ambiguity
  (a bare `fuse` mount is never flagged) — a false positive (refusing a local
  disk) is worse than a false negative, per the issue's guidance.
  `WatcherManager::spawn_for_index` now refuses to start a watcher for a
  network-mounted root instead of silently starting one that can never fire,
  and records the actionable reason. Surfaced on `GET /health`
  (`indexes_watcher_network_degraded`, folded into the existing
  `"ok"`/`"degraded"` convention from issue #1870) and
  `GET /indexes/:id/status` (`watcher.active` / `watcher.network_mount_degraded`
  / `watcher.degraded_reason`), naming `POST /indexes/:id/index-file` and
  `POST /indexes/:id/remove-file` as the next step. This mirrors the
  codebase's existing "log at WARN + degrade, never fail registration"
  convention for watcher failures rather than introducing a new hard-refusal
  semantic.
- **Part 1 (docs):** officially documents those two endpoints (plus the
  `index_file`/`remove_file` MCP tools) as the supported,
  stability-committed incremental-indexing path for network-mounted and
  build/serve-split deployments, with a worked example script, in
  `crates/trusty-search/README.md` and `CLAUDE.md`'s endpoint catalogue.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p trusty-search --lib` — 1169 passed, 0 failed (new tests:
      `network_fs::tests::*` pin the pure name/magic classifiers plus a
      real-tempdir false-positive guard; `watcher_manager::tests::*` inject
      `MountKind::Network`/`Local` via `spawn_for_index_with_mount_kind` to
      pin the refuse-and-report path and the local-unaffected path without a
      real NFS mount; `tests_health::health_surfaces_watcher_network_degraded_count`
      covers the `/health` JSON surface end-to-end)
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --exclude trusty-mpm-gui --exclude trusty-code-gui --exclude trusty-agents-ui -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `cargo check --workspace --exclude trusty-mpm-gui --exclude trusty-code-gui --exclude trusty-agents-ui` — clean
- [x] `cargo test --workspace --exclude trusty-mpm-gui --exclude trusty-code-gui --exclude trusty-agents-ui --no-fail-fast` — only 2 pre-existing/unrelated failures (trusty-agents `checkpoint_resume` parallel-load flake; trusty-code `run_task` test needing a live trusty-memory daemon), neither touched by this change
- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check` — clean

🤖🤖🤖 Generated with trusty-mpm — https://github.com/bobmatnyc/trusty-tools


Closes #3408

body: Finishes the one-mechanism seam for the Skeleton. GET /api/v1/kommons/nodes now ships the registry's authoritative buckets; the client keeps its compile-time BUCKETS union (for the exhaustive Record<Bucket> layout maps) and warnOnBucketDrift validates it against the server at load, warning on divergence instead of silently dropping nodes. Option A (validate + keep type-safety). Verified: rubocop clean; request-spec asserts buckets == NodeRegistry::BUCKETS; prettier/eslint/tsc clean on changed TS. Vitest drift test runs in CI (local env lacks fake-indexeddb setup dep).

author: luciferyang
body:
## Summary

System columns (`_rowid`, `_rowaddr`, `_rowoffset`, `_row_created_at_version`, `_row_last_updated_at_version`) are virtual: they are injected at read time and never stored. If a stored top-level manifest field happens to share one of these names, the injected system column collides with it on the next scan, panicking in `Projection::to_schema` at `schema.extend(...).unwrap()`.

The write/insert path already rejects these names (#7797), but the schema-evolution and raw-commit paths had no guard: `add_columns`, `alter_columns` (rename), `drop_columns`, `Dataset::merge`, and user-built `Operation`s committed through `Dataset::commit` / `CommitBuilder` (including the Python and Java bindings) could all still land a reserved name in the stored schema.

This adds a single guard at the one commit chokepoint, `Transaction::build_manifest`, which every schema-bearing operation (`Overwrite` / `Merge` / `Project`) flows through. Other operations reuse the current manifest schema and cannot introduce a new name, so guarding this one spot covers every path. The check is top-level only, matching where the collision actually happens.

## Grandfathering

Only newly introduced names are rejected. A reserved name already present in the current manifest schema is grandfathered, because schema evolution re-commits the full existing schema and older versions permitted some of these names (the row-version columns were reserved only recently). Rejecting a pre-existing name here would lock such a dataset out of all schema evolution.

## Notes for reviewers

The guard fires at commit time, so `merge` / `add_columns` write their new column data files before the rejection, leaving orphan data files on a rejected commit. This is a strict improvement over the previous silent corruption, and the orphans are reclaimed by version cleanup.

The two guards are intentionally asymmetric: the write/insert guard (#7797) rejects all five names unconditionally, while this commit-time guard grandfathers names already in the manifest. The write path is strictly stricter; the commit-time path must let legacy datasets keep evolving.

## Test plan

- `build_manifest_rejects_newly_introduced_system_column_name` / `build_manifest_grandfathers_preexisting_system_column_name` — unit tests over the guard's two branches.
- `schema_evolution_rejects_reserved_system_column_names` — 5 cases (one per name) over `add_columns` and `alter_columns` rename.
- `merge_rejects_reserved_system_column_names` — 5 cases over `Dataset::merge`.
- `cargo fmt --all` and `cargo clippy --all --tests --benches -- -D warnings`.

  * Existing datasets that already contain reserved system columns remain compatible.
  * Updated errors to clearly indicate the attempted column name is reserved.

* **Tests**

## Summary

The AnA Command Center's two action affordances handed off to chat instead of executing. This actions-pass wires both to their **real, audited** backends — replacing the last "hand to AnA chat" stand-ins on this surface with genuine, honestly-rendered execution.

**Run workflow** → `POST /api/orchestration/execute`
- The executor runs every step server-side and returns the terminal `WorkflowExecution`.
- The surface **confirms first** (the run mutates objects and is audited), shows an honest spinner while the POST is in flight, then renders the **real** result: step statuses, summary, blockers, and created/updated objects — verbatim server output.
- The former fabricated `setTimeout` step animation stays removed. The executor returns terminal state (no step stream), so the in-flight UI is an honest spinner, not a faked progress bar.

**Dispatch a recommendation** → routed on the engine's `actionPayload.actionType`
- A **workflow-template id** → `/api/orchestration/execute`.
- A real **AIActionType** → `POST /api/ai-actions/execute` (`sourceSurface: 'recommendation'`), handling both the sync (`200`) and async-queue (`202` / `status:'queued'`) responses honestly — "queued" is never rendered as "done".
- When the recommendation carries **no** `actionPayload`, the button reads **"Ask AnA"** and hands the suggestion to chat — no fabricated execution.

Both executors write GxP-relevant `regulatory_audit_logs` rows (SHA-256 integrity hash, user-attributed), so the "recorded to the audit trail · 21 CFR Part 11" claim on the result is truthful. The client `Rec` type is corrected to match the real `Recommendation` shape (`targetObjectId` + `actionPayload`), which the previous interface omitted.

No `Math.random` / `Date.now` / mock. Every rendered value is verbatim server output or an honest empty/error state.

## Type of Change

- Feature wiring (UI → real backend), GA-quality. Single file: `client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/AnaCommand.tsx`.
- No schema, route, or server changes — consumes existing, verified endpoints (`/api/orchestration/execute`, `/api/orchestration/executions/:id`, `/api/ai-actions/execute`).

Arc 2, brief 1 — first post of the "Running a Fleet, Not a Demo" arc. Direct sequel to [Your Second Agent Is the Hard One](/blog/your-second-agent-is-the-hard-one) (PR #34): that post argued the failures move *into the space between* agents; this one is about engineering that space.

body:
## Problem

The app crashed on import with sqlalchemy.exc.InvalidRequestError because create_async_engine received a psycopg2-based URL. Railway's Postgres plugin injects DATABASE_URL as postgresql://..., which SQLAlchemy resolves to the synchronous psycopg2 driver, incompatible with the async engine. This caused uvicorn workers to die before binding to $PORT, failing the /health healthcheck.

## Solution

Added a _normalize_async_url helper in backend/app/database/base.py that rewrites postgresql:// and postgres:// schemes to postgresql+asyncpg://, and applied it in build_engine() before calling create_async_engine. asyncpg is already a dependency, so no requirements changes were needed.

- **Modified** `backend/app/database/base.py`

author: srobroek
body:
Refs #1208. One line of behaviour; the rest is comment.

## The finding

`e2e.yml` shares a single concurrency group across every push to `main`, and `cancel-in-progress: true` applied there too. Merges during a campaign land seconds apart, so **each merge killed the previous main run and none ever survived to report.**

Measured directly from the run history, not inferred:

| run | head | created | ended | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 29726962192 | `0aced5f0` | 08:10:18 | **08:19:23** | cancelled |
| 29727493804 | `971e7b11` | **08:19:22** | 08:21:14 | cancelled |

The first died one second after the second was created; the second died two seconds after the push that followed. **Ten consecutive main runs** went the same way — of the twelve most recent, only two were not cancelled.

## Why it matters

The Real-UI E2E suite has not been gating `main` at all. That is the structural half of #1203 and the reason #1208 was so hard to pin down: the suite *looked* configured while reporting nothing, and the absence of red reads as green.

It also explains the observed sequence on #1208 — main was believed green, then the first uncancelled main run in hours (`29717774194`) immediately failed on two shards.

## The change

```yaml
cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != refs/heads/main }}
```

Superseded runs are still cancelled on branches, where it is correct and saves real runner time. On `main` they are allowed to finish.

**This does not serialise indefinitely.** With `cancel-in-progress: false`, GitHub keeps at most the in-flight run plus the newest queued run and discards intermediate pending ones — so the cost is bounded at ~2 runs per group, not one per merge, while guaranteeing that one completes.

## Scope I deliberately did not take

`ci.yml` and `release-gate.yml` carry the **identical** blanket setting, so main-side integration and unit regressions are just as invisible.

I did not touch them: #1216, #1212 and #1247 are all live in `ci.yml` right now, and a fourth lane editing it would be gratuitous. Reported on #1203 so it lands with whoever owns that file next. `release-gate.yml` may also be deliberate for release gating — worth a decision rather than a blanket sweep.

## Verification

- YAML parses; the expression renders as `${{ github.ref != refs/heads/main }}` (GitHub evaluates `cancel-in-progress` expressions — this is the documented idiom).
- The real proof is post-merge: main E2E runs should start reaching a conclusion instead of `cancelled`. Worth watching the first few, since this is a config change whose effect cannot be observed from a PR branch — on this branch the old behaviour still (correctly) applies.

author: taklin1
body:
Closes #60. Prolonge #53 (Révélation bord-franc) déjà mergée dans l'épopée #41.

## Problème

La Révélation déploie l'Étendu **autour** du curseur au bord haut : aucun `mouseEntered` natif ne se produit. Si le curseur repart ensuite **sans jamais survoler le panneau**, `hoverDidChange(false)` ne se déclenche jamais, `scheduleRecede` n'est pas armé, et l'Étendu **reste ouvert** (cause racine du body #60).

## Solution

Repli géométrique. Le moniteur souris global (déjà en place, coquille mince) demande désormais, après `shouldReveal`, à une nouvelle **fonction pure** `IslandController.shouldRecede(at:in:)` si le curseur a clairement quitté la Révélation. Quand l'Étendu est ouvert **et** que le panneau n'est pas survolé, il arme **une seule fois** le même recede anti-clignotement (délai de grâce ~300 ms inchangé).

- `shouldRecede` : `true` si le curseur descend sous la profondeur de maintien (`recedeKeepAliveDepth` 220 pt, couvre la hauteur du panneau) **ou** sort de la bande de recede (`recedeBandWidth` 340 pt).
- **Hystérésis** : bande de recede (340) > bande de révélation (280) ⇒ un liseré entre les deux où ni révélation ni recede ne se déclenchent : l'oscillation brève au bord ne clignote pas.
- Le survol natif (`isHovering`) reste l'autorité sur « le curseur est sur le panneau » : le repli géométrique ne le combat jamais. Nominal intact (`keepVisible` maintient à l'entrée ; recede à la sortie).
- Ré-entrer dans la bande (`reveal()`) ou sur le panneau (hover) annule un recede en attente (pas de clignotement).

## Périmètre

Strict #60 : `Sources/IslandUI/IslandController.swift` (+ fonction pure, entrée `recedeIfClearOfPanel()`, seam de test `isExtendedDeployed`) et `Sources/Island/main.swift` (branchement du moniteur). Pas touché au Peek, à la mascotte barre menus, à l'Acquittement. **Version et `CHANGELOG.md` intouchés** (réconciliation orchestrateur).

## Tests

- **TDD** : `Tests/IslandUITests/RecedeTests.swift` (rouge d'abord). Géométrie pure (repli sous le bord, hors bande, maintien au bord / sur le panneau, liseré d'hystérésis) + wiring contrôleur (« bord puis sortie de bande sans survol ⇒ repli » ; no-op si Masqué).
- `swift build` ✅ · `swift test` ✅ **169 tests**.
- **FP `/agentic-tests`** ✅ : app réelle sur 41414, session injectée, curseur synthétique CGEvent au bord → trace `révélation: 2 session card(s)`, puis descente hors bande sans survol → trace `masqué (curseur quitte le panneau)`.

## Changelog proposé

- #60 Durci le recede de la Révélation : repli géométrique (`shouldRecede`) quand le curseur quitte la bande sans survoler le panneau, avec hystérésis anti-clignotement (bande recede 340 > révélation 280).

author: gen16k
body:
> **Stacked on #109** (`base: feat/835-executor-lease`). Review the top commit only;
> GitHub retargets this to `main` automatically when #109 merges.

## The §9 defect, stated correctly

The spec said "12 min < 30 min, so the executor dies mid-download". That was wrong, and
the corrected measurement is in waired-ai/waired#872:

- The 12-minute literal at `cmd/waired/login_client.go:60` bounds **only the pre-`Active`
  poll** — the `LoginPhaseActive` case ends in `return nil`.
- What actually bounds post-login residency is `benchPollDeadline = 10 min`, and on an
  engine-less host `benchNoEngineGrace` collapses it to **3 min**.
- The NAVI onboarding host **is** the engine-less host. The operator's time to read the
  offer card and click "Yes" sits entirely inside that 3-minute window.

So the executor was gone before the wizard's first instruction arrived.

## Residency is a loop condition, not a check

At `LoginPhaseActive` **no desired-state frame has arrived yet** — the agent marks a setup
active only when one does, and that happens after the operator clicks in the browser. A
single check here would always read `active=false`, keep the legacy deadline, and lose.

`awaitSetupBudget` polls until the setup goes active (→ the 30-minute budget, matched to the
CP's setup ticket TTL) or `setupAwaitGrace` elapses (→ the legacy deadline, unchanged).

The grace is the **executor's own patience**, not a daemon-reported state: the daemon cannot
know a setup ticket was issued — the ticket lives control-plane-side and never reaches the
agent (§8.1). Reporting `pending` from the daemon could mean nothing more than "no frame
yet", which is not a decision input.

## §4.2 prompt suppression, finally delivered

Two prompts block on stdin immediately after login:

| prompt | why it must not run during browser setup |
|---|---|
| `runPostLoginIntegration` consent (`login_client.go:88`) | the wizard is on screen; the terminal silently blocks |
| `benchmarkWithScanner` (`login_client.go:111`) | it can offer to **switch the active model** — a second writer racing `desired_model_id`, and a recommendation §20.6 forbids in v1 |

Both are skipped while a setup is driving the host, and both run **exactly as today**
otherwise. The executor attaches **before** them — attaching after would arrive minutes late.

## Enter-to-background: built, not just wired

This affordance did not exist on the daemon path. `waitForBundledModel` now takes an explicit
budget and an optional `enterListener`, and during a setup it no longer lets the `no_engine`
grace end the wait — the executor is about to install the very engine that grace was written
to give up on. Pressing Enter releases the lease (the wizard switches to "run this here"
rather than spinning), drains the pending scanner read per `init_enter.go`'s contract, and
resumes the normal CLI tail.

## What is guaranteed unchanged (acceptance item 12)

Pinned by tests, not by assertion:

- `--no-browser` and `--non-interactive` → legacy budget, both prompts run, no listener
- a daemon that **404s** the executor routes (older than this feature) → the session is
  **inert**; every method is a no-op and the flow is the pre-#835 one
- the standalone `init` path (`main.go`) → `benchPollDeadline`, no executor, no backgrounding
- the four existing `waitForBundledModel` tests pass **unmodified apart from the new
  arguments**, which is the regression bar

Ctrl-C / SIGTERM release the lease before the process dies, so the wizard reports
`executor_gone` promptly instead of waiting out the 45 s TTL.

## Verification

```
gofmt -l .            # clean
go vet ./...          # clean
golangci-lint run     # 0 issues
go test ./... -timeout 10m   # all pass
make verify-cross     # clean
```

New tests: `cmd/waired/setup_executor_test.go` (8 cases — older-daemon inertness, attach /
heartbeat / release, the install phase surviving heartbeats, unelevated reporting, waiting for
the click, grace fallback, Enter backgrounding, non-interactive skip) and two additions to
`cmd/waired/init_pull_test.go` (no_engine grace ignored during setup; Enter backgrounds the
wait).

Docs: `docs-site/.../getting-started/first-run.mdx` + the `ja/` mirror — what the new terminal
message means, that the terminal should stay open, and what Enter does.

## Not in this PR

The executor does not **install** anything yet — it only holds the lease and reports. That is
PR-H, which reuses `installOllama` / `engineInstallDecision` / `handStateToServiceUser`
verbatim.

## Refs

- Refs waired-ai/waired#835 · design: waired-ai/waired#872 · daemon side: #109

body:
## What changed

- Detect a public HTTP callback before starting Notion OAuth.
- Return a dedicated `CONNECTOR_OAUTH_HTTPS_REQUIRED` error with actionable localized guidance instead of the generic invalid-credentials message.
- Keep the check scoped to Notion; loopback HTTP and all other connectors retain their existing behavior.

## Root cause

The OAuth callback is derived from `request.base_url`. When Octop is accessed through a public HTTP address, Notion rejects dynamic client registration because non-loopback Notion callback URLs must use HTTPS. The existing error path then presents the generic connector credentials message.

## Impact

Only Notion OAuth on a public HTTP address receives the new error. No Docker, configuration, callback construction, or MCP transport behavior is changed.

## Validation

- `make lint`
- Focused pytest suite: 21 passed
- The integration test verifies that Notion OAuth is not started for a public HTTP callback and that the dedicated error code is returned

author: lmeyerov
body:
**Stacked on #1746** — review that one first; this PR's diff is only the chain half.

## What this fixes

#1741: on the polars engine, `MATCH (a {id: 'p0'})-[*1..2]-(b) RETURN b` returned `{p0, p1, p2}` where pandas returns `{p1, p2}`. **Silently wrong rows, not an error.** After this PR both engines return `{p1, p2}`.

## Root cause (corrected — the original write-up was wrong)

The first diagnosis said "polars lacks pandas' backtrack avoidance". Direct A/B refutes that: both engines return **identical node sets** and **identical final `_nodes`**; only the alias flag diverges.

The actual pandas rule is a **hop-distance gate** (`compute/chain.py` ~456-501): a node named after an edge op is aliased only when `min_hop <= hop <= max_hop`. The seed's hop label is null under an undirected walk, so it fails the gate and loses the alias. polars had no hop labels at all, so it could not run the gate — #1746 adds the labels, this PR adds the gate.

## Implementation

- **Auto-inject** `label_node_hops` whenever an edge op is variable-length or output-sliced, mirroring `ast.py:621-625` `needs_auto_labels`.
- **Gate** the alias by semi-joining against the `[min_hop, max_hop]` window in `_apply_node_names`.
- The hop distance travels *with the wavefront*, so it lands on the **named node step's own frame**, not the preceding edge step's. The gate reads it there. (This cost a debugging round — worth knowing if you touch it.)
- Also corrects the label rule under `return_as_wave_front` — the mode the chain *always* hops in. `visited_nodes` starts empty there, but pandas labels a backtracked-to seed null in **both** modes, so the undirected label-seen set is now pre-seeded with the seeds unconditionally.

## Verification

- **4892 passed** across `graphistry/tests/compute/gfql` + `test_compute_hops.py` + `test_compute_chain.py`.
- The 59 failures in that selection are **byte-identical to `origin/master`'s** on the same environment (temporal / cudf / viz) — I ran the same selection on a detached master worktree and diffed the failure lists: **zero new failures**.
- 8 new tests pin the gate: pandas-parity across four varlen patterns, the backtracked seed explicitly, a negative case proving fixed-length hops are *not* gated, and a no-leak check on the injected column.

## Residual gap (kept on #1741)

`min_hops > 1` chains get no gate — requesting labels there would turn a currently-native chain into an NIE, since those labels come from the layered backward walk (`hop.py:676-778`), which is not yet ported.

## Follow-up

Once this lands, **#1742 closes unmerged** — it was the interim honest-NIE decline for exactly this shape, and a raise is the wrong end state (per review feedback). Its test flips from "raises" to "matches the pandas oracle".

body:
**Tranche 5** of the AWS-conformance + capability-completion program (spec #77).

riz already walks the live function route table to build the MCP tool list. The **same walk** now emits an OpenAPI 3.1 document — one operation per declared route, path params typed from the route template, query params + request body from `[function.X.mcp]`. Every function is simultaneously an MCP tool at `/_riz/mcp` **and** an OpenAPI operation, both from one table, both served as routes. No annotations, no separate spec file to drift.

### Design
- `src/system/openapi.rs`: a pure `build_document()` over `OperationSource`, testable without a live `RizState`. `ANY` expands to the standard method set (OpenAPI has no "any" operation); `operationId`s are globally unique without a numeric-suffix loop. **OpenAPI 3.1 aligns with JSON Schema 2020-12**, so `mcp.body` transfers verbatim. **No new deps.**
- Served public at `GET /openapi.json` in `build_app` (like `/health` + the agent card), and added to the `system_surface` source-of-truth table so it appears in `riz routes` and `/_riz/registry`.

### Tests
- Unit: path-param / query / body mapping; `ANY` expansion + unique `operationId`s; greedy path params
- Live: boots riz, fetches `/openapi.json`, asserts `3.1.0` + a typed path parameter

body:
## Summary

The full-screen commentable-html demo reports on the site showed the browser's generic globe
favicon instead of the CMH pink chat-bubble mark. The affected demos were `report-taxi.html`
("NYC Taxi 2014 Report") and `report-community-garden.html` ("Planning a Community Garden").

Root cause: the CMH template shell bakes a `<link rel="icon" ...>` data-URI favicon into the head,
so documents built from the shell get it. But those two example SOURCES
(`dev/examples/src/report-taxi.html`, `report-community-garden.html`) are full standalone documents
authored before the favicon was added and carry their own `<head>` with no favicon. The build
assembles them as-is, so the shipped reports and the synced site demos lacked it. The other five
examples already had it.

This PR:

- Adds the CMH favicon to the two example sources, so the rebuilt `examples/report-*.html` and the
  synced `site/dist/commentable-html/demo/report-*.html` now show the CMH mark.
- Enforces it so it cannot regress: the validator now warns (an error under `--strict`, the
  mandatory finalize path) when a document has no `<link rel="icon">` favicon with a non-empty
  `href` in its head (`CMH-KIND-05`). A legacy `rel="shortcut icon"` counts; an empty `href` does not.
- Makes the tooling guarantee it: `retrofit.py` injects the CMH favicon into a favicon-less host
  head, and `upgrade.py` adds it when migrating a pre-favicon document. Neither duplicates an
  existing icon link.

## Type

- [x] Improvement or fix to an existing plugin
- [ ] New plugin (maintainer only)
- [ ] Docs or repo tooling

## Multi-duck review (required)

- [x] Multi-Duck passed (2 rounds of multi-duck review)
- [ ] Multi-Duck opted out - reason: <a real, specific reason>

## Checklist

- [x] New or changed feature/behavior has a matching feature-id row in the owning spec and a covering automated test named in that row (`CMH-KIND-05`; `tests/test_validate_kind.py` `FaviconTests`, `tests/test_retrofit.py`, `tests/test_upgrade.py`)
- [x] Version bumped per CONTRIBUTING when a published plugin changed (1.185.0 -> 1.187.0 in `plugin.json`, both `.claude-plugin` copies, and both manifests)
- [x] The changed plugin's `CHANGELOG.md` updated when its version changed
- [x] `python scripts/validate_marketplace.py` passes locally
- [x] `python scripts/validate_markdown.py` passes locally

## Notes

The favicon is head-only and invisible in a body screenshot, so the tutorial screenshots are
unchanged (a spurious Windows-vs-Linux font-metric checklist-shot regeneration was reverted to the
CI-validated Linux shot). All generated artifacts were rebuilt with `scripts/rebuild_all.py` and the
`build.py --check --check-fixtures`, `build_spec.py --check`, and `build_site_data.py --check` drift
guards pass.

### Multi-duck review

Two rounds ran across Anthropic (Opus 4.8/4.7, Sonnet 5), OpenAI (GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-5.3-Codex, GPT-5.4),
Google (Gemini 3.1 Pro), and Microsoft MAI models. Round 1 (8 ducks, prisms) found and I fixed: a
detection inconsistency (retrofit/upgrade over-matched `apple-touch-icon` and ignored empty `href`,
diverging from the validator), the validator capturing icon links document-wide (body-only favicon
suppressed the warning), and an editing slip that had orphaned `test_nonportable_asset_options_match_new_document`.
Round 2 (6 ducks, consensus) found and I fixed: `data-rel`/`data-href` being misread as `rel`/`href`,
the regex scanning inside `<script>`/`<style>` text, an empirically-verified O(n^2) blowup on
adversarial input, and an implicit-`<body>` head-scope gap - all resolved by rewriting the shared
detection on `html.parser.HTMLParser` (matching the validator) and giving the validator parser the same
robust head-scope. Security duck (Sonnet 5) confirmed no ReDoS/XSS/CSP issue remains.

Closes #518

author: fbaensch-beilstein
body:
## Summary

Improves Markush R-group extraction end-to-end: definition parsing, scaffold scoping, structural alt-group support, positional tuple tables, and coordinates on enumerated structures.

## What changed

- **Scaffold-scoped definitions** — R-group definitions are now resolved per scaffold (nearest block per label) instead of a page-flat `putIfAbsent` map that silently dropped duplicate labels. Multiple scaffolds on one page that reuse the same label (e.g. `m48800432-2` has two distinct `R` legends, 8 vs 6 values) now each get their own definition. New `RGroupDefinitionBlock` carries each text node's definitions + position.
- **Hardened text parsing** — handles multiple `label =` per node, `;` separators, chained `R1 = R2 = H`, scheme-number stripping (`13:`), trailing-annotation stripping (`H Keq 1` → `H`), and soft-wrapped continuation value lines.
- **Structural `NamedAlternativeGroup` support** — new `AltGroupVisitor` collects `CDAltGroup`s via the previously-unused `visitNamedAlternativeGroup` hook; `SubstanceXtractor.resolveAltGroupDefinitions` converts each alternative fragment to a substituent SMILES and injects it into the handler.
- **Positional tuple tables** — correlated `R1/R2` rows (`R1=H,R2=H` / `R1=F,R2=H` / `R1=H,R2=F`) enumerate as their explicit rows instead of the cartesian product, eliminating spurious combinations (e.g. the invented `R1=F,R2=F`). New `CorrelatedGroup`.
- **Coordinates on grafted atoms** — substituents parsed from SMILES carry no coordinates; enumerated structures are now laid out via `AbbreviationLayout` (scaffold held fixed), so they no longer contain null-coordinate atoms.

## Tests

New `TextVisitorTest`, `MarkushHandlerTest`, `MarkushBugTest` plus fixtures under `src/test/resources/cheminf/bugs/markush/`. Full suite green; Spotless clean.

## Notes

- The `.gitignore` change present in the working tree is unrelated and intentionally left out of this branch.
- Known follow-ups (not in scope): missing common abbreviations (`Me`, ...) in `lookups/*.smi`; pairing the `expandedRGroups` fallback with InChI-tolerance for unresolved-R structures.
