author: jsl124
body:
Supersedes the branch's original scope (min-runs enforcement + admin recalculation), which is still included in the earlier commits.

## Premium parity

Premium exclusion was not an isolated leaderboard decision: `premiumEarnsXp: false` awarded premium runners 0 XP, so their level, division and leaderboard score froze on upgrade, and `excludePremium: true` then hid that permanent zero behind "Monthly ranking is not available for this account yet."

The PDD requires that Premium confer no competitive **advantage**, not that Premium Users are barred from progression. Both defaults flip, and the hard-coded `isPremium` branches now defer to config — including `completeCoolDown`, which ignored the config plane entirely. Both suppression and exclusion remain supported configurations.

## Streak milestone bonus

`config/progression.streakRewards` was stored and validated but never paid out. It is now resolved on the crossing run, exempt from the per-activity cap but clamped by remaining daily room, paying only the highest milestone when several are crossed at once.

## Fixes found by adversarial review of this PR

- **Milestone bonuses could be farmed indefinitely.** `previousStreak` is derived from plan-bounded history, and `generatedPlans/{uid}.createdAt` is owner-writable — resetting it collapsed the baseline and made every milestone re-earnable, with the minted XP flowing into leaderboard standings. Now gated on a `highestPaidStreakMilestoneDays` high-water mark, protected as a backend-owned key.
- **Stale `ineligible_premium` current views.** Owners with no contribution this period were never re-planned, so the freed premium accounts kept seeing the old message indefinitely. Views are now re-evaluated on every run.
- **Config drift check crashed hosted CI.** It read the `website/` mirror unconditionally; that is a separate repository absent from this checkout. It now skips loudly.

## Evidence

- `npm test` **294/294**, 0 fail
- `npm run test:feed` 41/42 — the failure is the pre-existing stale `feedCallableSurface` export-surface assertion, untouched by this PR
- Governance CI green

## Known follow-ups (not addressed here)

- `streakRewards` 14-day (220) and 30-day (600) exceed the 200 daily cap and can never pay in full; config validation does not warn. Needs a balance decision.
- `qualifyingRunCount` is not written on zero-XP runs, so it can under-count.
- `premiumEarnsXp` / `excludePremium` are not type-validated; a stored `"false"` string silently inverts them.

author: reidmorrison
body:
Burns down two of the known tech-debt items, targeted at the 5.1 line.

## Deprecations (warn now, remove in v6)

Each emits a Ruby deprecation warning via `Kernel.warn(category: :deprecated)`, so it is **silent by default** and shown when deprecation warnings are enabled (e.g. `ruby -W:deprecated`, or Rails development mode).

- **`:sentry`** appender (`Appender::Sentry`, backed by the end-of-life `sentry-raven` gem) → use `:sentry_ruby`.
- **`:new_relic`** appender (`Appender::NewRelic`, error events via `newrelic_rpm`) → use `:new_relic_logs`.
- **`type:`** on the Elasticsearch/OpenSearch appenders (`:elasticsearch`, `:elasticsearch_http`, `:opensearch`).

### `type:` is now fully inert

Document `_type` has been unused since Elasticsearch 7, so `type:` is now ignored on **all** server versions:

- the bulk appenders no longer send a `_type` in the bulk index metadata;
- `version_supports_type?` (and its ES-client-version override) is removed;
- the HTTP appender posts to the typeless `POST /{index}-DATE/_doc` endpoint instead of the old `/{index}-DATE/{type}` (which defaulted to `/log` and stopped working on ES 7+).

The `type:` keyword remains only to emit the deprecation warning.

> Note: bare `warn` inside a `Subscriber` resolves to `Base#warn` (a log-level method), so the appenders call `Kernel.warn` explicitly.

## Test consolidation

Folds the batch-mode tests into `async_test.rb` as a nested `"batch mode"` describe and deletes `async_batch_test.rb`, whose name referenced the `Appender::AsyncBatch` class removed in v5.

## Docs / CHANGELOG

`docs/appenders.md` Sentry + New Relic sections gained deprecation notes; the 5.1.0 CHANGELOG entry gained a `### Deprecated` section; `docs/llms-full.txt` regenerated.

## Testing

Full suite green: `1431 tests, 0 failures` (10 MongoDB skips), RSpec 22/22, rubocop clean.

author: tada5hi
body:
Implements #797.

## Summary

The simple dialect's filter wire grammar (`filter[age]=>=18`, `filter[name]=~oh~`, `filter[id]=!1,2`) was spelled three times by hand — the decode if-cascade in parser-simple's `value.ts`, the 15-case encode switch in codec-url's simple `FiltersVisitor`, and the template-literal input union in `types.ts`. This PR collapses all three into one declarative table in a new `parser-simple/src/parameter/filters/wire/` module.

### The table + complement derivation

`FILTER_WIRE_SPEC` holds **8 rows, one per positive marker operator** (declared order = decode precedence). Negation twins are not rows: they derive from the `complementOf` relation in core's `FILTER_OPERATOR_SEMANTICS` (#792), so the wire table repeats nothing and the frozen `'!<5'` → `lt 5` quirk falls out by construction (the ordering family has no complements). `in`/`nin` stay a value *shape* (comma list through the `eq` spelling), not a marker.

### Per-caller contracts

- `decodeFilterWireValue(input)` returns a verdict (`{ success: true, condition } | { success: false, code }`) — the parser applies the schema drop-vs-throw policy and nothing else. The empty-value post-check that previously lived inside `SimpleFiltersParser` (`''`, `'!'`, `'<='`, `'~~'` decode to empty conditions) is absorbed as the `valueEmpty` verdict — the last piece of wire knowledge leaves the parser.
- `encodeFilterWireValue(condition)` throws typed `AdapterError`s (subset law is unconditional) and **self-verifies every emitted token by re-decoding it** through the same table. The grammar has no escaping, so collisions are value-content-induced (`eq 'foo~'` would re-decode as `startsWith 'foo'`) — per the RFC, the round-trip check survives *inside* the codec instead of dying, but it disappears from codec-url and from the public API.

### Derived typed input (fixes a live drift bug)

The `parseTyped` input union is now computed from the table's literal `prefix`/`suffix` types plus the complement relation. The hand-written union had **drifted**: it only contained prefix forms, so the runtime-accepted `` `${V}~` `` (startsWith), `` `~${V}~` `` (contains) and their `!` forms were type errors. The derived union is exactly legacy + those 4 members — a compile-time-only widening. Compile-time `Equals` pins (`wire/checks.ts`, checked by `build:types`, not exported from the barrel) freeze the derived types against table or core-semantics changes.

### Export changes (pre-GA)

| Symbol | Fate |
|---|---|
| `parseFilterScalar` | unchanged, re-homed to `wire/scalar.ts` — dialect-shared scalar vocabulary (parser-expression + expression encoder untouched) |
| `parseFilterValue`, `serializeFilterValue` | internalized |
| `parseFilterWireValue` | replaced by `decodeFilterWireValue` |
| `URLFilterOperator` enum | deleted — marker chars now exist once, in the table |
| new | `FILTER_WIRE_SPEC`, `FILTER_WIRE_NEGATION`, `decodeFilterWireValue`, `encodeFilterWireValue`, `FilterWireDecodeFailure` + wire types |

codec-url's simple encoder shrinks by ~130 lines and keeps only the structural subset law (flat root-AND, one condition per field); its imports drop to `encodeFilterWireValue`.

## Acceptance gate (wire frozen byte-for-byte)

- **Every pre-existing spec passes with zero assertion changes**: parser-simple 126, codec-url 234, full `nx run-many -t test` green across all 8 test projects (uncached).
- New boundary spec `filters-wire.spec.ts` (65 cases): the grammar's first direct token↔condition coverage, pinning the frozen quirks (`'!<5'` → `lt 5`, `'~'` → `contains '~'`, `'~5~'` → `contains '5'` raw, `','` → `in []`, markers inert inside lists) plus two agreement probes — every row decodes back to its own operator (order = precedence, no shadowing) and every wire-expressible complement twin spells as `'!'` + its positive form, matched against `FILTER_OPERATOR_SEMANTICS`.
- Type-check cost of the derivation on parser-simple (`tsc --extendedDiagnostics`): Types 4180 → 4554, Instantiations 6780 → 7590, check time 0.09s → 0.11s.

## Out of scope (flagged in #797)

A real boolean through `parseTyped` throws in value normalization and the condition is dropped, although the input type advertises booleans — pre-existing, wire-frozen; separate issue to follow.

author: imrohitagrawal
body:
Closes #200.

`_env_guard.sh` did not check `CITEVYN_DEMO_API_KEY`, so an operator who copied `prod.env.example` and skipped the field passed the guard, `deploy.sh` proceeded, and the api died at boot on a pydantic error **after** the 60s health poll had burned — reporting only `api health=unknown`.

Adding the check turned out to be the easy part. Review found four ways the first attempt was bypassable or actively harmful; all are fixed here, each reproduced before being fixed.

## 1. HIGH — forcing a strong key broke the browser demo, behind a green gate

`frontend/src/lib/api.ts:48` bakes `VITE_API_DEMO_KEY ?? "local-demo-key"` in at **build** time and nothing passed that build arg.

It is worse than the issue described: **the prod stack serves no frontend at all.** There is no frontend service, no frontend Dockerfile and no `file_server` — `Caddyfile` proxies every path to `api:8000`. The bundle is built out of band by `make demo-frontend`, so nothing in the deploy path ever looks at it. Every browser request would 401 while `deploy-verify` stayed green, because it curls with the key straight out of `.env`.

Fixed in two halves, because either alone is a trap:
- `make demo-frontend` threads `CITEVYN_DEMO_API_KEY` from `infra/docker/.env` into the Vite build (quote/whitespace-normalised the same way `read_env` does).
- `deploy_verify.sh` **fails** when `frontend/dist` has the default baked in while `.env` carries a different key. A gate that cannot see the artifact it is gating is not a gate.

## 2. HIGH — `_strip` peeled only the trailing end

The Python predicate it mirrors is `value.strip()` (`config.py:54-55`) — symmetric. Reproduced: `CITEVYN_DEMO_API_KEY="  local-demo-key"` is 16 chars with two leading spaces, so it is neither `== 'local-demo-key'` nor `< 16`. It **passed the guard and then crash-looped the api** on the exact check the guard exists to pre-empt. The asymmetry fed six other fields too.

## 3. HIGH — `CITEVYN_ADMIN_API_KEY` had the identical gap

It was only ever compared against the Makefile bootstrap stub, so empty, absent, and the **published** code default `local-admin-key` (`config.py:71`) all passed — and that is the key that promotes an index and reads the budget. Both keys now go through one `_assert_strong_key` helper.

The suite's own accept-fixture used `realadminkey` — 12 chars, which the app **rejects**. The fixtures encoded an invalid production value.

## 4. MEDIUM — the test suite inherited the caller's environment

A case that deliberately omits a key read the operator's exported value instead of empty. Reproduced: `32 passed` clean, `31 passed / 1 failed` with `CITEVYN_DEMO_API_KEY` exported. `deploy_verify.sh` documents exporting it as a supported workflow and this suite now runs in CI, so that is a red build that is not a regression. `assert_guard` now scrubs `CITEVYN_*`/`POSTGRES_*` in the child using bash-3.2-safe prefix expansion — not `env -i`, which drops `PATH` and breaks the guard's own `grep`/`tr`/`chmod`.

## 5. LOW — the compose comment omitted `backup`

It is profile-gated and easy to miss, but it receives the whole `.env` and runs a shell in a postgres image with a host bind-mount.

## Also: the template could not pass its own guard

`prod.env.example` shipped `CITEVYN_LLM_PROVIDER=stub`, which the guard rejects outright — so a literal `cp prod.env.example .env` could not pass even after every blank was filled in. Now empty. Its `Required:` block listed 3 of the 7 fields the guard demands and never mentioned the 16-char floor. Added `CITEVYN_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` too: the code default is `('http://localhost:3000',)`, so a bundle served from the public host is CORS-blocked even with a correct key.

## Verification

- `tests/shell/test_env_guard.sh`: **40 passed** (was 32). 8 new cases — leading whitespace on both the default and length branches, and the admin key's empty / absent / published-default / case-variant / 15-char / 16-char boundary.
- **Mutations**, each confirmed applied by inspection before the result was believed: reverting `_strip` to trailing-only kills 2 cases; removing the admin check kills 5.
- The env-scrub fix verified by re-running the whole suite with both keys exported: **40/0**.
- `docker compose --profile prod config` still valid; `make -n demo-frontend` parses.

## Risk / rollback

Ops config, one Makefile recipe and the env guard — no backend or frontend source change. The guard is strictly more restrictive, so the failure mode of a mistake is a refused deploy, not a silent bad one. Note for the operator: **this makes a previously-passing `.env` fail if the admin key is under 16 chars** — that is intended, since the app would reject it at boot anyway.

author: jonaslagoni
body:
## Summary

- Adds the **popup (vault) leg of the forward OAuth confirm grant handoff**: a COOP-free `GET /oauth/launch` landing page that receives a single-use **grant** from the widget over the still-alive `window.opener` link *at open time*, stores it in tab `sessionStorage`, and navigates to the provider's authorize URL.
- Makes `oauth/callback` **self-confirm in-tab** with `{ confirm_token, grant }` (unauthenticated — the grant is the auth) after the provider round-trip, so no backwards `postMessage` to `window.opener` is needed. This fixes embedded connections sticking at `pending_confirmation` when Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy (COOP) severs `window.opener` during the provider's navigation chain.
- Keeps the legacy `oauth_complete` opener relay fully armed as the fallback rung with its gate **unchanged**, so the change is additive and safe for older widgets and for a unify rollback.

**Related Issue**: [GH-9546](https://github.com/apideck-io/unify/issues/9546)

## What changed

### New popup landing page (`/oauth/launch`)
A bare, COOP-free page (modeled on `callback.tsx`, no `Layout`) that the widget opens while the `window.opener` link is still alive:

- **Anti-phishing gate (pre-consent)**: if `window.opener` is null **or** a `sessionStorage` write-read probe fails, it renders a loud error and refuses **before** posting ready or navigating.
- Otherwise it posts `oauth_launch_ready` to the opener every 250 ms until answered.
- On an `oauth_launch_start` message **from the opener** (`event.source === window.opener`), it stores the grant under `apideck_oauth_grant_${serviceId}`, stops repeating, removes the listener, and `window.location.assign(authorizeUrl)`.
- **Source-identity check only** — no `event.origin` check or origin allowlist (honors the recorded "do not touch origin" constraint).

### Callback in-tab grant self-confirm (`/oauth/callback`)
A new grant self-confirm rung is added **ahead of** the legacy relay, with the legacy ladder preserved byte-for-byte:

1. **Grant self-confirm (new, nonce-independent)**: read + clear the grant for the hash `service_id`; if a grant is present with `confirm_token` + `service_id` + `unified_api`, POST `{ confirm_token, grant }` unauthenticated and close. On any failure it falls through to the legacy ladder (the grant attempt `return`s on success; its `catch` falls into the same synchronous fallback ladder the no-grant path reaches).
2. **Legacy opener relay (unchanged)**: `oauth_complete` when `nonce && confirm_token && service_id && window.opener` — gate **not** widened, still requires `nonce`.
3. **Error relay / in-page server error (unchanged)**.
4. **Null-opener strand (the one legacy behavior change)**: a success-shaped hash (`nonce && confirm_token && service_id`) with no opener now renders a **loud in-page error** instead of the old silent `window.close()`. Any hash lacking `nonce` still closes silently.

### New utility module (`src/utils/oauthGrantHandoff.ts`)
Pure, parameter-object functions next to `oauthCsrf.ts` (no React context):
- `storeGrant(serviceId, grant)` / `readAndClearGrant(serviceId)` — sessionStorage-backed, **single-use** (read + remove in one step).
- `probeSessionStorage()` — write-read-remove round-trip; `false` on mismatch or any thrown error.
- `confirmWithGrant({ unifiedApi, serviceId, confirmToken, grant })` — POSTs `{ confirm_token, grant }` to `/vault/connections/{unifiedApi}/{serviceId}/confirm` with **no** `Authorization` / `X-APIDECK-APP-ID` / `X-APIDECK-CONSUMER-ID` headers (contrast the JWT-authenticated `callConfirmEndpoint`).

### New wire-protocol types (`src/types/OAuthGrantHandoff.ts`)
`LaunchReadyMessage` / `LaunchStartMessage` (mirrors vault-core's exported contract; vault-core is the source of truth) and `IGrantConfirmResponse` (aliases the existing `IConfirmResponse` to avoid drift).

### Security invariants (grep-verified in CI-style checks)
- The grant **never appears in any URL** — it travels only over the live opener `postMessage` handshake and then only through tab `sessionStorage`. The launch URL carries only the non-secret `service_id`.
- **COOP is not introduced** anywhere (`next.config.js` unchanged).
- **No `event.origin` check / origin allowlist** is added.

## How has this been tested?

**80 tests passing across 10 test suites** (up from 47/7). TDD red-green per component — every new branch/timeout/error/fallback has a named test.

- **`oauthGrantHandoff.test.ts`** (11 tests): `storeGrant` (key format / no collision), `readAndClearGrant` (read / single-use removal / missing), `probeSessionStorage` (success / throw / no residue), `confirmWithGrant` (unauthenticated POST shape / returns data / propagates error).
- **`launch.test.tsx`** (9 tests): ready post + 250 ms repeat; loud error on null opener; loud error on storage-probe failure; grant store + `assign(authorizeUrl)` on valid start; repeat stops after start; foreign-`event.source` ignored; wrong `data.type` ignored; interval + listener cleaned up on unmount.
- **`callback.test.tsx`** (17 tests, extended): grant self-confirm POST + close; single-use grant removal before POST resolves; no double-confirm when self-confirm succeeds; fallback to legacy relay on POST reject; fallback when no grant; fallback when `unified_api` absent; loud error on success-shaped/no-grant/no-opener; **silent close preserved for a no-`nonce` hash (legacy gate not widened)**; plus all preserved legacy behaviors.

Verification results:
- [x] `yarn test` — 80 tests passing (10 suites)
- [x] `yarn typecheck` — clean
- [x] `yarn lint` — clean
- [x] Grant never URL-carried — `grep -rn "grant" src/ | grep -iE "searchParams|\?grant|&grant"` returns empty
- [x] COOP never introduced — `grep -rin "opener-policy|embedder-policy|content-security-policy" next.config.js src/` returns empty
- [x] No `event.origin` check — `grep -rn "event.origin|\.origin ===" src/pages/oauth/ src/utils/oauthGrantHandoff.ts` returns empty
- [ ] Manual `dev` matrix: (a) launch page with a stub opener answering `oauth_launch_start` → grant stored, tab navigates; (b) callback with seeded grant + `unified_api` hash → self-confirm POST fires; (c) callback with no grant but an opener → legacy `oauth_complete` still posts; (d) callback success-shaped, no grant, no opener → loud error
- [ ] Manual: opening `/oauth/launch?service_id=x` directly (no opener) shows the loud error and never navigates
- [ ] Cross-browser spot check (Chrome, Firefox, Safari) once the vault-core widget + unify legs exist

## Deployment & rollout notes

**Deployment order is load-bearing**: unify (grant mint + `/confirm` accepting `{ confirm_token, grant }` + `unified_api` in the callback fragment) → **this vault leg** → vault-core widget release.

This leg is **safe to ship early**: with no vault-core widget opening the launch URL, `/oauth/launch` is simply never reached, and the callback self-confirm degrades to the legacy opener relay whenever a grant or `unified_api` is absent. A unify rollback degrades the callback to the legacy relay per attempt. No stored client state persists across sessions (the grant is single-use and session-scoped).

**Sole legacy-path behavior change**: the null-opener success-shaped strand (silent close → loud error).

## Changelog

Added a COOP-free `/oauth/launch` popup landing page and in-tab grant self-confirm in `/oauth/callback` so embedded OAuth connections no longer stick at `pending_confirmation` when COOP severs `window.opener`. The legacy opener relay remains as a fallback.

author: ro80t
body:
## Summary
- Removed the standalone `container` job in `ci.yml`. It only built and started the docker-compose container as a bare fail-fast check, but `typecheck` (the job it gated via `needs`) already does exactly that as its own first two steps. Every PR paid for a full extra sequential build-and-start round trip with no unique verification value; `typecheck` now runs directly and still fails just as fast if the image can't build.
- Fixed the `devcontainer` job's Docker layer cache so it actually works. `cacheFrom` pointed at a `ghcr.io` image tag that was never pushed (`push` was hardcoded to `never`), so this job was always a full cold build on every run. Now the image is pushed on pushes to `main`/`release-*` branches, so PR runs of this job can pull warm layers instead of rebuilding from scratch.
- Added a turbo cache directory (`.cache/turbo`, alongside the existing `.cache/bun/install` pattern) and persisted it via `actions/cache` in the shared `Setup Container` composite action. `turbo.json` already leaves the `typecheck`/`lint` tasks cacheable (only `build`/`test`/`setup` have `cache: false`, left untouched since that looks like a deliberate choice), but the cache directory lived inside the `node_modules` docker named volume, which doesn't survive past a single job's container — so the cache was built and then immediately discarded every run. Verified locally in the devcontainer: `typecheck` went from ~57s to ~1.3s and `lint` from ~65s to ~1.3s on a warm cache.

## Test plan
- [x] `bun run lint` (all packages, cold and warm cache)
- [x] `bun run typecheck` (all packages, cold and warm cache)
- [x] Confirm on an actual PR run that `typecheck` still gates `build`/`lint`/`test` correctly with `container` removed
- [x] Confirm a push to `main` successfully pushes the devcontainer image to `ghcr.io`, and that a subsequent PR's `devcontainer` job pulls cached layers from it

Live: `idrun_b00209b6f66d` — `matchMode=channel-review-id`, `matchCount=1`, `matchedSource=visible-text`, `outline=outlined`, `operatorConfirmed=true`. Read-only throughout: nothing clicked, navigated, typed, pasted, opened, or submitted.

## The interesting part: the first run failed, honestly

`idrun_34686ac82c82` returned `ZERO_MATCH` over 13 rows with an untruncated scan — while the id was **present in the review-list network response**. The runtime reported that split rather than calling a payload match a row match, and refused to fall back to the calibrated flow.

The product owner then pointed out the list scrolls horizontally and the `리뷰글번호` column sits off to the right. It was a **rendering** problem, not an exposure problem: those cells were not in the DOM. The 6-of-13 visible-token count was the tell.

Both runs are kept. The negative is the evidence that makes the positive precise ([D-036](../blob/feat/naver-review-id-reconciliation/docs/action-window-runtime/decisions.md)).

## What changed as a result

- **In-session rescan** — a miss no longer ends the run; the operator adjusts the view, the runtime re-reads (bounded). The runtime still never scrolls or clicks.
- **Exclusive-ancestor scope** — the scan widens from the innermost row container to the outermost ancestor containing *that row and no other*, so a wrapper-borne id is attributed to exactly one row and cannot create a second claimant.
- **Truncation is reported** — `rowsTruncated` / `tokensTruncated` surface in the output and the record, and the "this surface does not expose the id" wording is suppressed whenever a cap bit.

## The pieces

- **`review-id-fingerprint/v1`** — new contract, three ports (Node / in-page `crypto.subtle` / Java), ASCII-only golden vectors with a padded case for **all 25 pinned whitespace code points**. Documented honestly as leak hygiene, not privacy: a 10-digit id space is enumerable.
- **The trace, proven by execution** — real parse→map chain over synthetic NAVER-shaped bytes: `리뷰글번호` → `CanonicalReview.externalId` → `reviews.external_id`, character-for-character.
- **The locator** — keyed by `(channel, sellerAccountId, channelReviewId)`. Cardinality is computed across **all rungs at once**; rung order only names the source of the surviving row.
- **The ladder** — visible text → anchor href → input value → `data-*` → page state, all fingerprinted in-page. Page-state and network rungs are **presence evidence only** (they cannot attribute a row) and are never fed to the locator.
- **Its own weakest-in-the-runtime approval flag** — a *mutating* flag is a **refusal**, not a stronger grant.

## Non-claims

- **NOT** a verified seller-account binding — the account comes from the request bundle and the session's account is never read back. The record says so in its own field (`sellerAccountBinding`). **Review identity only.**
- **NOT** a claim the id is always reachable — it is reachable *where the column has rendered*.
- **NOT** reply/composer/submission progress; nothing minted or posted. B1 stays `[EXT]`. One target, one account, one channel.
- `상품주문번호` deliberately **not** used as a key: not the imported identity, and classified High sensitivity.

## Verification

Collector typecheck clean · suite **4089 passed / 61 skipped** · browser rung green (cross-port parity, exact/duplicate/zero/secondary-mismatch, wrapper-borne id, hostile `href`, DOM byte-identical after teardown) · backend `./gradlew test` BUILD SUCCESSFUL · `git diff --check` clean · `package.json`/`package-lock.json` untouched.

**Independent read-only review before the live runs: 1 HIGH + 8 MEDIUM.** All fixed and **mutation-tested** (revert each fix → tests fail). The HIGH was a rung-first search that could report `matchCount: 1` while two rows genuinely carried the identity — a defect one of my own tests had asserted as correct.

author: accuser
body:
An accessibility and UX review of all six screens turned up a set of issues ranging from a page that renders blank to text failing WCAG AA contrast. This addresses all of them.

## The three biggest

**Navigation was buttons, not links.** The header nav, KSB rows, back links, Edit and Add evidence all called `router.push` from a `<button>`. They couldn't be cmd/middle-clicked into a new tab, had no hover URL preview or "copy link", and screen readers announced them as buttons. The active tab was marked by tint alone.

They're `next/link` now with `aria-current="page"`. `HoverDiv` gained an `href` mode so a row renders as an `<a>` when it navigates and stays a `<button>` when it acts in place. Three router actions this made redundant are gone, and the "Repository folder" card is a deep link (`/repository?open=K1`) rather than set-state-then-navigate.

**A zero-result filter rendered a blank page.** Every category group filtered out and the page simply ended below the chips — reproducible with **In progress** + **Knowledge test**. The chip still read "In progress 2", so it looked broken. There's now a named empty state ("Nothing is both *in progress* and assessed by *knowledge test*") with a Clear filters action, plus a live region announcing the count. Group headers read "1 of 8 KSBs" when filtered instead of claiming the unfiltered total.

**Contrast failed AA widely.** `#a1a1aa` (2.56:1) was carrying real content — counts, helper text, empty states, table headers — across 33 uses.

| Before | Colour | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| 2.56:1 | `#a1a1aa` on white | counts, helper text, empty states |
| 1.48:1 | `#d4d4d8` | Coverage "—" cells |
| 4.40:1 | `#71717a` on `#f4f4f5` | inactive nav + role tabs |

An audit against the rendered DOM also caught three I'd missed by reading: `InlineCode` inheriting muted colour onto its own grey chip, the evidence-type description on the selected card's violet tint, and three `categoryMeta` colours at 3.5–4.0:1 on their own tints. All screens now pass, including the coach view.

## Also fixed

- **Coverage was a div grid** — six columns, a styled header row, no row/column association. Now a real `<table>` with `scope="col"`/`scope="row"`, an sr-only caption and a focusable scroll region.
- **`manifestWarning` was plumbed end to end and never rendered** — a repo whose `datafolio.yml` named an unusable standard silently got the default one with no explanation.
- **`state.loading` was only read by `KsbDetail`** — the other screens painted "0 of 19 approved" and an empty repo tree before data arrived, which reads as data loss.
- **The add-evidence form** — labels associated via `htmlFor` instead of duplicated `aria-label`; submit stays enabled and explains itself (`role="alert"` + `aria-invalid`) then moves focus to the field, since a disabled button with no stated reason can't even be tabbed to; the dropzone accepts drops as it appears to, with an `accept` filter, size hint and remove control; `reader.onerror` surfaces failures instead of silently doing nothing.
- Focus moves to the confirm button when Delete swaps it in (it was dropping to `<body>`), `tabIndex` on scroll containers, 24px tap targets on icon buttons, a skip link, `aria-pressed` on filter chips and the role toggle, and `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Font sizes are `rem`, so text respects the browser's font-size setting (verified: scales to 18.75px at a 125% setting), and the accidental 13.5/12.5/11.5px scale is normalised onto whole pixels.
- Dropped `motion` — a dependency with zero imports.

## Two notes for the reviewer

**A bug found along the way:** the file input was `display: none`, which removes it from the tab order — upload was completely keyboard-inaccessible. It's now visually hidden but focusable, with the label showing the focus ring via `:focus-within`.

**A correction to my own review:** I initially reported focus rings as missing. Tabbing through showed the browser default *was* present — the real problem was that it was undesigned amber, near-invisible on the indigo and near-black surfaces. There's a proper `:focus-visible` ring now, with a light variant for dark panels.

**Not done:** the shared primitives are still inline `style={{}}`, so `HoverDiv` still reimplements `:hover` in React state and dark mode remains out of reach. That's a refactor rather than a fix, so I left it out of this PR.

## Verification

`tsc --noEmit`, `eslint` and all seven test suites pass. Every flow driven in the browser end to end with no console errors; contrast audited against the rendered DOM per screen; mobile checked at 375px (page doesn't scroll sideways, the table pans in its own container).

author: orchestra-agent-app[bot]
body:
## Summary

For a field extension `K/k` and `t : K` transcendental over `k`, the affine-chart evaluation `Belyi.P1.awayEval k t : (k[X₀,X₁]_{X₁})₀ →+* K` (which sends the affine coordinate `X₀/X₁` to `t`) is **injective**, so its kernel is `⊥`.

New file `Belyi/P1/ChartInjective.lean`:

* `Belyi.P1.aeval_isHomogeneous_eq_zero_of_transcendental` — a homogeneous polynomial killed by `aeval ![t,1]` (for transcendental `t`) is zero;
* `Belyi.P1.awayEval_injective` — `awayEval k t` is injective;
* `Belyi.P1.ker_awayEval` — `RingHom.ker (awayEval k t) = ⊥`.

## Why this matters (context in #46)

The existing `Belyi.P1.not_isClosed_singleton_point_of_transcendental` (`Belyi/P1/Transcendental.lean`) shows the image prime `ker (awayEval k t)` is *not maximal* — enough for the finite-fibers / quasi-finiteness half of B1. This PR upgrades that to `ker = ⊥`, i.e. the point `Belyi.P1.point k t` attached to a transcendental element is the **generic point of the affine chart**. That is the algebraic core of the *dominance/surjectivity* half of B1's main theorem ("the induced morphism `X ⟶ ℙ¹` is finite **and surjective**").

## Method

Every chart element is `a / X₁ⁿ` with `a` homogeneous of degree `n`, evaluating to `aeval ![t,1] a` (`Belyi.P1.awayEval_mk`, `HomogeneousLocalization.Away.mk_surjective`). Evaluation at `(t,1)` factors as dehomogenisation `X₁ ↦ 1` into `k[X]` followed by `Polynomial.aeval t`; for transcendental `t` the latter is injective (`transcendental_iff_injective`), and a homogeneous polynomial is recovered from its dehomogenisation via `Polynomial.homogenize` (`Polynomial.homogenize_eq_of_isHomogeneous`), so `a = 0`.

## Follow-up left on #46 (surjectivity)

With `ker = ⊥` in hand, surjectivity of `Belyi.homOfFunctionField k X hX t` for transcendental `t` reduces to `IsDominant`, which is `DenseRange`, and (since `X` is irreducible with `homOfFunctionField_genericPoint`) to `closure {point k t (closedPoint)} = univ`. Via `ProjectiveSpectrum.zeroLocus_vanishingIdeal_eq_closure` + `vanishingIdeal_singleton` + `zeroLocus_bot` that is exactly `(point k t (closedPoint)).asHomogeneousIdeal = ⊥`, which this injectivity supplies at the level of homogeneous elements — the remaining step is the `Proj.awayι`↔homogeneous-ideal chart correspondence identifying the point's homogeneous ideal with `⊥`. Then `Surjective` is automatic (`IsFinite → IsIntegralHom → UniversallyClosed`, plus `IsDominant`, gives `Surjective.of_universallyClosed_of_isDominant`).

## Validation

Sorry-free; `./.orchestra/validation.sh` green (3088 jobs, `mk_all --check` clean, `lake build --wfail` clean). Imported into `Belyi.lean`.

author: takato7
body:
This PR adds support for a randomly generated card preset (`CardDeck`).

The card generation logic is as follows:

1. Each `CardValue` (number or operator) is assigned a weight based on the configuration (referred to as the base weight).
2. The weights are converted into probabilities in the range of 0 to 1 using the softmax function.
3. A `CardValue` is randomly selected according to the calculated probabilities, and its weight is reduced.
4. The reduction amount is calculated by multiplying its base weight by the reduction factor.
5. Steps 2–4 are repeated until the predetermined number of cards has been generated.

Cards are then dealt from the deck to the hand. When the deck runs out of cards, a new set of cards is generated and added to the deck.

Refactors:
- Introduce `CardManager` to coordinate interactions between `CardHand`, `CardSelection`, and `CardDeck`.
- Introduce `CombatManager` to handle validation, evaluation, and execution based on the selected cards.

author: rapidposeidon
body:
Companion docs PR to [RapidataAI/rapidata-evaluator#302](https://github.com/RapidataAI/rapidata-evaluator/pull/302), which adds explicit `rawWinner`/`rawWinnerIndex` and `weightedWinner`/`weightedWinnerIndex` to Compare/Ranking results.

## Why

Results exposed raw counts, weighted user-score sums, and both ratios, but only **one** generic `winner`/`winner_index` — which follows the **weighted** result. On close votes the raw-majority and weighted winners can differ, so a consumer could unintentionally read the weighted winner as a raw majority (reported from SDK integration, Compare task).

## What this PR does (docs only)

Updates `docs/understanding_the_results.md`:

- Documents `rawWinner`/`rawWinnerIndex` and `weightedWinner`/`weightedWinnerIndex` — both winners, their shared index space (`Both`/`Neither` as trailing indexes), and the **`null`-on-tie / no-clear-winner** behavior.
- Marks the generic `winner`/`winner_index` as **deprecated aliases** of the weighted fields. Because the result payload is a plain JSON dict there's no type-level deprecation hook, so docs are the deprecation channel (runtime typed accessors / warnings are the sibling *stabilize result schema + typed accessors* effort's job, reading these same field names).
- Clarifies how `summedUserScores` is summed (per-voter aggregated `userScore`) and how `summedUserScoresRatios` normalizes it.
- Adds the example fields + a note on the aggregator **version floor (4.1.0)** so readers know older result files fall back to `winner`/`winner_index`.

No SDK code changes here — the canonical fields are produced server-side by the evaluator (design decision: evaluator is the single source of truth).

```sql

update public.children set device_trust = 'ask' where device_trust = 'watch';

alter table public.device_requests drop constraint if exists device_requests_status_check;

drop policy if exists "kid_nudges_own" on public.kid_nudges;
create policy "kid_nudges_own" on public.kid_nudges
  for all using (auth.uid() = user_id) with check (auth.uid() = user_id);

create index if not exists kid_nudges_unseen_by_child
```

author: kalekoi
body:
## Purpose

Add a reproducible, fail-closed Task 12 contract for the final five-node PulseDAG v2.3.0 private-testnet rehearsal without claiming that the real rehearsal has already passed.

The live gate must run one exact candidate on separate hosts or genuinely isolated network namespaces, prove external-mining progress, exercise restart and bounded partition/rejoin, and emit a checksummed private-testnet `GO` or `NO-GO` evidence bundle.

## Changes

- Add a strict five-node inventory example with one seed, four ordinary nodes, loopback-only RPC, structured remote transports, an exact candidate SHA, bounded thresholds, and explicit isolate/restore argv hooks.
- Add `multi_host_rehearsal.py`, a standard-library controller that:
  - validates the inventory fail-closed;
  - verifies clean source checkouts at the exact candidate SHA;
  - runs Task 07 preflight and Task 09 lifecycle verification on every host;
  - starts the seed before ordinary nodes;
  - collects `/health`, `/status`, `/sync/status`, `/p2p/status`, and `/checks` through each host's loopback RPC;
  - requires healthy process/listener state, a successful consistency audit, and `overall_ok=true` node checks;
  - requires `libp2p-real`, fresh non-degraded P2P status, real-peer semantics, canonical `synced`/`steady` readiness, no selected-tip mismatch, zero replay gap, and bounded height spread;
  - treats the production `live_sync_error_active` field as the numeric counter exposed by the RPC contract;
  - allows the explicit zero-peer readiness exception only for the selected node during the bounded partition phase;
  - proves external-mining progress before and after fault injection;
  - exercises ordinary-node restart, bounded P2P isolation, exact restoration, rejoin, and convergence;
  - writes immutable JSON evidence, `GO`/`NO-GO`, and SHA-256 checksums;
  - rejects duplicate checksum paths and verifies that a `GO` bundle contains every mandatory phase and has not been modified.
- Add deterministic fake-transport regression coverage for the successful path, production RPC field types, health/check failures, readiness failures, invalid topology/RPC exposure, missing GO phases, duplicate checksum paths, and evidence tampering.
- Add a canonical Task 12 runbook with topology, access, fault-hook, evidence, GO, and NO-GO requirements.
- Add a dedicated Actions workflow:
  - ordinary PRs run the deterministic contract, syntax, inventory, English-comment, and repository-hygiene gates;
  - the real five-node rehearsal is manual, protected, self-hosted, exact-candidate pinned, and uploads evidence even on `NO-GO`;
  - the final live job passes only when the verified decision is `GO`.
- Mark Task 11 merged and Task 12 active in the v2.3.0 roadmap, while keeping Task 13 blocked on real verified Task 12 evidence and separate approval.
- Repair two stale v2.2.13 documentation links by pinning them to the immutable release tag.

## Validation

Repository validation on the current candidate includes:

- `python3 -m py_compile scripts/private_testnet/multi_host_rehearsal.py scripts/tests/test_v2_3_0_multi_host_rehearsal.py`
- `python3 scripts/tests/test_v2_3_0_multi_host_rehearsal.py` — 7 tests passed
- example inventory validation — PASS for exactly five nodes
- English-comment validation — PASS
- repository hygiene — PASS
- Task 12 contract workflow — PASS

The broader Lint, RPC/release, runbook, and pre-burn-in workflows also run against the exact PR head.

## Impact

- Operator impact: one controlled procedure replaces ad hoc multi-host commands and makes restart/partition/rejoin evidence reviewable.
- Developer impact: the rehearsal contract and verifier have deterministic regression coverage without requiring private hosts in ordinary CI.
- Release impact: Task 13 remains blocked until a protected live run records a verified `GO` for the exact candidate SHA.

## Risk and rollback

The primary risk is an operator-specific transport or fault hook affecting more than the intended P2P path. The inventory accepts only structured argv, the runbook requires out-of-band access and idempotent exact restoration, and the controller always attempts restore after an isolation attempt. The tooling and workflow can be reverted without changing protocol or stored node state.

## Guardrails

- `VERSION` and Cargo remain `2.2.20`.
- `public_testnet_ready=false` remains mandatory.
- The 30-day public-testnet clock remains not started and cannot be backdated by this evidence.
- Mining remains external; no embedded pool logic.
- Smart contracts remain out of scope.
- No consensus, storage-format, node RPC, miner protocol, release-tag, or public-testnet-launch change.
- Merging this PR does **not** complete Task 12 by itself; only a real protected execution with a verified `GO` bundle can do that.

author: akkart-aws
body:
## What?
The positional flush then rings only one rail's doorbell; the other rail's batch is never submitted and the transfer hangs. nixlbench doesn't hit this: one buffer per device = one rail list.

## Why?
FI_MORE WRITE batching (#1626) flushes the doorbell positionally (last of each 16-group / last of the transfer), which is only correct when every descriptor in a group is on the same rail.  But each descriptor's rail comes from its own buffer's selected_rails, so a transfer spanning buffers with different rail lists (e.g. dynamo's many DRAM registrations) alternates physical rails within a group. 

## How?
postXfer precomputes the flush decision per physical rail (walking descriptors backwards, the first rail seen is its last post), and prepareAndSubmitTransfer takes a bool apply_fi_more instead of deciding positionally. Batching is opt-in, so unmarked descriptors (READ, striped, rail-less) flush.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Performance Improvements**
  * Improved Libfabric WRITE batching by precomputing per-descriptor `FI_MORE` decisions, with tighter rail-aligned round-robin selection for better endpoint targeting.
* **Behavior Changes**
  * WRITE posts now respect controlled “flush” boundaries more consistently; behavior differs between single-path posting and chunked/thread-pool posting to avoid incorrect “last post” assumptions.
  * READ behavior remains unchanged.
* **Configuration**
  * Added `NIXL_LIBFABRIC_FI_MORE_BATCH_SIZE` (default: 16) to limit consecutive WRITE descriptors eligible for `FI_MORE` batching before flushing.

# Habits
## 1a Habits foundation

`src/utils/date.ts`: date key lokal, weekday bitmask, `calculateCurrentStreak()` (dengan grace period — belum "mark done" hari ini gak langsung motong streak), formatter tanggal Indonesia.
- `useHabitsStore`: CRUD, archive (bukan hard-delete — histori streak/heatmap gak boleh hilang), `toggleHabitToday` (auto-update `bestStreak` kalau kepecahin).
- `useTodosStore`: CRUD sederhana, hard-delete (todos emang ephemeral, beda karakteristik dari habit).
- **Navigasi**: `index.tsx` (Goals) di-rename jadi `goals.tsx`, `index.tsx` baru = Today (landing default). FAB sekarang context-aware: Today→tambah habit, Goals→tambah goal, History→disembunyikan.
- **Today screen**: checklist habits + todos, progress bar "X dari Y selesai", tap checkbox = toggle (haptic), tap row habit = ke detail (screen-nya nyusul di 1d), quick-add todo inline (gak perlu screen terpisah).
- `CelebrationOverlay`: muncul sekali pas transisi ke "semua selesai" (edge-triggered, gak nyala ulang tiap render, gak nyala pas mount kalau kebetulan udah selesai dari sesi lain).

## 1b Habit form
- `HabitIconPicker.tsx` — grid ~24 ikon (`MaterialCommunityIcons`), tiap nama diverifikasi satu-satu langsung dari glyph map yang ke-bundle (bukan ditebak dari ingatan) — kesehatan/fitness, mindfulness, belajar, kreatif, lifestyle. Tap-to-pick doang, sesuai spek awal (gak ada free-search).
- `HabitColorPicker.tsx` — 10 warna vivid, sengaja beda dari `accentByKey` pastel goal karena warna ini nanti juga mewarnai cell heatmap (pastel gak keliatan bedanya di cell kecil).
- `app/habit/add.tsx` — form lengkap: nama, ikon, warna, frekuensi (Setiap hari / Hari tertentu + 7 chip weekday), reminder (toggle + preset waktu, pola sama kayak `ReminderSheet.tsx` biar konsisten).

## 1c Habit detail heatmap
- `HabitHeatmap.tsx` — grid GitHub-style murni pakai `View` (gak nambah dependency SVG/chart), 30 minggu histori, kolom = minggu (Senin di atas), warna sesuai `habit.color`, auto-scroll ke minggu terbaru pas dibuka. Sengaja gak dibedain "gak due" vs "due tapi kelewat" biar gampang dibaca sekilas.

author: fonixian
body:
This probably fixes #176. The old version stored NaN in `last_x `and `last_y `(used for getting the delta of the mouse movement) when there was no previous x,y position. For example, at the start of the program or when enabling/disabling the mouse.

This meant that when we disable the mouse (e.g., when holding LMBT to move the camera), X and Y become NaN until the mouse is moved. If we zoom during that period, the calculations occur with NaN values because I pass last_x and last_y forward into the scroll event, because GLFW does not provide the current cursor position when scrolling.

The fix is that instead of using NaN values, I now call GLFW.GetCursorPos.

author: macieklamberski
body:
dev.to already had a resolver for `.c-embed`, the card for an external link. A link to another dev.to post renders differently, and in two shapes.

They are two generations of one generator, not two co-existing card types. `.ltag__link--embedded` (wrapping `.crayons-story`) is what Forem emits today; `.ltag__link` is what it emitted from 2019 until March 2026. Forem compiles liquid tags to HTML at save time and stores the result, so older articles keep the older markup forever and both shapes stay in circulation. Each gets its own resolver.

Both were confirmed to survive into the feed body: dev.to puts the full body in `description` and its feed sanitizer keeps `div`, `a`, `img`, `h1`-`h6` and `span` along with `class`, `href` and `src`.

With three resolvers in the file, the existing one is renamed `devtoCiteResolver` → `devtoLinkCiteResolver`: `link` against `post` is the axis that tells them apart, and a bare name no longer says which card it means. It was never exported from the package, so nothing outside `defaultCiteResolvers` referenced it. The tests for all three now live in `devto.test.ts`, matching every other cite file and the way `substack.test.ts` already holds two resolvers.

Notes on what is deliberately not mapped:

- No date. The current shape's `<time>` carries no year and its `datetime` attribute is stripped by the feed sanitizer; the older shape packs the date into the byline as a display string (`Name ・ Aug 25 '22`). Neither is machine-readable.
- No thumbnail. These cards render with Forem's basic feed style, which emits no cover image.
- Description is usually absent. Only a post with a context note or a status preview carries any text beside the title.

The older shape needs one guard: the Medium liquid tag renders into the same `.ltag__link` class tree. It is separated by `.ltag__link__servicename`, which only Medium emits.

No corpus prevalence figure: the corpus volume is offline.

author: marcusdavidg
body:
Closes #265

## What this does

Adds `preview_payout_deep(id, amount) -> Result<Vec<(Address, i128)>, Error>` to the splitter contract. This is the deep variant of `preview_payout` that resolves every `Recipient::Split` child recursively down to leaf `Recipient::Account` addresses.

## Contract (`contracts/splitter/src/lib.rs`)

### New public method: `preview_payout_deep`

```rust
pub fn preview_payout_deep(env: Env, id: u64, amount: i128) -> Result<Vec<(Address, i128)>, Error>
```

- Returns `(Address, i128)` pairs — leaf address alongside its final amount. No more positional-zip against `get_split`.
- Recurses through `Recipient::Split` children by loading each child split and applying `amounts()` at each level.
- **Same rounding as `pay`**: uses the existing `amounts()` helper at every level, so dust-to-last-recipient behaviour is bit-for-bit identical to an actual payment.
- **Aggregates duplicates**: if the same address appears as a leaf under multiple branches, amounts are summed into a single entry.
- **Depth-bounded**: new constant `MAX_PREVIEW_DEPTH = 8`. Calls that would exceed the cap return `Error::BadChildSplit`. At 32 recipients per split that covers trees with millions of theoretical leaf slots — far more than any real-world routing tree.

### New private helper: `resolve_deep`

Recursive implementation with an injected `depth` counter. Separated from the public entry point so the guard and accumulation logic stay readable.

## SDK (`sdk/src/index.ts`)

- `preview_payout_deep` added to the `Client` interface with return type `Result<Array<readonly [string, i128]>>`.
- Added to the `fromJSON` map.

## App (`app/src/lib/tributary.ts`)

- `previewPayoutDeep(id, amount)` helper wraps the SDK call and returns `{ address: string; amount: bigint }[]` for easy consumption by the Pay tab and the tree visualisation (#75).

## Docs (`README.md`)

Added `preview_payout_deep` row to the Contract API table.

## Tests (8 new, all pass — 49 total)

| Test | What it verifies |
|---|---|
| `deep_preview_flat_split_matches_shallow_preview` | Flat split returns same numbers as `preview_payout`, paired with addresses |
| `deep_preview_two_level_tree` | 2-level tree resolves correctly; preview matches actual `pay` + `distribute` |
| `deep_preview_three_level_tree` | 3-level tree resolves correctly; preview matches actual `pay` + `distribute` chain |
| `deep_preview_aggregates_shared_leaf_address` | Same address under two branches → single aggregated entry |
| `deep_preview_dust_rounding_matches_actual_pay` | Tricky 3-way dust share at child level — preview matches real payout exactly |
| `deep_preview_rejects_non_positive_amount` | `InvalidAmount` for 0 and negative inputs |
| `deep_preview_rejects_unknown_split` | `SplitNotFound` for non-existent split id |
| `deep_preview_depth_cap_is_enforced` | 9-deep chain returns `BadChildSplit`; 8-deep succeeds and sums to input amount |

## Acceptance criteria

| Criteria | Status |
|---|---|
| Deep preview resolves nested splits to leaf accounts with exact final amounts | ✅ |
| Leaf amounts sum to the input amount | ✅ tested at 2-level, 3-level, dust cases |
| Preview matches what an actual payment produces | ✅ two-level and three-level verified |
| Recursion is depth-bounded and the bound is documented | ✅ `MAX_PREVIEW_DEPTH = 8` in lib.rs doc-comment |
| #69 and #75 can be built on it | ✅ `previewPayoutDeep` app helper ready to use |

author: julienmartel
body:
Daily docs sweep — four stale claims in the in-repo docs. The web guide is updated separately in nebelhaus/workshop#21.

## Corrected

- **`CLAUDE.md:139`** — said "CI then builds the ad-hoc-signed `.app`". CI signs with Apple **Developer ID** (hardened runtime) and notarizes. `e528c29` fixed this in the README but missed here; this was the last "ad-hoc" string in the tree. Phrasing matches `README.md:31`. (`bb5712d`, `7601902`; verified against `.github/workflows/release.yml`.)
- **`README.md:100`** — claimed Messages mode "remains gated until `platform-imessage` has passed a signed-host vetting/validation pass". Wrong: the shipping read path is `LiveIMessageProvider`, constructed unconditionally for `.messages` at `InboxModel.swift:340-344`. That vetting gate applies only to the dormant `PlatformIMessageProvider`, which the UI never constructs. Stale since ADR 0002 was accepted.
- **`README.md:80`** — presented **Load Earlier Messages** as the way to scroll back. Since `46e0b17` pages are 100 messages and load automatically within ~1.5 screens of the top (`prefetchDistance = 1_200`, `ConversationView.swift:471-506`); the button survives as a fallback. Reworded so the automatic path leads.
- **`ARCHITECTURE.md:577`** — the user-facing message list documented only "Attachment unavailable." `64d54c1` added a distinct iCloud-offloaded state ("In iCloud — open in Messages to download" on file rows, "In iCloud" on gallery tiles). Added the missing state.

## Left alone (deliberately)

- **The gated platform-imessage tapback write overlay** (`de27e6a`) — **reverted in `5868ade`; it did not ship.** Confirmed against the final tree, not the commit log: `CompositeMessagesProvider.swift`, `PlatformWriteBackend.swift` and `CompositeWriteOverlayTests.swift` are all absent, and there are zero code hits for `platformWritesEnabled`, `addReaction`, `canReact` or `sendTapback`. Every statement that trill is read-only and cannot send tapbacks is still correct and was deliberately not touched. Worth flagging loudly because this is the one change in the range that could have inverted the project's central promise.
- **`0d98ce8` vs `384cb0c`** — the same provider-health re-probe, twice. The first died in the revert; the second re-landed it. The feature *did* ship; only the first commit is a ghost.
- **Version stamps and the signing/notarization CI work** — no doc consequence beyond the `CLAUDE.md` line above.

## Needs code, not docs

author: rpavlovictt
body:
Adds `CCLRuleBook` for `all_gather` / `reduce_scatter` / `all_reduce`, keeping their inputs and outputs interleaved (L1 or DRAM), never L1-sharded.

**Why:** the op-model constraint query validates a CCL op's sharded layout against the *per-device* tensor shape, but at runtime a mesh tensor sharded on a non-cluster mesh axis carries the *global* shape. Metal builds the CCL output `TensorSpec` from that global shape and can fail its shard-grid-fit check (`tensor_spec.cpp`) — a sharded layout the query accepted crashes at runtime. This stops the optimizer from ever offering such a layout.

Mirrors the existing `SliceRuleBook` / `MeshPartitionRuleBook` pattern (`rejectAllSharded` input filter, `nonShardedOutputHints`, `shouldExploreReshards=false`). Interleaved CCL is unaffected.

Re-enabling valid L1-sharded CCL on multi-axis meshes needs per-value mesh-distribution tracking; tracked separately.

The PR keeps A7 quarantined, the canonical Fan blocked and L5 absent. It includes a machine-readable summary and semantic validation workflow. body: The purpose of this PR is to add a DSS (Dependency Selector Syntax) skill with `@vltpkg/query` so coding agents can explain and compose selector queries for users unfamiliar with the syntax. ## Changes - Stored in-package at `src/query` under `skills/` and added to the publish files list, matching the layout proposed in https://github.com/vltpkg/vltpkg/issues/1540 where install discovers packaged `SKILL.md` files and mounts them into the project's root skills/ folder. ### The skill (`src/query/skills/dss-query/`) - `SKILL.md` — response contract (query first, one-line explanation, bare **Examples** tail, jargon glossed in place, verified docs deep link), a compose-from-goal workflow, core syntax table, common recipes, and a security-auditing section covering the threat / vulnerability / capability / hygiene selector families - `REFERENCE.md` — selector-by-selector detail - Every factual claim is verified against engine source: `--view` values, `:license()` category kinds (not license IDs), `:workspace` ⇒ `vlt.json`, security selector list, docs anchor slugs ### The evals (`src/query/skills/dss-query/evals/`) "Evaluate a skill" uses `skill-creator` plugin to evaluate skills according to (see `evals/README.md`): | Layer | Method | CI-gateable? | | --- | --- | --- | | Content correctness | parse + execute documented selectors against the real engine | yes — deterministic | | Content efficacy | with-skill vs baseline subagent differential, graded deterministically | not as a hard gate | | Trigger efficacy | repeated trigger-rate sampling | no — monitor only | - `evals.json` — 7 prompts (composition, decomposition, mistake-correction, and three security-auditing scenarios) with per-eval assertions - `grade.mjs` — **no LLM judge**: extracts selectors from answers, parses via `@vltpkg/dss-parser`, executes structural selectors against the in-memory fixture graph (top-level comma split defeats the engine's loose mode; `:outdated`/security selectors are parse-only so grading stays offline), plus shape/style regex assertions See https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#run-evals-with-skill-creator (I know, this is not really the best framework but I don't want to install another dependency til we're sure we are committed to skill eval as a whole. I personally would prefer BrainTrust or PromptFoo) Because the angle I plan on pushing is security-related, I want to include some kind of proofing or improvement measure for the skill. ### Measured results (with-skill vs baseline, single run per config) | Iteration | Baseline | Pass-rate lift | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | no skill | +6pts | correctness lift ≈ 0 on a strong model — value was style + ~45% faster answers | | 2 | pre-edit snapshot | +10pts | inlining security guidance removed 3–5 REFERENCE.md round-trips (−6.3s/answer) | | 3 | pre-edit snapshot | **+23pts (100% pass)** | Examples/gloss/docs-link contract; every baseline failure is exactly a feature the round added | ## Why the original `claude -p` harness was removed The first harness checked whether the Skill tool fired in headless mode. Testing showed that measures model mood, not skill quality: in agentic print mode, models answer directly (run `vlt`, read the repo) instead of invoking skills, and slash-command syntax isn't processed. Its selector-"validity" check was also weak — `parse()` alone doesn't reject semantically invalid DSS (#1680). Both lessons are baked into the layered approach and documented in `evals/README.md` and `AGENTS.md`. ## Notes for reviewers - `evals/` is excluded from the published `@vltpkg/query` package (`files` field) — repo tooling only - The eval workspace (transcripts, gradings, benchmarks) is local and gitignored; `.gitignore` gains a negation so `grade.mjs` isn't swallowed by the `/src/**/*.mjs` build-artifact rule - Future follow-ups (not in this PR): standalone Layer-1 doc-selector CI sweep, and a `skill-evals.yml` workflow (manual + nightly + path-filtered, non-blocking)

body:
## Summary

The board's **Inbox** section duplicated the chat sidebar and required its own expensive server-side scan (`listChats(..., boardInbox: true)`) on board load. This PR moves card triage into the sidebar and removes the inbox entirely — frontend and backend.

### Chat sidebar kebab menu
- Each chat row's bookmark + delete buttons are replaced by a single **⋮ menu**: *Bookmark, Create card, Add to card…, Delete*. The two card options only appear when the chat has no `metadata.cardId`.
- The popup uses `position: fixed` (escapes the sidebar's `overflow: auto` clipping), flips upward near the viewport bottom, and closes on click-away, scroll, resize, and Escape.
- **Create card** promotes the chat instantly using its title (same derivation as the old board promote). **Add to card…** reuses the existing `CardPicker` modal; on a failed assign/create the picker stays open so the failure is visible and retryable.
- Shared `MenuRow` (+ `MenuItem` type) extracted from `PromptInput`'s hamburger menu; both menus now use it.

### Board inbox removal
- `Board.tsx` loses all inbox state/fetching/JSX; `InboxRow.tsx` deleted. Boards now load with a single `GET /api/cards`.
- Backend cleanup: `boardInbox` query filter, `PATCH /api/chats/:id/board`, and `setBoardDismissed` removed. Existing `metadata.boardDismissed` values on old chats are inert leftovers (no migration needed).

## Testing
- Full build (shared/backend/frontend) and all **839 tests** pass; eslint 0 errors.
- Exercised end-to-end against the dev server with playwright: menu options gate correctly on card membership (4 options → 2 after carding), create/assign verified via API (card membership, chat counts), bookmark/delete flows unchanged (delete still confirms), works in flat and tree layouts, board renders no inbox and makes zero `boardInbox` requests, removed route 404s, console clean.
- Self-review ran an 8-angle finder + verify pass; the two cheap correctness wins were applied (menu close-on-scroll/Escape, picker stays open on failure). Known follow-ups (not blocking): sidebar card actions log errors to console rather than surfacing a banner (matches the existing `Chat.tsx` CardPicker pattern), optimistic metadata patching + title derivation could be shared helpers, and the popup shell could be extracted alongside `MenuRow`.

author: jitokim
body:
## Summary

Documents the operational gotcha behind a confusing message: a typed action (kill / interrupt / inject) reporting `no unambiguous claude surface — attach (↵) and act manually`.

## Why

The install docs listed the commands but never stated the **ordering consequence**. The `SessionStart` hook records a session's identity (pid ↔ tty ↔ window) only when that session *starts*. So a `claude` session already running when `hooks install` ran is **observed** (fleetops reads its transcript) but never **registered** — and a typed action against it can't resolve an unambiguous target, so it falls back to a manual hint. That reads like a failure but is fleetops refusing to guess which terminal to type into.

Diagnosed live: of five running interactive sessions, only the one started after the hooks were active was in the registry; the four started earlier (Jul 17–18, before the `SessionStart` hook was recording) were not, and every kill against them hit this message.

## Changes (docs only)

- **Quick start / hooks section** — a caveat: install the hooks *before* starting the sessions you want to act on; sessions already running register only on their next start; nothing re-registers retroactively.
- **Known rough edges** — a named entry for the `no unambiguous claude surface` message and its three causes: started before hooks, a headless `claude -p` session with no surface, or a stale binding after a terminal restart (the last is #62, still being hardened).

## Not changed

Behavior. The fallback itself is correct — refusing to act beats acting on the wrong session. A separate improvement could make the *message* name its own cause; filed as a follow-up thought, not done here.

author: andrejkanuch
body:
Structural redesign of receipt-scan → maintenance capture, grounded in real prod data (a Honda Africa Twin service invoice that collapsed into one opaque record). Plan: `features/Receipt-scan/EXECUTION_PLAN.md`; findings: `docs/plans/receipt-scan-structure-redesign-2026-07-20.md`.

## Problem (from prod)
A multi-line service invoice saved as **one** blob maintenance task: line items discarded (`parts_needed` null), `completed_mileage` null despite the odometer being applied, VAT silently stuffed in the misc `cost` bucket, auto-expense mis-dated. Maintenance history was also invisible due to a GraphQL enum 500 (fixed separately, already live).

## Phases in this PR
- **P0 (done, live):** `MaintenanceTaskSource` enum fix deployed — `maintenanceTasks` no longer 500s on `receipt_scan`.
- **P1:** canonical `MaintenanceServiceType` taxonomy (17 types, single source of truth in `@motovault/types`) + `GqlMaintenanceServiceType` mirror with a compile-time sync guard + deterministic accent-insensitive EN/ES `classifyServiceType` (tested against the OEM top-10 names + the real Spanish invoice lines).
- **P2 (applied to prod `00169`/`00170`):** `maintenance_tasks` financial-wrapper cols (`total_amount`/`tax_amount`/`tax_rate`) + new `maintenance_task_line_items` table (own-user RLS, `service_type` CHECK). Additive-only, no backfill, no live impact; security advisors clean.
- **P3 (incoming in this PR):** API save path — persist line items + `completedMileage` + total/tax wrapper, fix `createFromTask` date/category, relax the reconcile gate, line-item DataLoader + resolver field.

## Design decisions (locked with owner)
- **No fuzzy auto-matching** of scanned lines to existing pending OEM tasks — a scan becomes a new *completed historical* record; per-type reminder projection is a later, user-confirmed phase.
- **Tax = total-owning wrapper:** the task holds the authoritative gross total + explicit optional tax; reconcile-or-total-only, never fabricate a bucket, never hard-block save.
- No backfill of the one existing mis-saved record — fix-forward only.

## Out of scope (later phases)
Extraction `lineItems[]` + prompt/date hardening (P4), review-card UI + overflow fix (P5), service-history display (P6), OEM normalization + reminder projection (P7).

author: spozhydaiev
body:
### Motivation
- Weekly summary sections can contain structured objects (e.g. `{ text: '…', person_id: 'person_9' }`) but the UI previously assumed primitive string list items and attempted to render raw values directly, causing React object-child render exceptions and a route-level error UI for valid HTTP 200 responses.
- The change centralizes normalization so all summary renderers receive a safe, typed UI model and the page stays resilient to schema variation or malformed items.

### Description
- Added a typed frontend view model `SummaryListItem` and replaced the old free-form `SummaryEntry` with a normalized shape containing `key`, `primaryText`, optional `secondaryText`, `sourceNoteIds`, and optional `personId`/`ticketKey`/`actionId` (`components/summaries/summary-normalization.ts`).
- Implemented a robust normalization layer in `normalizeSummaryContent` and helpers (`entries`, `entry`, `sourceIds`, id/field extractors) that safely converts strings, primitives, and documented structured objects into `SummaryListItem` instances and returns `[]` for `null`/`undefined` collections.
- Updated weekly/daily mapping to respect the OpenAPI-backed fields (use `content.summary` / `weekly_overview` as overview when present) and to explicitly include `highlights` and `actions` for weekly summaries.
- Updated the renderer so `Section` only renders normalized `primaryText`/`secondaryText` and only links to `/people/[id]` or `/tickets/[key]` when normalized IDs are present, and shows source-note chips for `note_` ids (`components/summaries/summary-utils.tsx`).
- Added safe fallback text `"Summary item unavailable"` for structured objects with no human-readable field and avoided `JSON.stringify` or rendering raw objects.
- Extended API typing to include the documented weekly `summary` field in `SummaryContent` to reflect `docs/openapi.yaml` (`lib/api/types.ts`).
- Added regression tests that cover structured weekly objects, malformed items, nullable/absent collections, mixed legacy/current items, navigation links, and the absence of `[object Object]` in rendered output (`components/summaries/summary-normalization.test.tsx`).

### Testing
- Ran `npm test` and the targeted test files and full suite passed: tests passed (all test files executed successfully).
- Ran `npm run typecheck` and TypeScript checks passed after adding the documented `summary` field to `SummaryContent`.
- Ran `npm run lint` which completed with existing pre-existing warnings (no new lint errors introduced).
- Ran `npm run build` and the production build completed successfully with pages compiled and generated.

author: rjwalters
body:
## Summary
`proofs/Proofs/Erdos53Problem.lean` (Erdős #53 — sums & products of distinct elements, Erdős–Szemerédi 1983 / Chang 2003) was a **definitions-only stub**: 9 defs, 0 theorems. This PR adds **12 axiom-free foundational lemmas** about the file's own definitions.

## New theorems (all axiom-free, host-verified under Lean v4.31.0)

| Theorem | Statement |
|---|---|
| `zero_mem_subsetSums` | `0` is always a subset sum (empty subset) |
| `mem_subsetSums_of_mem` | each `a ∈ A` is a subset sum (singleton) |
| `mem_subsetProducts_of_mem` | each `a ∈ A` is a subset product |
| `subsetSums_subset_sumsOrProducts` / `subsetProducts_subset_sumsOrProducts` | both feed into `sumsOrProducts` |
| `subsetSums_card_le` | `\|subsetSums A\| ≤ 2^{\|A\|}` (image of the powerset) |
| `subsetSums_mono` | subset sums monotone in the ground set |
| `subsetSumCount_le_card` / `subsetProductCount_le_card` | union count dominates each count |
| `sumset_card_le` / `productset_card_le` | `\|A+A\|, \|A·A\| ≤ \|A\|²` |
| `subsetSums_empty` | `subsetSums ∅ = {0}` |

## Verification
- `lake env lean Proofs/Erdos53Problem.lean` — compiles clean (host, v4.31.0).
- `#print axioms` on the new theorems lists only `propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound` — **axiom-free** (no `sorryAx`, no `Lean.ofReduceBool`).
- Meta synced: `theoremCount` 0 → 12, `lineCount` 116 → 197; `assumptions` / `proofStrategy` updated honestly.

## Status
**Outcome**: progress (definitions-only stub → 12 axiom-free foundational lemmas). The deep results (Chang 2003 affirmative resolution, Erdős–Szemerédi `exp(c·(log|A|)²·loglog|A|)` upper bound) remain documented-only, needing additive combinatorics beyond current Mathlib.

author: adrianwedd
body:
Detail pages rendered `{title} — Adrian Wedd`. The suffix is 14 characters spent on a word every visitor can already see in the domain, and Google truncates title links by pixel width — shorter titles survive intact on more screens.

Index and pagination pages keep it; "Blog" or "Gallery" alone is ambiguous in a tab strip or a SERP.

Gated on an explicit `siteNameInTitle` prop rather than the existing `type` prop: projects detail pages pass `type="website"`, so keying off `type` would both miss them and risk a later change silently altering `og:type` and the WebPage JSON-LD branch.

**Content titles are untouched** — this addresses the "73 over-length titles" item in #555 without any content edits. That number counted the rendered `<title>` including the suffix; only 8 frontmatter titles exceed 60 chars on their own, and those stay as written.

## Verification
Measured on the built artifact, not the source: all 7 detail templates emit unsuffixed titles; index, tag and pagination pages retain the suffix; homepage still `Adrian Wedd`. JSON-LD `headline`/`name` were already using the raw title, so structured data is unchanged. Unit tests (90), `astro check` and lint all pass.

## QA
codex / agy / hermes all reviewed against the built output. No correctness, schema, accessibility or missed-call-site findings from any of the three. Codex caught two inaccuracies in my doc comment (14 chars not 15; Google has no fixed character limit) — both fixed in the follow-up commit.

author: bombadiltom
body:
## What changed

- All sources moved to `src/` as typed ES classes, compiled to `dist/` with `tsc` (strict mode); the old prototype-based `index.js` and `accessories/*.js` are removed
- The `global.Service`/`global.Characteristic` pattern is replaced by a small `src/hap.ts` module that captures `api.hap` and the `PlatformAccessory` constructor at plugin init
- Platform logic now lives in `src/platform.ts`, with device-number lists as named constants and shared API payload types in `src/types.ts`
- Dependencies modernized: axios ^1, axios-cookiejar-support ^4 (new `wrapper()` API), tough-cookie ^4; the unused, deprecated `request` dependency is dropped
- Package builds on install via the `prepare` script; npm ships only `dist/` and `config.schema.json`
- Output stays CommonJS, so the plugin remains loadable by homebridge 1.6+ as well as 2.x
- Version bumped to 1.0.0

## Bugs fixed along the way

The type checker surfaced several latent bugs that are fixed in the migration:

- Bare `Characteristic` references (missing `global.`) in the blinds, dimmer, switch, and door-sensor classes
- Wrong `this` inside the door-sensor state callback
- Dimmer `setBrightness` invoking its HomeKit callback twice on error
- `password_hashed` config flag was parsed but never assigned (no-op statement); hashed-password configs behave the same
- `data.ndame` log typo

## How it was tested

Ran the built plugin under homebridge 2.2.0 (node 22) against a mock HomePilot HTTP server covering all 11 device types: salted-password login, device/meter/scene discovery, accessory creation, periodic polling reads, and a restart restoring all accessories from homebridge's cache through `configureAccessory` — all clean. Also verified on a second machine via `npm install -g .`.

## Notes for reviewers

- Pre-existing and untouched: `config.schema.json` spells one option `add_enviroment_sensor` while the code reads `add_environment_sensor`, so that UI toggle never had an effect; left as-is since changing either side affects existing configs
- The homebridge type-only imports use `with { 'resolution-mode': 'import' }` because homebridge 2.x is pure ESM while this package compiles to CommonJS

body:
## What kind of change does this PR introduce?

A feature and build-system update that adds Avalonia support, ReactiveUI.Primitives variants, central package management, MinVer versioning, and NUKE-based automation.

## What is the new behavior?

- Provides lean and System.Reactive-compatible ReactiveUI.Primitives packages for WPF and Avalonia.
- Shares canonical WPF/Avalonia sources safely through compile-time namespace isolation.
- Builds the complete `Localisation.slnx` graph through analyzer-clean NUKE entry points.
- Uses centrally managed NuGet versions, StyleSharp/Roslynator analysis, and MinVer with a consistent `v1.1.x` policy.
- Validates pushes and pull requests with TUnit on Microsoft Testing Platform and Cobertura coverage.
- Gates release packing on the tested Release build, preserves symbol packages, and pins release/signing dependencies.

## What is the current behavior?

The main branch contains only the WPF package, relies on direct package versions, System.Reactive/StyleCop/Nerdbank.GitVersioning integration, and legacy build workflows without the new Avalonia/reactive variants or NUKE release validation.

- [x] Tests have been added or updated (for bug fixes / features) 
- [ ] Docs have been added or updated (for bug fixes / features)

author: hirokimorikawa
body:
## Summary

- `docs/10-mechanics/06-soft-body-particles.md` の設計 §2.2 の距離拘束のみを持つ XPBD `SoftBody` を実装した(`crates/sim-mechanics/src/soft_body.rs`)。`MechanicsSolver` とは独立に動作する(`sim_statistical::BrownianParticleSet` と同様のパターン)。曲げ拘束・体積拘束(布・ゼリー)・剛体/流体との結合・自己衝突は未実装のまま残した。
- M13(懸垂線): 端点をピン留めしたロープを非伸縮に近いコンプライアンスで垂らし、静止形状を懸垂線 $y=a\cosh(x/a)$ と比較。パラメータ $a$ は全長・端点間隔から二分法で逆算した。
- M14(伸び): ロープをほぼ質量ゼロにして先端に集中荷重(質量 $W/g$)を吊るし、直列ばね則で各セグメントの剛性を配分して、全体の伸び $\delta=WL_0/(EA)$ と比較した。
- M14 の実装検証中に、既定のサブステップ数(4)では特定の高剛性・軽量質点比のシナリオで伸びが理論値の約5.6倍に収束してしまうことを発見した。デバッグ用の使い捨てバイナリで追跡した結果、各セグメントの質点-バネ系の固有振動周期が既定のサブステップ幅より短く、粗いサブステップでは正しい剛性に収束しない(古典的な PBD/XPBD の下収束アーティファクト)ことが原因と判明。このテスト固有の高剛性シナリオに合わせてサブステップ数を増やすことで解消した(設計 §4「サブステップ優先(反復より分割が精度に効く)」の実地確認)。
- `docs/22-roadmap/02-feature-checklist.md` を更新(XPBD・M13・M14 チェック、現在地)。

- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test --workspace`(M13・M14 含め全緑)
