author: copilot
body:
Replaces the shop owner's paper register with a mobile-first, installable PWA that manages customers, inventory, rentals, returns/settlement, and reporting — working fully offline.

The app lives in `app/` (React + TypeScript + Vite). All data persists locally in **IndexedDB (Dexie)**; the data layer is isolated behind Dexie tables so cloud sync (e.g. Supabase) can be layered on later without touching screens.

### Screens
- **Customers** — CRUD, ID capture (front/back + selfie), duplicate detection by phone/ID, per-customer history, spend, outstanding balance, trust/blacklist.
- **Inventory** — unique code/QR, per-hour/day/week pricing, replacement value + suggested deposit, photos, QR scan, maintenance log & due indicators.
- **New Rental** — multi-tool cart with per-item pricing mode, live estimate, deposit suggestion, handover photos, "physical ID held" toggle, auto-generated agreement, WhatsApp/SMS send.
- **Active Rentals** — live elapsed time + running charge, overdue highlighting, sort/filter, call/WhatsApp/return quick actions.
- **Return & Settlement** — duration→rent, deposit balance (refund/extra), late/damage (capped at tool value)/discount, handover-vs-return photo compare, cash/UPI/card + partial payments, digital receipt.
- **History**, **Reports**, **Notifications**, **Settings** — search/filter + PDF/CSV export; earnings/utilization/dues + revenue chart; due/overdue/maintenance alerts; currency/tax/rounding/deposit/late-fee config, shop profile, staff accounts & roles, backup/restore, delete-data.

### Security
- PIN lock with multi-staff accounts (owner/staff roles); PINs stored as salted SHA-256 hashes.
- ID photos/selfies **encrypted at rest** with AES-GCM, key derived from the PIN via PBKDF2 and cached only in memory after unlock.

### Data & templates
- Seeded sample data (2 staff, 4 customers, 8 tools) created on first launch.
- Plain-text, shop-branded agreement/receipt templates in `app/src/lib/templates.ts`.

Rent maths and settlement are centralized in `app/src/lib/money.ts`, e.g.:

```ts
// deposit − (rent + late + damage − discount + tax) → refund or extra to collect
const s = computeSettlement(rental, returnTime, settings, { damageFee, discount });
s.refund > 0 ? refund(s.refund) : collect(s.extraToCollect);
```

### Notes for reviewers
- PWA is configured with `base: './'` so it deploys under any sub-path; `app/dist` is a static bundle hostable anywhere over HTTPS.
- Camera/QR degrade gracefully to a file-input fallback when no camera is available.
- Setup and deployment steps are documented in the root `README.md`.

author: uzcustomer
body:
## Summary
Implements deduplication logic to ensure each HEMIS curriculum has exactly one namunaviy (template) curriculum. When multiple namunaviy curricula exist for the same HEMIS curriculum, the system now keeps only the canonical one (most complete by subject count, or latest by ID if tied) and removes duplicates.

## Key Changes

- **New Console Command**: `DedupeNamunaviyCurricula`
  - Identifies and reports duplicate namunaviy curricula grouped by HEMIS curriculum ID
  - Supports dry-run mode (default) and `--apply` flag for actual deletion
  - Cascades delete subjects and comparisons when removing duplicates

- **Model Enhancement**: `ManualCurriculum::canonicalRank()`
  - Static method that returns a sortable rank `[subject_count, curriculum_id]`
  - Used consistently across all deduplication logic to select the canonical curriculum
  - Supports pre-loaded `subjects_count` for efficiency

- **Upload Logic**: `CurriculumCheckController::store()` and `storeBulk()`
  - When uploading a new namunaviy curriculum, automatically replaces any existing namunaviy curricula for the same HEMIS curriculum
  - Tracks newly created curriculum IDs to avoid deleting them
  - Provides user feedback when old namunaviy curricula are replaced

- **Comparison Resolution**: `CurriculumCheckController::resolveGroup()`
  - When resolving a comparison group, always uses the canonical namunaviy curriculum
  - Ensures consistent results even if an old/incomplete duplicate was referenced

- **Curriculum Check Index**: `CurriculumCheckController::index()`
  - Filters grouped comparisons to show only the canonical namunaviy per HEMIS curriculum
  - Prevents duplicate rows and incorrect "not found in template" results

## Implementation Details

- All deduplication uses the same `canonicalRank()` method for consistency
- Deletion is wrapped in database transactions to ensure data integrity
- Cascade deletes handle cleanup of subjects and saved comparisons
- User-facing messages inform when duplicates are replaced during upload

author: coreylyn
body:
## Linked issue

- Closes #294 (parent #289)

## Change summary

Implements Portable directory removal for Uninstall execution: apps with no uninstall command but a trusted install location can be permanently removed after explicit per-run `--allow-permanent` authorization (separate from `--execute`).

### What changed

- **pathsafe**: Added `ValidatePortableRemovalPath` method (refactored `ValidateDeletePath` to share common logic). The portable variant rejects volume roots, Windows tree (root+descendants), Program Files roots (exact only; per-app descendants like `C:\Program Files\MyApp` are allowed), user profile root, and AppData roots. User Protection rules apply deny-only. Reparse/hardlink rejected. Existence revalidated via Lstat.
- **uninstall/execute.go**: Replaced the `portable_removal_not_supported` skip with actual portable removal when authorized. New `executePortableRemoval` function with safety gates: auth gate -> process-stop gate -> trusted install location validation -> cancel check -> permanent removal. Added `ActionPortableRemoval`, `SkipPortableRemovalNotAuthorized`, `ReasonPortableRemovalFailed` constants. Added `AllowPermanent`, `PermanentRemover` to `ExecuteOptions`. Added `PortableRemovalPath` to `AppOutcome`.
- **uninstall/history.go**: Records portable removal with `Path=installLocation`, `PlannedAction=portable_removal`, actual `Action`/`Result`; distinguishes from Recycle Bin leftover deletion.
- **cli/root.go**: Added `--allow-permanent` flag to uninstall command; wires into `ExecuteOptions.AllowPermanent`. Updated help text.
- **AGENTS.md**: Updated product boundaries to reflect portable removal is now implemented.

## Verification results

- `go build ./...` — pass
- `go vet ./internal/core/pathsafe/... ./internal/uninstall/... ./internal/cli/...` — pass (pre-existing vet issue in `internal/clean/suggestion_internal_test.go` is unrelated)
- `gofmt -l` on all changed files — clean
- `go test ./...` — all pass

## Safety checklist

- [x] **Authorization split**: `--allow-permanent` is separate from `--execute`; without it portable targets are skipped with `portable_removal_not_authorized` and nothing is permanently deleted
- [x] **No silent fallback**: a failed official uninstaller never falls back to portable install-tree deletion (classification-based branching; verified by test)
- [x] **Dangerous-root rejection**: volume roots, Windows tree, Program Files roots, user profile root, AppData roots are rejected with `dangerous_root`; per-app descendants under Program Files/AppData are allowed
- [x] **Protection**: user Protection rules apply deny-only; protected paths skipped, never force-deleted; ProtectionLoadError gate aborts run before mutation
- [x] **Permanent deletion only**: portable removal uses `FilesystemPermanentRemover` (ordinary filesystem removal), NOT the Recycle Bin; never silently falls back
- [x] **Revalidation**: install location revalidated via Lstat immediately before deletion
- [x] **Fakes in tests**: tests inject `fakePermanentRemover` (records calls, does NOT delete) and real `pathsafe.Validator` with temp directories; no real permanent deletion occurs in tests
- [x] **History**: records planned vs actual permanent action with install location path; distinguishes from Recycle Bin leftover deletion

## Test coverage

- Authorization split (not-authorized -> skip, authorized -> delete, execution policy actions list)
- Non-fallback (failed official uninstaller with install location does not trigger portable deletion)
- Protection suppression (protected install location skipped, sibling freed)
- Dangerous-root rejection (volume root, Windows root, Program Files root)
- History recording (authorized success + not-authorized skip)
- Process-stop gate (running app skipped without authorization)
- Partial-risk failure (failed removal records `portable_removal_failed` with mutation-may-have-begun warning)
- CLI `--allow-permanent` flag wiring
- pathsafe `ValidatePortableRemovalPath` (dangerous roots, Program Files descendant allowed, AppData descendant allowed, Protection rules, unsafe forms, missing path)

## Remaining risks

- Pre-existing `go vet` issue in `internal/clean/suggestion_internal_test.go` (unrelated to this change).
- `/code-review` skill not run (potential stall risk); thorough self-review completed against all safety constraints.

## Confirms no real permanent deletion in tests

All tests inject `fakePermanentRemover` which records calls without deleting. Tests assert real temp directories still exist after Execute returns.

The Stripe charge idempotency key previously included `Date.now()`, which meant any network retry would create a brand new charge on Stripe instead of safely returning the existing one. This was a double-charge risk on timeout or network failure.

Fixed to use just the job ID as the key, so retries always resolve to the same charge.

  and reports an error on any unhandled state.

 This is especially useful when working with AI agents that edit dialogue

author: rmyndharis
yerzhansa
body:
## Problem

The daemon has two sync lanes. The store capture lane reads configuration through a live closure, so credentials applied later via the `configureRuntime` RPC are picked up. The reference lane baked its intervals.icu credentials into the production fetcher once at daemon boot. The desktop app never persists secrets into `config.yaml` — they live in the OS-encrypted vault and are re-applied over RPC after the daemon starts — so on every desktop install the reference lane booted with an empty key and stayed empty forever: each scheduled sync failed immediately with "Either apiKey or bearerToken must be provided". Reproduced on a real install: vault held the key, chat and store capture worked, reference sync failed on every tick.

## Fix

- The reference runtime accepts an optional live credential reader; the static `intervals` object remains the fallback for unchanged callers.
- Credential resolution moved from fetcher construction to every sync run: each invocation resolves current values and builds that run's HTTP client from them, so a key applied between two scheduled ticks is used by the next tick.
- Coach composition passes a closure over its active configuration, which observes `configureRuntime` replacements.

## Verification

- New reference-runtime coverage: changing the live values between two runs is observed by the second run; the static configuration shape still works.
- New composition coverage: after applying a runtime configuration with a new key, the reader handed to the reference bootstrap yields the new key and athlete id.
- Full repo gate green (4,613 tests); desktop build plus runtime and security smokes green.

body:
## Summary

Move hosted persistence from disk-backed SQLite to Neon PostgreSQL and replace the custom SQLite migration system with Alembic.

This also completes the Render Free build and startup path: Render builds the Python and pnpm workspaces from the repository root, packages the production UI and optimized WASM into the FastAPI service, applies migrations under an advisory lock, and starts the application only after the database reaches the expected Alembic head.

## What changed

- Added Psycopg 3 database URL normalization and PostgreSQL pool settings.
- Added a reviewed 24-table Alembic baseline.
- Retired the numbered SQLite migrations, custom runner, and SQLite backup tooling.
- Added an atomic SQLite-to-PostgreSQL importer with integrity checks, sequence repair, verification, dry-run, and explicit commit modes.
- Added separate migration and runtime database URLs.
- Updated readiness to check PostgreSQL connectivity, required tables, Alembic head, packaged UI, R2 configuration, and the verified compendium artifact.
- Updated the Render Free Blueprint to build the complete monorepo without a disk or paid pre-deploy command.
- Added production UI packaging and deterministic optimized WASM checks.
- Added PostgreSQL integration coverage for constraints, foreign keys, row locking, concurrent idempotency, readiness mismatch, and stale pooled connections.
- Made R2 administration output bounded and credential-safe.
- Updated current deployment, migration, recovery, configuration, security, testing, and release documentation.

## Data migration

The existing development SQLite data was imported into Neon in one transaction after a successful dry run.

The import verified table counts and sequences, skipped 17 invalid legacy asset rows explicitly, merged 50 historical audit rows, restored 16 session-asset links, and cleared two stale optional entity-character links.

The Neon database is at `0001_postgresql_baseline`, and Alembic reports no model/schema drift.

## Validation

- Server: 958 passed, 10 skipped
- PostgreSQL/Alembic against an isolated Neon schema: 14 passed
- Web UI: 2,759 passed
- Rust: 243 passed
- Core table: 147 passed
- TypeScript, Ruff, documentation, production build/package, WASM reproducibility, Alembic head, and drift checks passed

## Deployment follow-up

- [ ] Create the restricted Neon runtime role.
- [ ] Set `DATABASE_URL` and `DATABASE_MIGRATION_URL` in Render.
- [ ] Grant the R2 token object-delete and bucket-list permissions.

Database rollback is not automatic. Prefer a reviewed forward migration; for the disposable development environment, recover through a verified Neon branch when necessary.

## Why now

Two things currently on `main` are actively wrong for anyone cloning the repo fresh:

- **`compile-pages` crashes on client-page compiles.** It queried `client_sessions`, a table dropped by migration 0011. A fresh deploy hits a missing relation. Fixed in `beb75a0`.
- **The public MCP tool schema shipped the maintainer's real name.** `complete_agent_task` and `request_agent_review` descriptions read "Completion receipt for Dave" / "needs Dave to inspect". Genericized in `d5794d5`.

## What's in it

**Security / hardening**
- Centralized access-key auth across Edge Functions, restored param clamps and 405 method guards (`bdc5f13`)
- Slack webhook HMAC verification now fails closed (`fcb94dc`)
- `service_role` RLS policy backfill on `agent_run_log`, `oe_watch_rulings`, `openrouter_calls` (`85fb77c`)
- Revoked `anon` EXECUTE on `resolve_project_slug` (`986f484`)

## Summary

An expired-on-disk Claude credential produced a permanent red `Claude token stale - open Claude Code to refresh` banner and forever-`--` CLAUDE tiles for users who stopped using Claude Code, and toggling Claude usage off never cleared it.

- Demote a `.staleToken` outcome with no Claude Code statusline activity within 48h to a muted `.info` "Claude inactive" note (`ProviderOutcome.inactive` + `TerminalKind`).

- Keep statusline liveness + value cache synced while off (invisible; no credential read/poll) so re-enable never wrongly demotes an actively-running Claude.
- A missing credential still shows actionable "run claude login"; a recently-active statusline keeps the actionable stale message.

Closes #126

author: bearscloud
body:
The repository has no committed architecture document. `docs/claude-native-rework-plan.md` is untracked and is a *plan*, not a description of what exists — and nine parallel PRs just implemented an architecture written down nowhere.

## What this covers

- **The four layers** — enforcement (hooks), orchestrator (Claude), executors (Codex, two mechanics), substrate (the SQLite MCP servers) — and why the single-writer rule makes whole classes of bad state unreachable rather than merely guarded.
- **Three integration mechanics** and why `codex exec` is its own mechanic rather than "another subagent" (shell layer, own sandbox, diff-based evidence).
- **State model** including schema v1 -> v2 and why read-only opens never migrate.
- **Integrity invariants** that must not be weakened, with the non-obvious reasoning — e.g. `schema_version` is excluded from the logical digest specifically so a migrating writable open cannot fail a caller's CAS.
- **Key decisions and their costs**, stated plainly, including that retiring CD leaves merges with no automated verification.

## Sharp edges

The section most likely to save someone a bad afternoon. Every item verified against source, several discovered while building the parallel units:

| Edge | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| Phase order is not enforced server-side | `phase_record` checks the name and the single-active-record rule only |
| `plan_replace` and `analysis_record` settle a phase **without** a process record (`app_workflow.py:1118`, `:1327`) | Phase status and process record legitimately disagree; consumers that check one will either re-run recorded work or wedge a healthy wave |
| `workflow_state` is one flattened paged stream | Phases, tasks, reviews, findings share the 50/200 budget — a single page routinely hides recorded phases |
| `current_phase` is nested at `wave.current_phase` | Reads as top-level in prose |
| No wave-listing tool | Discovery goes through `waves/*/` on disk, confirmed against the DB |
| Registration writes to the target repo; a fresh DB is 192 KB | Why `.bears/`, `waves/`, `.claude/` are excluded from the budget walk |

## Known debt

Recorded rather than silently carried: the contract file still named `-v1.sql` while containing v2, two error codes missing from the contract and README, the workflow script not yet referenced from the manifest, the executor brief format being provisional, and the absence of CD.

Targets `chore/claude-native-prerequisite`, consistent with the other units.

body:
https://mcritchie.studio/tasks/seal-retries-boot-window

## Round 2 — review feedback resolved
Carl: request-changes (3 findings). Jasper: merge-ready, no blockers. The seam is unchanged — caller-side retry, `bin/prod-smoke` stays a single-shot standalone tool — which Jasper's verdict specifically endorsed.

| # | Finding | Resolution |
|---|---------|------------|
| 1 | **Real test sleeps** | Measured and confirmed: `test/lib/release_cli_test.rb` drives the REAL seal in a subprocess, so its red-seal tests each slept a genuine 30s (~90s of the mapped lane). `test_helper` now arms `SEAL_RETRY_NO_SLEEP=1` suite-wide and the policy raises `RealSleepError` naming the fix; `SEAL_RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS=0` lets subprocess tests exercise the retry path free. **The suite now runs ~90s faster than before this task existed.** |
| 2 | **Static-only integration coverage** | The verdict composition moved out of the script into `Release::SealRun` (retry + `SmokeSeal` + summary), so the integration lane RUNS it and asserts the seal a ship would record — transient → GREEN carrying the retry note, persistent → RED with the exact rollback commands, first-pass → one run and no sleep. Plus a subprocess test proving the models load Rails-free. The source tripwire survives only as a supplement. |
| 3 | **Missing ship docs** | The retry changes what a shipping operator sees — a ~30s pause and a green seal saying "retried once". Documented in the G4 gate doc, Avi's `production-deploy` SOP (including that a red seal now means the failure **persisted**), and the ship row of the devops-cycle design. |

Rebased onto current `accepted` (#596, #599 et al). Diff scope verified: only the seal step, its models, their tests, the three docs, and `test_helper`'s guard.

## Bug
rel-20260720-c06235's post-ship seal ran seconds after the Actions deploy, caught `GET /tasks` non-OK inside the dyno boot/restart window, and recorded a RED seal on a healthy prod (re-run sealed 5/5 green).

## Fix
- **`app/models/release/seal_retry.rb`** — the retry policy: first failure waits 30s and retries ONCE; only a persisting failure stays red; a first-attempt pass never sleeps.
- **`app/models/release/seal_run.rb`** — composes that retry with `SmokeSeal` into the recorded verdict and its summary, so step 5c's behavior is testable on real objects.
- **`bin/release.rb`** — step 5c calls the composition and keeps what a script should own: chdir, capture, telemetry, narration. Seal contract unchanged: non-blocking, never auto-rolls-back.

## Test evidence
Red-first both rounds. Round 2: 12 failures/errors across the three findings before the fix → all green after. `bin/fast-check` green at `db646c9b3842` (25 mapped + 5 spine paths, rubocop clean on 8 files).

author: simone-mariotti-prima
body:
## What

Adds OpenTelemetry 0.32 support via a new `tracing_opentelemetry_0_32` feature,
following the existing per-version feature pattern:

| Crate | Version |
|-------|---------|
| `opentelemetry` | 0.32 |
| `opentelemetry_sdk` | 0.32 |
| `tracing-opentelemetry` | 0.33 |

The default `tracing_opentelemetry` feature now targets 0.32 (previously 0.31).

## Changes

- `Cargo.toml`: add `opentelemetry_0_32_pkg`, `opentelemetry_sdk_0_32_pkg`,
  `tracing-opentelemetry_0_33_pkg` optional deps; add the
  `tracing_opentelemetry_0_32` feature; bump the default alias to it.
- `src/request/otel.rs`: add the matching `#[cfg(feature = "tracing_opentelemetry_0_32")]`
  `otel_crates` re-export block.
- `Makefile.toml`: add `tracing_opentelemetry_0_32` to `AVAILABLE_OTEL_FEATURES`
  so the test / clippy / deny matrices cover it.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: Unreleased entry.
- `Cargo.lock`: regenerated.

## Why

`prima-tracing 0.25.0` already supports OpenTelemetry 0.32, so `prima_bridge`
should be extended to support it too and stay aligned across the tracing stack.

Otherwise, a service on otel 0.32 that also uses `prima_bridge` ends up with a
dual otel-version tree (0.31 via prima_bridge's default feature + 0.32 from the
app), which risks silently breaking trace-context propagation on outgoing HTTP
requests.

## Verification (local)

Run per the CI otel matrix with the new feature:

- `cargo check --no-default-features --features tracing_opentelemetry_0_32` -> clean
- `cargo clippy --no-default-features --features tracing_opentelemetry_0_32 --all-targets -- -D warnings` -> clean
- `cargo fmt --check` -> clean
- `cargo test --no-run --features gzip` (default feature = otel 0.32) -> compiles

Version bumped to 0.31.0 (minor, additive) so it can be released right after merge; downstream services can then pin 0.31.0 and move to otel 0.32 without a dual-version tree.

author: rudrakshi-gupta
body:
# Sync WPBakery elements with the redesigned 2.0 blocks (Video Gallery, Audio, Video) 

Issue - rtCamp/godam-plugin-wp#19

## Summary

The GoDAM 2.0 redesign added new attributes and controls to the Video Gallery, Audio, and Video blocks, but the corresponding **WPBakery (Visual Composer)** elements were never updated, so those options were missing from the page builder. This PR brings all three WPBakery elements (and their shortcodes) up to parity with the redesigned Gutenberg blocks, and fixes the Video block preview not rendering inside the WPBakery inline editor.

Branch: `update/godam-blocks-wp-bakery` → `develop`

## Background

Each GoDAM media block has a matching WPBakery element that renders through a shortcode (`base` → shortcode name), and each shortcode reuses the block's server template/`render.php`. When the blocks were redesigned, the new attributes were added to the blocks and their templates, but not surfaced in the WPBakery element params or mapped in the shortcodes — so WPBakery users couldn't configure them.

One important constraint throughout: WordPress' `shortcode_parse_atts()` lowercases every attribute name, so WPBakery params use lowercase/snake_case names that are then mapped to the blocks' camelCase attribute keys in each shortcode.

## Changes by block

### Video Gallery (`godam/gallery-v2`)
- **Layout:** added the **List** option (Grid / Carousel / List) — the block gained List in the redesign.
- **Interaction:** added an **Interaction** dropdown — *Play on hover* (default) vs *Autoplay all videos* — mapped to the block's mutually-exclusive `autoplay` / `playOnHover` booleans.
- **Show Play Button:** added a checkbox mapped to `showPlayButton`.
- Shortcode (`[godam_video_gallery]`): accepts `interaction` and `show_play_button`, splits `interaction` into `autoplay`/`playOnHover`, and passes `showPlayButton` to the shared template (which already consumes all three; playOnHover/showPlayButton default to `true`, matching the block).

Files: `inc/classes/wpbakery-elements/class-wpb-godam-video-gallery.php`, `inc/classes/shortcodes/class-godam-video-gallery.php`.

### Audio (`godam/audio`)
- **Added** the redesign's attributes as params: **Audio Title** (`audio_title` → `audioTitle`), **Description** (`description`), **Thumbnail** (`thumbnail`, empty falls back to the GoDAM-generated cover), **Show Transcript** (`show_transcript` → `showTranscript`, default on) and **Show Chapters** (`show_chapters` → `showChapters`, default on).
- **Removed** the obsolete **Caption** param — the redesign dropped it from the block and `render.php` no longer reads it.
- Selector param JS: auto-populates **Audio Title** and **Description** from the attachment on selection (parity with the block's `onSelectAudio`), and targets the `src` hidden field specifically via `[name="src"]` instead of any hidden field.
- Shortcode (`[godam_audio]`): maps the new snake_case atts to the block's camelCase keys the shared `render.php` consumes (transcript/chapters default to `true`).

Files: `inc/classes/wpbakery-elements/class-wpb-godam-audio.php`, `inc/classes/shortcodes/class-godam-audio.php`, `assets/src/js/wpbakery/wpbakery-audio-selector-param.js`.

### Video (`godam/video`)
- **Added** the two new Playback-Controls toggles the redesign introduced: **Show Transcription** (`show_transcription` → `showTranscription`) and **Show Caption** (`show_caption` → `showCaption`), both defaulting to Yes (matching the block toggles' `true` defaults).
- Shortcode (`[godam_video]`): maps these to the block's camelCase attributes **only when explicitly provided**, so hand-written `[godam_video]` shortcodes keep the template's own defaults (transcription on; caption derived from the attachment's Display-captions setting). The template already honors an explicit `showCaption`/`showTranscription`.

Files: `inc/classes/wpbakery-elements/class-wpb-godam-video.php`, `inc/classes/shortcodes/class-godam-player.php`.

### Fix: Video preview not rendering in the WPBakery inline editor

**Problem:** In the WPBakery inline editor the Video block showed only a play button on a zero-height area — the player was stuck in its pre-init state (`easydam-video-container.loading` / `vjs-hidden`, 0×0).

**Root cause:** `godam-player/frontend.js` initialized players **only** on `DOMContentLoaded`. WPBakery renders the shortcode markup into its preview iframe *after* that event has already fired, so `PlayerManager` never ran against the block and the player was never initialized. (Gutenberg avoids this by rendering its own React player in the editor; WPBakery uses the shortcode path.)

**Fix (in `assets/src/js/godam-player/frontend.js`):**
- Run initialization immediately when the DOM is already parsed (`readyState` fallback), not only on `DOMContentLoaded`.
- Add deferred re-init passes (300/1200/3000 ms). `PlayerManager.initializeVideo()` is idempotent — guarded by `data-godam-initialized` — so a re-run only initializes players that were missed; on a normal front-end load where everything is already initialized this is a cheap `querySelector` no-op.
- In a WPBakery editor preview only (detected via the `#vc_inline-frame` wrapper / `vc_editor` body class), attach a `MutationObserver` that re-initializes on demand as elements are re-rendered during editing. No observer is attached on the published front end.

Verified live in the inline editor: after a plain reload the player initializes on its own (0×0 → 645×363, `loading` cleared, `data-godam-initialized="1"`). Because the changes are additive and idempotent, published-page behavior is unchanged (init still runs once; the deferred passes find nothing pending).

## How to test

1. Ensure WPBakery (`js_composer`) is active. Run `npm run build:js` and `npm run build:blocks` (build artifacts under `assets/build/` are gitignored).
2. **Video Gallery:** add the GoDAM → Video Gallery element; confirm Layout offers List, the Interaction dropdown switches autoplay/hover, and Show Play Button toggles the overlay on the front end.
3. **Audio:** add the Audio element, select an audio file → Title/Description auto-fill; set a Thumbnail; toggle Show Transcript / Show Chapters and confirm on the front end.
4. **Video:** add the Video element; toggle Show Transcription / Show Caption and confirm the transcript button / captions on the front end.
5. **Editor preview:** open the WPBakery inline editor on a page with a Video element and confirm the player renders (not just a play button) after load.

## Notes for reviewers

- Build files (`assets/build/**`) are gitignored — rebuild with `npm run build:js` / `npm run build:blocks`.
- The `frontend.js` change is on the shared player bundle used by all render paths; it is additive and idempotent (single init on the front end; deferred passes are no-ops when nothing is pending).

## Demo Video

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f864eb05-e9a7-4c0e-acc3-1839bf66f7e7

body: Closes #2220 Builds the physical ADR archive lane and the safety net every later lifecycle operation depends on. **No ADR is archived by this PR** — it lands the lane and the guard, movement comes later. ## Changes | File | What | |---|---| | `.red/adr/archive/.gitkeep` | the append-only archive lane, empty | | `.red/adr/INDEX.md` | new **Archived** section documenting the convention | | `apps/dev/src/core/adr-governance.ts` | governance primitives extracted (new) | | `apps/dev/tests/adr-governance.test.ts` | guard extended to treat archived as first-class | ## Human review — sensitive path This parked as `blocked:sensitive-path` because it touches `.red/adr/`, which is correct: the ADR tree is exactly the surface that should require a human before landing. Reviewed against the issue's acceptance, with particular attention to whether the guards are **enforced** rather than merely present — an exported-but-unwired guard is worse than none, because it reads as protection. All three are wired into live tests, not just exported: ``` adr-governance.test.ts:40 undocumentedGaps([...active, ...archived], index) adr-governance.test.ts:49 archivedRecordViolations({ file, text }) adr-governance.test.ts:59 appendOnlyViolations(present, deleted) ``` `deletedArchivePaths(ROOT, ARCHIVE_REL)` reads real git state rather than a fixture, so **removing a file from the archive fails CI** — which is the property the issue asked for. The guard is itself covered: `:83` stays green when an ADR migrates into the archive, `:91` goes red when an archived number disappears. Net effect on the protected surface is to **strengthen** it: the bijection now spans `active ∪ archived`, terminal records must carry a `superseded-by:` successor pointer, and archive deletions are rejected. ## One policy note, not a blocker `superseded` and `deprecated` must name a successor, but `inert` may write `superseded-by: none (inert)`. That is a reasonable carve-out for a record that shipped and stopped being guidance — and it is also the only door through which an ADR leaves the active set without pointing anywhere. Worth watching that `inert` stays rare, or the archive becomes a graveyard rather than an index. Unblocks the chain #2222 → #2223 → #2224. --- Need help on this PR? Tag /codesmith with what you need. Autofix is disabled.

body:
Follow-up to #112. The first mirror deploy on `main` failed during `Collecting page data` with `TypeError: Invalid URL, input: ''`.

## Cause

The deploy workflow passes `${{ vars.NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL }}`, and that repo variable is not set — so the build received an **empty string**, not `undefined`. The `?? "https://ml-viz-ruby.vercel.app"` fallbacks in `next.config.ts` and `src/lib/site.ts` only catch nullish values, so `SITE_URL` became `""` and `metadataBase: new URL(SITE_URL)` in `layout.tsx` threw at build time.

author: mauricecarrier7
body:
## What

`AudiobookPlaybackModel.updateLockScreenCoverArtwork` built its `MPMediaItemArtwork` with a plain (non-`@Sendable`) request handler that closes over `image`:

```swift
let itemArtwork = MPMediaItemArtwork(boundsSize: image.size) { _ in image }
```

MediaPlayer invokes **and destroys** that handler on its own background queue (it rasterizes lazily via `-[MPMediaItemArtwork jpegDataWithSize:]` when building the Now-Playing / lock-screen info). The block-destroy released the captured `UIImage` off-main, racing the image's main-thread lifetime → **`block_destroy_helper` EXC_BREAKPOINT**.

## Crash

Crashlytics **`e672637`** — `[PalaceAudiobookToolkit] block_destroy_helper.46`, FATAL, on Palace 3.2.0 audiobook opens.

## Fix

Capture an immutable local and mark the handler `@Sendable`, so the block's captured state is provably safe to build/tear-down off the main thread. This **mirrors the app-side `NowPlayingCoordinator` fix (Palace #1218)**, which resolved the *identical* crash on the app's own now-playing artwork path — zero recurrence on 3.3.0 builds since.

## Verification

- Toolkit CI is the build gate.
- Runtime confirmation is via Crashlytics (zero new `e672637` on builds carrying this fix) — the trap can't be reproduced on demand (needs MediaPlayer to rasterize + release within the racing window).

The kiro agent JSON's prompt field was pointed at the installed package's own copy of AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS.md, resolved from the project/site-packages path at install time. Moving the checkout or reinstalling into a different venv left the prompt pointing at a stale, nonexistent path.

author: shashiraj75
body:
## Incident

A production US Daily Picks request correctly returned `resource_busy` while `US_YFINANCE_HEAVY` was held by a Multibagger refresh, but it left behind a committed `queued` Daily Picks job with no lease and no background runner.

Confirmed ghost job:

`e49d84bf-c19e-4c1c-9a2e-5c1da3f676c3`

## Root cause

`postgres_store` uses a connection pool configured with `autocommit=True`.

The previous reservation functions inserted the job row and lease row as separate autocommitted statements, then attempted `conn.rollback()` when the lease insert conflicted. At that point, the job insert had already committed.

Affected functions:

- `try_reserve_daily_picks_job_with_lease`
- `try_reserve_multibagger_job_with_lease`

## Fix

Both reservation paths now use one explicit Psycopg transaction covering the job insert and lease insert.

A private internal outcome exception exits conflict paths through transaction rollback before the existing public return string is produced.

Public signatures and outcomes remain unchanged.

## Validation

- exact production ghost-row condition reproduced against the previous implementation;
- focused transaction tests pass against the candidate and fail against the previous implementation;
- all three required atomicity mutations were detected;
- lifecycle tests: 76 passed;
- related job-state tests: 100 passed;
- complete backend suite: 3233 passed;
- independent review: PASS WITH REQUIRED FOLLOWUP.

## Scope

Changed only:

- `backend/services/postgres_store.py`
- `backend/tests/regression/test_weekly_multibagger_lifecycle.py`

No schema, route, scheduler, workflow, timeout, frontend or production-data change.

## Separate follow-up

The following pre-existing autocommit risks were reviewed and classified as non-blocking follow-ups; they are intentionally excluded from this PR:

- `try_claim_queued_multibagger_job`;
- `reconcile_stale_multibagger_jobs`;
- `reconcile_stale_daily_picks_jobs`.

## Deployment and recovery

This PR does not recover the existing ghost row and does not rerun US Daily Picks. Those actions require separate authorization after merge and deployment verification.

author: stenehrlich-tuleva
body:
Backend slice for letting the **second parent** of a child see and join the child's savings-fund account. Draft — compliance sign-off (Maria) gates the merge, not the review.

## What it does
When one parent opens a child's account, we capture the **other** guardian(s) from the population register and create a `PENDING_KYC` `parent_child_link` for each. That link **grants no access** — it only lets the other parent *discover* the child (`GET /v1/me/pending-child-onboardings`) and later *join* via their own onboarding/KYC, which activates the link.

## The invariant (a pending link must never authorize anything)
Enforced at the **repository** so it can't be forgotten at a call site: the three "active representation" / "other active parents" `@Query` methods bake in `status = ACTIVE`. Verified every consumer inherits it:
- **Role switch** — `RoleSwitchService.getRoles` (ACTIVE-only finder) + `switchToRepresentedChild` guard via `isActiveRepresentation`.
- **Parent payments** — `PaymentVerificationService.isAuthorizedRemitter` → `isActiveRepresentation` (now ACTIVE-only).
- **Notification sender** — `ParentChildLinkNotificationSender.otherActiveParents` reads the repo directly; that finder is now ACTIVE-only.

The unfiltered `…AndRelationshipType` finder is used **only** by registration/activation, never on an auth path. Tests prove each path excludes PENDING (`ParentChildLinkRepositoryTest`, `RoleSwitchServiceTest#switchToPendingChildIsRejected`, `builderDefaultsStatusToActive`).

## How the co-parent is found
A child-subject custody query — `fetchCustodyRights(requester, subject)` — returns both guardians (RR already returns the full record; verified live). The cache is **bypassed** for it so each requester's X-Road call is distinct and audited. A direction-neutral `Guardian` type is used instead of overloading the parent-oriented `CustodyRight` (whose `childPersonalCode`/`childAlive` fields are wrong-way-round for a child subject).

## Deviations flagged for review
1. **Activation is on `KycCheckPerformedEvent`, not `SavingsFundOnboardingCompletedEvent`.** The child's aggregate completion fires once (first parent only); the KYC-check event fires per parent, so activation stays per-co-parent and endpoint-agnostic. It gates on `PERSONAL_ONBOARDING` + risk `LOW/NONE` (MEDIUM/HIGH never activate). The acting parent isn't on the event (subject is the child), so it's read from the synchronous request's `SecurityContext`.
2. **⚠️ Known end-to-end gap (the piece to design next):** the existing KYC survey is submitted by a parent *role-switched to the child* — but the invariant (correctly) blocks role-switching to a PENDING child, so a co-parent **cannot yet drive the child's KYC** through the current endpoint, and their activation won't fire. All backend building blocks are in place (`resolvePendingChildCode` — scoped join resolution; `activate`; the completion listener). The missing piece is the **frontend join flow + a dedicated join endpoint** that mints a scoped child capability from the resolved pending id, so the co-parent can complete the child's KYC without a prior active role-switch. Deliberately did **not** activate on onboarding-start (that would grant access before KYC).
3. **`registerPending` uses portable find-first + save, not `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`** (H2 test DB lacks `ON CONFLICT`). Same guarantees (idempotent, never downgrades ACTIVE, silent). Residual: a same-instant race where two guardians open the *same* child could hit the unique constraint; `ChildOnboardingService` swallows it (log + continue) so the opening parent's onboarding is unaffected.

## Tests
`compileJava`/`compileTestJava` clean; targeted suites green (`ParentChildLink*`, `Custody*`, `RoleSwitch*`, `ChildOnboarding*`, `PopulationRegister*` — 122 tests, incl. a new `ParentChildLinkActivationListenerTest`). One transient H2 flake (shared in-memory schema drop across many Spring contexts, a known repo infra issue) did not reproduce on re-run.

## Next
Frontend PR (switcher merge + join flow) + the join endpoint that closes gap #2.

author: he-weiwen
body:
Currently padded shared layout cannot vectorise for permuted register orders - the `largestVectorisation` utility gates permutation with

```cpp
allowPerm = !maybeMaxVecElems.has_value(); 
```

which confuses two separate concerns: 1. whether to allow permutation 2. whether there’s a cap to the vectorisation size. 

I believe the original intention was to guarantee that an identical register ordering is used in both the global-register and the shared-register parts of the vectorisation proof for `cp.async` (#7314), where `maybeMaxVecElems` is supplied as the global-reg vectorisation size ('maxVec'), so in effect its just “don’t allow permute when reasoning about gloabl - shared traffic”.

However, the padded shared layout, which isn’t linear on GF(2) itself, uses a linearised layout for the purpose of the layout maths and prevent vectorising across padding boundary by using the padding interval as value to `maybeMaxVecElems`. There’s no reason why permuting registers shouldn’t work here - it’s just renaming SSA values and purely logical.

This patch lifted `allowPerm` as a separate argument to `largestVectorisation` (including indirectly through `lowerLdSt` / `lowerLdStShared`)and switched it to `true` for every call site that vectorise a padded shared encoding to register traffic (generic local_load/store and nvidia `st.async`). The behaviour remain unchanged for all other uses of `largestVectorisation` .


| callsite | purpose | MaybeMaxVecElem | allowPerm |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Utility.cpp` `lowerLocalLdSt` | `local_load`/`local_store` (incl. padded) | `getMinInterval` if padded, else `nullopt` | `false → true` |
| `Ops.cpp` `AsyncSharedStoreOp::verify` |  `st.async` verification | `getMinInterval` if padded, else `nullopt` | `false → true` |
| nv `MemoryOpToLLVM` `lowerAsyncSharedStore` |  `st.async' lowering | `getMinInterval` if padded, else `nullopt` | `false → true` |
| nv `LoadStoreOpToLLVM`  | `cp.async`  | `maxVec` | `false` |
| amd `LoadStoreOpToLLVM`  | AMD async direct to LDS  | `vec` | `false` |
| *amd `MemoryOpToLLVM`  | `ds_read_tr4_b64`  | `tileSize` | `false` |
| `Utility.cpp: finalizeTensorAtomicResults` | atomic-rmw staged ld/st | `{}` | `true` |
| lib + nv `ConvertLayoutOpToLLVM` (x4) | convert_layout via shared | `{}` (default) | `true` |
| `AccelerateAMDMatmul.cpp` | scale-preshuffle vec probe | `nullopt` | `true` |
| `GenericSwizzling.cpp` | swizzle / bank-conflict vec calc | `nullopt` | `true` |


*Note: By the same reasoning, permuting may also be safe for lowering AMD `ds_read_tr4_b64` - but it seems a missed vectorisation due to permuting register isn’t representable in the IR, so this patch conservatively didn’t touch it.

author: lexfrei
body:
## What this PR does

The `keycloak-configure` pre-delete teardown Job clears the Flux `HelmRelease` finalizers as its final step so the release can be uninstalled. That final `kubectl patch` targeted a hardcoded namespace that does not match where the release actually installs. The release installs into `cozy-keycloak`, and the teardown Job's own RBAC — a `Role` + `RoleBinding` granting `patch` on the `HelmRelease` by release name — is created in the release namespace, but the patch was aimed at `cozy-system`.

The result is a deadlock: the Job's `ServiceAccount` is `Forbidden` to patch the `HelmRelease` in the mismatched namespace, so the Job errors and retries forever, the `HelmRelease` sticks in `Terminating`, and the Helm release wedges in status `uninstalling`. This blocks any teardown or reinstall of the component.

The fix templates both the release name and the namespace from `{{ .Release.Name }}` / `{{ .Release.Namespace }}`, so the patch targets the namespace where the `HelmRelease` lives and where the teardown RBAC grants access. I also added a helm-unittest that pins the rendered target, guards against the hardcoded namespace regressing, and asserts the patch tracks the release name and namespace.

### Screenshots

N/A — no UI changes.

### Release note

```release-note
fix(keycloak-configure): fix the pre-delete teardown Job so uninstalling the release no longer wedges — it now patches the HelmRelease in the release namespace instead of a hardcoded one
```

author: wmadden-electric
body:
The two-step create in `postgres/Database.ts` — `POST /v1/projects/{projectId}/databases` then `PATCH /v1/databases/{databaseId}` `{ branchId }` — is the same shape ADR-0034 removed from the state database, and it carries the same unsafe window for user databases. #113 filed it as a known latent bug and left it out of scope; this closes it. (Supersedes #122, which was stacked on #113 before it merged.)

## Why the two-step is unsafe

A database created without a `branchId` is **born on the project's default Branch, never branchless** — `createPrismaPostgresDatabase` calls `getOrCreateDefaultBranch` inside its create transaction. ADR-0034 records the same platform fact. So on a **named-stage** deploy the two-step put the user's database on the **default Branch — production's** — and only moved it on the `PATCH`. A failed `PATCH`, or a CLI that died between the two calls, stranded a user database on production's Branch.

## The fix

Use the **flat** `POST /v1/databases`, which takes `projectId`, `name`, `region` (`'inherit'` supported), `isDefault`, and `branchId` in one request and validates the Branch before creating the row. This is what `state/bootstrap.ts`'s `createStateDatabase` does — the reference for this change.

The flat endpoint is **not atomic**: the platform still creates the row and attaches the Branch in two server-side steps. This **narrows** the window — one request, Branch validated before the row exists, no client-crash window between two calls — it does not close it. A failed attach can still leave a stray empty database, which costs a quota slot rather than correctness: the same residual #113 accepted for the state database. The comment in the code says exactly this and does not claim atomicity.

The `PATCH` stays on the **observed** path only, where there is no create to strand anything and it is what moves a database that drifted off its Branch back onto it.

## Scope checked

`compute/ComputeService.ts` and `compute/EnvironmentVariable.ts` already name the Branch in their create bodies — ComputeService with a comment explaining why — so neither needed a change. Rechecked against current `main`. Only `postgres/Database.ts` had the two-step.

## Verified

Re-run against current `main`, not carried over from the earlier branch: `typecheck` clean (which is what proves the flat body conforms to the SDK's `postV1Databases` schema, `branchId` included, on the installed 1.47.0), 123/123 lowering tests pass, cast ratchet `delta=0`. The tests were confirmed to catch the regression rather than merely pass: restoring `main`'s version of the source fails 3 of 5, and the fake client now throws on the project-scoped route so reaching for it fails loudly instead of silently passing.

author: zhengbuqian
body:
pr: #51625
issue: #51489
issue: #51567
issue: #51568

## What changed

- Canonicalize mixed-type JSON `IN` expressions into homogeneous predicates.
- Partition JSON values by their concrete type: bool, int64, float, string, and array.
- Keep int64 and float values in separate predicates to avoid precision loss around `2^53`.
- Make the following expression optimizations type-aware for JSON:
  - `== OR` to `IN`
  - `!= AND` to `NOT IN`
  - combinations involving `IN`, equality, inequality, and range predicates
- Lower JSON array-valued membership to equality branches because segcore does not support array-valued `TermExpr`.
- Apply JSON term canonicalization even when expression optimization is disabled.
- Allow scalar JSON `NOT(x == value)` to be rewritten as `x != value` while preserving UNKNOWN for null, missing paths, and type mismatches.
- Add a segcore validation guard that rejects heterogeneous JSON `TermExpr` values before selecting raw data, JSON stats, or JSON path index execution paths.

## Root cause

A JSON `TermExpr` could contain values with different protobuf value types. Segcore selected its executor from the first value, causing later values to be interpreted using the wrong type.

The optimizer could also combine different JSON literal types back into a single `TermExpr`. Additionally, converting mixed integer and floating-point values to float could lose int64 precision.

## Behavior

For example:

```text
json["key"] in [1, 2, "3"]
```

is normalized to:

```text
json["key"] in [1, 2] OR json["key"] == "3"
```

Mixed-type `NOT IN` remains a negation of the complete split membership expression, preserving three-valued logic:

```text
NOT(json["key"] in [1, 2] OR json["key"] == "3")
```

Non-JSON columns continue to use their statically determined schema type.

## Verification

- Go parser and rewriter tests:

```bash
go test -tags dynamic,test -gcflags="all=-N -l" -count=1 ./internal/parser/planparserv2/...
```

- Segcore mixed JSON Term validation test.
- Raw JSON filtering three-valued semantics tests.
- JSON path index precision and `!=` semantics tests.
- JSON stats/shredding null, missing-path, and large-int64 precision tests.

author: ilbertt
body:
On macOS 26 (Tahoe) the app icon rendered with a gray frame around it — in Finder after installing from the DMG, and in push notifications.

Tahoe masks every app icon to its own rounded-rect shape. Our icon was a pre-rounded squircle with transparent corners, so the system's default gray backing plate showed through around it. The fix is to ship a full-bleed, opaque square and let the OS apply the rounding.

`logo.{svg,png}` stays the rounded brand mark used in the README; `icon.{svg,png}` is the new full-bleed source, and `apps/mcping/build/icon.png` now points at it.

### Motivation
- The Blackhawks ICS calendar normalizer marks every ICS event as `"FUT"`, which caused `fetch_blackhawks_last_game()` and `fetch_blackhawks_live_game()` to never see API-derived `OFF` or live states when the calendar contained entries.

### Description
- Introduced `_fetch_blackhawks_api_schedule_games()` to fetch the NHL API schedule independently of the ICS helper in `data_fetch.py`.
- Converted the existing schedule helper into `_fetch_blackhawks_schedule_games(prefer_ics: bool = True)` which prefers ICS for schedule/next lookups but falls back to the API; left next-game logic unchanged to still prefer ICS results via `fetch_blackhawks_next_game()`.
- Updated `fetch_blackhawks_last_game()` and `fetch_blackhawks_live_game()` to read from the new `_fetch_blackhawks_api_schedule_games()` so API `OFF` and live states are preserved even when ICS entries exist.
- Added regression tests in `tests/test_data_fetch_blackhawks_ics.py` to verify that `fetch_blackhawks_last_game()` and `fetch_blackhawks_live_game()` return API stateful results when the ICS schedule only contains FUT entries.

## Summary
Follow-up to #121, fixing a CodeRabbit finding that landed just after that PR merged.

- The unified timeline's synthetic event ids were derived from each event's position in the sorted/sliced array (`${type}-${rawDate}-${i}`). Since that position shifts whenever a newer event is inserted ahead of existing ones, every event after the insertion point would get a *different* id on the next render — churning React keys and unnecessarily remounting timeline rows that hadn't actually changed.

body:
## Production surface — Rack (desktop) + Tap (mobile), bound to the real engine

Sheds the throwaway reference UI and ships the two directions Daniel picked, as **one responsive surface** over `window.LUFSRec`. Design pass history: three directions → Rack + Tap → this build.

### What changed
- **`index.html`** — engine block (`window.LUFSRec`) preserved **byte-for-byte**; the reference-UI `<style>` + DOM + UI `<script>` replaced with the production surface.
- **`icons/icon.svg`** — new little-brother favicon (also inlined as the tab favicon data-URI in `index.html`).
- **`sw.js`** — `CACHE` bumped `lufs-rec-v0.2.0` → `lufs-rec-v0.3.0`.

### The surface (responsive, single binding)
- **≥ 820px — Rack · Graphite.** Channel strip (mode + device inputs + grants) · meter-bridge (dial + L/R meters + dBFS scale) · **live kslider keyboard monitor** in the bridge · stat readouts · per-take bar-waveform + sequencer-grid piano roll.
- **< 820px — Tap · Full-bleed.** Segmented mode pill · big radial dial with ring-meter · caps-forward line · full-width record bar · colour-railed takes with line-waveform + note-lane roll. Full-bleed (no device frame) = the most device-agnostic install target.

### Frontend wiring (what it binds to — no engine forking)
- **Capabilities:** reads `LUFSRec.caps` (`secure`, `midi`, `gum`, `worklet`, `iframed`, `iOS`) → caps chip, mobile caps-line ("audio-only, no Web MIDI here" on iOS), insecure/iframed banner, and mode-aware enable gating.
- **Devices:** `grantAudio()` / `grantMidi()` / `refreshAudioDevices()` populate the selects.
- **Capture:** `setMode` / `setName` / `start({mode,device,midiPort})` / `stop()`.
- **Live:** `onStatus({elapsed_s, level, frames, midi, drop})` drives the dial timer, L/R meters, ring-meter, and stat grid. `onMidi({status,data})` drives the midimon **and lights the kslider** in real time.
- **Per take:** waveform from `take.audio.peaks`, piano roll from `take.midi.notes`, checks from `take.verification.checks` (gating vs. info shown honestly), transport from `take.transport` (one control set → play/scrub, playheads, and **kslider re-lights on scrub-back**). Downloads use `take._wavBlob`, `take._midiEvents`, and `LUFSRec.serializeTake(take)`.
- **PWA:** registers `./sw.js`; all paths relative.

### Verification (ran locally — verifier ethos)
- `bash scripts/verify` → **VERIFY: PASS** (zero external origins ✓, all refs relative ✓, versioned SW cache ✓, well-formed + marker ✓).
- `bash scripts/package` → **green**, dist provenance emitted (5 files, 61,468 b, artifact `sha256 7188af3f…` on the local staging tree; the real digest is recomputed at deploy).
- Rendered + eyeballed at desktop and 414px mobile widths.

### Notes for the reviewer (Ciani)
1. **Engine untouched** — please confirm the `window.LUFSRec` block is identical to `main` (diff should be limited to head `<style>`, body DOM, and the second `<script>`).
2. **Provenance** is a deploy-time artifact (`scripts/package` → `dist/`), not committed — no action here; the artifact digest will change (expected).
3. **Two honest gaps to weigh (surface-driven, engine-owned):**
   - **Per-channel live meters.** `onStatus.level` is a single aggregate, so L and R currently show the same value. A per-track live level in the status payload (the same shape as the earlier levels-stream note) would make the L/R VU truthful. Cosmetic until then; flagged, not faked.
   - **Fonts.** Zero-external-origins means no webfont link, so the surface uses a system stack (brand is Host Grotesk / Public Sans / Space Mono). Self-hosting those as local `woff2` under a relative path keeps `external-origins = none` **and** restores the brand type — happy to do that follow-up if you want it in this release.

Branch off `main`, no force-push, `.github/workflows` untouched (deploy stays staged in `ci/`).

author: trpaslik444
body:
Implementuje `docs/INVITE_FEDERATION_REDESIGN.md` §3.4 (bod 2 doporučeného pořadí PR).

> **Nezávislé na #15** (rules sync) — dá se review/merge zvlášť.

## Proč na firemním backendu

Dnes se zvací odkaz kopíruje ručně. Centrální projekt běží na **Sparku** a e-maily posílat nemůže → odesílání je **firemní-backendová schopnost**: pozvánka odchází z domény firmy (její SPF/DKIM), centrál nedrží mail tajemství ani nenese náklady. Konzistentní s federačním modelem.

## Rozhodnutí: callable funkce, ne „Trigger Email from Firestore"

Návrh nabízel obě cesty. Zvolena **callable funkce**, protože extension **nemá kam pověsit autorizaci** — kdokoli, kdo smí zapsat do `mail/{id}`, by rozeslal libovolný obsah a libovolný odkaz podepsaný **DKIM firmy**. To je otevřená relay a přesně ten typ díry, který jsme právě zavírali v `pendingInvites` (#396). Callable ověří volajícího **dřív**, než sáhne na providera. Extension je navíc SMTP-orientovaná, což se s vybraným Resendem tluče.

## Bezpečnostní model

Funkce **nevěří klientovi nic kromě identity**:

| # | Kontrola |
|---|---|
| 1 | Volající je přihlášený do firemního backendu (přes `authExchange`, uid == centrální uid) |
| 2 | Je **správcem projektu** — zrcadlí `canManageProject()` z `firestore.rules` (role `admin` na projektu NEBO workspace owner/admin) |
| 3 | Pozvánka `workspaces/{wid}/invites/{token}` **skutečně existuje**, patří danému projektu, je **schválená** (#367), nepoužitá a neexpirovaná |
| 4 | `inviteUrl` míří na origin z **allowlistu** a **obsahuje daný token** |

Body 3 a 4 nejsou kosmetika — bez nich je funkce mail relay firemní domény. Adresná pozvánka navíc smí odejít jen na svůj `inviteeEmail`.

## Provider

Rozhraní `MailProvider` v samostatném modulu (`mailProvider.ts`), implementovaný **Resend** jako default (čisté HTTPS API, žádná SMTP závislost v balíčku, DKIM per doménu). Integrační bod pro **SendGrid** i **SMTP** je v kódu popsaný konkrétně. Klíč jde přes Functions secret, nikdy do repa.

Když mail nakonfigurovaný není → `failed-precondition` a FE spadne zpět na dnešní **„zkopírovat odkaz"**. Podporovaný režim, ne chyba.

## Ověření

`npm run check` → **17/17**. Ověřuje mj. že allowlist odmítne phishing na cizí doméně, lookalike doménu (`openbuildos.web.app.evil.com`), `http://`, odkaz na **cizí token**, `javascript:` schéma i subdoménu povolené domény; a že e-mail odmítne **CRLF injektáž hlaviček**. Legitimní tvary odkazu (krátký #400 i legacy s `k`) projdou.

## Mimochodem

`.gitignore` měl `functions/lib/` kotvené na kořen repa, takže build output v `selfhost/functions/lib/` **nikdy neignoroval**. Opraveno na `**/functions/lib/`.

## Zbývá (ne v tomto PR)

- **FE volání** po `handleCreateInvite` (`SettingsPage.tsx`) s fallbackem na kopírování — patří do FE repa.
- **Pointer v `functions/README.md`** — vynechán schválně, aby PR nekolidoval s rozpracovaným `revokeShareLinkAndRotateToken`. Setup je zatím v `selfhost/docs/INVITE_EMAIL.md`.

## Deploy

⚠️ **NEDEPLOYOVÁNO.** Vyžaduje Blaze (bbfs má) + secrety:

```
firebase functions:secrets:set RESEND_API_KEY --project bbfs-openbuildos --account Info@bbfs.cz
firebase functions:secrets:set INVITE_MAIL_FROM --project bbfs-openbuildos --account Info@bbfs.cz
firebase deploy --only functions --project bbfs-openbuildos --account Info@bbfs.cz
```

Předtím je potřeba ověřit doménu u Resendu. Deploy až pod dozorem — živý klient.

author: alvaroalonso-0
body:
Round-2 tester feedback **S4** (Doug's only real confusion): the dashboard activity feed valued every tick at **$0.00** because it summed a usually-empty portfolio-positions snapshot instead of the amount the dispatch actually moved — while Basescan showed the swaps plainly.

Token-amount approach (no price oracle): the agent has the calldata at dispatch time, so it decodes the amount there and stamps it on the event — no UI-side calldata decoding, no new dependency. For a stablecoin agent that amount **is** the dollar figure.

- **New `lib/dispatch-value.ts`** — decode the standard ERC-20 amount (`approve` / `transfer` / `transferFrom`) from calldata; format via the token's on-chain `decimals`. Undecodable calls (router swaps) → null (no amount shown, **never a fabricated $0.00**).
- **`run.ts`** — stamps `amount` + `tokenSymbol` + `tokenDecimals` + `amountKind` onto each `dispatch_approved`/`_executed`/`_reverted` event (decimals & symbol read on-chain, cached; native `value` handled).
- **Dashboard.jsx** — dispatch rows now show e.g. `5 USDC · 0x1234…` (an `approve` is labelled "allowance", not a transfer); the tick header no longer renders $0.00 from an empty snapshot.

Tests: +6 decoder cases; **CLI 74 + UI 72 green**, typecheck + build clean.

author: shahzadhaider1
body:
### Problem
With `scan_all_installations` enabled alongside `scan_users`, scans fail on org members' personal repos:
Configured repos were not found in any GitHub App installation: Member enumeration adds members' public personal repos as scan units, but the installation mapping in `ChunkUnit` rejects any repo that no app installation owns. GitHub App installations only ever contain repos owned by the installing account, so member personal repos can never match, even though they're public and clone fine with the default installation token (single-installation mode scans them without issue). A single unmappable unit also fails the whole run.

### Changes
- Enumeration: repos discovered outside installation listings (member personal repos) are now mapped to the default installation up front, so the mapping in ChunkUnit short-circuits with no extra API calls.
- Chunk time: for the case where `ChunkUnit` runs without enumeration state, a new fallback (mapRemainingAccessibleRepos) runs after installation listings and metadata matching both miss; if the default installation token can read the repo, it's mapped to the default installation and scanned; if not, the mapping still fails closed.
- `ensureRepoInstallation` does its check-and-set under a single lock so a concurrent mapping to a real installation is never overwritten.

### Testing
- New regression tests: member personal repo maps to the default installation (both at enumeration and chunk time); an unreadable repo still fails the mapping, so the check doesn't become fail-open.
- Flipped `TestMapExplicitReposToInstallationsRejectsRepoMissingFromInstallationList` -> `FallsBackToDefaultForReadableRepo`: its mock declares the repo readable by the default token, which is exactly the case this change legalizes. Host-mismatch, wiki, and inaccessible-repo rejection tests pass unchanged.
- Verified end-to-end against a real GitHub App on a test org: previously the scan died on the first member repo; now all org and member repos scan cleanly with identical results to a single-installation run.

### Checklist:
* [x] Tests passing (`make test-community`)?
* [x] Lint passing (`make lint` this requires [golangci-lint](https://golangci-lint.run/welcome/install/#local-installation))?

body:
## Summary

`DatabaseSeeder` already created a default admin login on a fresh install (`php artisan migrate:fresh --seed`, per the documented setup flow), but it had two problems:

- The password was hardcoded to the literal string `"password"` via `User::factory()->create()` — a well-known default, unsafe if this seeder is ever run against a real deployment.
- It used `create()` keyed on a hardcoded email, so re-running `db:seed` against a non-empty database (anything short of `migrate:fresh`) threw a duplicate-email error.

## Changes

- `admin_email`/`admin_password` added to `config/app.php`, reading `ADMIN_EMAIL` (default `admin@example.com`) and `ADMIN_PASSWORD` (default unset) from the environment.
- `DatabaseSeeder` now uses `User::updateOrCreate()` keyed on email — safe to re-run — and only calls `assignRole('Admin')` if the role isn't already assigned.
- If `ADMIN_PASSWORD` isn't set, the seeder generates a random 16-character password and prints it once via `$this->command->warn()`, instead of silently using `"password"`.
- `ADMIN_EMAIL`/`ADMIN_PASSWORD` documented in `.env.example`.

## Validation

- `php artisan db:seed --class=DatabaseSeeder` — confirms admin created with a generated password, printed to console.
- Re-ran the same command a second time — no duplicate-email error, no duplicate role assignment.
- `ADMIN_PASSWORD=... php artisan db:seed` — confirms the pinned password hashes correctly (verified via `Hash::check`) and no password is printed when it's explicitly set.
- `php artisan test --filter=Auth` — all 20 existing auth/role tests pass unchanged.

Not tied to a specific tracked issue — this is a standalone hardening fix for the seeded admin account used by the documented fresh-install flow (`apps/api/README.md` Step 7 / `migrate:fresh --seed`).

author: dfaure-kdab
body: Text: report the longest word as the min width when word-wrapping A word-wrapping Text reported a min width of 0, so a layout that has to shrink could squeeze it to nothing. With several texts in a row this is easy to hit: none of them sets a stretch factor, so each item gives up the same number of pixels, and a short text loses its whole width while the long ones next to it have barely moved. Measure the min- and max-content width with parley and use them as the min and preferred width. Both come out of a single layout, so this replaces the previous measurement rather than adding one: benchmarked at +3.5%, against +97% for measuring the minimum separately. The min has to be measured with OverflowWrap::Normal: for display we set OverflowWrap::Anywhere so overlong words break instead of overflowing, but that also makes every cluster a break opportunity, which would collapse the min-content width to a single character. A line limit drops the paragraphs that are not drawn, from both widths, so a word on a dropped line neither widens the item nor pushes the minimum above the preferred width. Note that the max-content width excludes trailing whitespace, so a word-wrapping text ending in spaces now has a slightly smaller preferred width than before. Every parley-backed renderer implements this. The software renderer only does so for vector fonts, mirroring the condition in its text_size(): with a bitmap font it returns None and both widths keep coming from text_size(), so they stay consistent with what that renderer actually draws. Such a text still has no minimum and can be squeezed away; the next commit fixes that. char-wrap keeps no minimum: it can legitimately break anywhere. Also spell out in the layout docs how shrinking is distributed. --- software renderer: min width for word-wrapping text with bitmap fonts The previous commit only gave word-wrapping text a minimum width on the parley path, so a build with EmbedTextures kept squeezing such text down to nothing. That is the configuration where the bitmap fonts win over system fonts for every text, so it was the whole text stack there. Add TextLayout::content_widths(): fragments end at line break opportunities and their width excludes trailing whitespace, so the widest fragment is the longest word. It measures both widths from one shaping pass, which matters on targets with little to spare. --- Before/after screenshots:

author: fieryzephyr
body:
## Problem (issue #110 — "Award points not given?")
Player award points were **0 for every user in every World Cup pool**, and it wasn't a scoring bug — **the winners could never be recorded**:

- `PUT /api/admin/player-award-results` exists on the backend, but **nothing in the frontend ever called it** — there was no admin screen for award results.
- Nothing auto-populates it either (football-data.org doesn't publish Golden Ball/Boot/Glove/Young Player/Fair Play).
- So `player_award_results` stayed empty and the scorer hit `if (!result) continue` → 0 for everyone ([index.js:1516](../blob/main/backend/index.js#L1516)).

Confirmed against a prod-backup copy: the table was `[]`.

## Change
Adds an **"Awards" tab** to the Admin Dashboard — one row per category showing the current winner (or an amber "Not set"), a dropdown, and Save:
- **Golden Ball / Boot / Glove / Young Player** → players, grouped by country (`/api/wc-players`, ~1,250 entries).
- **Fair Play** → team list.

## Why the Admin Dashboard (not Pool Settings)
`player_award_results` has **no `pool_id`** and `award_category` is **UNIQUE** — one set of winners for the whole tournament — and the endpoint is `requireAdminToken` (site admin). The *per-pool* award controls (lock / void) correctly stay in Pool Settings.

## Behaviour
- Re-saving a category **upserts**, replacing the previous winner (no duplicate rows).
- Points are **computed live** on every leaderboard/Breakdown request — correcting a wrong entry recalculates immediately, nothing cached. (Worth knowing: a correction silently drops points from anyone who briefly matched the wrong winner.)

## Verified
On a prod-backup copy, setting all five stored the correct shape (`player_id` for player awards, `team_id` for Fair Play) and immediately yielded **724 correct picks → 3,539 points across 632 participants**. Frontend lint clean. Frontend-only; no schema or backend change.

## After merge
The winners still need entering **on production** (the local test doesn't touch it). Per FIFA: Golden Ball **Rodri**, Golden Boot **Kylian Mbappé**, Golden Glove **Unai Simón**, Young Player **Pau Cubarsí**, Fair Play **Netherlands**.

## Summary

This branch combines the completed UI refresh and platform capability ports
with the OpenRouter provider consolidation.

### OpenRouter consolidation

- Replaces direct Cortecs and Mistral runtime paths with one server-side
  OpenRouter integration for chat, OCR, batch/live transcription and TTS.
- Adds the dynamic ZDR-compatible model catalogue, per-capability admin
  allowlists/defaults, TTS voice governance, safe one-time model fallback and
  paid atomic activation probes.
- Enforces `provider.zdr=true` and `provider.data_collection=deny` on every AI
  workload; keys and raw provider errors remain server-side.
- Migrates budgets, prices and usage accounting to USD without FX conversion,
  synchronizes allowed-model prices and records actual OpenRouter costs.
- Moves the Vexa transcription bridge to OpenRouter, normalizes TTS PCM before
  WAV concatenation and uses OpenRouter file parsing for scanned PDFs.
- Removes legacy provider panels/routes/runtime hosts and fixed production
  model IDs; keeps historical usage metadata and additive legacy columns.
- Adds the complete OpenSpec change under
  `openspec/changes/consolidate-ai-providers-openrouter/`.

### Earlier branch scope

- Quiet-precision UI tokens, shared primitives, screen passes, dark-theme AA
  fixes and accessibility improvements.
- Audit chain/export, budget runtime, offline field capture, bilingual export,
  PDF redaction and related platform capabilities.

  cleanup migration after the soak.

body:
## Resumen
Prepara el API de producto para **connection pooling** (Neon PgBouncer) — el "cambio de escala #1" del roadmap. La app corriendo usa un `DATABASE_URL` pooled (alta concurrencia); las migraciones usan `DIRECT_URL` (el pooler rompe el motor de migraciones).

## Cambios
| Archivo | Cambio |
|---|---|
| `apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma` | datasource declara `directUrl = env("DIRECT_URL")` |
| `apps/api/src/config/env.schema.ts` | `DIRECT_URL` opcional |
| `apps/api/test/setup-env.ts` | `DIRECT_URL` defaultea a `DATABASE_URL` (sin pooler local) |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | el step de migrate del producto pasa `DIRECT_URL` |
| `apps/api/.env.example` | documenta el split pooled/direct |

## Gotcha verificado empíricamente
`prisma validate`/`migrate` **fallan** (P1012) si el schema referencia `DIRECT_URL` y no está seteada; `prisma generate` **no** la necesita → **el Docker build está a salvo** (solo hace generate). Por eso el fix defaultea `DIRECT_URL` en dev/test/CI y solo el step de migrate lo setea explícito.

## Scope
Solo el API de producto (vivo en Neon). `viewpro-api` recibirá lo mismo cuando se deploye.

## Verificación
- [x] `prisma validate` OK (con DIRECT_URL)
- [x] `db:generate` OK **sin** DIRECT_URL → Docker build no afectado
- [x] `typecheck` limpio · e2e 17/17
- [ ] CI (migrate con DIRECT_URL + suite completa) — prueba final en este PR

## Activación en prod (no-código)
En Neon: usar el endpoint **pooled** (`?pgbouncer=true`) en `DATABASE_URL` y el **direct** en `DIRECT_URL`.

author: rmpgutah
body:
## Summary

The remainder of Group J ("child-process/network hardening") of the 10-group Electron desktop hardening program — **the final group of the entire 100-function program**. Group J's Tasks 1-4 (`buildSandboxedChildEnv`, `scheduleChildProcessTimeout` + its SIGTERM→SIGKILL escalation fixes, `isAtConcurrencyLimit`, `isAllowedBinaryName` + the per-tool `nmap-full`/`nmap-vuln` timeout override) were already merged separately via [#2906](https://github.com/rmpgutah/rmpg-flex/pull/2906) (built concurrently in a parallel session before this branch's remaining tasks landed). This PR is Tasks 5-10 plus a handful of fixes, properly merged onto current `main`.

1. **`isAllowedApiHost`** — exact-match host-pinning (no subdomain bypass) applied to every outbound `net.request` in `desktop/` — `geo:ip-locate`, `syncManager.js`'s pull/push/token-refresh calls, and `connectivityMonitor.js`'s health check (the last one was missed on the first pass, caught and fixed in review)
2. **`parseIpLocateResponse`** — fail-closed shape validation (`Number.isFinite`) on the Google Geolocation API response before it flows to the renderer, preserving the exact prior external contract
3. **`withRequestTimeout`** — a hand-rolled Promise/timer race (not bare `Promise.race`) with explicit cleanup on both settlement paths, hard-bounding `geo:ip-locate`, `offline:trigger-sync`, and `syncManager.js`'s previously fully-unbounded token-refresh call
4. **`formatSecurityAuditLine`/`appendSecurityAuditLog`** — a local, desktop-only JSON audit trail for PIN generation, recon spawn, backup import/export, and shortcut registration — every logged payload independently verified to contain only non-sensitive identifiers, never a PIN/secret/content value
5. Expanded Group F's insecure-command-line-flag list (`remote-debugging-port`/`-address`, `no-sandbox`, `allow-insecure-localhost`, `disable-site-isolation-trials`) and escalates a packaged-build violation into the new audit log
6. **`runHardeningSelfTest`** — aggregates Groups F/G/J's startup checks into one non-blocking diagnostic; rigorously verified (two independent defense-in-depth layers, hand-traced) to never block app launch under any failure combination — this is function #100 of the entire program

## Known items for reviewer attention

- **Task 5's "all `net.request` sites covered" claim was initially false** — `connectivityMonitor.js`'s health check was missed. Caught in review, fixed in-branch. A later whole-branch pass re-audited and found a 5th site (`main.js`'s own startup connectivity check) that was already correctly covered.
- **Mid-session shared-worktree hazard**: this branch (in its prior form) was hard-reset to `origin` by an external concurrent process partway through Task 5, discarding one local commit — fully recovered via `git reflog` and cherry-picked cleanly. A subsequent merge of `origin/main` also silently broke `sessionAuth.test.js`'s import (dropped `extractSessionIdentity` from the destructure) — caught by running the full suite rather than accepting an initial "pre-existing, unrelated" framing at face value, fixed directly.
- **This PR's base branch required a rebuild**: the original branch's PR (#2913) went stale when #2906 merged an earlier snapshot of the same shared branch under an identical name. This PR is that same work, freshly merged onto current `main` with conflicts resolved (kept both sides' additions — `main`'s Task 8 audit-log calls plus this branch's rest of the wiring).
- **One low-severity consistency gap found in the final whole-branch review**: `recon:check-binary` still spread the full parent env into its `command -v` probe child, unlike its sibling `recon:tool-spawn`. Fixed by reusing `buildSandboxedChildEnv`. Severity was low — `bash -c "command -v x"` is a builtin that never executes the target, so nothing actually received the leaked env.

## Test plan

- [x] `cd desktop && npm rebuild better-sqlite3 && npm test` — 398/398 passing (Node ABI), then `npm run rebuild` to restore Electron ABI
- [x] `node --check` on every touched file
- [x] No duplicate function definitions after the merge-conflict resolution (confirmed via grep: each of `runHardeningSelfTest`/`isAllowedApiHost`/`parseIpLocateResponse`/`withRequestTimeout` defined exactly once)
- [x] Full root vitest suite (231 files / 1913 tests) green
- [x] Final whole-branch holistic review (Opus, on the pre-rebuild branch) — cross-task consistency confirmed across the complete `childProcessGuard.js`, `geo:ip-locate`'s 3-layer stack (host-pin → timeout → shape validation) confirmed to compose correctly, `net.request` completeness re-audited, the never-blocks-startup guarantee independently hand-traced through both defense-in-depth layers
- [ ] Real device — manual verification of a live geolocation fallback lookup, an actual sync cycle, and the packaged-build startup self-test's console/audit-log output has not been performed in this session

## Program completion

This closes out the 10-group Electron desktop-shell hardening program. All 10 groups (F, G, H, A, B, C, D, E, I, J) are now merged or open for merge.
