body:
## Summary

The settlement engine was initializing Prisma with `new PrismaClient({ log: ... })` and setting `process.env.DATABASE_URL` as a side-effect, while the api-gateway and indexer both use a proper `pg.Pool → PrismaPg → PrismaClient` setup. This meant the settlement engine had an unbounded default connection pool with no configurable timeout.

## Changes

- **`services/settlement-engine/package.json`** — Add `pg@^8.22.0`, `@prisma/adapter-pg@^7.8.0`, and `@types/pg@^8.20.0` dependencies (matching api-gateway versions)
- **`services/settlement-engine/src/index.ts`** — Remove `process.env.DATABASE_URL` mutation; construct `pg.Pool` with explicit `max` and `connectionTimeoutMillis` from `env.DATABASE_POOL_SIZE` / `env.DATABASE_POOL_TIMEOUT`; wrap in `PrismaPg` adapter; pass adapter to `PrismaClient`
- **`services/settlement-engine/src/prisma-adapter.test.ts`** — 9 new tape tests verifying the adapter pattern (imports, pool config, adapter wrapping, PrismaClient setup, no side-effect)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] pg.Pool, PrismaPg adapter, and explicit pool config matching the gateway pattern
- [x] buildPrismaConnectionUrl result used with the adapter (not setting process.env.DATABASE_URL)
- [x] process.env.DATABASE_URL side-effect removed
- [x] Pool size and timeout configurable via DATABASE_POOL_SIZE / DATABASE_POOL_TIMEOUT env vars
- [x] Test verifying the adapter is configured correctly

## Testing

All 51 tests pass:
- 36 settlement-precision tests
- 7 genReqId-usage tests
- 9 prisma-adapter tests (new)

Closes #253

body:
## Summary

Adds a curated operational-knowledge wiki in [Open Knowledge Format v0.1](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/knowledge-catalog/blob/main/okf/SPEC.md), a uv-managed Python tool that validates and indexes it, and Claude Code skills so both humans and agents can maintain it.

### `wiki/` — the OKF bundle
- Root `index.md` (declares `okf_version: "0.1"`), `log.md` update history, and three sections: `infrastructure/`, `playbooks/`, `services/`.
- Nine concept pages migrated from existing docs (postgresql, nats, rabbitmq, ldap, haproxy, tls certs, build/deploy workflow, plus `notes/storage.md` split into OpenEBS and Longhorn-teardown pages). Migration is copy-not-move: originals stay put and each page's `resource` field points back at its source.
- `maintaining-the-wiki.md` documents page anatomy, reserved files, and the change procedure.
- Subdirectory `index.md` files are generated from page frontmatter, never hand-edited.

### `scripts/okf/` — validator and indexer
- `uv run okf check wiki` — conformance ERRORs (OKF001–007: missing/malformed frontmatter, empty `type`, reserved-file violations, unreadable files) and lint WARNs (OKF101–110: dead links, missing recommended fields, index drift, log ordering, links escaping the bundle, symlinked directories). Text or `--format json` output; exit codes 0/1/2; `--strict` promotes warnings.
- `uv run okf index wiki` — regenerates subdirectory indexes; `--check` reports drift without writing.
- PyYAML is the only runtime dependency; stdlib argparse CLI; 74 table-driven pytest cases; ruff-clean.

### `skills/` — five new Claude Code skills
`writing-wiki-pages`, `migrating-docs-to-wiki`, `searching-the-wiki`, `validating-the-wiki`, and `updating-the-wiki` (an end-of-task staleness check that fires after ordinary deployment work). A committed `.claude/skills -> ../skills` symlink makes Claude Code auto-discover all repo skills at session start (verified with a headless session), and a new `CLAUDE.md` makes the staleness check a standing instruction.

## Test plan
- `cd scripts/okf && uv run pytest` — 74 passed
- `uv run ruff check .` and `uv run ruff format --check .` — clean
- `uv run okf check --strict ../../wiki` and `uv run okf index --check ../../wiki` — 0 errors, 0 warnings, no drift across 15 files
- Negative tests: an emptied `type` produces `ERROR OKF003` (exit 1); a dead link produces `WARN OKF101` (exit 0, exit 1 with `--strict`)
- Headless `claude -p` session in the repo lists all skills via the symlink

author: copilot
body:
The `Post next step content` job was failing during workflow handoff because the next workflow was enabled by display name and errored when GitHub could not resolve that name. This change makes the handoff resilient when the next workflow is already active or only reliably addressable by file name.

- **Root cause**
  - `gh workflow enable "Step 2"` / `gh workflow enable "Step 3"` depended on workflow display names.
  - In the failing run, GitHub returned `could not find any workflows named Step 2`, causing the job to fail after comments had already been posted.

- **Workflow handoff changes**
  - Resolve the next workflow by file name instead of display name:
    - `2-step.yml`
    - `3-last-step.yml`
  - Query the next workflow state before enabling it.
  - Skip `gh workflow enable` when the target workflow is already active.

- **Failure mode reduction**
  - Reorder the handoff so the current workflow is disabled only after the next workflow has been confirmed or safely skipped.
  - This avoids leaving the exercise progression in a broken intermediate state if workflow lookup fails.

- **Example**
  ```yaml
  run: |
    next_workflow_state="$(gh workflow view "2-step.yml" --json state --jq '.state')"

    if [ "$next_workflow_state" != "active" ]; then
      gh workflow enable "2-step.yml"
    else
      echo "Workflow 2-step.yml is already active."
    fi

    gh workflow disable "${{github.workflow}}"
  ```

## Problem
Cloudflare Workers AI expects message content as a plain string. OpenAI-compatible clients send content as an array of content parts. LiteLLM was forwarding the array unchanged, causing Cloudflare to return:

Override _transform_messages in CloudflareChatConfig to flatten content-part arrays to a single joined string before forwarding. Non-text parts are dropped. Plain string content passes through unchanged.

Fixes #33984

author: mvalee
body:
## Problem

`get_edge_invalidation_candidates` matches every `RELATES_TO` edge touching either endpoint of a candidate edge, collects them all, and only then slices to `RELEVANT_SCHEMA_LIMIT` (10). Each collected row carries `fact_embedding`, plus `attributes: properties(e)` which repeats the same embedding.

On a graph with high-degree entities this materialises an entire neighbourhood in order to return ten rows.

## Measurements

Neo4j 5.26 Community, ~32.6k `Episodic` / ~22.8k `Entity` / ~101k `RELATES_TO`, 1024-dim embeddings. Sampling `SHOW TRANSACTIONS` at 150ms intervals:

- a single call peaked at **712 MiB against a 716.8 MiB** `db.memory.transaction.total.max`
- after raising the pool to **1.4 GiB**, the same query still exhausted it

Both figures are ceiling-bounded rather than true demand, which is the point: the collect is unbounded, so no pool size fixes it. Cost tracks the degree of the busiest entity, which grows monotonically as a graph fills. In our deployment the top entity had a `RELATES_TO` degree of 15,535.

## Why this is more than a slow query

The resulting `TransientError` reaches `await job()` in `AsyncWorker.worker()`, which catches only `asyncio.CancelledError`. The ingestion worker dies and is never respawned, while `POST /messages` keeps returning `202` and `/healthcheck` keeps returning OK. Ingestion stops with every health surface green.

## Fix

Neo4j's `CALL` subquery applies `ORDER BY` + `LIMIT` per `edge` row, so at most `$limit` rows per candidate ever materialise. Same rows, same order.

## Verification

Both queries run against a production graph with identical inputs:

**Correctness** - across 40 sampled candidate edges, results are identical as sets (same keys, same match counts, same uuids). Two differed only in ordering, which is the equal-score tie case and is already non-deterministic in the current query.

**Memory** - `PROFILE` on edges attached to the highest-degree entity:

| | memory | time |
|---|---|---|
| before | 571,073,600 bytes (544.6 MiB) | 7,416 ms |
| after | 588,488 bytes (0.56 MiB) | 5,303 ms |

Roughly 970x less memory, and faster.

## Scope

Gated to `GraphProvider.NEO4J`. The default branch also serves FalkorDB, whose `CALL` subquery support I could not verify, so it is left untouched. Kuzu and Neptune are unchanged.

Two related things I noticed but deliberately did **not** change, happy to follow up if useful:

- The Kuzu branch already applies `LIMIT` before `collect`, but after `UNWIND` without a per-row subquery, so it appears to cap total matches rather than matches per candidate edge.
- `get_relevant_edges` has the same collect-then-slice shape. It is pair-constrained so far cheaper (8 MiB worst case measured here), and keeping it out keeps this PR reviewable.

Related: #723 and #763 (the worker-death amplification described above is what makes these token/limit issues expensive in practice).

author: yossicharash
body:
Fixes three of six calendar issues reported by the user. The other three could not be reproduced from the code and are listed at the bottom.

## 1. Task attachment links break ("file not found")

**Root cause.** Attachments are uploaded to S3 with no ACL, and the resulting plain URL is stored in the DB and handed straight to the browser. On a bucket that blocks public access — the AWS default since 2023 — every such link returns 403, which surfaces in the UI as "file not found" when reopening a task. On a bucket that *doesn't* block it, every attachment is world-readable to anyone holding the URL.

Every other S3 consumer in this codebase reads objects **through the backend** with server credentials (`unforeseen_transactions.py`, `group_transaction_drafts.py`, `report_service.py`). Task attachments were the sole exception, and no presigning helper existed anywhere in the repo.

**Fix.** `_attachment_file_url` now exchanges the stored URL for a short-lived signed URL on each read. The S3 wrapper is `lru_cache`d because signing runs once per attachment when rendering a task or a chat, and building a boto3 client per call is expensive. Signing is a local computation — no network round-trip. TTL is configurable via `AWS_S3_PRESIGNED_URL_TTL_SECONDS` (default 1h).

No frontend change was needed: `fileAttachmentUrl` already passes absolute `https://` URLs through untouched.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This does **not** recover files written to local disk during any period when `AWS_S3_BUCKET` was unset in production. Render's disk is ephemeral and those objects are gone. Rows whose `file_path` does not start with `https://` identify the lost files.
>
> Verify the AWS env vars are set on Render before deploying, otherwise the code still falls back to ephemeral local disk and the problem returns.

## 2. Searching the calendar by task number returns nothing

The client-side filter matched only title, assignee/participant names, and label names. The task number was never in the search fields, so any numeric query came back empty. Added the task `id` and `unique_tag` to the haystack.

## 3. Backlog tasks cannot be edited

`TaskDetailModal` renders its edit button only when given an `onEdit` callback. `BacklogPanel` opened the modal without one, so the button simply never appeared. Wired it to the calendar's existing `openEditModal`, and made a successful save refresh the backlog list instead of waiting for its 60-second poll.

## Testing

New `backend/tests/test_task_attachment_urls.py` — 7 tests covering signing, single client construction across repeated calls, and the local/empty path fallbacks. All pass.

Existing task suites: **81 passed**. `test_observability.py` fails collection (`No module named 'backend.core.exceptions.observability'`) — pre-existing and unrelated.

Frontend `tsc` reports no new errors in the touched files.

Not verified end-to-end in a browser: the backend runs remotely on Render and requires authentication, so the flows could not be exercised locally.

## Still open

Three reported issues could not be reproduced from the code and need more detail:

- **Recurring tasks** — the logic looks complete end to end (form, payload, backend normalization, the DB query that pulls in series starting in the past, and frontend occurrence expansion). Need to know whether occurrences don't appear at all, appear on wrong dates, or completing one occurrence affects the whole series.
- **Day-view scrolling** — a fix attempt already exists in `TaskCalendar.css:367`. Need to know whether it's the all-day strip or the timed grid, and on which device (mobile and desktop get different height settings).
- **Usernames in task chat** — in both chat implementations the name renders in grey on white, and only for other people's messages. A screenshot would help.

author: sinfjell
body:
## What

Adds one consolidated tool, `get_performance_metrics(date=None)`, that answers *"where is my running fitness right now?"* in a single call. It folds three Garmin endpoints into one LLM-friendly response:

- **`lactate_threshold`** — threshold heart rate (LTHR, bpm) + threshold pace, converting Garmin's raw m/s into a `"M:SS/km"` string (plus decimal min/km and raw m/s). Garmin's "heart rate threshold" and "lactate threshold" are the same value, so this covers both.
- **`vo2max`** — precise decimal VO2 max + rounded value + fitness age.
- **`race_predictions`** — 5k / 10k / half-marathon / marathon predicted times, converted from seconds to clock strings.

## Why one tool, not four

The repo's differentiator is a small, focused tool set (roadmap "Posisjoneringsvakt": cap ~11–12 tools). Lactate threshold, VO2 max, and race predictions all answer the same question and belong together — matching the roadmap's Phase 3 "prestasjons-/terskelhistorikk" grouping. This keeps the total at **10 tools**.

## Robustness

- Each of the three sections is fetched **independently**: if one Garmin endpoint is unavailable it degrades to `{"error": ...}` while the others still return.
- Every section carries its own `measured_date`, so stale values (Garmin often serves a VO2 max reading days old) are visible rather than silently presented as "today" — aligns with the roadmap's "mark incomplete/dated data" principle.
- Speed→pace and seconds→clock conversions handle zero/missing/non-numeric input by returning `null`.

## Tests & checks

- 5 new unit tests (network-free, fake-client pattern matching the existing suite): full reshape, per-section failure isolation, date defaulting, and both conversion helpers' edge cases.
- Full suite green (13 passed), `ruff check .` clean, `garmin-mcp --list-tools` exits 0 with the new tool registered.

## Deploy note

The hosted connector uses `uvx --from git+...@main` **without** `--refresh`, so after merge the Hetzner instance needs the cache-refresh step (`uvx --refresh ... --list-tools` as the site-user, then `systemctl restart garmin-mcp`) before the new tool is live — same procedure as documented for prior merges.

body:
## Before / After

**Before:** sim-lab had no firsthand reproduction of the grim-trigger folk-theorem threshold from Ideas Lab PROPOSAL 223.

**After:** `sims/verdict-236-grim-trigger-folk-theorem/` holds a stdlib-only verifier, its captured `run-stdout.txt`, and a `probe-report.md` ruling **APPROVE**, proving the exact threshold two independent ways (exact rational identity + Monte-Carlo) with a full-64 reproducible digest.

## How

In the infinitely-repeated symmetric Prisoner's Dilemma with stage payoffs **T > R > P > S**, grim-trigger (cooperate until any defection, then defect forever) sustains mutual cooperation as a subgame-perfect equilibrium **iff the discount factor delta ≥ delta\*** where the EXACT threshold is

    delta* = (T − R) / (T − P)

By the one-shot-deviation principle V_C(delta)=R/(1−delta) and V_D(delta)=T+delta·P/(1−delta); indifference reduces to R−T+delta·(T−P)=0, so the incentive gap is exactly zero at delta\*. The continuation-probability statistic D_i=(R−P)·H_i−(T−P) has E[D]=0 exactly at delta\* (since 1−delta\*=(R−P)/(T−P)).

Six gates, each read in its own direction:
- **G1** exact indifference (Fraction): headline (5,3,1,0) → delta\*==1/2 AND V_C−V_D==0 — PASS
- **G2** exact grid (Fraction): (5,3,1,0)→1/2, (5,4,1,0)→1/4, (5,2,1,0)→3/4, (9,8,1,0)→1/8, every gap==0, 0<delta\*<1 — PASS
- **G3** Monte-Carlo agreement at delta\*=0.5, |z|<3: z=1.404082 — PASS
- **G4** MC grid, every |z|<3: max|z|=1.150506 — PASS
- **G5** falsifiability, wrong-Sucker formula (T−R)/(T−S)=2/5 (theory E[D]=−2/3) REJECTED at |z|>6: z=−140.372466 — PASS
- **G6** falsifiability, below-threshold delta\*/2=0.25 (theory E[D]=−4/3) REJECTED at z<−6: z=−448.661725 — PASS

`all_pass=true`, `first_failing_gate=null`. SEED=20260717, Z_GATE=3.0, N_MC=200000 (no bump needed). Determinism holds both ways (in-process double-run guard + separate cross-invocation byte-identical). `python3 bootstrap.py check --strict` exits 0.

author: sgtoj
body:
## what

- Top-level `import:` entries in `atmos.yaml` now resolve relative to the directory containing that `atmos.yaml`, not the current working directory. Running a command from a subdirectory no longer breaks imports like `import: [".atmos/commands/**/*"]`.
- Anchoring is scoped to **config-sourced empty and dot-relative** base paths (`""`, `.`, `./`, `..`, `../…`). Bare paths (`foo`), absolute paths, `!cwd`, and runtime overrides (`ATMOS_BASE_PATH`, `--base-path`, the `atmos_base_path` provider parameter) keep their existing resolution semantics.
- Base-path provenance is tracked across multiple `--config` files and through imported declarations, so a later `--config` file's imports anchor to the file that actually declared the effective `base_path`.
- Nested imports (local and go-getter adapters) resolve a declared relative `base_path` against the importing file's directory via a shared helper.

## why

- `mergeImports` resolved the import base path with `filepath.Abs(base_path)`, which anchors to the current working directory. With the common empty or dot-relative `base_path` (e.g. `.`), running `atmos` from a nested directory resolved `import:` globs against the subdirectory and failed to find them — for example, `atmos.yaml` at `/repo/acme` with `import: [".atmos/commands/**/*"]`, invoked from `/repo/acme/somepath`, looked for `.atmos/commands` under `somepath`.
- Imports should anchor to the atmos root (the directory of the discovered `atmos.yaml`), consistent with how `base_path` is resolved for config-file sources.
- The change preserves the established source-aware convention (runtime/CLI/env dot paths → CWD; bare paths → git-root search; `!cwd` → CWD), so anchoring is limited to config-sourced empty and dot-relative values.

## references

- Fix record: `docs/fixes/2026-07-20-config-imports-relative-to-config-dir.md`.
- Related base-path work: `docs/prd/base-path-resolution-semantics.md`, `docs/fixes/2026-03-17-failed-to-find-import-base-path-resolution.md`.
- Testing: `go build ./...`; `go test ./pkg/config/... ./internal/exec/... ./cmd/...`; the new CWD-independence tests fail on the pre-fix code (import resolves against CWD) and pass after; `go test ./pkg/config ./pkg/config/adapters -shuffle=on -count=10` for registry isolation.

author: agourakis82
body:
## What — a batch of **10** per-group verbs

All dense direct-index over keys 0..1023 (no hashing — the `bf_groupby_sum` contract), all row-aligned:

| verb | meaning |
|---|---|
| `bf_expanding_max_by` / `bf_expanding_min_by` | expanding max/min ≡ per-group running extremum → delegate to `bf_cummax_by`/`bf_cummin_by` |
| `bf_cumprod_by` | per-group cumulative **product** (overflows to inf like pandas) |
| `bf_zscore_by` | `(val − group_mean)/group_std` — canonical per-group **standardisation** |
| `bf_demean_by` | `val − group_mean` (centering) |
| `bf_minmax_scale_by` | `(val − group_min)/(group_max − group_min)` → **[0,1]** |
| `bf_sem_by` | `std/√n` — group **standard error of the mean** |
| `bf_range_by` | group `max − min`, broadcast |
| `bf_head_mask_by` / `bf_tail_mask_by` | 0/1 mask of the **first/last n** rows per group (`groupby().head(n)`/`.tail(n)`) |

The five stat-broadcast verbs share one dense two-pass Welford+min/max engine; degenerate groups yield 0 where pandas yields NaN.

## Run-proof (ops gate, `BIGFRAME_OPS_GATE_OK`)

- expanding max/min match `cummax`/`cummin` byte-for-byte; cumprod of 1,2,3,4,5,6 → 1,2,6,24,120,720;
- on a `{2,4,6,8,10}` group: demean −4..4, range 8, minmax 0/0.5/1, zscore mid 0 & hi 1.2649, sem 1.4142;
- head(3)/tail(3) mark exactly 3 rows per group at the right positions;
- (offline) all match pandas (cumprod/zscore/demean/minmax/sem/range/head/tail) over 8k rows / 40 groups = **0 diffs**.

## Benchmark (1M rows, 1000 dense keys)

| op | Sounio ms | pandas ms | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| cumprod_by | ~12 | ~17 | **0.70× — win** |
| zscore_by | ~270 | ~694 | **0.39× — win** |
| head/tail_mask_by | single-pass | | **win** |

## Scope
- stdlib only — **no compiler changes**. Heap ⇒ NATIVE + `lean_single` engine.
- Files: `stdlib/data/bigframe_ops.sio`, `tests/stdlib/data/test_bigframe_ops_stdlib.sio`, `scripts/bench/RESULTS.md`.

## What

Removes ~270 lines of dead `MPKitProtocol` template scaffolding from the Rokt kit — empty stub methods that only returned `success` without performing any work.

Removed from [`MPKitRokt.m`](https://github.com/mParticle/mparticle-apple-sdk/blob/main/Kits/rokt/rokt/Sources/mParticle-Rokt/MPKitRokt.m):

`#[cfg(feature = "instruments")]` block in `prover/src/lib.rs`.

The **continuation** path never went through that block: `prove_epoch` and
`prove_global` in `prover/src/continuation.rs` call `Prover::multi_prove`
directly. `multi_prove` *does* `instruments::store(MultiProveTiming { .. })` for
every call, so the per-table data was already being computed and stored — but
nothing on the continuation path ever printed it. Result:
`prove --continuations` with `--features instruments` produced **no** per-table
report at all.

## Fix

Feature-gated only (zero cost, and byte-for-byte identical compile, when the
feature is off):

- `prover/src/instruments.rs`: factor the mp-derived per-table block out of
  `print_report` into a shared `print_multi_prove(mp, total)` helper, and add
  `print_epoch_report(label)` which drains the timing stored by the preceding
  `multi_prove` via `stark::instruments::take()` and formats it with that same
  helper (so both paths format from a single source of truth). Also inlined a
  literal into one `eprintln!` format string to silence a pre-existing
  `clippy::print_literal` that only trips under `--features instruments`;
  rendered output is unchanged.
- `prover/src/continuation.rs`: after each `Prover::multi_prove`, call
  `print_epoch_report`, labeled `EPOCH N` for each epoch (from the 1-based
  `EpochStart.label`) and `GLOBAL` for the cross-epoch memory proof.

The monolithic path's output is unchanged (same statements, same order — the
mp block was moved into a function and called with the same `mp`/`total`). No
proving logic changed; this is purely gated reporting.

Note on `GLOBAL`: its per-epoch `total` is derived from the sum of the proving
phases, so for a trivially small global proof (a couple of tiny tables that run
in parallel) individual table percentages can exceed 100% — an honest artifact
of parallel per-table timing against a tiny sequential-phase denominator (the
monolithic formatter has the same parallel overlap, just diluted by a larger
wall-clock total). The `EPOCH N` reports, which carry the real work, read
normally.

## Verification

Built and ran a continuation prove that exercises `prove_epoch` (x2) +
`prove_global`:

```
cargo build --release -p cli --features instruments
./target/release/cli prove executor/program_artifacts/asm/fib_iterative_500k.elf \
    --output /tmp/cont.proof --continuations --epoch-size-log2 18
```

Per-epoch reports now print. Sample (trimmed):

```
=== EPOCH 0 ===
  Phase                                    Wall      %
  --------------------------------------------------------
  Pre-pass (domains/twiddles)             0.03s    1.0%
  Round 1                                 1.30s   38.8%
    Main trace commits                    0.59s          17.7%
    ...
  Rounds 2-4                              2.01s   60.1%
      BITWISE              1.0M           0.82s          24.5%
      MEMW_R               524K           0.47s          13.9%
      EQ                    66K           0.32s           9.7%
      CPU                  262K           0.32s           9.6%
      ...
      (16 others)                         0.67s          20.0%
      -- sub-operation totals (all tables) --
      R4  queries & openings              1.09s          32.7%
      R3  OOD evaluation                  0.66s          19.7%
      ...
  Total FFT                               0.79s   23.6%
  Total Merkle                            0.86s   25.7%
  --------------------------------------------------------
  TOTAL                                   3.34s

=== EPOCH 1 ===
  ... (same layout) ...

=== GLOBAL ===
  ... (same layout) ...
```

- Feature ON: reports print per epoch (`EPOCH 0`, `EPOCH 1`, `GLOBAL`).
- Feature OFF (`cargo build --release -p cli`): zero instruments lines in the
  continuation prove output; compiles clean (all new code is
  `#[cfg(feature = "instruments")]`).
- `cargo test --release -p lambda-vm-prover --lib`: 521 passed, 0 failed.
- `clippy --features instruments` (which CI's `make lint` does not exercise)
  is clean on the changed crates; all three `make lint` clippy passes exit 0;
  `cargo fmt --check` is clean on the changed crates.

author: danieletranchina88-hub
body:
## Il problema segnalato
La mappa ICON-2I non mostrava fronti a nessuna ora. Diagnosi sul run 12z reale (scaricato e strumentato gate per gate):

1. **Il fronte freddo in ingresso dalla Francia era rilevato** (+18h `cold conf 0.59` esattamente dove lo vede ECMWF, +36h già sul Piemonte) **ma a ore alterne**: nelle ore intermedie il gradiente termico oscillava un soffio sotto la soglia dura di 2 K/100km → la catena si spezzava → nessuna traccia → nessuna pubblicazione. Le soglie severe per-ora ricreavano al livello del rilevamento lo stesso effetto "knife-edge" già eliminato al livello della pubblicazione.
2. **La guida ECMWF era quasi vuota**: pubblicava solo i propri fronti *tracciati* (3 feature su 21 scadenze) — come riferimento per la conferma incrociata era inutilizzabile.
3. Il resto degli zeri era **onesto**: i bordi di sola umidità (ΔTv misurate tra −0.9 e −2.1 K) sono correttamente esclusi dal Gate 1b.

## Le correzioni
- **Pavimenti per-ora ridotti** (baroclinicità 1.3 K/100km, vento 1.5/0.15, confidenza 0.50) e **soglie piene spostate a mediane della traccia** (baroclinicità ≥ 2, vento ≥ 2 o convergenza ≥ 0.2, confidenza ≥ 0.55): severe sul fronte nel suo complesso, tolleranti verso l'oscillazione oraria. Le protezioni anti-artefatti (copertura ≥ 50%, vita minima, geometria, Tv, saccatura, vorticità) restano invariate.
- **`candidate_lines()`**: il catalogo ECMWF esporta anche i candidati pre-tracciamento (campo `candidates`) e la conferma delle tracce ICON usa quelli — riferimento denso a ogni scadenza, fail-open se assente.

## Validazione su entrambi i run reali
| Run | Prima | Dopo |
|---|---|---|
| 12z (quello della segnalazione) | 0 fronti a tutte le ore | **fronte francese: traccia continua +16→+35h** (11 rilevamenti) + boundary centro-italiana; zero onesto prima/dopo |
| 00z | conteggi lisci | invariato nel merito, **0 lampeggi**, nessun ritorno degli artefatti diurni |
| Suite sintetica (6 scenari + continuità) | verde | verde |

Metodi: `theta-e-850-tracked-v7` / `theta-e-850-icon2i-tracked-v9`. Docs aggiornate.

## Nota
Al primo run dopo il merge la guida ECMWF avrà ancora il vecchio formato (senza `candidates`): la conferma usa i fronti pubblicati come ripiego e resta per lo più fail-open; dal run successivo la guida sarà completa.

author: graemef
body:
Two comments at the subscription-restore seam attributed session-blind boot to a *resumed* MCP child. Claude Code injects `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` into the child env on a resumed seat as well as a fresh one, so "resumed" is the wrong subject for that sentence.

**This narrows the subject; it does not invert the claim.** Those sentences are the stated reason the restore is forked rather than awaited inline. Replacing them with "the id is present on resume" would document an unconditional env source at the seam and delete the fork's justification — a comments-only change that reads as a licence to await inline. The population that genuinely boots without an id is a host that does not inject one at all, and for that host the id cannot arrive until the seat itself acts, so the fork rationale stands unchanged.

A reviewer should be able to check exactly that: the fork-not-await reasoning, the `Deferred` once-guard, the store-presence resume signal and the persistent-mode exception are all untouched.

**Warrants differ between the two clauses, and the comments state both as behaviour without marking which is which:**

- Claude Code boot-env presence on a fresh and a resumed seat is **measured** — `/proc/<pid>/environ` of commy-mcp children across a fresh session and two `--resume`s, one workstation, CC 2.1.215.
- The non-CC path (`session_id` supplied in tool-call arguments) is **ratified design**, not an observation. No non-CC host was measured here.

`packages/mcp/bootstrap.ts` is deliberately untouched — it already scopes this correctly and already carries the version-pinned Claude Code measurement, which is where a version-pinned fact belongs.

The tool-call feeder is named as requiring an *acting* seat: a listen-only non-CC seat never fires it. That is a known residual gap, recorded and accepted; naming it here is descriptive, not a change to it.

**No logic depends on the false scoping.** The parking exists for hosts that inject nothing, which the narrowed sentence describes directly — nothing in the surrounding code was written against the "resumed child" reading. Comments only; no behaviour change.

author: proggeramlug
body:
## Summary

Fixes #6726. `new globalThis.Set()` compiled but produced an object without any Set methods — `new globalThis.Set().has(42)` threw `TypeError: has is not a function`. The plain `new Set()` and the local-alias `const S = globalThis.Set; new S()` forms both worked, so the failure was specific to constructing through the inline member-expression callee.

## Root cause

The bare-identifier `new <Builtin>()` arm in `lower_new` routes every built-in constructor to its real allocator — `Set` → `Expr::SetNew`, `Map` → `MapNew`, `Date` → `DateNew`, the Error family, typed arrays, boxed primitives, `Proxy`, `WeakRef`, and so on. A **member-expression** callee (`globalThis.Set`) never reaches that arm: it falls through to `lower_new_non_ident` → `Expr::NewDynamic`.

For the data-structure builtins — whose construction lives in a dedicated HIR variant rather than in codegen's `lower_builtin_new` — codegen's `try_static_class_name` then rerouted the `PropertyGet { globalThis, "Set" }` callee to `lower_new("Set")`, which has **no `Set`/`Map`/`Date` arm** and dead-ended at a `class_id=0` empty-object placeholder. (The `const S = globalThis.Set; new S()` form works because a `LocalGet` callee instead reaches the runtime `js_new_function_construct` helper, which *does* recognise the reified global builtin thunks.)

## Fix

In `lower_new`, detect the `new globalThis.<Ident>(...)` callee — the real global object (`globalThis` not lexically rebound) with a recognised built-in constructor name — and re-dispatch through a synthesized bare-identifier `new <Ident>(...)`. A member callee then constructs the exact same intrinsic as the plain form.

- Placed **after** `lower_new_member_native`, so the already-working member paths (`URL` / streams / fetch / worker-messaging) are untouched.
- A shadowing local (`const globalThis = { Set: ... }`) suppresses the re-dispatch via the `ctx.lookup_local("globalThis").is_none()` guard, so it keeps using the local object — matching Node.
- Recursion terminates: the synthesized callee is an `Ident`, not a `Member`.

## Testing

`test-files/test_gap_new_globalthis_builtin_6726.ts` covers the repro plus `Set`/`Map`/`Date`/`WeakMap`/`WeakSet`/`TypeError`/`Array`/`Promise` through `globalThis`, and the two forms that already worked (bare + local alias) as regression guards. Perry output is **byte-for-byte identical to Node**.

Verified manually against Node, all matching:

```
new globalThis.Set().has(42)            → false
new globalThis.Set([1,2,2,3]).size      → 3
new globalThis.Map([["a",1]]).get("a")  → 1
new globalThis.Date(0).getTime()        → 0
new globalThis.TypeError("boom")        → instanceof Error, name "TypeError"
new globalThis.Uint8Array(3)            → real typed array
new globalThis.RegExp("a.c","g")        → real regex
new globalThis.Proxy(...)               → real proxy
const globalThis = {...}; new globalThis.Set()  → uses the local (shadow respected)
```

`cargo test -p perry-hir --lib` passes (247/247). No version bump / changelog per the contributor-PR convention.

author: ludovicocordara-rgb
body:
Dashboard polish pass (Ludo, 2026-07-20). Five things, all on `/dashboard`.

## 1. The greeting name is editable

Click the name in "How can I help you, Ludo?" and type. Enter saves, Escape cancels.

It writes `kr_users.full_name` through the **existing** `POST /api/kr/account/profile` — the same field and endpoint `/account` already uses. No migration, no new column, no second source of truth for a person's name. Clearing the box falls back to the derived email local-part instead of erroring, since `full_name` is nullable and the greeting already knew how to degrade.

The save is optimistic (the headline is the control, so it should respond on Enter) with rollback and a visible message if the write fails — it never leaves a name on screen that isn't actually stored.

## 2. "Today on your desk" no longer renders a row of zeros

It used to print every counter unconditionally, so on a quiet day it read `0 companies tracked · 0 new filings · 0 watchlist movers`. Most days are quiet days.

Now a segment appears only when its count is non-zero, and the whole line unmounts when nothing happened — the search hero just stands alone, which is the honest rendering of "no news".

Two deliberate calls:
- **"companies tracked" is gone.** It's a static roster size, not news; it's already the count in the My Companies header; and being non-zero for anyone with a watchlist it would have pinned the line on screen forever and defeated the hiding.
- **Each segment carries its own window** (`3 new filings this week · 2 movers today`). Filings and Edge are 7-day counts and movers is the current session, so labelling the whole line "today" would have been wrong about two of the three.

## 3. My Companies / My Funds / Saved actually line up now

They drifted because they're three components that each grew their own spacing. The fix is structural: every vertical measurement now lives in `DeskCard.tsx` (`DESK_ROW_H`, `DeskToolbar`, `DeskRow`) and the three cards may only compose it.

The actual culprit: **My Companies rendered a sort-pill row that Funds and Saved did not**, pushing its first row ~34px below theirs. `DeskToolbar` is now always rendered at a fixed height, empty or not. Secondary causes fixed too — Saved was `py-3.5` against the rosters' `py-3`, and fund names wrapped freely so fund rows varied in height (they now clamp to two lines *inside* a fixed-height row, so short names still show in full but can't knock the column out of step).

Also: row hairlines were hardcoded `border-white/[0.06]`, **invisible on the light theme's `#ffffff` card**. They're `border-border` now, so the separators exist in both themes.

## 4. My Funds sorts A–Z and by return

Return stays the default (the ranked read is the point of the card), A–Z is the opt-in for finding a manager in a long roster.

One rule is compliance, not preference, and is pinned by a test: **a fund with no scored 1-yr return never sorts as though it returned 0%.** It has no full 4-quarter, ≥10-name record, so treating null as zero would rank an unmeasured book above every genuine loser and imply a return we didn't measure. Unscored funds sink to the bottom in name order.

## 5. Krypton Edge earns its place on the page

The band was a list of tickers with a "2 new" chip — it advertised that primary research exists without showing any of it. It now leads with the **newest management answer**: company, the question we asked, and a pull-quote from the answer, with the ticker list demoted to a quiet footer. It also gets a band heading, which it was the only band lacking.

**Gating (please check this line specifically).** Answer bodies are the moat. The excerpt renders only inside the pre-existing `showEdge` branch — `canSeeInstitutionalEdgeEntry(user)` → `hasInstitutionalEdgeAccess`, the same durable entitlement that unlocks the full Q&A on `/edge/[ticker]`. Belt and braces: `edgeQuote` is derived from `edgeCompanies`, which is already `[]` unless `showEdge && hasFollows`, so it resolves to `null` for an unentitled viewer even before the render branch. Nothing reaches the RSC payload. The underlying read is management-only by default.

## Look

Editorial research-note treatment, per Ludo's pick: brand serif section headers at a wide letterspace over a hairline rule, tabular figures, token-driven borders that render in both themes.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `npx eslint --max-warnings 0 app/dashboard` — clean
- `npx vitest run` — **8274 passed**, 109 skipped, 0 failed (includes 11 new tests)
- `npm run build` — succeeded
- `/dashboard` served **200** against a real session on a local dev server

New tests cover `pullQuote` (word-boundary truncation — a quote attributed to a named executive must never be cut mid-word) and `sortFunds` (the null-return rule above).

**Not verified:** I did not visually confirm the rendering in a browser — this repo's `CLAUDE.md` forbids the Chrome MCP tools in favour of gstack's `/browse`, which isn't installed in my environment. Please eyeball the Vercel preview, particularly the three-column alignment and the Edge pull-quote in both light and dark mode.

author: awanish14
body:
## Purpose

Documentation-only checkpoint recording the milestone reached at `main` @ `c0586a7` (PR #75 merged,
main CI green): **Business Discovery has crossed from contracts/questionnaire/scoring into canonical
Draft BIF construction.**

Adds one file: `docs/reviews/BUSINESS_DISCOVERY_TO_BIF_CHECKPOINT.md`.

**No implementation is started by this PR.**

## What the document records

| § | Content |
|---|---|
| 1 | **Milestone summary** — AGE can deterministically produce a canonical `Draft` BIF from a `BusinessDiscoveryProfile` without fabricating timestamps, IDs, sections, provenance, completeness or confidence, with a table of how each is obtained instead |
| 2 | **Deterministic flow** — profile → questionnaire validation → completeness + discovery confidence scoring → field-level evidence → canonical Draft BIF |
| 3 | **PR history #67 → #75** — what each PR added, including the pre-merge refinement inside #75 |
| 4 | **Current guarantees** — purity/determinism, required caller context, construction honesty, provenance, score separation, integration boundary |
| 5 | **Intentionally partial areas** — provisional confidence, the two completeness metrics, 7-of-12 section coverage with a per-section table, and why each omission stands |
| 6 | **What must not be done next** — with the reason each would be harmful, not just the prohibition |
| 7 | **Next-slice evaluation** — five options assessed, one recommended |
| 8 | **Proposed scope** for the recommended slice, with hard boundaries |
| 9 | **Hard boundaries** for this PR |

## Two distinctions worth surfacing

Both were verified against the tree rather than assumed, and both are easy to lose track of later:

**1. The CLI demo does not consume the real BIF.** It consumes the PR #69 `mapBusinessDiscoveryToBifContext`
*projection* — a read-only, display-shaped context that is deliberately **not** a BIF. Searching
`mapBusinessDiscoveryToBifDraft` across `apps/` and `packages/` returns only the mapper's own source,
its barrel export and its tests. So "nothing consumes the real Draft BIF yet" is accurate, while a
flat "no demo-runtime integration" would not have been — the demo *is* wired to discovery, just to
the projection. The document states it precisely and tabulates the two outputs side by side.

**2. ADR-0025 is `Proposed`, and its Decision 3 does not match the implementation.** The ADR says
map completeness directly; the merged mapper computes BIF population completeness instead, because
publishing the intake's 97 on a BIF built from 10 of 84 fields would have overstated how populated
the BIF is. That divergence was deliberate and is documented in code and in PR #75, which was scoped
to exclude ADR changes.

Crucially, **ADR-0025 has never been ratified** — its status field reads `Status: Proposed`. (The one
"Accepted" inside that file refers to ADR-0020, Branch Flow Governance, which is unrelated.) So this
is a proposal that implementation experience improved upon, not an accepted decision being
contravened. The checkpoint therefore records that **Decision 3 should be revised before ADR-0025 is
accepted**, rather than accepting it as written and then amending or superseding it — there is no
ratified decision to contravene and no supersession record to create, so the proposal can simply be
corrected to describe the two-metric approach and put forward for acceptance as a coherent whole.

**This PR does not edit ADR-0025** — it remains at `Status: Proposed`, exactly as it stands on
`main`. The checkpoint *describes* that status; it does not set or change it.

## Recommendation: Option A — BIF scoring layer

Five options were evaluated (scoring layer · capability consumption · persistence · API/Web exposure
· expanded mapping coverage). **Option A is recommended.**

PR #75 deliberately left `bif.confidenceScore` as a provisional `0` at root and every section,
because no honest value existed and `discoveryConfidenceScore` measures a different thing. Before any
capability consumes a BIF, AGE needs a deterministic scoring layer defining what **BIF intelligence
confidence** means, separately from discovery input confidence.

Options B, C and D are blocked by the same gap, and each is expensive to unwind: they bake the
current provisional semantics into a consumer, a stored record, or a public response respectively.
Option E (expand coverage) is valid and independent, but should not go first — it makes the BIF
*wider* without making it *more trustworthy*, and its real blocker is upstream in the questionnaire
(discovery captures unclassified free text where BIF wants typed buckets), not in the mapper.

§8 proposes a narrow package-level scope for Option A, and flags an **open question to settle before
any code**: does a section populated by 1 of 9 fields, all user-confirmed, score *low* confidence
(little corroboration) or *high* (everything present is directly client-stated)? Those give opposite
answers and determine the whole layer.

§8 also names a **governance prerequisite**: revise ADR-0025 Decision 3 to describe the two-metric
approach, settle the confidence question, and then put the ADR forward for acceptance as a coherent
whole. That is one reviewed governance change instead of accept-then-amend, and it means the scoring
layer gets built against a ratified decision rather than a stale proposal — as its own reviewed
change, not as a side effect of an implementation slice.

## Commits

| SHA | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `de9b66d` | Add the checkpoint document |
| `9581466` | **Correction** — the first commit stated ADR-0025 is Accepted; it is `Proposed`. Corrects all three status mentions and re-frames the §5/§6/§8 governance recommendation from "amend or supersede" to "revise Decision 3 before acceptance" |

The error was caught during pre-merge verification, before merge.

## Confirmations

- **Documentation-only** — one file, `docs/reviews/BUSINESS_DISCOVERY_TO_BIF_CHECKPOINT.md`. The full
  diff vs `main` is a single added path.
- **No code changes. No package changes** — no source file, no `package.json`, no lockfile.
- **No API, Web, DB or persistence changes.**
- **No ADR status changes, and ADR-0025 is not edited** — `git diff main...HEAD -- docs/adrs/` is
  empty. ADR-0025 remains at `Status: Proposed`; this checkpoint describes that status rather than
  setting it.
- **No SAGE changes. `develop` untouched** — still at `7245dcc`.
- **No implementation started** — §7/§8 are a recommendation and a proposed scope awaiting approval.
- Prettier: `--write` then `--check` → "All matched files use Prettier code style!"
- Base: `main` @ `c0586a707cff53bbe6b23d5a9c83f7242089e276`.

author: alemtuzlak
body:
## WebSocket transport

Adds WebSockets as a third streaming transport alongside SSE and NDJSON, reusing the delivery-durability seam that landed in #955. Full-duplex, conversation-scoped, resumable.

### Server (`@tanstack/ai`)
- `toWebSocketStream(socket, request, { onRun, durability?, batch?, heartbeatMs?, idleTimeoutMs?, debug? })` — portable core that pumps a conversation over an already-accepted WHATWG `WebSocketLike` server socket (Node via `ws`, Bun, etc.).
- `toWebSocketResponse(request, init)` — thin wrapper that upgrades via `WebSocketPair` and returns a 101 `Response` on Cloudflare Workers/Durable Objects; throws elsewhere, pointing you to `toWebSocketStream`.
- `resumeWebSocketStream(socket, { adapter })` / `resumeWebSocketResponse({ adapter })` — read-only replay of a run from the durability log (no model call).
- Because one socket outlives many `chat()` turns (client-tool resubmits, follow-up messages), you pass an `onRun(ctx) => AsyncIterable<StreamChunk>` factory instead of a prebuilt stream — it's called per inbound `RunAgentInput` frame. Durability is keyed per turn and reuses the existing `durableStreamSource` (now exported), so server→client frames carry the same `{ id, chunk }` envelope as NDJSON.
- Conversation-scoped lifecycle: stays open across turns; closes on client close, an `{ type: 'abort', runId }` frame (aborts only that turn), or idle timeout; periodic `{ type: 'ping' }` heartbeat.

### Client (`@tanstack/ai-client`, re-exported from `ai-react`/`-solid`/`-vue`/`-svelte`/`-angular`)
- `webSocket(url, options)` — full-duplex `subscribe` + `send` connection adapter for `useChat`. `send()` writes a `RunAgentInput` frame; `subscribe()` yields inbound chunks, ignores heartbeats, unwraps durable envelopes, and **auto-reconnects** a dropped durable run by reopening with `?runId=&offset=` (browsers can't set a `Last-Event-ID` handshake header, so the offset rides in the URL).
- Reconnect bookkeeping (offset de-dupe, no-progress ceiling → `StreamReconnectLimitError`) is shared with the HTTP adapters via the new `createReconnectTracker`. A fatal drop surfaces to the consumer instead of hanging.

### Testing
- Unit: `@tanstack/ai` stream-to-websocket 18/18; `@tanstack/ai-client` connection-adapter suites 63/63 (incl. reconnect, fatal-drop-surfacing, and open-promise-race regressions).
- E2E: a provider-free WebSocket arm on the delivery-durability harness (Vite `upgrade` hook + `ws`) — ordered stream + reconnect-resume, 2/2; SSE/NDJSON regression 6/6.
- Example: a `/websocket-chat` route in `examples/ts-react-chat` (type-checks + builds).
- Docs: `docs/resumable-streams/` overview + advanced + new WebSockets page; kiira-typechecked snippets, both server and client halves.

### Notes / follow-ups (v2, documented)
- Client `stop()` does not emit an `{ type: 'abort' }` frame today — per-turn abort is via socket close (aborts all turns). The protocol primitive exists server-side.
- One shared `webSocket()` connection assumes a single in-flight run at a time.

body:
## Summary This is PR 1/3 for the bounded streaming Discovery work proposed in #1340. It adds the tenant-safe coordination foundation without enabling Discovery or changing the existing Hedge scheduler. - Add versioned, tenant-scoped session bindings with atomic read/reconcile, generation CAS, null tombstones, cooldown markers, and ABA protection. - Keep rolling upgrades compatible through guarded legacy mirrors and fail closed when legacy ownership cannot be proven. - Add a runtime Redis capability gate tied to the active connection lifecycle. Unsupported multi-key Lua or `CROSSSLOT` falls back to the existing legacy path and keeps Discovery ineligible. - Add owner-token Discovery lease acquire/renew/release primitives and include them in the isolated capability probe. - Make legacy expected-provider clear and provider-scoped terminate value-checked so a stale `P` cleanup cannot delete a concurrent `P -> Q` failover. - Preserve generation CAS for force/failover winners so a late request cannot overwrite a newer binding. ## Rollout This PR does not start provider fan-out. Existing routing remains authoritative until the follow-up scheduler and the final, default-off configuration switch are both merged and explicitly enabled. ## Validation - Binding/session unit suites: 62 tests passed. - `bun run typecheck` - `bun run format:check` - Redis integration coverage is included and runs when `REDIS_URL` is configured. ## Stack - Follow-up backend scheduler: #1348 - Final configuration/API/UI layer: #1349 Refs #1340.

Greptile Summary

 This PR introduces the tenant-safe, versioned session-binding foundation for the Discovery work. It adds generation-based CAS with ABA protection, null tombstones, cooldown markers, and a capability gate backed by a live Redis probe — without touching any Discovery fan-out logic. Existing routing stays authoritative; the scheduler and feature flag come in follow-up PRs. - **Core Lua scripts** (`lua-scripts.ts`): six new multi-key Lua scripts (READ_OR_RECONCILE, CAS, TOUCH, CLEAR, TERMINATE, two lease scripts) plus two single-key conditional scripts for rolling-upgrade mirror safety. All operations validate ownership, mirror consistency, and generation in a single atomic step. - **Capability gate** (`session-binding.ts`): module-level connection-lifecycle tracking resets capability state on Redis reconnect, funnels all versioned operations through a `readyVersionedClient` guard, and deduplicates concurrent probes via a cached Promise. - **Session-manager and proxy wiring**: every binding callsite branches between the versioned CAS path and a tenant-validated legacy fallback; the hedge heartbeat fires periodic `TOUCH_SESSION_BINDING` and issues a final touch at stream boundary before side-effects are committed.

Confidence Score: 5/5

 Safe to merge — no P0 or P1 issues found after thorough analysis of all 25 changed files. Lua scripts are atomic and fail-closed, ABA protection via generation UUIDs is correct, the capability gate correctly blocks all versioned operations when the probe fails, the hedge heartbeat has proper in-flight deduplication and a complete() barrier before side-effects are committed, and the tenant content-hash key change correctly scopes sessions to keyId. All previously raised concerns are correctly addressed. No files require special attention. The two largest new files (session-binding.ts and lua-scripts.ts) are the most complex but are well-structured and internally consistent.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/lib/redis/lua-scripts.ts | Adds 9 Lua scripts for atomic session-binding operations: READ_OR_RECONCILE (legacy upgrade), CAS (generation-based ABA-protected write), TOUCH (TTL refresh), CLEAR (provider removal + cooldown marker), TERMINATE (null tombstone), plus single-key conditional helpers for legacy mirror management and discovery lease primitives. Logic is thorough and fail-closed. | | src/lib/redis/session-binding.ts | New 1,539-line module owning the versioned binding lifecycle: capability gate (probe + epoch tracking), key builders, evalBindingScript with NOSCRIPT fallback, mutateLegacySessionBindingSafely with TOCTOU-safe pre/post canonical checks, and all public wrappers. Design is robust; no blocking issues found. | | src/lib/session-manager.ts | Wires versioned binding into all public APIs (bind, get, clear, terminate, storeSessionHash) with clean legacy fallback paths; adds tenant-scoped content-hash key, cooldown check, TTL-interval helper, and touchVersionedSessionBinding. The CAS path for forceUpdate/isFailoverSuccess is intentional per PR design. | | src/app/v1/_lib/proxy/response-handler.ts | Adds startHedgeBindingHeartbeat with touchInFlight deduplication and complete() barrier before commitSideEffects; updates clearSessionBinding to use versioned snapshot path with legacy fallback only when legacyClearAllowed. | | src/app/v1/_lib/proxy/forwarder.ts | commitWinner gates hedgeBindingAuthorityPromise on isActualHedgeWin, returns typed DeferredStreamingHedgeBindingAuthority, passes keyId through clearSessionProviderBinding, and replaces manual provider-clear loops with a single SessionManager.clearSessionProviders call. | | src/lib/session-tracker.ts | Removes EXPIRE for legacy binding keys from refreshSessionTTL pipeline (now managed by Lua scripts); adds conditional mutateLegacySessionBindingSafely only when versioned capability is unavailable. | | src/lib/redis/client.ts | Adds redisClientUrl tracking so URL changes trigger stale-client replacement rather than silently reusing a connection pointed at the old endpoint. | | src/app/v1/_lib/proxy/stream-finalization.ts | Adds DeferredStreamingBindingHeartbeat and DeferredStreamingHedgeBindingAuthority types and optional heartbeat/authority fields to DeferredStreamingFinalization to wire the new versioned-clear and heartbeat paths. |

author: reednaa
body:
## Summary

A consolidation pass over the input/output settlers, encoding library, and Polymer
oracle. Removes redundant Tron-specific contracts, collapses the encode-then-hash
layer into single-pass hashers, adds native-ETH support across all escrow paths,
and lands the Solana→EVM proof path for Polymer. Net −1,077/+4,612 (most of the
additions are tests and mocks).

## Changes

### Input settlers — native ETH + simplification
- Native ETH inputs now supported on **all** escrow variants (self-funded, `openFor`,
  and the order-purchase path); `msg.value` is the sole funding source and is checked
  for exact equality.
- Strict balance-delta check on ERC-3009 collections (rejects fee-on-transfer shortfalls
  on that path).
- Hoisted `_validateUser` to `InputSettlerBase`; single-pass `_open`.
- Removed the standalone `InputSettlerEscrowTron.sol` and `SafeTransferLib.tron.sol`;
  Tron behaviour now lives in `InputSettlerEscrowLIFI.tron.sol` (USDT payout via
  `SafeTRC20.safeTransferUSDT`, Tron Permit2 address override).

### Encoding — direct-hash `MandateOutputEncodingLib`
- Fold `keccak256(encode*(...))` into no-alloc inline-assembly hashers; delete the eight
  public byte encoders. Preimages are byte-identical to the retired encoders.
- New `hashFillDescription(+Memory)` / `hashNotFilledDescription(+Memory)`; ~27–31% gas
  reduction per op. Memory variants use `mcopy` (requires a Cancun VM / java-tron ≥ 4.8.0).

### Output settler
- Non-fill path: bounds-check the refund output index; named payload offsets.

### Polymer oracle — Solana → EVM proofs
- Add the Solana→EVM proof path (`receiveSolanaMessage`), keyed on the Polymer-authenticated
  `returnedProgramId` (self-namespacing preserved).
- Decode Solana logs as **raw base64** (`application(32) || payload`), matching Polymer's
  live prover — the previous prefix-parse reverted on every real proof and was masked by a
  mock emitting the wrong format.
- Moved the test-only `Base58` helper and `MockCrossL2ProverV2` out of `src/` into
  `test/`; `src/` now ships only the oracle contracts + vendored prover interface.
- Added an env-gated live devnet fork test validated end-to-end against a real
  `oracle_polymer::submit` proof.

## Test & snapshots
- Extensive new coverage: native-ETH escrow/purchase suites, `MandateOutputHash` equivalence
  tests vs a reference encoder, output not-filled suite, Polymer Solana suites.
- Gas snapshots regenerated (`snapshots/*.json`).

## Notes for reviewers
- No behavioural change to the attestation/self-namespacing security model; the encoding
  refactor is preimage-preserving (equivalence-tested).
- The `mcopy`-based hashers require a Cancun-capable VM on every target chain (incl. Tron).

author: crispysizzlin
body:
## What changed

- adds a Quantower C# strategy for MES using a 15-minute opening range, breakout/retest entry, trade-based VWAP, relative volume, and persistent top-five Level 2 confirmation
- adds all-in sizing with commission and slippage allowances, attached protection, account exclusivity, prop-floor-aware risk caps, stale-feed shutdowns, daily threshold refresh, and session flattening
- adds a dependency-free Python research engine with next-bar execution, pessimistic same-bar handling, explicit commissions, adverse slippage, automatic double-cost stress, exact trade-value VWAP support, and L2 freshness enforcement
- adds Lucid-style EOD trailing-drawdown and best-day consistency simulation
- adds PSR, moving-block bootstrap, production gates, tests, dated rule references, data contracts, and deployment/validation documentation

## Why

Raw ORB results are not stable enough to treat as a standalone edge. This implementation uses the opening range as a level, then requires a retest plus VWAP/volume regime alignment and fast order-book confirmation. The repository deliberately separates a bar-only baseline from the full L2 hypothesis.

## Validation

- `PYTHONPATH=research python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`: 19 tests passed
- Python bytecode compilation passed
- JSON configuration validation passed
- C# braces balanced and syntax-tree parsing found no error nodes
- remote diff verified as 29 intended files, one commit ahead of `main`

## Required before any funded use

This is a research prototype, not a profitability claim. It still requires:

- compilation against the user's installed Quantower/Visual Studio SDK on Windows
- historical MES/ES trade and top-five depth data with contract/roll lineage
- frozen walk-forward and locked out-of-sample tests, including doubled costs
- at least 20 untouched Rithmic paper sessions with fill, rejection, restart, bracket, and stale-feed reconciliation
- current account-agreement/dashboard rule verification and a human promotion decision

The strategy defaults to refusing live startup unless a current prop liquidation threshold is entered.

body:
## Diagnosed failure chain
1. The staged Railway configuration reduced the canonical 300-second readiness window to 30 seconds.
2. Production preflight accepted `AMOS_RM2_STATUS=paused` without rejecting `AMOS_STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_REQUIRED=true`, even though application startup correctly rejects that contradiction.
3. When recovery began without any retained healthy Railway rollback target, rollback correctly recorded that absence but its verifier still demanded a healthy Railway response and falsely marked rollback failed.

## Permanent correction
- Use a 300-second `/api/health/ready` window in the immutable Railway stage.
- Fail preflight on RM.2/encryption contradictions in both paused and active postures.
- In no-baseline recovery, verify Netlify was restored and explicitly preserve Railway’s pre-existing unavailable state without claiming a successful Railway restoration.
- Add regression coverage for the timeout and paused encryption boundary.

- Strict lint passed.

author: ratulmaharaj
body:
Fixes #41.

## Everyone sees the controls

Agent controls were the organiser's alone. They're the room's now — an agent talking over the meeting is everyone's problem, and making one person the only one who can mute it is how a call derails while five people wait for them to notice.

## Every control announces itself

Controls now carry who pressed them, and the room gets a toast, exactly as the issue describes:

- `Amin set Scout's response mode to raise-hand`
- `Gwinyai interrupted Scout`
- `Ratul deafened Echo`

LiveKit doesn't echo a data message back to its sender, so the actor toasts locally ("You muted Scout") while everyone else toasts on receipt. Both paths call the same `describeAgentControl` so the wording can't drift between them, and repeats of the same control on the same agent collapse via `toastId` instead of stacking up the corner.

Removing an agent has no data message of its own — it goes through the control API — so it publishes a notice the bridge ignores. It fires on the mutation's `onSuccess`, so a removal the server refused is never reported to the room as done.

## Host settings (from your comment)

Two toggles in Settings, host-only, under "Everyone in this meeting can":

- **Control agents** — mute, interrupt, zap, change turn policy
- **Invite agents** — from the registry or by URL

They live in **room metadata**, not a data message, so someone who joins later is bound by them too and LiveKit pushes changes to everyone already in the room.

Both default to **on**, matching the issue's "all participants should see agent controls". If you'd rather invites stayed host-only by default, that's a one-line change in `defaultRoomSettings`.

## Worth knowing: the invite routes had no auth at all

While wiring the toggle I found `/api/rooms/[slug]/agents` and `/agents/[id]` did no host check whatsoever — the UI hid the buttons and the endpoints took anyone's word for it. So a "reserved" room would have been one crafted request away from being unreserved, and the toggle would have been decoration.

Both routes now check the setting, and accept the organiser's key via an `x-host-key` header (a header rather than a body field, so it works uniformly for `DELETE`). The host-key verification itself moved into `lib/server/host.ts`; `moderate/route.ts` now uses that instead of its own copy.

## Disabled, not hidden

When a host reserves controls, the buttons stay visible and go inert, with the tip explaining whose they are. A control you can see and can't press explains itself; one that isn't there leaves people wondering why nobody can stop the agent.

## Testing

Adds vitest to `packages/shared` (it had none) for the protocol helpers — 19 tests. Two worth calling out:

- one iterates every member of the control-type enum and fails if a new control ships without a sentence to announce it
- settings parsing has to default to **open** for rooms created before settings existed, which is easy to get backwards and would silently lock down every existing meeting

`pnpm lint && pnpm -r typecheck && pnpm -r test && pnpm -r build` all pass (34 tests). Not exercised in a live multi-participant meeting — the toast wording and the host-toggle round trip are the parts most worth a manual look.

author: vincentzed
body:
Decode context parallelism (DCP) for DSA models (GLM-5.x, DeepSeek V3.2). Extends the MLA DCP path (#14194) to sparse attention.

1. KV cache is interleaved across DCP ranks (`slot % dcp_size`), same as MLA DCP. KV capacity multiplies by dcp_size: 2,292,288 tokens/rank physical -> 4,252,416 logical at dcp2 on the default fp8 KV stack.
2. Indexer K cache is replicated (sized `size * dcp`, indexed by global slot). The indexer is all ReplicatedLinear, so every rank computes identical top-k. Each rank keeps only its owned slots (filter + divide in the index transform kernels).
3. Decode and extend both all-gather q across the DCP group (ranks hold different TP head groups), run sparse attention on the local shard, and LSE-combine (`cp_lse_ag_out_rs_mla`, base-2).
4. trtllm backends only (the sm100 defaults, asserted at launch): the sparse kernel scans a counted valid-first prefix, not -1 skipping. The owner filter is followed by descending-sort compaction, and per-row counts are passed as seq_lens. Needs `return_lse` (flashinfer >= 0.6.14). flashmla_sparse was only used during bring-up and its DCP support is removed (ba054051).
6. Composes with dp-attention (requires `attn_tp_size % dcp_size == 0`) and with EP (TEP4 + DCP4 measured 0.915 GSM8K at 200q). EAGLE works, experimental, needs flashinfer >= 0.6.15 (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3238). Prefill CP + DCP is rejected at launch, see F7.
7. `ag_rs` stays the comm-backend default. On a single NVSwitch node at dcp2 it is ~8% faster than `a2a` (multi-node is the opposite, see #21637).

Tested on 4x/8x B300 (sm103), GLM-5.2 NVFP4 / FP8 / BF16, flashinfer 0.6.14/0.6.15, sgl-kernel 0.4.5.

![GLM-5.2-NVFP4 DCP Pareto](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vincentzed/sglang/bench-assets/assets/pareto_glm52_dcp.png)

The concurrency sweep for each line stops at that config's measured KV capacity, so every point is queue-free. TP4 has the best latency wherever it fits and ends at 68 users (32K) / 17 users (128K); DCP2 and DCP4 continue to 127/180 and 32/45.

**Median TPOT (ms) at concurrency 1:**

| context | TP4 | DCP2 | DCP4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 32K | 6.67 | 11.27 | 11.74 |
| 128K | 6.86 | 12.04 | 12.57 |

### KV cache capacity (measured `max_total_num_tokens`, fp8 KV defaults)

| parallelism | mem-fraction | physical tokens/rank | logical KV tokens | vs tp4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| tp4 | 0.85 | 2,292,288 | 2,292,288 | 1.0x |
| tp4 dcp2 | 0.82 | 2,126,208 | 4,252,416 | 1.85x |
| tp4 dcp4 (dcp = tp size) | 0.70 | 1,504,192 | 6,016,768 | 2.62x |

Logical capacity scales sub-linearly because mem-fraction has to drop to fund the per-dcp allocations (see F-list). The launch log prints the physical per-rank count; metrics report the logical one.

## Commands

Common: `--host 127.0.0.1 --port 31510`.

Accuracy evals (fresh server per config, first run discarded for JIT warm-up):
- GSM8K: `python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --num-shots 8 --num-questions 1319 --parallel 200 --port 31510`
- AIME25: `sgl-eval run aime25 --base-url http://127.0.0.1:31510/v1 --num-examples 30 --n-repeats 4 --num-threads 30 --max-tokens 64000 --temperature 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --thinking` (install: `pip install git+https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-eval`). Scores are read from metrics.json, error_rate is 0.0 on every row. `--thinking` is required, otherwise the answer stays in the reasoning channel and scoring breaks. More than ~30 threads causes request errors that count as wrong answers.

### Accuracy (GSM8K 8-shot 1319q / AIME25 pass@1 avg-of-4)

| checkpoint | stack | parallelism | GSM8K | AIME25 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NVFP4 | trtllm + fp8 KV (defaults) | tp4 | 0.945 | 0.875 |
| NVFP4 | trtllm + fp8 KV (defaults) | tp4 dcp2 | 0.939 | 0.925 |
| NVFP4 | trtllm + fp8 KV (defaults) | tp4 dcp4 | 0.940 | 0.917 |
| FP8 | trtllm + fp8 KV (defaults) | tp4 | 0.944 | 0.908 |
| FP8 | trtllm + fp8 KV (defaults) | tp4 dcp2 | 0.940 | 0.883 |
| NVFP4 | defaults + dp-attention | tp4 dp2 dcp2 | 0.939 | 0.917 |
| NVFP4 | defaults + EAGLE 5-1-6 | tp4 | 0.942 | 0.933 |
| NVFP4 | defaults + EAGLE 5-1-6 | tp4 dcp2 | 0.939 | 0.883 |

GSM8K 0.939-0.945, AIME25 0.875-0.933 (pass@1 sem ~0.02-0.04 per run). All DCP rows are within noise of baseline.

dcp4 needs `--mem-fraction-static 0.70 --cuda-graph-max-bs 256`. Pool sizing does not yet account for the allocations that grow with dcp: the replicated index-K buffers, the trtllm workspace, the indexer capture workspace, and the widened-q extend transients.
```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 --tp 4 --dcp-size 4 \
  --quantization modelopt_fp4 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.70 --cuda-graph-max-bs 256 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31510
``` Bench: `python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31510 --dataset-name random --random-input-len <ISL> --random-output-len <OSL> --random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts <N> --max-concurrency <CC>` (flush cache between points).

### Validated configurations (full commands)

**8. Prefill CP only, tp4.** TTFT -48% to -55% at 128k.
```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 --tp 4 \
  --enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave --quantization modelopt_fp4 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 32768 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31510
```

**10. trtllm + fp8 KV (sm100 defaults), tp4 baseline**
```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 --tp 4 \
  --quantization modelopt_fp4 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31510
```

**11. trtllm + fp8 KV, tp4 + dcp2.** 4,252,416 logical KV tokens.
```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 --tp 4 --dcp-size 2 \
  --quantization modelopt_fp4 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.82 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31510
```

**13. dp-attention, tp4 dp2 baseline, trtllm defaults**
```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 --tp 4 \
  --dp-size 2 --enable-dp-attention \
  --quantization modelopt_fp4 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.80 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31510
```

**14. dp-attention + DCP, tp4 dp2 dcp2, trtllm defaults.** Requires `attn_tp_size % dcp_size == 0`.
```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 --tp 4 \
  --dp-size 2 --enable-dp-attention --dcp-size 2 \
  --quantization modelopt_fp4 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.75 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31510
```

**16. EAGLE 5-1-6, no DCP, default kernel stack.** Needs flashinfer >= 0.6.15 (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3238).
```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 --tp 4 \
  --quantization modelopt_fp4 \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 5 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31510
```

**17. EAGLE 5-1-6 + dcp2, default kernel stack, experimental.** Accept length 4.35-4.61. Verify runs through the trtllm LSE path.
```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 --tp 4 --dcp-size 2 \
  --quantization modelopt_fp4 \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 5 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.80 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31510
```

### Not working (full commands)

**F1. EAGLE + DCP is experimental (configs 16-17).** Main now pins flashinfer 0.6.15.post1, which has the flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3238 draft MoE fix, so the stock install works.

**F2. bf16 KV cache under DCP.** Works with explicit backends: `--kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 --dsa-prefill-backend trtllm --dsa-decode-backend trtllm` scores 0.935 GSM8K (200q) at dcp2. Without the explicit flags, bf16 KV auto-resolves the prefill backend to flashmla_sparse and DCP rejects it at launch.

author: elanroth
body: The current statement is false as written: the sum over `Finset.range n` stops at i = n-1, so every term has a factor `s.2 ^ (n - i)` with n - i ≥ 1. Taking S = {(1, 0)} (primitive, since gcd 1 0 = 1) the sum is 0 for every choice of n and a, never 1. With `range (n + 1)` the i = n term `a n * x ^ n` is included, matching the doc comment (`a₀xⁿ + a₁xⁿ⁻¹y + ... + aₙyⁿ`) and the original problem.

author: eawrceqa
body:
## Problem

`_detect_metric_field()` in `agentic_core/schema_inference.py:96` decides whether a numeric column should become an aggregatable metric in the auto-generated semantic layer. It excludes "ID-like" fields with a **substring** test:

```python
if any(p in name_lower for p in ["_id", "id", "code", "编号", "year", "月", "日"]):
    return False
```

Because `"id"` is checked as a substring, it matches any field name that merely *contains* those two letters. Common measurement columns are silently dropped from metrics: `width`, `humidity`, `grid_load`, `candidate_count`, and similar. On data upload (`POST /api/data/upload` → `infer_schema`), these valid metrics never make it into the semantic layer, so the assistant can't aggregate them.

Note this is inconsistent with the sibling function `_detect_id_field()` (same file), which already matches ID patterns precisely via `endswith` / equality rather than substring.

## Reproduction

Loading the module and calling `infer_schema` on genuine (non-ID, low-cardinality) float measurements:

```
metrics detected by infer_schema: ['总营收']
  humidity   type=float  is_metric=False is_id=False
  width      type=float  is_metric=False is_id=False
  revenue    type=float  is_metric=True  is_id=False
```

`width` and `humidity` have `is_id=False` — they are legitimate metrics — yet are excluded purely because their names contain `id`.

## Fix

Match `id` / `_id` precisely (standalone name or `_id` suffix), mirroring `_detect_id_field`:

```python
if name_lower == "id" or name_lower.endswith("_id"):
    return False
if any(p in name_lower for p in ["code", "编号", "year", "月", "日"]):
    return False
```

After the fix, the same input yields:

```
metrics detected by infer_schema: ['平均湿度', '总营收', '平均宽度']
  humidity  is_metric=True
  width     is_metric=True
```

and real ID columns are still excluded (`id`, `vehicle_id`, `user_id` → not metrics).

## Verification

- `python -m py_compile agentic_core/schema_inference.py` passes.
- Ran the module directly (via importlib, so it doesn't pull the package's optional `strands` import) before and after the change; confirmed the excluded measurement fields are recovered and that `id` / `*_id` columns stay excluded.

The change is limited to the name-matching heuristic in `_detect_metric_field`; the `code` / `编号` / `year` / `月` / `日` matches are preserved unchanged.

author: jdx
body:
## Why

fnox keeps its MSRV (`rust-version` in `Cargo.toml`) **behind** latest-stable Rust on purpose: it's built from source by packagers that provide their own, often older, `rustc` — Linux distro `cargo install`s against a distro-provided toolchain, and nixpkgs (one shared, conservative `rustc` for the whole tree). Raising the MSRV can make fnox unbuildable there.

This keeps biting via renovate: e.g. [#622](https://github.com/jdx/fnox/pull/622) (aws-sdk → 1.9.0) raises the required compiler to **rustc 1.94.1**, so `cargo msrv verify` fails. The tempting "fix" is to bump the MSRV — but that's exactly what we don't want to do.

## What

- **`.cargo/config.toml`** — set `resolver.incompatible-rust-versions = "fallback"` (the workspace is already on `resolver = "3"`). Now `cargo update`/`cargo add` prefer dependency versions compatible with our declared MSRV instead of dragging the floor up.
- **`AGENTS.md`** — new "Minimum Supported Rust Version (MSRV)" section spelling out the policy and how it relates to (but is independent of) the glibc floor.
- **`Cargo.toml`** — a comment next to `rust-version` so the rule is visible at the point of temptation: *don't raise MSRV for a dependency; pin the dependency instead.*

No dependency versions change here, so `msrv`/build/test are unaffected on this PR.

_This PR was generated by Claude Code._

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Documentation and Cargo resolver config only; no runtime code or dependency version changes.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **MSRV-aware Cargo resolution** via new `.cargo/config.toml` with `resolver.incompatible-rust-versions = "fallback"`, so `cargo update` / `cargo add` prefer crates compatible with the workspace `rust-version` instead of silently requiring a newer rustc.
> 
> Documents the **packager-first MSRV policy** in `AGENTS.md` (keep MSRV behind latest stable; pin dependencies rather than raising MSRV when Renovate bumps need a newer compiler) and adds matching comments beside `rust-version` in `Cargo.toml`. **No dependency or `rust-version` value changes** in this PR.

author: sitejob-nl
body:
## Waarom

Op 17 juni/17 juli is afgesproken dat matching alleen draait over kandidaten die een recruiter heeft toegelaten — "AI moet niet over slechte kandidaten lopen". In de code stond `nieuw` gewoon in `ACTIVE_STATUSES`, en dat is precies de status waarop Carerix-imports binnenkomen. Netto werden ~2000 nooit-beoordeelde mensen gerangschikt en aan klanten voorgesteld.

De poort simpelweg dichtzetten kon niet: er stonden **9** kandidaten op `werkzoekend` tegen **2062** op `nieuw`. Matching zou van ~2071 naar 9 kandidaten zijn gegaan.

## Wat er is gebeurd

**Data (al uitgevoerd op productie, JA Werkt-org).** De Carerix-historie is eenmalig als toegelaten gemarkeerd — akkoord van Kas. 1992 bereikbare kandidaten van `nieuw` → `werkzoekend`. De 70 zonder telefoon én e-mail blijven op `nieuw`: zonder contactgegevens is er geen kandidaat om voor te stellen.

| | vóór | na |
|---|---|---|
| werkzoekend | 9 | **2001** |
| nieuw | 2062 | 70 |

Terugrolrecept: `rollback-toelating-20260720.sql` (zet alles terug behalve de 9 die al toegelaten waren).

**Code.** Statuslijsten naar `_shared/matching-core.ts` als één bron van waarheid:

- `MATCHABLE_CANDIDATE_STATUSES` = `beschikbaar`, `werkzoekend` — `nieuw` en `in_behandeling` eruit. Die laatste betekent "recruiter volgt op", dus vóór het toelatingsbesluit.
- `UNSCORABLE_CANDIDATE_STATUSES` = `afgewezen`, `uitgeschreven`, `niet_beschikbaar` — `calculate-match` filterde helemaal niet op status, waardoor een afgewezen kandidaat alsnog een verse matchscore op zijn dossier kreeg. Geeft nu 409. `geplaatst` staat er bewust niet bij: een bestaande plaatsing herberekenen is legitiem.

## Operationeel gevolg — lezen vóór merge

Nieuwe Carerix-syncs en website-instroom komen binnen op `nieuw` en worden **pas gematcht ná toelating** in de instroomfunnel. Dat is de bedoelde werking, maar het is nieuw gedrag: wie gewend was dat een verse import meteen in de shortlist opdook, moet nu eerst door "Toelaten als kandidaat".

## Verificatie

- `deno check` op beide edge functions — groen
- `npm run typecheck`, `lint` (0 errors), `build`, `test` — **490 tests / 57 files** groen
- 5 regressietests op de poort, met expliciet de `nieuw`-case als bewaking

## Na merge

`rank-candidates` en `calculate-match` moeten gedeployd worden (beide raken `_shared/matching-core.ts`). `rank-vacancies` importeert dezelfde kern en gaat voor de zekerheid mee.
