author: notaparlaymaker
body:
### Motivation
- Implement the Informational Relativity Principle so evidential assessments are always relative to an explicit `VerificationFrame` rather than being intrinsic to a claim.
- Replace single scalar trust outputs with a multidimensional measurement vector and separate policy-driven verdicts so verdicts are swappable and versioned independently.
- Provide frame-diff attribution and ensure integrity fields (`claim_hash`, `frame_hash`, `evidence_root`, `receipt_hash`, `signatures`) live only under an `integrity` object in receipts.

### Description
- Renamed claim-extraction confidence to `process_confidence` across claim types, evidence-bundle schemas, the `factual-consensus` program, and fixtures to remove a naked `confidence` claim field.
- Added `verifier-node/src/scoring/informationalRelativity.ts` implementing `VerificationFrame`, deterministic canonical serialization + `hashVerificationFrame`, a verdict-free `MeasurementVector` and `evaluateEvidence`, versioned verdict policy primitives (`VersionedVerdictPolicy`, `applyVerdictPolicy`), `verifyInFrame`, `diffAssessmentReceipts` with heuristic normalized attribution, and `createInformationalRelativityReceipt` producing the target receipt shape with integrity-only commitments.
- Added unit tests in `verifier-node/test/informationalRelativity.test.ts` covering deterministic frame hashing, measurement-only evaluation, policy versioning (different verdicts from same measurements), abstention as a first-class result, diffs with normalized attributions, and integrity placement in receipts.
- Left calibration unchanged and skipped `calibration_confidence` because the repository benchmark dataset is below the configured minimum sample size (decision per Step 6 requirement).

### Testing
- Ran a targeted claim-object audit using `rg` to validate removal of naked claim-level `"confidence"` fields for claim extraction, which confirmed updated claim-level fields now use `process_confidence` (passed).
- Added unit tests under `verifier-node/test/informationalRelativity.test.ts` but running the repository test command `npm test -- --runInBand` in this environment failed because `jest` is not installed (`sh: 1: jest: not found`) so the new tests were not executed here (blocked).
- Attempted typecheck with `npx --no-install tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` but it failed due to missing `@types/jest` and `@types/node` in the environment and a pre-existing `moduleResolution=node10` deprecation (blocked).
- Verified benchmark size with a Node one-liner which showed the factual-QA benchmark has 10 samples while calibration requires 100 samples, so calibration was intentionally skipped (passed).
- Performed `git diff --check` and basic repository hygiene checks which passed; committed changes as `feat(verifier): add frame-relative assessments`.

If you want, I can (A) run the newly added Jest tests once the environment has `jest` and type definitions installed, (B) open follow-ups to propagate `process_confidence` naming to any remaining non-claim confidence fields that should be renamed, or (C) adjust policy thresholds and attribution weights to taste.

author: jeffredodd
body:
## Summary

Fixes six mobile-only overflow/rendering bugs, found via the original iPhone bug report plus a full app sweep (static audit of six overflow-prone pattern classes + dynamic 393px sweep of all 27 route states, seeded long-name data, and every interactive popup surface). All reproduced and re-verified in both Chromium and WebKit (iPhone emulation).

### Commit 1 — original report
1. **Editor toolbar pickers ran off-screen.** The tiptap `ToolbarDropdown` (Variables / Colors / Formatting / Formula) is anchored `absolute left-0` with no collision handling; a 274px panel opened at x=275 on a 393px viewport. It now measures the open panel and shifts it into view (re-clamping on panel/window resize), capped at `100vw - 16px`.
2. **Board previews overflowed their frame ("overlapping colors").** The dashboard Active Display and setup wizard rendered raw `BoardDisplay` (needs ~372px; the dashboard card offers ~320px on phones), clipping the first column and spilling color chips over the frame. Both now use `ScaledBoardDisplay`.

### Commit 2 — sweep findings
3. **Select dropdowns blew out with long item names (app-wide).** `SelectContent` had no max-width; Radix sizes the panel to the widest item and only clamps *position*, so a long page name produced a **659px-wide** dropdown on a 393px screen. Capped at `calc(100vw-16px)` in `ui/select.tsx` — long items now wrap. Covers the schedule form, gap-default select, plugin page pickers, etc.
4. **Collections cards never truncated.** The CardHeader grid item lacked `min-w-0`, so long names inflated the header row to ~755px via min-content propagation (Badge is `whitespace-nowrap`). Fixed with `min-w-0` at the grid item + truncating spans for the title and page chips.
5. **Schedule calendar zoom slider rendered off-screen** on phones (top bar needs ~500px). The bar now wraps, dropping the zoom control to its own right-aligned line.
6. **Schedule form day chips clipped** (Sun/Fri half-cut). Chip rows now wrap.

Everything else swept came back clean: settings tab strip scrolls, all tables have scroll/clip wrappers with responsive column hiding, timezone/time-picker portals stay in-viewport, Radix dropdown width overrides are ≤320px (collision-safe), media/canvas elements are fluid.

## Test plan

- [x] Reproduced all six at 393×852 before fixing (Chromium + WebKit); re-verified fixed in both engines
- [x] Desktop (1280px) spot-checked unchanged for calendar, collections, selects
- [x] 5 new Playwright regression tests in `web/tests/mobile-critical-flows.spec.ts` — each verified to fail on the unfixed code; full mobile spec: 16/16 passing
- [x] Full web unit suite green in the dev container (95 files, 1186 passed)

author: kyle-sexton
body:
## Summary

Adopts the shared **ci-status** composite from `ci-workflows` and performs the coordinated `v0.6.1 -> v0.7.0` pin bump that the repo's single-SHA supply-chain test requires — in one PR because the two cannot be separated.

### 1. Adopt the ci-status composite (behavior-preserving)

`ci.yml`'s `ci-status` job previously aggregated lane results with an inline `env: RESULTS` + `run:` shell loop. That step is replaced with a `uses:` of `melodic-software/ci-workflows/.github/actions/ci-status`, passing the **byte-identical** folded `RESULTS` scalar as the `results:` input. The job shell is otherwise untouched — same `name`, `if: always()`, 20-item `needs:` list, `runs-on`, and `timeout-minutes`.

The call sets `treat-skipped-as: pass` **explicitly**. This is the composite's default, so behavior is unchanged: a `skipped` lane still passes, preserving this repo's long-standing `success|skipped` gate semantics. Setting it at the call site keeps that policy legible and makes the divergence from the strict repos (which use `treat-skipped-as: fail`) intentional and visible rather than an invisible default.

### 2. Coordinated pin bump forced by the single-SHA test

`.github/scripts/workflow-pin-metadata.test.cjs` enforces that **every** `melodic-software/ci-workflows/` reference resolves to exactly **one** SHA / release version. The ci-status composite only exists at **v0.7.0** (`87fb95c3b05fa318b9dd8c2c164cc550071a1ccb`), so introducing it while the other references stayed at v0.6.1 would break that invariant. Every ci-workflows reference therefore moves together, in this one commit:

- 16 pinned references in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (lane actions + `zizmor.yml` + `go-quality.yml`)
- `do-not-merge.yml`, `link-check.yml`, `pr-issue-linkage.yml`, `pr-title.yml` (1 each)
- the **new** ci-status composite reference (+1)

Total inventoried references: **20 -> 21**. Also updated in lockstep:

- `release/dependencies.json` — the `melodic-software/ci-workflows` pin now records `87fb95c...`.
- `workflow-pin-metadata.test.cjs` constants — `ciWorkflowsSha`, `ciWorkflowsVersion` (`v0.6.1 -> v0.7.0`), and `expectedCiWorkflowsReferences` (`20 -> 21`); the stale v0.6.1 assertion-message text was reconciled at the same time.

Confirmed against the `ci-workflows` tree at `87fb95c` that every referenced action and reusable workflow exists at that SHA — v0.7.0 is a superset of the v0.6.1 tree.

### Incidental hardening that rides along with the bump

The v0.7.0 ci-status composite also carries fixes that come with the shared implementation: a `nullglob`-safe results split, correct multi-line block-scalar parsing (an inline `read` would stop at the first newline), and an empty-`results` guard that fails a miswired gate rather than reporting a vacuous pass. These are improvements over the inline loop this PR removes; they change no passing-path behavior for this repo.

### Verification

- `node --test .github/scripts/*.test.cjs` — **28 pass, 0 fail**, including the pin-inventory and ci-status-gateway tests.
- `actionlint` — clean.
- Straggler sweep `grep -rn '90f1c54|1d3762c' .github release` — no hits; version sweep for `v0.6.1` — no hits.

No related issue: rollout of the decision recorded in melodic-software/ci-workflows#163.

## Related

- melodic-software/ci-workflows#163 — the decision this PR rolls out (shared ci-status composite with `treat-skipped-as` policy input).
- `melodic-software/ci-workflows` release **v0.7.0** (`87fb95c3b05fa318b9dd8c2c164cc550071a1ccb`) — the release that first contains the ci-status composite and the SHA every reference now pins.

author: pcarrino58
body:
Fix the issue where typing in column B doesn't look up a word and present options, and doesn't auto-propagate to matching rows.

* The `InitializeMatcher` function in `Matcher.bas` was truncated and was missing the critical lines to initialize dictionaries (`EnsureDictionaries`) and build the caching logic (`BuildLookupCache wsLookup`). Because this was broken, the caching logic to load lookup strings (`mLookupPhraseSet`) was empty and uninitialized. 
* Consequently, `IsValidOutputList` function would always exit since `mLookupPhraseSet` was Nothing.
* `Sheet5.cls` logic requires `IsValidOutputList` to process lookups, dropdown validation, and auto-propagation. By restoring the correct `InitializeMatcher` function initialization logic, we ensure these dictionaries are populated properly so that `IsValidOutputList`, `BuildSearchDropdown`, and learning/auto propagation logic functions correctly.
* In `IsValidOutputList`, added explicit assignment for `IsValidOutputList = False` rather than relying on default implicit return for readability.

author: johnnybyzhang
body:
## 摘要

为 Claude `/v1/messages` 增加一条面向 Codex Responses API 的协议桥接路径，让 Claude App、Claude Code 等客户端继续按 Claude Messages 协议工作，同时复用 CPA 现有的 Codex OAuth、模型路由和上游连接。

这条路径不引入新的服务，也不增加 endpoint 或 target model 配置。CPA 仍然只是路由器：普通请求发往当前 Codex 上游的 `/responses`；当 Claude 自己发出自动压缩请求时，同一条路由直接改用该上游的 `/responses/compact`。上游模型沿用请求解码后的模型，不做额外覆盖。

## 背景

Claude 客户端会根据流式 usage 判断上下文消耗，并自行决定何时压缩、重放和继续会话。Codex Responses 流此前只有结束事件携带完整 usage；长时间运行的主会话或 worker 在执行过程中看不到持续增长的 token 数，容易在客户端尚未触发自动压缩前耗尽上下文。

此外，`/responses/compact` 返回的压缩状态包含不透明加密数据，后续重放必须继续使用生成该状态的原始 Codex 凭据。普通请求不应因此被固定到某个凭据，只有携带压缩状态的续接请求需要保持 auth affinity。

## 实现

### `/v1/messages` → Codex Responses

- 仅在 Claude 客户端模型 ID 解码为 GPT 模型时启用 bridge；原生 Claude 和其他 provider 的现有路径保持不变。
- 非流式和 SSE 流式请求都通过现有 Codex executor 调用 `/responses`，再转换为 Claude Messages 响应，并把客户端看到的模型 ID 恢复为原值。
- 请求继续使用 CPA 原有的 Codex OAuth 选择和上游配置。
- WebSocket 只在所选 auth 明确启用时使用，否则回退到 HTTP/SSE。

### Claude 驱动的自动压缩

- 只识别 Claude 自动压缩提示中稳定的内部约束组合，普通的“总结对话”请求仍走 `/responses`，避免误判。
- 压缩请求保留完整历史，Claude 提供的自定义压缩要求作为最后一条输入随 transcript 一起送往 `/responses/compact`。
- 上游返回的 message 与 opaque compaction item 会封装进带版本、模型和 auth ID 的 capsule，再作为标准 Claude 文本响应返回。
- 后续请求会校验 capsule 的边界、大小、版本、模型和 item 类型，移除对 Claude 可见的 marker，并把不透明状态放回 Codex input 前部。
- 初次压缩仍使用正常 auth 调度；只有重放 capsule 时才固定到原始 auth，确保加密状态可用。
- 流式 compact 请求在内部缓冲 `/responses/compact` 的结果，再按 Claude SSE 事件序列输出。

### 运行中的 token usage

- `message_start` 提供本地计算的输入 token 数，供 Claude 从响应开始阶段就建立上下文基线。
- HTTP 和 WebSocket 路径都会发送累计的 `message_delta.usage.output_tokens`，覆盖文本、工具参数和 reasoning summary 等增量。
- 对上游未实时公开的 reasoning token 数，使用保守估算生成 `output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens`；如果客户端启用 thinking-token-count beta，也会发送符合 Claude 事件形状的 `estimated_tokens`。(仍在测试中)
- `response.completed` 中的上游 usage 始终覆盖本地估算，作为本轮最终准确值；Codex 内部 prompt cache 不会伪装成 Anthropic cache-control usage。
- bridge 使用 200k 的 Claude 兼容上下文边界。超过边界时返回 `context_too_large`，由 Claude 客户端执行原生 compact-and-retry。

### 稳定性修正

- HTTP 上游已经建立连接后不增加网络超时；取消下游 context 时，空闲流会及时关闭 scanner、response body、ticker 和输出 channel。
- 公共 `CountTokens` 保持精确计数；用于 bridge 上下文预算的 256-token 保守 framing allowance 不再污染公开结果。
- compaction marker 只在独立分隔的完整 capsule 上生效，源码或对话中引用 marker 常量不会被误当成重放状态。

## 用户侧效果

- Claude 客户端无需修改，也无需了解 Codex Responses 协议。
- 主会话和 workflow worker 可以在响应进行过程中看到累计 token usage，而不是等整轮结束。
- 自动压缩仍由 Claude 决定何时触发；CPA 只负责协议转换、路由 `/responses/compact` 和安全重放。
- 普通 Codex OAuth 轮转行为保持不变，压缩状态则能稳定续接到原始凭据。

## 验证

覆盖范围包括 handler 路由、compact 检测与重放、HTTP/SSE、WebSocket、usage 累计、reasoning token 估算、取消清理、精确 CountTokens 和 HTTP fallback。

```bash
go test ./internal/runtime/executor -run 'TestCodex.*(Bridge|Cancel|Count|Websocket)|TestValidateClaudeBridgeContextWindow|TestClaudeThinkingTokenCountRequested|TestApplyClaudeResponsesCompactionReplay' -count=1
go test ./internal/runtime/executor/helps -run 'TestClaude(StreamUsage|CumulativeUsage|ApplyMessageStart|ThinkingToken)' -count=1
go test ./sdk/api/handlers/claude -count=1
go test ./internal/translator/codex/claude -count=1
go test -race ./internal/runtime/executor -run 'TestCodex.*(Bridge|Cancel|Count|Websocket)|TestValidateClaudeBridgeContextWindow|TestClaudeThinkingTokenCountRequested|TestApplyClaudeResponsesCompactionReplay' -count=1
go test -race ./internal/runtime/executor/helps -run 'TestClaude(StreamUsage|CumulativeUsage|ApplyMessageStart|ThinkingToken)' -count=1
go test -race ./sdk/api/handlers/claude -count=1
go test ./...
go build -o test-output ./cmd/server && rm test-output
```

本地端到端验证使用未修改的 Claude Code `2.1.211` 和 CPA localhost 实例，通过程序化工具调用持续生成上下文；测试观察到 `tool_calls=6`、`compact_boundaries=1`，最终输出 `CLAUDE_NATIVE_AUTOCOMPACT_E2E_OK`。测试期间只降低了触发阈值，没有修改 Claude 客户端。

## 范围

本 PR 只修改 Claude/Codex bridge 所需的 handler、executor、translator、usage helper 及对应测试，共 13 个文件；不涉及文档、模型目录或其他 provider 的改动。

author: mmarmol
body:
## What

Adds a structured GitHub issue form and disables freeform ("blank") issues, so
outside users are channeled into filing actionable bug reports rather than
arbitrary issues.

- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml` — a bug-report form (durin version,
  surface, what happened, repro steps, logs, environment; version / surface /
  what-happened / repro are required).
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml` — `blank_issues_enabled: false` plus a
  contact link routing security reports to the private advisories flow (never a
  public issue), consistent with `SECURITY.md`.

## Why

The repo is public and had no issue templates — issues were freeform. This
channels outside users into structured bug reports (and routes security
privately), while everything else (PRs, merges) stays gated exactly as before.

author: kevinthelago
body:
Closes #3481. Slice 2 of migrating the app's own UI into the graphs (slice 1: #3462). **The first slice that touches the page**, and the one that establishes the pattern every later slice depends on.

## Why these three
#3462 deliberately did **not** catalogue `FleetHealth`/`CostEnergy`/`FleetLessons`: they read everything from the store and take **no props**, so their records would have had `props: []` — describing something nothing can reuse or render. They were also the easiest three to fix, because the behavioural part of each is one or two hook lines and everything from `return (` down was already a pure function of one derived object.

## The split
| View | What the host keeps |
|---|---|
| `FleetHealthView(health, permLoaded)` | 2 store reads + the coord log + the `bsc logs perm` poll → `buildFleetHealth` |
| `CostEnergyView(cost, co2)` | the `bsc logs cost` poll + aggregation |
| `FleetLessonsView(lessons, loaded)` | the store read + the lesson poll |

**No behaviour or visual change** — each host renders its view with exactly what it computed before.

One deliberate call: `dangerCount` is derived **inside** `FleetHealthView` rather than passed. It is a pure function of `health.counts`, so making it a prop would let a caller contradict the data it is rendering.

## Records + tests
Adds the three to the packaged `fleet` kit (**9 records** now), with real prop contracts and working import snippets — they are exported, so unlike slice 1's file-local components the `srcText` shows a genuine import.

The colocated render tests are as much the point as the split: this markup could previously only be tested by mocking a store read, a coordination poll **and** a `bsc` call. Now the interesting cases are directly reachable — loading vs genuinely-empty (the distinction these cards exist to make), and the truncation boundaries where the withheld remainder must be stated rather than silently dropped.

> Two fixture bugs surfaced, both caught by **running** the tests rather than reading them: an `as Lesson` cast silenced a missing required field that `lessonTitle` dereferences, and a blank `rule` made the title fall back to `mistake` so both rendered identical text. Fixed by fully typing the fixture (no cast) and giving it realistic distinct values — not by loosening the assertions.

## Gate
`typecheck` clean · `eslint` clean on all changed files · **8/8 render tests green** · record constraints verified (lowercase-unique ids, no collision with the 66 react-ui records, in-vocabulary shapes, no artifact-only `source`). Re-gated after merging develop.

author: jmenziessmith
body:
Executes the cleanup handoff in `docs/handoffs/2026-07-20-tick-runner-decomposition.md`: `src/core/tick-runner.ts` had grown by accretion to ~1700 lines. This splits its independent concerns into focused `createX(deps)` modules that mirror the existing `sink-router.ts`/`policy-engine.ts` shape, and unifies the one piece of logic that had silently forked.

## Eligibility unification (the "fix first" step)
`shouldMarkPending` and the `runRunnerTick` candidate predicate implemented the same "is this issue eligible, on a known stage, with a next action" question as two independent chains. They had **already diverged** in the awaiting-approval branch (one used `needsWakeAction`, the other the three actionable resolvers). Both now call a single `policy.resolveNextEligibleAction(issue, config)`.

The unified predicate adopts the three-resolver semantics: it preserves `shouldMarkPending` exactly, and tightens the runner candidate so an awaiting-approval issue with only a *conversational* comment no longer gets selected and then falls straight through to `idle` — which previously blocked the whole runner tick from reaching a later actionable issue. This is the only intentional behaviour change; all existing end-to-end tests pass unmodified.

## Extractions (pure move + narrow-the-interface, no behaviour change)
| Module | Concern |
|---|---|
| `lib/format.ts` | cost/duration/token formatting (pure) |
| `core/event-builders.ts` | publish-intent & labels payload shaping |
| `core/outbox.ts` | outbound delivery, bounded retry, dead-lettering |
| `core/event-resolver.ts` | unkeyed-event → work-item correlation / mint |
| `core/stale-run-reconciler.ts` | stale running-record reconciliation |
| `core/workspace-cleanup.ts` | closed-issue workspace/transcript cleanup |

Each takes only the slice of deps it needs. Every invariant-explaining comment (per-event stamping, `rebuildFromEvents` ordering, crash/replay healing) moved **verbatim** with its code. `stale-run-reconciler` takes `deliverOutboundEvent` as an injected function so it doesn't import the outbox module directly. Also applied the opportunistic fix from the handoff: inlined the `workspaceModeForCustomCommand` one-line wrapper.

`tick-runner.ts` drops from ~1697 to ~890 lines. The plan's ~500 target isn't fully met: the remainder is `runRunnerTick`, the irreducible tick orchestration the handoff says should stay — decomposing it further is called out there as separate follow-up.

## Tests
- New isolated unit tests for `lib/format.ts` (12) and `core/outbox.ts` (5), plus direct tests for `policy.resolveNextEligibleAction` (3).
- Full suite: **563 passing** / 2 skipped. `npm run lint` and `npm run build` clean.

> Note: `npm run format:check` flags files locally because this Windows checkout has `core.autocrlf=true` (it flags untouched files like `src/main.ts` too); the committed blobs are LF and prettier-clean, so it passes on CI.

author: kvaps
body:
## What this does

Adds opt-in ComputePlane placement for the code-executing apps in this catalog — `jupyterhub`, `langflow`, and `comfyui`. Each chart gains a `computePlane` toggle (default `false`): with the toggle off every chart renders exactly as on `main` today, fully co-located in the tenant namespace; with the toggle on, the untrusted workload is remote-applied onto the tenant's hidden ComputePlane cluster.

## How it works

The management-side release renders an inner Flux `HelmRelease` carrying `spec.kubeConfig.secretRef` → Secret `computeplane-cluster-admin-kubeconfig` (key `super-admin.svc`), plus `targetNamespace`/`storageNamespace` set to the tenant namespace and `install.createNamespace: true`, so the management helm-controller applies the chart into the ComputePlane — no Flux needs to run inside it.

The OIDC gatekeeper (oauth2-proxy) moves inside the ComputePlane as another remote-applied HelmRelease; only the `KeycloakClient` registration and the generated client/cookie Secrets stay on management (injected via Flux `valuesFrom`).

The bundled Postgres becomes a raw CNPG `Cluster` kept on the management cluster (hidden private dependency); the workload reaches it cross-cluster by DNS, with credentials injected via `valuesFrom` (JupyterHub) or generated-and-passed-as-values (Langflow).

Exposure: a per-app management Ingress (`<release>-computeplane`, ssl-passthrough) proxies the app host to the `computeplane-cluster-ingress-nginx` Service the computeplane module creates in the tenant namespace, so no management LoadBalancer is allocated.

For ComfyUI the workload manifests are additionally packaged as an in-repo `packages/system/comfyui-workload` chart (registered as HelmChart `cozyllm-comfyui-workload` from the cozyllm GitRepository) so the inner HelmRelease has a chart to carry remotely; in co-located mode the same manifests render directly from the app chart as before.

Also included: registration of the upstream oauth2-proxy HelmRepository (namespace `external-oauth2-proxy`), a small platform cleanup dropping the invalid `sourceRef.namespace` field from HelmChart resources, and `docs/compute-plane.md` describing the consumer pattern.

## Provenance

Ported from the original aenix-org/cozyllm#8, adapted to the final ComputePlane contract (cozystack#3280): derived secret name (`computeplane-cluster-admin-kubeconfig`), no in-cluster Flux required, litellm excluded (stays ManagementPlane). Unlike the original, placement is opt-in per app instance instead of unconditional, so existing installs without the computeplane module keep working unchanged.

## Merge gating

This should merge only after cozystack#3280 (the `computeplane` tenant module) ships in a Cozystack release; until then `computePlane: true` has nothing to target. Default-off behavior is unaffected.

## Validation

`helm lint` + `helm template` pass for every app in both modes; with `computePlane: false` renders are identical to `main` (modulo freshly generated random secrets); with `computePlane: true` the inner HelmReleases carry the documented secret name, `targetNamespace`, and `createNamespace`. The repo CI contract tests pass locally, and markdownlint is clean.

author: alexwolson
body:
The site sheet showed a grab handle but had no drag gesture, so swiping down —
the expected way to close a bottom sheet — did nothing useful and instead let
the browser overscroll/pull-to-refresh the whole page (overscroll-behavior was
only on body, but viewport overscroll propagates from html, which was 'auto').

- Add a real swipe-to-dismiss: a non-passive touch drag that engages only when
  the sheet content is at the top and the finger moves down (so it never fights
  content scrolling), follows the finger, and closes past a ~90px threshold or
  springs back. preventDefault during the drag stops the page overscroll.
- overscroll-behavior: none on html (not just body) kills viewport pull-to-refresh.
- overscroll-behavior: contain on the sheet so its internal scroll never chains.

Verified with synthetic touch drags: 160px drag dismisses, 30px springs back.

author: lopster568
body:
## What
Turns the existing (idle) heuristic threat detector from **log-only** into **optional enforcement**.

## Why
`internal/threat/detector.go` already scores every query (entropy, DGA-hex, base64, digit-ratio, length, subdomain-depth), but `ProcessDNSQuery` only logged the result ("non-blocking, just scoring"). There was no way to actually block a high-confidence suspicious domain that isn't already on a blocklist or block policy.

## How
- New dataplane config: `threat_block_threshold` (float, default `0` = disabled) and `threat_block_dryrun` (bool). Env overrides: `THREAT_BLOCK_THRESHOLD`, `THREAT_BLOCK_DRYRUN`.
- In the allow path, a query with `IsSuspicious && ThreatScore >= threshold` is blocked via the existing `respondBlocked` (reason `threat:<method>`). Dry-run logs a would-be block and still forwards.
- Decision logic extracted into `shouldEnforceThreat` (pure) + `threatDecision` (enum) for testability.

## Safety / compatibility
- **Default `threshold: 0` is the exact current behaviour** (log-only) — no regression.
- The detector's existing CDN/infra allowlist limits false positives; `dryrun` lets operators A/B before enforcing.
- Blocklist and block-policy paths are unchanged and still take precedence over threat enforcement.

## Tests
`go test ./...` is green. Added: threshold-gating table, decision enum, an end-to-end enforced block (`abcdef0123456789.example.com` → `dga_hex`), and a default-off assertion.

Implements idea **I-001** from the DNS-security feature backlog.

author: surveit
body:
## Summary
Found by actually dry-running a two-stage DSA hate-speech monitoring pipeline end-to-end against a real Meltwater export, not just unit tests:

- **`llm_transform` tool-calling reliability**: the compiler now tells the authoring model that the runtime executor answers *only* via a `submit_answer` tool call — a prose-only reply is silently discarded (row records "submitted nothing") even when the model's reasoning was correct. This was causing real, non-deterministic row failures, worse on cheaper/faster models. The compiler now also tells it this tradeoff explicitly.
- **`human_review_queue`'s real fixed contract**: unlike `python_frame_function`, this stage type actively projects its output onto exactly the declared `output_schema` and drops everything else. A compiled workflow that invented plausible-but-wrong column names (`review_decision`/`reviewer_notes` instead of the real `decision`/`review_notes`/`reviewer_id`/`reviewed_at`) silently lost all its data — every downstream stage reading it failed. Compiler now documents the real contract.
- **Empty-row output shape**: a row-mapped stage (`llm_transform`/`python_row_function`) with zero surviving rows produced a `pd.DataFrame([])` with **zero columns**, not just zero rows — every downstream stage doing `df['some_column']` raised `KeyError` on what should be a normal "nothing survived this stage" outcome. Now falls back to the real upstream columns (+ any new columns the stage adds).

All three were reproduced and fixed against a real running pipeline (not synthetic), and verified end-to-end after the fix — 638 real rows processed, results correctly ranked/tiered with no crashes.

Also carries in-flight work from a parallel session on the same branch (live per-row run-log streaming, run detail page updates) that was uncommitted alongside these fixes.

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest tests/` — full suite passes (all green)
- [x] Manually reproduced each bug against a real 689-row Meltwater export before fixing
- [x] Re-ran the same pipeline after each fix to confirm resolution

body:
First two of the invoice-downstream items.

## #1 — Progress bar moves on both sides
Generating an invoice now advances the order `received → invoiced` (server-side, sets `invoiced_at`). Both timelines already had an "Invoiced" step that never lit up — now it does, on the supplier timeline **and** the crew LifecycleTimeline. Regenerating an already-invoiced/paid order won't walk the status backwards.

author: dschenk
body:
## What this fixes

A sessionless Streamable HTTP MCP connection can remain fully usable through POST responses even when its optional SSE GET stream is unavailable.

LibreChat currently ignores a small set of pre-session GET status codes, but other GET-only failures—such as an HTTP 502 or a timeout before response headers—are treated as failures of the whole transport. That tears down the working POST channel and can create a repeated reconnect cycle.

## Change

Track failures originating from the optional Streamable HTTP GET so they can be distinguished from failed POST requests.

When the failure belongs to that GET, no MCP session exists, and the error is not an OAuth challenge, LibreChat now logs one warning and preserves the working POST transport.

## Safety boundaries

The existing error and reconnect behavior remains unchanged for:

- OAuth and insufficient-authorization failures
- failures associated with an established MCP session
- POST and tool-call failures
- legacy SSE transports
- SDK exhaustion of its own SSE reconnection attempts

## Behavior

Before:

`sessionless POST works → optional GET fails → whole connection is rebuilt`

After:

`sessionless POST works → optional GET fails → POST channel remains usable`

## Verification

- Added real sessionless Streamable HTTP regressions for an HTTP 502 and a pre-header timeout.
- Added negative coverage for OAuth, active-session, legacy-SSE, and ordinary transport failures.
- `npx jest src/mcp/__tests__/MCPConnection.test.ts src/mcp/__tests__/MCPConnectionAgentLifecycle.test.ts src/mcp/__tests__/MCPManager.test.ts src/mcp/__tests__/reconnection-storm.test.ts --runInBand --coverage=false` — 152 passed

author: jamesbrink
body:
## Summary

Adds a production-ready prepared prompt-expansion workflow to Desktop Generate. Expansion now follows the exact generation host, turns Batch N into N reviewable prompts, and queues one independently tracked sibling per edited variation.

The change also makes remote expansion recoverable in context: missing expansion models can be pulled on the frozen host with live Connecting, Starting, Queued, Pulling, Ready, failed, and cancelled states shown directly in Generate.

## User experience

- Batch 1 keeps the fast **Expand** and undo workflow.
- Batch values greater than 1 change the action to **Prepare N variations**.
- Auto, Most capable, and pinned host policies resolve once before expansion; the concrete host is shown and remains frozen through generation.
- Returned prompts open in an inline review workspace before GPU jobs are queued.
- Each prompt can be edited or removed; reducing two prompts to one uses an explicit confirmation.
- **Regenerate all**, **Refresh variations**, and **Discard prepared batch** provide intentional lifecycle controls.
- Source prompt, model, model family, batch count, host policy, and host connectivity changes preserve the reviewed set but mark it stale with a specific reason.
- Stale or blank prompts cannot be submitted.
- Partial generation failures preserve successful siblings and identify the failed variation.
- Focus restoration, live regions, progress semantics, keyboard operation, and reduced-motion behavior are covered.

## Remote-host behavior

- Expansion, source preprocessing, model pulls, retries, and every generation sibling use one frozen `HostRoute`.
- No silent fallback, reroute, or batch resizing occurs.
- `/api/capabilities` gains an additive optional expansion group; older hosts remain compatible and are treated as unknown rather than unavailable.
- Capability discovery reports local configuration/model facts without pretending an external API backend is reachable.
- Capabilities and download progress are cached per authenticated host target.
- Expansion-model pull progress reuses `useDownloadsStore` as the single authority and follows the exact returned/observed job ID.
- Bare manifest names such as `qwen3-expand` correctly associate with canonical rows such as `qwen3-expand:q8`; catalog IDs retain literal identity.

## Batch and Gallery provenance

Each prepared sibling carries additive, backward-compatible metadata:

- `original_prompt`
- `batch_id`
- one-based `batch_index`
- `batch_count`

These fields survive ordinary generation, automatic long-video chain projection, durable chain jobs/resume, stitched completion events, SQLite `metadata_json`, remote completion, and Gallery inspection. Legacy requests and rows deserialize with absent fields.

## Parser hardening

Some expansion backends return repeated singleton JSON arrays such as:

```text
["prompt one"]
["prompt two"]
["prompt three"]
```

The shared Rust parser now unwraps that form, and Desktop defensively normalizes it for older remote servers so brackets and quotes never appear in the prepared editors.

## Architecture

- New pure prepared-expansion lifecycle and validation helpers.
- New inline `PreparedExpansionBatch` component.
- New shared `ExpansionPullStatus` component and pull-state reducer.
- Batch request planning supports ordered per-item prompts while preserving existing callers.
- Prepared and quick expansion submissions use request/submission guards to reject late responses and preprocessing races.
- Per-host expansion capability and download-state association extend existing stores rather than introducing polling or a parallel state authority.

## Documentation

Updated the changelog, README, canonical project/agent guidance, Desktop architecture/design/feature-parity/server API docs, and VitePress Desktop/Expansion/API/feature-matrix pages.

## Verification

- Desktop Vitest: **153 files, 1,400 tests passed**
- Desktop TypeScript typecheck and production Vite build passed
- Desktop Prettier check passed
- Web Vitest: **46 files, 319 tests passed**
- Web typecheck and production build passed
- Website format check, documentation verifier, and VitePress production build passed
- `cargo test --workspace` passed in `nix develop`
- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` passed in `nix develop`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed in `nix develop`
- `cargo check -p mold-ai --features preview,discord,expand,tui,webp,mp4` passed
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passed
- `git diff --check` passed
- Multiple independent Traycer reviews completed with zero remaining findings

## Manual QA note

The native Desktop dev application built and launched successfully. The user supplied live screenshots that exposed and drove fixes for the missing-model recovery and singleton-array formatting paths. Automated component and integration coverage exercises the complete state machine; final hands-on cross-theme/narrow-width inspection was limited because the local UI-control bridge was unavailable.

body:
## Summary Two newly-disclosed HIGH advisories in **transitive production** dependencies started failing the `audit` CI check on every PR audited after they were published (surfaced on the in-flight memory PRs #725/#726; they'd fail on `main` too on a re-audit). Both are transitive — no source uses them directly. - **brace-expansion** — DoS via exponential-time `{}` expansion ([GHSA-3jxr-9vmj-r5cp](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3jxr-9vmj-r5cp)); affected `<1.1.16` and `>=2.0.0 <2.1.2`. Tree had `1.1.13` + `2.0.3`. - **shell-quote** — quadratic-complexity DoS in `parse()` ([GHSA-395f-4hp3-45gv](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-395f-4hp3-45gv)); affected `<=1.8.4`. The existing `shell-quote: ">=1.8.4"` override no longer covers it (1.8.4 is now in-range). ## Change Version-scoped `pnpm.overrides` (matching the repo's existing style, e.g. `ws@6`, `minimatch@10`): ```jsonc "brace-expansion@1": ">=1.1.16 <2.0.0", "brace-expansion@2": ">=2.1.2 <3.0.0", // 5.x already unaffected "shell-quote": ">=1.10.0 <2.0.0" // was >=1.8.4 ``` Resolved: `brace-expansion` → 1.1.16 + 2.1.2, `shell-quote` → 1.10.0. `node scripts/audit.mjs` → **no high/critical prod vulnerabilities**. Lockfile-only + `package.json` overrides; no source changes. Typecheck + full suite green. ## Why separate Landing this on `main` clears the `audit` check for **all** open + future PRs at once, rather than patching it into each feature branch. ## Breaking Changes None — transitive utility bumps within the same major (brace-expansion) / minor (shell-quote 1.8→1.10) lines. --- > [!NOTE] > **Low Risk** > Lockfile-only transitive patch/minor bumps within existing majors; no app code or API surface changes. > > **Overview** > Updates **pnpm overrides** and the lockfile so CI `audit` passes after two new HIGH advisories on transitive deps—no application source changes. > > **shell-quote** is bumped from `>=1.8.4` to `>=1.10.0 <2.0.0` (resolved **1.10.0**) to address a DoS in `parse()`. **brace-expansion** gets version-scoped overrides for the 1.x and 2.x lines (`>=1.1.16` and `>=2.1.2`), replacing **1.1.13** / **2.0.3** in the tree and fixing exponential-time `{}` expansion DoS. Lockfile entries for `minimatch` and `react-devtools-core` pick up the new transitive versions. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 8c580710c30c9a5e5f232a390520a621c037567e. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

Greptile Summary

This PR updates transitive dependencies to clear two security advisories. The main changes are: - Raises `shell-quote` from 1.8.4 to 1.10.0. - Raises `brace-expansion` 1.x and 2.x to patched releases. - Adds major-scoped pnpm overrides and updates the lockfile.

Confidence Score: 5/5

This looks safe to merge. - No blocking issues found in the changed code.

author: bradenterry
body:
## Problem

Claude Code prints a `<hook> failed with non-blocking status code` warning whenever a hook exits non-zero or writes anything to stderr. The status emitter is wired to `PreToolUse` with matcher `*`, so a single failure mode repeats on every tool call (reported as `PreToolUse:Read hook error ... failed with non-blocking status code`).

One such mode was real and reproducible: when the sessions directory cannot be created (deleted extension global storage, a synced `~/.claude/settings.json` whose `--dir` path belongs to another machine, a read-only or full disk), the emitter's last-resort `writeFileSync` threw uncaught and the process exited 1 with a stack trace on stderr.

## Fix

- **`hooks/agent-worktrees-emit.mjs`** - wrap the whole run; the emitter now swallows any failure and always exits 0 silently. A status update that can't land is dropped, never surfaced as a hook error.
- **`src/hooks.ts`** - the hook command now runs `node --no-warnings`, so node's own startup warnings (deprecation/experimental, varying by node version) can't hit stderr before the script runs and get reported as hook errors. The changed command auto-repairs into `settings.json` via the existing `syncHooks` path on activation.
- **`test/emitter.test.js`** - regression test: unwritable state dir must produce exit 0 with empty stdout/stderr.
- README (mechanism), MARKETPLACE (user-facing note), CHANGELOG `3.4.7` entry.

author: andrewlaack
body:
Packages Mealie (self-hosted recipe manager) for OpenHost with zero-click owner single sign-on.

Mealie has a per-recipe cooking timeline (I Made This dated entries with notes, photos, ratings), a good fit for iterating on a recipe across multiple cooking attempts.

SSO uses Pattern D: an in-container OIDC identity provider (oidc_bridge/server.py) trusts the OpenHost router X-OpenHost-Is-Owner header to mint OIDC authorization codes (auth-code + PKCE) for the single zone owner. Mealie is configured with OIDC_AUTO_REDIRECT and ALLOW_PASSWORD_LOGIN=false, so the owner never sees a login form and is auto-provisioned on first login. Non-owner visitors are bounced to the OpenHost zone login by the router. There is no anonymous public-sharing surface.

The OIDC discovery document advertises a public authorization_endpoint (browser-facing) but loopback token/jwks/userinfo endpoints (server-facing), so Mealie backend calls stay in-container and do not hairpin through the router.

nginx fronts :8080, routing /_oidc/* to the bridge and everything else to Mealie on loopback :9000, and serves a static /_healthz for cold-start. Mealie state is kept under the OpenHost data mount via the DATA_DIR env var (the image /app/data VOLUME is left untouched). No user password is written to disk; the only on-disk artifacts are the bridge signing key and a client secret, both non-user-credentials documented as such.

Deployed and verified end-to-end on a live instance: Mealie v3.20.1 boots, the full OIDC handshake completes (owner auto-redirect, PKCE code exchange, id_token validation, session issued), and unauthenticated visitors are redirected to the zone login. Vetted with fable in agentic mode (multiple parallel runs), clean.

author: timsehn
body:
## The bug

When both branches `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` on the same table, the merge classified it as a clean schema merge, set `skipRowMerge`, and took ours' table **wholesale** — then reapplied only theirs' *added-column* values by name (`migrateSchemaRowData`). The three-way row merge never ran, so on that path:

- theirs' edits to **shared** (pre-existing) columns were silently dropped,
- theirs' **row deletions** were silently dropped, and
- two branches editing the **same row** raised **no conflict**.

Reachable through ordinary DDL+DML — silent data loss and lost conflicts, which a version-control engine must never do. Verified against real Dolt:

```
ancestor: t(id,a) = {1:one, 5:five, 9:nine}
ours:     ADD COLUMN b
theirs:   ADD COLUMN c; UPDATE a='five-theirs' WHERE id=5; DELETE WHERE id=9
```
Dolt → `{1:one, 5:five-theirs}` (row 9 deleted). doltlite (before) → `{1:one, 5:five, 9:nine}` — theirs' edit and delete lost.

## The fix

The dual-add case now runs the real **cell-level** `mergeTableRows`. Theirs' records are first remapped into the merged column order (ours' columns, then theirs' added columns, keyed by name) via a new byte-level `normalizeTheirsToMergedLayout`, so the positional per-cell merge reads each cell at the right ordinal; schema evolution stays as the existing post-merge `ALTER`s. This preserves theirs' deletes and shared-column edits, combines each side's new column, and conflicts only on a genuine same-cell edit.

Root sub-fix: `tryCellMerge` treated a field beyond a record's stored width as "absent/newly-added" rather than as NULL, so it falsely conflicted when the two sides' rows had different widths (the normal case here). It now treats an absent trailing field as NULL (SQLite omits trailing NULLs) — making the per-cell merge span records of different widths — and drops trailing NULLs so the merged row re-encodes canonically. This also hardens ordinary ADD COLUMN merges.

The old additive `migrateSchemaRowData` path (`doltlite_schema_merge.c`) and the now-unused `doltliteBindField` are removed (dead-code gate).

## Validation

- New oracle scenarios in `vc_oracle_merge_test.sh` (theirs edit+delete, each side sets its own new column on the same row, theirs adds a row with its new column, same-cell conflict) — **fail before, pass after**, matching real Dolt.
- New self-contained gate in `doltlite_schema_merge.sh` (7 assertions).
- Manually verified against Dolt across the edge matrix: secondary index on an edited column, WITHOUT ROWID, multi-column adds each side, new-row-with-added-col.
- Full local regression green: battery **88/88 suites**, C corpus **309,835/309,835**, merge oracle **71/71**, schema_merge oracle **37/37**, checkout/diff/status/conflicts/revert-cherrypick/fk_merge oracles green, dead-code gate **PASS**.

Found via the deep code review (core-engine correctness pass).

First end-to-end vertical slice — the orchestrator composes a
`ChainedPipeline[MigrationContext]` with three stages, the Input Pipeline
authenticates and discovers agents, and Migration/Output stages are empty
pass-throughs until their tasks land.

### Orchestrator (`src/service/mtk_orchestrator.py`)

- Composition root: builds three stage pipelines, chains them via
  `ChainedPipeline[MigrationContext]().add(...).add(...).add(...)`, runs the
  pipeline, renders the report, and closes the Logger session.
- Logger lifecycle: `start_session` before pipeline, `Reporter.render()` +
  `logger.close()` in `finally` — always produces the two-file session bundle.
- Default mode: `ExecutionMode.READONLY`.

### Input Pipeline steps (`src/modules/preprocessing/steps/`)

All steps are `MigrationPipelineStep` subclasses with

author: carstenartur
body:
## Summary

Seventh implementation slice of #46, stacked on PR #71.

- installs a step-specific WRF runner into the existing reproducible WRF image
- adds pinned, isolated container execution for `real.exe` and `wrf.exe`
- uses separate persistent work directories so initialization artifacts and logs are not overwritten by simulation
- routes WPS and WRF steps through one worker executor entrypoint
- hard-links or copies only managed `met_em`, `wrfinput` and `wrfbdy` handoff files
- resets frozen namelists and previous outputs on every retry
- publishes structured simulation time, simulated duration, output count and ETA from `rsl.out.0000`
- requires real `wrfinput`/`wrfbdy` and `wrfout` artifacts before success
- classifies namelist, domain, input, memory, disk, numerical and process failures
- keeps postprocessing and result indexing explicitly unavailable

## Container isolation

The host executor verifies the immutable WRF image identity before start and runs the pinned selector with no network, read-only root filesystem, dropped capabilities, no-new-privileges, bounded PIDs, optional CPU/memory limits and only read-only specification plus managed read-write run mounts.

## Tests

Focused tests cover:

- pinned WRF image inspection, selector and sandbox command
- WPS/WRF dispatcher routing and unsupported-step classification
- immutable namelist reset on retry
- symlink-safe met_em/wrfinput handoff and output indexing
- structured WRF timing/ETA parsing from representative `rsl` lines

The existing reproducible Docker workflow compiles and verifies the actual `real.exe`, `wrf.exe`, Python runtime and installed step runner.

## Scope boundary

This PR supplies the real initialization and model container steps. A complete scientific acceptance run still requires real WPS geography input plus real postprocessing and result-indexing executors. The Xaver micro-run remains the final acceptance target.

## Stacking

This PR is intentionally based on `feature/real-wps-container-executor` / PR #71 and will be retargeted after the preceding PRs merge with ancestry preserved.

- Exchange the app session and navigate immediately after accepted provisioning (`202` or recognized `provisioning_conflict`) without a starting/preparing/loading interstitial or artificial pre-boot poll.
- Route the CLI device flow through `/?device_return=…`, where the platform serves the existing **Booting Matrix OS** page until the running shell is reachable, then complete the preserved return to `/auth/device`.
- Keep failures inline on the chooser with approved generic copy, while preserving the genuine `402` billing-settlement retry.
- Mirror the Settings frame and immediate boot handoff in the self-contained platform fallback.

### 1360 × 796

![Desktop Default installs chooser](https://github.com/HamedMP/matrix-os/blob/codex/settings-agent-selection/specs/099-onboarding-journey/screenshots/settings-default-installs-desktop.png?raw=1)

![Mobile Default installs chooser](https://github.com/HamedMP/matrix-os/blob/codex/settings-agent-selection/specs/099-onboarding-journey/screenshots/settings-default-installs-mobile.png?raw=1)

## Tests

- Affected Settings, BootSequence, BillingGate, OnboardingGate, RuntimeManager, and platform fallback suites: **201 passed**.
- `pnpm --filter platform exec tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.typecheck.json`: passed.
- `npx react-doctor@latest shell --verbose --scope changed --base origin/main --include-untracked --no-score`: no issues found.
- `bash scripts/review/check-patterns.sh --diff origin/main`: no violations; audited warnings are a four-item bounded selector Set and string `.join()` false positives.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`: passed.
- The shell-wide typecheck still reports three pre-existing errors in unrelated `Desktop.tsx`, `VocalPanel.tsx`, and `MobileShell.tsx` files.
- A full local `pnpm run test` was attempted, but the constrained runner caused widespread unrelated process/network test timeouts (CLI, heartbeat, app-runtime, zellij, and Codex runtime suites); it was stopped after the affected suites had passed independently. PR CI is the authoritative full-suite result.

## Invariants

- **Source of truth:** The platform journey/billing state remains authoritative for whether the chooser is shown. `/api/auth/provision-runtime` remains authoritative for provisioning acceptance, and `/api/auth/app-session` remains authoritative for the browser handoff. The existing `developerTools` request array is unchanged.
- **Lock/transaction scope:** No database writes, locks, transactions, or schema behavior are added. The client performs two ordered, timeout-bounded requests; the session exchange starts only after provisioning is accepted.
- **Acceptable orphan states:** Provisioning may be accepted while app-session exchange fails. The chooser remains visible with a generic retry error, and the existing idempotent `provisioning_conflict` response lets the user retry safely without starting a duplicate VPS.
- **Auth source of truth:** Clerk supplies the bearer token for provisioning and session exchange. The server-issued app-session cookie remains authoritative for platform routing; non-running machines render the existing boot page, and only a server-verified running shell completes a preserved CLI device return.
- **Deferred scope:** Public onboarding docs/screenshots belong in a separate `FinnaAI/matrix-os-site` PR. After merge, this pre-VPS change requires a platform/app-shell redeploy; publishing a customer host bundle alone will not update this surface.

author: simonx1
body:
## What

MCP 2025-11-25, `server/tools.mdx` — Output Schema:

> If an output schema is provided:
> - Servers **MUST** provide structured results that conform to this schema.
> - Clients **SHOULD** validate structured results against this schema.

`Client#call_tool` now validates a result's `structuredContent` against the called tool's declared `outputSchema`:

- New self-contained `MCPClient::SchemaValidator` (no new gem dependency), following the codebase's existing schema-checking approach (cf. `ElicitationValidator`). Supported keywords: `type` (incl. type arrays), `enum`, `const`, `properties`/`required`, `items`/`minItems`/`maxItems`, `minLength`/`maxLength`/`pattern`, `minimum`/`maximum`/`exclusiveMinimum`/`exclusiveMaximum`. The full JSON Schema 2020-12 vocabulary (`$ref`/`$defs`, `allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf`/`not`, conditionals, `additionalProperties`, format assertions, ...) is documented as out of scope; unrecognized keywords are ignored rather than misapplied, so the validator never rejects data that conforms to the schema.
- On mismatch the client logs a warning naming the tool and the schema errors, and — with the opt-in strictness knob `Client.new(..., validate_structured_content: :strict)` — raises `MCPClient::Errors::ValidationError` (default `:warn` only logs). Unknown modes are rejected with `ArgumentError`.
- Error results (`isError: true`) and results without `structuredContent` are exempt. `Tool#output_schema` was verified to already be parsed from `tools/list` (`outputSchema`, string or symbol keys).

## Tests

New `spec/lib/mcp_client/structured_content_validation_spec.rb` (24 examples, written first / confirmed red):

- `SchemaValidator`: conforming data, type mismatches (top-level, nested with JSON-pointer paths, array items), enum, string bounds and pattern, inclusive/exclusive numeric bounds, array size bounds, 2020-12 whole-float integers, type arrays, out-of-scope keywords ignored, symbol-keyed schemas/data.
- `Client#call_tool`: `:warn` logs and still returns the result; conforming/absent `structuredContent`, schema-less tools, and `isError` results stay silent; `:strict` raises `ValidationError` (and still logs); invalid knob value rejected.

Full suite: `bundle exec rspec` — 1344 examples, 0 failures. `bundle exec rubocop` — 112 files inspected, no offenses.

Part of an MCP 2025-11-25 compliance audit of this gem against the official spec.

body:
## Summary

Makes `npm run lint` (`eslint .`) exit 0 on `webapp` without disabling any eslint rules or config. Depends on #16 (merged) — deps weren't installable before that, so lint couldn't even run.

**Scoping correction (per work-unit spec):** the board item cited an empty catch in `webapp/src/utils/signingRequest.ts`, but that file doesn't exist on `beta` (it's from an unmerged feature branch). This PR fixes the errors eslint actually reports on `beta` HEAD instead.

## Lint output — before

```
webapp/src/components/PDFView.tsx
    9:32  error  Unexpected any. Specify a different type  @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
   24:33  error  Unexpected any. Specify a different type  @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
   69:31  error  Unexpected any. Specify a different type  @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
   86:32  error  Unexpected any. Specify a different type  @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
  206:34  error  Unexpected any. Specify a different type  @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
  233:38  error  Unexpected any. Specify a different type  @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any

webapp/src/components/SignatureCanvas.tsx
  43:6  warning  React Hook useEffect has missing dependencies: 'height' and 'width'  react-hooks/exhaustive-deps

webapp/src/components/SignatureDraggable.tsx
   8:15  error  Unexpected any. Specify a different type  @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
  45:23  error  Unexpected any. Specify a different type  @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
  66:26  error  Unexpected any. Specify a different type  @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any

webapp/src/pages/PDFUploader.tsx
  49:30  error  Unexpected any. Specify a different type  @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
  71:27  error  Unexpected any. Specify a different type  @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any

✖ 12 problems (11 errors, 1 warning)
```

## Lint output — after

```
webapp/src/components/SignatureCanvas.tsx
  43:6  warning  React Hook useEffect has missing dependencies: 'height' and 'width'  react-hooks/exhaustive-deps

✖ 1 problem (0 errors, 1 warning)
```

`eslint .` exits 0 (warnings don't fail the default `eslint .` invocation; there's no `--max-warnings` set). This pre-existing warning is untouched — fixing it isn't required for a green exit and is out of scope for this lint pass.

## What changed (all 11 errors were `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` from `props: any`)

- **`PDFView.tsx`**: gave every internal component (`PDFView`, `ZoomablePDF`, `PDFSignature`, `PDFPageButtons`, `AddSignatureButton`) a real prop type instead of `props: any`. `onLoadError`'s `error: any` → `error: Error` (matches `react-pdf`'s `OnDocumentLoadError` type). The `modal` state was really `boolean | string` all along (`setModal(id)` is called with a field id) — typed it correctly instead of the inferred `boolean` that `any` had been hiding.
- **`SignatureDraggable.tsx`**: `setModal: any` → `Dispatch<SetStateAction<boolean | string>>`; `onDragStart`'s `(e: any, data)` → `(e: MouseEvent, data: DraggableData)` (react-rnd's real callback signature); `onPointerDown`'s `(e: any)` → `(e: PointerEvent<HTMLDivElement>)` (react-rnd spreads unrecognized props like this one onto the root `<div>`, confirmed by reading its render source).
- **`PDFUploader.tsx`**: typed `UploadButton`/`PDFUpload`'s `props: any` to their actual shape (`handleUpload: (e: React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => void`, optional `text`).

**One behavior-relevant fix required by proper typing** (called out per the acceptance criteria): `PDFPageButtons`' "Next" button did `Math.min(prev + 1, numPages)` where `numPages: number | null`. Under `any` this silently compiled; once typed correctly it's a real compile error, and the pre-existing runtime behavior when `numPages` was `null` (before the PDF's metadata loads) was actually `Math.min(x, null)` coercing `null` → `0`, resetting the page to 0. Guarded with `numPages ?? prev + 1`: normal-path (numPages loaded) behavior is byte-for-byte identical; the transient pre-load-null edge case now just increments the page counter instead of resetting to 0.

No rules were disabled and no `eslint-disable` comments were added anywhere.

## Verification

- `npm ci` — clean, reproducible (via #16's committed `vendor/xiro-ui` stub)
- `npm run lint` — exit 0 (was exit 1 / 11 errors)
- `npm run build` (`tsc -b && vite build`) — passes
- `npm run test:unit` — 21/21 pass
- `npm run test:e2e` — **1 pre-existing failure, unrelated to this change and not introduced by it.** `tests/pdf-view-load-error.spec.ts` expects the generic fallback message ("Unable to load this PDF document") but the app correctly surfaces pdf.js's real error text ("Invalid PDF structure."). Verified this fails identically on unmodified `beta` HEAD (`4f6e254`) before any change in this PR — it's an assertion/fixture mismatch in the test itself, out of scope for a lint-only work unit.

Not merging — leaving for review per Red Ops contract.

author: brentrager
body:
## Problem
The Rust logger fabricated a uuid for `traceId` and carried no span id, so its lines couldn't be joined to the OpenTelemetry traces they belong to. And `emit` writes **stdout-direct**, so lines never reached `@smooai/observability`'s OTLP logs appender (a `tracing_subscriber::Layer`) — even once that pipeline exists. Correlation fix, pearl **th-de3805**.

## Solution
Two halves, depending on the OpenTelemetry **API only** (`opentelemetry`, `trace` feature) — never `@smooai/observability` (that would be circular):

1. **Real trace/span ids.** At log-build time, when an OTel span is active, override `traceId` with the span's real W3C trace_id and attach `spanId` (new `spanId` context key). No active span → the seeded uuid stays (prior behavior). New `context::active_otel_trace_context()` reads `opentelemetry::Context::current()`.

2. **Tee to the `tracing` facade.** Each emitted line is also fired as a `tracing` event at the matching level (message → body, full JSON payload → `log` field), so the observability appender turns it into an OTLP log record. The event fires while the same OTel span is still active, so the appender's SDK logger stamps the record's trace_id/span_id from the current context — **matching** the ids this crate already put in the payload. Gated by a new `otel_bridge` option that defaults to the **same env enablement** as the observability logs pipeline (`SMOOAI_OBSERVABILITY_ENDPOINT` set and `SMOOAI_OBSERVABILITY_DISABLED` not truthy). Off → `emit` stays stdout-direct with zero `tracing` overhead.

## Verification
`cargo build`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` (clean), `cargo fmt --check` (clean), `cargo test` — **20 passed** (16 existing + 4 new). New `tests/otel_correlation.rs`:
- `log_within_active_span_carries_real_trace_and_span_id` — asserts `traceId`/`spanId` equal the active span's **real** ids. **Actually verified, not just compiled**: mutating the expected trace_id fails the test (real captured id `595170f2…` vs the zeroed value).
- `log_without_active_span_falls_back_to_uuid` — no span → uuid `traceId`, no `spanId`.
- `enabled_bridge_tees_line_to_tracing` — one line → one `tracing` event at the matching level with the message as body (captured via a test subscriber layer).
- `disabled_bridge_does_not_tee` — off → no `tracing` events.

Branched off `main` (the repo's default work branch is a feature branch). No deploy. End-to-end join through the real observability appender was **not** exercised here — that lives in `@smooai/observability` (companion PR adds the logs signal) and the follow-up dogfood wiring.

author: hereliesaz
body:
> #35 (tap-to-select) and #36 (selection outline) have merged to `main`; this completes the interactive-editing foundation: **select → see → resize**.

Adds **corner resize handles** to the selection: a dot at each corner of the active layer's bounding box, and a drag that begins on a corner **scales the layer about its centre**.

## What changed
- **`SelectionHandles`** — draws the four corner dots and hosts the drag. It sits **above** the pan-gesture box and only consumes a gesture that **starts on a handle** (via `CanvasHitTest.nearestCornerIndex`); a drag elsewhere is left unconsumed, so **panning and tap-select still work**. Uses `awaitEachGesture`, which waits for pointers-up between gestures, so the early return on a non-handle down can't busy-loop.
- The scale is applied as an incremental "zoom" through the existing **`onTransformGesture`** path (a single-finger pinch), reusing the proven transform + linked-group + history/persistence lifecycle (`onGestureStart`/`onGestureEnd` bracket the drag). **No new transform math.**
- **`CanvasHitTest.nearestCornerIndex(...)`** — pure handle-targeting helper.

## Verification
Handle-targeting is unit-tested (nearest-within-radius for two corners + the no-hit case), on top of the existing hit-test/corner geometry tests. The scaling itself is the already-shipped `onTransformGesture`, so no new math to verify.

## The six headline fixes

1. **Services are keyboard-operable.** The grid card is now a stretched-`<button>` (Enter opens the drawer; nested Deploy stays independently clickable) and canvas nodes are focusable `role="button"`s with Enter/Space and a status-bearing accessible name. Previously **opening a service required a mouse** — the app's core action was unusable by keyboard.
2. **Every overlay implements the dialog pattern.** New shared `useDialogFocus` hook — initial focus, Tab trap, Escape-to-close, focus restore, and an overlay stack so a modal opened from a popup layers correctly. Applied to the service drawer, GitHub deploy modal, projects panel, changes modal, and QuickDeploy popup. Drawer tabs gained full `tablist` semantics with arrow-key nav.

author: veronicaz41
body:
## What

`cmdHookForward` (the `__hook` PostToolUse forwarder, Mode B tool-output capture) POSTed captured payloads to whatever URL `BEAGLE_HOOK_ENDPOINT` named. The comment promised "the daemon's loopback receiver", but nothing enforced it — and this is the only outbound network call in the backend, in the product whose core promise is that captured data never leaves the machine.

The fetch is now gated on `isLoopbackHookEndpoint()`: an exact-match allowlist (`127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`, `localhost`) over the WHATWG-parsed hostname. A non-loopback endpoint is a **silent no-op** (still exits 0) — the hook's never-disrupt-the-agent contract holds.

## Why exact-match

- The endpoint is constructed in exactly one place — `cmdRun` sets `http://127.0.0.1:<otlpPort>/v1/hook`; nothing in src/install/ builds it (the shim re-execs `beagle run`). A strict allowlist can't break a legitimate caller.
- The URL parser canonicalizes equivalent spellings before the check (`127.1`/`0x7f000001` → `127.0.0.1`, `LOCALHOST` → `localhost`, long-form IPv6 → `[::1]`), so those pass.
- Spoof-shaped hosts (`127.0.0.1.evil.example`, trailing-dot `localhost.`) are refused rather than resolved — a sub-2s best-effort hook should never do DNS to learn where a name really points.

## Tests

- Unit matrix over the validator (canonical forms, parser-normalized equivalents, spoofs, garbage).
- End-to-end delivery: a live loopback receiver gets the exact payload + `x-beagle-run` header (this path had no coverage before).
- Blocking test with a deterministic observable: endpoint host `localhost.` *does* resolve to the test's 127.0.0.1-bound receiver (verified empirically) but fails the allowlist → receiver must record **zero** hits. Ran it with the guard unwired first: it failed with `hits: 1`, so it genuinely catches an unguarded fetch.

`bun run check` (lint + LOC budget + tsc + 631 tests) is green.

author: prajyotbankade
body:
## What changed

- Added `_check_trunk_ahead_of_origin(backlog_path, ok, issues)` to `skills/backlog-manager/backlog/cli.py` (~line 1096, before the `doctor` command)
- Wired it into `doctor` as check #6, running alongside `_check_backlog_divergence`
- Added `skills/backlog-manager/tests/test_doctor_trunk_ahead.py` with 15 tests covering all spec cases

## Why

When `backlog commit` runs on local trunk (main) and a direct push to origin is blocked by the pre-commit hook, local trunk drifts ahead of origin/main by backlog-only commits. Any feature branch cut from local trunk inherits those commits, so the PR diff against `origin/main` includes `backlog.json`. This is invisible when diffing against local main.

The new check detects this drift before a branch is cut: it compares `git rev-list origin/<trunk>..<trunk>` and then `git diff --name-only origin/<trunk>..<trunk>` — if the only changed path is `backlog.json`, it emits a warning with commit count and remediation guidance. Normal unpushed code (non-backlog files) generates only a neutral note.

The check is read-only: no fetch, no mutation, graceful degradation on any error.

## Test plan

- [x] `backlog-only ahead` → warning with correct commit count (`test_warns_with_correct_commit_count`, `test_warns_with_two_backlog_commits`)
- [x] Warning appears in `doctor` CLI output with exit code 1 (`test_warning_via_doctor_command_exits_nonzero`)
- [x] Warning includes remediation guidance (`test_warning_mentions_remediation`)
- [x] Local trunk in sync with origin → neutral 'in sync' note, no warning (`test_in_sync_no_warning`, `test_in_sync_via_doctor_command_passes`)
- [x] Ahead with non-backlog files → NO drift warning, neutral note (`test_no_warning_when_non_backlog_files_changed`, `test_neutral_note_when_non_backlog_files_changed`)
- [x] Ahead with both backlog + code files → NO drift warning (`test_no_warning_when_backlog_and_code_both_changed`)
- [x] No origin remote → graceful skip, no crash (`test_no_crash_no_origin`, `test_no_crash_no_origin_via_doctor`)
- [x] `origin/<trunk>` ref absent → graceful skip (`test_graceful_skip_when_origin_ref_absent`, `test_no_crash_when_origin_ref_absent_via_doctor`)
- [x] Outside git repo → graceful skip (`test_graceful_skip_outside_git_repo`)
- [x] Both checks run in doctor: existing `_check_backlog_divergence` behavior unchanged (`test_both_checks_run_in_doctor`)
- [x] Full suite: 415 tests passed

Closes backlog item #118

author: ffleurey
body:
Closes seven engine facade gaps, ordered by value, plus review fixes on the same branch.

### New engine operations (CLI/MCP parity)

- **`delete_session`** — cascading delete (child sessions, turns, rounds, parts, raw exchanges) with a scheduler guard: rejects with `session_already_queued` while the session has an active or queued job.
- **`rename_session`** — title update (trimmed, 1–200 chars; bumps `updated_at`).
- **`abort_session`** — targeted per-session abort returning `aborted` / `dequeued` / `not-running`. The scheduler gains `abortTargeted(sessionId)` alongside the existing global abort.

All three are backend catalog operations, so they surface function-for-function as `mcpscope delete_session|rename_session|abort_session` CLI commands, `mcpscope_*` MCP tools, and `engine.deleteSession/renameSession/abortSession` on the embeddable engine facade.

### Runtime quality of life

- **Queue position in status** — `status` reports `queue_position` (1-based) when a session has a pending draft turn not yet executing; the CLI text output shows it too.
- **Distinct `aborted` terminal** — user aborts are detected in stream-failure classification: turn status `aborted`, round finish reason `cancelled`, `turn-failed` event `errorType: 'aborted'`.
- **Typed `provider_unreachable`** — ECONNREFUSED, DNS failures, and fetch network errors classify as `errorType: 'provider_unreachable'` on `turn-failed`.
- **Optional title on create** — `title` is optional across engine, MCP, HTTP, and CLI (`mcpscope create [title]`); defaults to `New session` and is auto-titled from the first prompt, emitting a new `session-title-changed` stream event.

### Internal wiring

Backend PATCH and DELETE session routes now delegate to `renameSessionOperation`/`deleteSessionOperation` instead of calling the repository directly, and a new `POST /api/sessions/:id/abort` route backs the abort. PATCH now returns the canonical `rename_session` result (`{ api_version, session_id, title }`); the frontend and CLI consumers were updated to match.

### Docs & tests

- EMBEDDING.md (facade methods, abort semantics, events), CLI.md and MCP.md (three new commands/tools, optional create title, `queue_position`).
- Tests: engine facade coverage for rename/abort/delete and first-prompt auto-titling, stream-error classification (`describeStreamFailure`), and route contracts for the operation-backed PATCH/abort endpoints.

### Formatting

Prettier pass over 53 files (mostly `packages/engine`) that were inconsistent with `.prettierrc`; each was mechanically verified to be formatting-only (prettier(main) is byte-identical to head). No behavioral changes in those files.

author: mjvolk3
body:
## Problem

`CpuExperimentLoaderMultiprocessing` forks workers (default start method) that share the parent dataset's open LMDB `env`. An env handle inherited across `fork()` keeps the parent's memory map + reader-table slot, so a read in the child raises `lmdb.MapResizedError: MDB_MAP_RESIZED` ("Database contents grew beyond environment mapsize") once the file has grown past that inherited mapping.

This surfaced in `compute_gene_set_parallel` during a **Kemmeren 2014** rebuild (~640 KB/record ⇒ ~954 MB file): the forked worker crashed, so `process()` never completed, no completion sentinel was written, and the dataset re-processed on every run — which would break the KG/Neo4j build.

## Fix

Reset `dataset.env = None` at the top of `worker_function` so each forked worker lazily opens its **own** env via `_init_db` on first access. This is the single chokepoint through which every parallel-read child touches the dataset, so it covers gene-set computation for all datasets.

## Verification

- Full Kemmeren 2014 rebuild through this code completes end-to-end: parallel gene-set → reference index → coverage assertion → completion sentinel (`pre_transform.pt`/`pre_filter.pt`), `Dataset size: 1484`, **zero** `MDB_MAP_RESIZED`/`Traceback`/`AssertionError`.
- Adds a focused regression test asserting the worker drops an inherited `env`.
- `ruff`, strict `mypy`, and the loader test suite (4 passed) all green.

body:
## Summary

Makes `LinkButton` wrap in a Kumo `Tooltip` when a `title` is provided, matching `Button`'s behavior. Previously an enabled `LinkButton` only set a native `title` attribute (browser default tooltip); it now surfaces the same styled Kumo tooltip on hover and focus.

The disabled `LinkButton` already got the Kumo tooltip because it delegates to `Button` — this closes the gap for the enabled anchor.

## Implementation

The enabled branch now builds the anchor as a variable and wraps it when `title` is set, mirroring `Button`'s `if (title)` path:

```tsx
const link = (
  <LinkComponent … >{…}</LinkComponent>
);

if (title) {
  return <Tooltip content={title} render={link} />;
}

return link;
```

The native `title={title}` passthrough on the anchor was removed so we don't get a double (native + Kumo) tooltip. `title` is already destructured out of the spread props, so nothing leaks onto the DOM.

## Tests

1 new test in `button.test.tsx`: an enabled `LinkButton` with `title` becomes a Base UI tooltip trigger (`data-base-ui-tooltip-trigger`) and does not set a native `title` attribute. All 24 `button.test.tsx` tests pass.

## Docs

- New `ButtonLinkTooltipDemo` in `ButtonDemo.tsx`
- New "Link with Tooltip" section on `/components/button`

body:
### Motivation
- Se reemplazó la lógica de parcheo temporal de métodos de egress (monkeypatching de `sendMessage`, `reply`, etc.) que provocaba un bloqueo del Event Loop al emitir `composing` sin restaurar correctamente el estado. 
- Se reutilizó la implementación probada extraída del respaldo (`Botcomposing.zip` / handler de Monkey-D-luffy-Bot) para un ciclo de presencia más seguro y no bloqueante. 
- Se añadieron validaciones defensivas en manejadores de eventos grupales para evitar emisiones/broadcasts con datos incompletos que causaban errores en tiempo de ejecución.

### Description
- Sustituido el parcheo de métodos de egress por un ciclo global `composing → ejecución → paused` implementado en `src/router/handler.js` usando `firePresenceUpdate` y `withCommandPresence`. 
- Añadida la función `canSendPresenceUpdate` y el conjunto `PRESENCE_STATES` con validaciones estrictas para `conn`, `state`, `jid` y existencia de `conn.ev` antes de intentar `sendPresenceUpdate`. 
- Eliminado el `patchPresenceEgressMethods`/`watchPresenceEgress` que manipulaba métodos de `conn` y se evitó mutación del socket; la emisión de presencia ahora se realiza no bloqueante con `queueMicrotask`. 
- Añadidas comprobaciones defensivas en `groupsUpdate` y `participantsUpdate` para validar `update.participants` y `this.ev` antes de procesar y llamar a plugins como `autodetect`/`welcome`.

### Testing
- Ejecutado `node --check src/router/handler.js` y pasó sin errores. 
- Ejecutado `npm test` (que corre `node --check index.js && node --check src/bootstrap/app.js && node --check src/router/handler.js`) y todos los chequeos automáticos finalizaron correctamente. 
- Ejecutado `git diff --check` para validar cambios y no se encontraron problemas de diff o whitespace; las pruebas automáticas documentadas en el PR pasaron exitosamente.

author: simonx1
body:
## What

Implements MCP 2025-11-25 tool calling in sampling (SEP-1577) and corrects the sampling error-code semantics.

`client/sampling.mdx` § Tools in Sampling:

> Clients **MUST** declare support for tool use via the `sampling.tools` capability to receive tool-enabled sampling requests. Servers **MUST NOT** send tool-enabled sampling requests to Clients that have not declared support for tool use via the `sampling.tools` capability.

`schema.ts` `CreateMessageRequestParams.tools` / `.toolChoice`:

> The client MUST return an error if this field is provided but ClientCapabilities.sampling.tools is not declared.

`client/sampling.mdx` § Error Handling:

> Clients **SHOULD** return errors for common failure cases:
> - User rejected sampling request: `-1`
> - Tool result missing in request: `-32602` (Invalid params)
> - Tool results mixed with other content: `-32602` (Invalid params)

Previously `Client#handle_sampling_request` extracted only `messages`/`modelPreferences`/`systemPrompt`/`maxTokens` (plus a fixed extras hash) and **silently dropped `tools` and `toolChoice`** — the host handler sampled without tools while the server believed its tools were being honored — and there was no way to declare `sampling.tools`. Additionally (F42, sampling half), internal handler exceptions and the no-handler fallback both used error code `-1`, which the spec reserves for "User rejected sampling request".

Changes:

- `Client.new(..., sampling_supports_tools: true)` opts the host handler into tool use: the declared capability becomes `"sampling": { "tools": {} }` (plumbed via a new `JsonRpcCommon#declare_sampling_tools` that the handler-derived capability derivation from #160 reads); without the opt-in it stays `"sampling": {}`.
- Arity-5+ sampling handlers now receive the complete `sampling/createMessage` params hash as their fifth argument — `includeContext`/`temperature`/`stopSequences`/`metadata` read exactly as before, plus `tools`, `toolChoice`, `_meta`, and any future fields. Arity 0-4 handler signatures are unchanged (backward compatible).
- A request carrying `tools`/`toolChoice` when `sampling.tools` was not declared is rejected with a JSON-RPC `-32602` (Invalid params) error instead of silently sampling without tools; the handler is never invoked.
- Tool-use responses (`content` array of `type: "tool_use"` blocks, `stopReason: "toolUse"`) pass through faithfully; when the handler returns tool_use content without a `stopReason`, it now defaults to `"toolUse"` instead of `"endTurn"`.
- Error codes: handler exceptions → `-32603` (Internal error); no-handler fallback → `-32601` (Method not found); `-1` is kept exclusively for genuine host rejections (handler returns `nil`), matching the elicitation error semantics already established on the base branch.

## Tests

- New `spec/lib/mcp_client/sampling_tool_use_spec.rb` (17 examples, written red-first): capability declaration (`sampling` vs `sampling.tools`, transport- and Client-level), `-32602` rejection of `tools`/`toolChoice` without the capability, forwarding of the complete params hash (tools/toolChoice/_meta) to arity-5+ handlers, faithful ToolUseContent passthrough with `stopReason: "toolUse"` (including the missing-stopReason default), and the F42 error codes (`-32603` internal / `-32601` no handler / `-1` reserved for rejection).
- Existing `client_sampling_spec.rb` error contexts updated with explicit code assertions and spec-citation comments.
- Full suite: 1361 examples, 0 failures. RuboCop: 113 files inspected, no offenses.

**Stacked on #160** (`fix/handler-derived-capabilities`) — the capability declaration builds on its handler-derived `JsonRpcCommon#client_capabilities`; merge after it.

Part of an MCP 2025-11-25 compliance audit of this gem against the official spec.
