author: bdraco
body:
Companion to ratgdo/esphome-build-action#16, which forwards CCACHE_DIR into the build container. Each of the 26 matrix jobs points ccache at a dir under HOME (inside the container's bind mount) and persists it with a per-firmware rolling cache key, restored from the newest prior entry on every run and saved fresh each run; roughly 26 entries around 50 MB each cycle under the 10 GB LRU quota, and pip is the only other cache user here.

Active now for the esp32 boards: esphome 2026.7.0 enables ccache for native ESP-IDF builds whenever the binary is on PATH, and it already ships in the image base. The esp8266 boards are unaffected until esphome/esphome#17722 lands in a release; their dir is created up front so the cache save stays quiet.

Measured on this PR, cold seed run versus warm rerun of the Build firmware step:

| Firmware | Cold | Warm |
|---|---|---|
| V32 Board Security+ 2.0 (esp32) | 296s | 148s |
| V32 Dry Contact (esp32) | 281s | 142s |
| ESP32 D1 Mini (esp32) | 280s | 162s |
| V2.5i (esp8266, control) | 160s | 148s |

Same mechanism on esphome-device-builder's native IDF CI job went 90s to 33s.

author: maxugly
body:
## 💡 What
Replaced `dev_alloc_skb` with `napi_alloc_skb` in the network driver's RX path (`sim_rx_dequeue`). Added a journal entry to `.jules/bolt.md` documenting this optimization pattern.

## 🎯 Why
`sim_rx_dequeue` operates in a NAPI polling context. Calling a generic slab allocator like `dev_alloc_skb` in this hotpath causes cache thrashing. Using `napi_alloc_skb` leverages the NAPI per-CPU cache locality, reducing lock contention and significantly improving packet processing throughput.

## 📊 Impact
Expected to increase packet processing performance and lower latency during bursts, as CPU cache thrashing on memory allocations is reduced. 

## 🔬 Measurement
Run `sudo ./scripts/nata-bench-once.sh` to measure packet throughput and compare against baseline. Use `perf` to profile CPU usage and observe reduced overhead in `kmem_cache_alloc_node` and network RX softirqs.

## Summary

Post-#58 batch across six themes: a security/correctness **hardening wave**, **theme + Ghostty UX** fixes, a comprehensive **README** update, a new **AI-tool config management** component, **homelab/shell fixes**, and the **macOS default-terminal pivot**. 28 commits, 48 files (+1772/−134). All specs/plans under `docs/superpowers/`; `bats tests/` + shellcheck + `zsh -n` + `cargo clippy` green throughout.

## Hardening wave — finish-wire declared contracts
From a 23-agent ultracode audit; all findings adversarially verified. Each defect was a contract that existed but was never wired end-to-end:

- **Profiles** (`96f4af4`) — repair the `PROFILE_TOOLCHAIN` install contract (typo'd var, wrong slug for 8 profiles, phantom scripts) + add **`claw profiles lint`** (CI-gated, validates all 18 profile contracts).
- **Install path** (`57b6dcc`) — fresh-Mac Homebrew-bash version gate, `provision.sh` brew-shellenv eval, dead kubectl/aws-iam-authenticator toolchain rows, `cargo:<crate>` fallback.
- **pkg manifest** (`0062c09`) — skip pipx/uv/claude shim symlinks; tag unknown binaries `manual` not `eget` (fixes capture-noise poisoning).
- **Theme split-brain** (`98b3502`, `0603f67`) — migrate the 4 flat themes to the directory layout, two-path readers (shell + Rust TUI), TUI `skip` → `Outcome::None`, palette-var straggler color.
- **Docs truth-up** (`eab0be8`) — ULTRAPLAN boxes, CLAUDE.md profile section (directory-per-profile), knowledge base.

Hook integrity + shell-dedupe + secret.sh leak fixes from the same wave landed in #58.

## Theme & Ghostty UX
- **Ghostty** (`7cd91cf`, `27cf11f`) — free the native ⌘\` (quick-terminal → ctrl+\`), stop copy-on-select clipboard clobber, drop surprising ⌘X remap, add tab cycling; 14pt macOS font + 140×52 cells tuned for the dashboards. Gate-0 diagnostics confirmed the title machinery is correct (renders in fresh windows).

## README
- **Comprehensive update** (`e362cec`) — the spine (three consolidation contracts), full command map (~20 previously-undocumented subcommands), and new sections for the theme engine, Rust TUI, Claude harness, secrets (sops), integrity, and AI stacks. Fixed stale claims (directory-per-profile, current repo tree).

## AI-tool config management (new component)
Brings **opencode** + **openwork** configuration under dot-files — spec → plan → subagent-driven TDD execution (`35bd769`, `81bb7da`, `d1807c1`, then `b08cbe6`, `9cf92ee`, `134a5e2`, `1183a54`, `c5c0eeb`):

- `scripts/utils/ai-config.sh` — POSIX engine (render/sync/status/setup), clin.sh mechanism, surfaced as **`claw ai config`**.
- opencode: portable base + managed-file sentinel (color tracks the terminal ANSI palette — no theme render; verified opencode has no config theme field).
- openwork: `server.json` rendered from the vault resolver + `~/OpenWork`, **seed-and-reconcile** (`_claw_managed` key) so it never clobbers GUI workspace edits; runtime files left generated; `tokens.json` surfaced by presence only, never rendered.
- `.zshrc` machine-local PATH-leak fix (`/Users/henry` → `$HOME`, + an adjacent acme.sh leak).

**Adopting live configs (`claw ai config setup`) is operator-gated — not run by this branch.** Lossless for current openwork workspaces.

## macOS default-terminal pivot (`2601975`, `0f9fc1d`, `bc595be`)

**Apple Terminal.app becomes the primary macOS terminal; Ghostty stays a fully
functional peer.** Ghostty remains the Linux/BD790i default — unchanged.

- `scripts/setup/macos-default-terminal.sh` was hardcoded to Ghostty. It now takes
  `--target terminal|ghostty` (default `terminal`) plus `--dry-run`, driven by a small
  registry — adding a terminal is one `case` arm plus one workflow bundle.
- New `terminal/macos/Open in Terminal.workflow`. It is an independent Services entry,
  so **both** Quick Actions can be installed at once and Finder offers each.
- `demote_other()` settles the one real policy call as **additive-only**: `--target`
  *grants* the login item / Dock pin / Quick Action, never revokes them from the other
  terminal. Chosen because it is the only variant that cannot destroy hand-arranged
  state (a Dock layout, a wanted login item). Cost: "primary" is documentation, not
  enforcement. The one sanctioned escalation (drop the other's login item only, never
  its Dock pin) is recorded inline.

**No shell-layer changes were needed** — the audit found the stack already
Terminal.app-safe: `progress.zsh` uses OSC 0 (universal), `fastfetch.zsh`'s `*)` arm
falls through to ASCII since Terminal.app supports neither the kitty nor iTerm2 image
protocol, and `ghostty-terminfo.zsh` is `TERM`-guarded. Documented in `terminal/README.md`.

## Homelab, shell & vault fixes
- **Fleet** (`fb334c5`, `dc77c53`) — ms-01 + traefik entrypoint moved to `192.168.1.110`
  after the DHCP churn; fleet cache updated.

- **PATH** (`c5c0eeb`, `54ae175`) — kill `/Users/henry` hardcoded leaks in the tracked

`bats tests/` (114 pass), `shellcheck -S error`, `zsh -n`, `cargo test` + `cargo clippy -D warnings` all green. AI-config feature passed per-task reviews + an opus whole-branch review (READY TO MERGE). Deferred Minors tracked on the SDD ledger.

author: gabrielnkl
body:
End-of-Turn Outcome Telemetry for Skills

Summary

Adds end-of-turn outcome telemetry — a third failure signal for skills.

Hermes already knew when the machinery broke and when the loop ended with text; this PR answers a question it never could: did the work actually hold up?

The answer is attributed to the skills that ran, flows into a per-skill sidecar, drives a needs_review curator flag, and is backed by a citation system — the judge can only blame a skill when it points at evidence that actually happened this turn.

Why

The curator's transitions (active → stale → archived) are driven purely by recency. A skill invoked constantly and failing constantly looks identical to one that works.

Outcome telemetry adds a failure dimension so unreliable skills get flagged instead of staying invisible.

Architecture

Three layers. Layers 0 and 1 are separately opt-in; Layer 2 is always-on, in-memory bookkeeping that the other two depend on.

Layer 1 — Mechanical Per-Skill Verifiers

tools/skill_verify.py

A skill's SKILL.md can declare metadata.hermes.verify:

  • run

  • optional applicability_check

  • timeout_seconds

After a turn that used the skill, the verifier subprocess runs and prints strict JSON:

{"success": true, "reason": "..."}

An applicability probe that exits non-zero yields SKIP — recorded as nothing, never a fake pass.

A turn-wide budget (total_verify_budget_seconds, default 60s) caps all verifier subprocesses.

Layer 0 — End-of-Turn Outcome Judge

agent/turn_outcome.py

After finalization, an auxiliary model judge answers:

Did the work hold up, not merely did the loop end?

It returns:

{
  "task_succeeded": true,
  "confidence": 0.95,
  "failure_points": [],
  "reason": "..."
}

The judge runs only when:

  • a verifier FAILED;

  • a used skill had no verifier (unverified residue — the common case); or

  • run: always is configured.

Down-Only, Dumb-Recorder Attribution

The attribution system deliberately only allows evidence to move outcomes downward:

  • A mechanical verifier FAIL is foreclosed: it is recorded, and no auxiliary judgment can overturn it.

  • On a confident evaluation success, a skill that ran unverified records NEUTRAL — a sample that slides the recovery window but never claims success.

  • When a mechanical FAIL is present, the eval's additional failure_points are ignored — a low-context judge cannot pin blame on an unrelated skill.

  • Verdicts are best-effort — a failure in the evaluation path never breaks the turn.

Recorder-Side Rejection — Blame Must Cite Evidence

Previously, the judge blamed skills using bare names. The recorder wrote those with the same sidecar status as a mechanical verifier's True/False — a conclusion stored as if it were a fact, with nothing downstream able to distinguish the two.

This closes that gap.

failure_points is now a citation:

[
  {
    "skill": "<name>",
    "evidence": [1, 3]
  }
]

The IDs point at a numbered evidence catalog built from this turn's real artifacts:

  • mechanical verifier verdicts;

  • tool errors, newly enumerated in finalize_turn with their tool names;

  • failed file mutations.

The recorder validates every citation mechanically before writing a False:

  • A citation to a verifier FAIL for the exact skill is hard — the citation itself is the evidence, and the failure lands regardless of confidence.

  • A citation to tool-error/file-mutation evidence, or no citation (legacy bare name), is gated — it remains confidence-gated because the skill attribution is judge-attributed.

  • Fabricated IDs, cited PASS results, and another skill's FAIL are rejected — the outcome is recorded as NEUTRAL, with the judge's reason preserved, never as a hard False.

  • Legacy bare-name failure_points still parse and behave exactly as before (confidence-gated), preserving backward compatibility.

Layer 2 — Per-Turn Skill Attribution

tools/skill_usage.py + agent/turn_context.py

The dumb recorder answers:

Which skills actually ran this turn?

At turn start, arm_turn_skill_accumulator points a ContextVar at the agent's _turn_used_skills.

The accumulator is:

  • written through the single bump_use() chokepoint;

  • read from the instance, so a subagent cannot pollute the parent's attribution;

  • disarmed at turn end, so out-of-turn bump_use() calls — preloads, cron, shared gateway threads — stop writing into a dead set.

Layer 2 is ungated, always-on bookkeeping. It is the reason neither a mechanical failure nor an eval-blamed skill can be pinned to a skill the turn never touched.

Declaring Is Not Consent — The Trust Boundary

A skill author may declare a verifier, but only the user grants permission to run it via:

hermes skills verify <name>

or:

/skills verify <name> [--disable]

Opt-in is gated by is_verify_optin_eligible():

Skill type | Eligible -- | -- Agent-created / curator-managed | Always Bundled built-ins | Only when curator.prune_builtins is enabled Hub-installed, external, protected, unmanaged | Never

Enabling is gated; disabling is always allowed. Consent therefore remains revocable even if a skill later drifts into ineligibility.

Sidecar Telemetry

tools/skill_usage.py

bump_outcome() records outcomes in a bounded window of the last 20 samples:

  • recent_outcomes

  • recent_outcome_reasons

  • failure_rate()

The needs_review flag:

  • turns on at ≥50% failures with ≥4 samples;

  • turns off on recovery;

  • clears when the skill is archived.

Curator Integration

agent/curator.py

needs_review skills are:

  • counted during automatic transitions;

  • promoted to priority candidates in the LLM review pass;

  • surfaced through:

    • </

author: velicanu
body:
The founding premise of `plan/04`, finally built. Until now the log lived only in React state — every open refetched it, and with no signal there was nothing to show and nothing you could do. Now it lives in IndexedDB, the UI always reads the local copy, and the network only ever adds to it.

## Three pieces, each testable alone

- **`store.js`** — three IndexedDB stores: `events` (keyed by `event_id`, so an event we wrote and later receive back updates one row instead of doubling), a per-group sync cursor, and an outbox. Plus the group key, held locally so a group can be *read* offline, not merely listed. Payloads stay sealed on disk, decrypted only on read — a stolen phone yields no more than a stolen backup.
- **`sync.js`** — push then pull. Pushing first means our own writes come back in the same pull carrying their real server ids, so local order never disagrees with everyone else's. Idempotent on `event_id`, so a retried push after a lost reply is a no-op, not a duplicate expense. A permanent refusal (ghosted, stale bundle) is dropped and surfaced rather than jamming every write behind it; a plain outage keeps everything queued.
- **`App.jsx`** — `GroupView` reads local-first and renders immediately, syncs in the background, and shows a line when writes are held or the network is gone. Writes hit the outbox and appear at once with a provisional id sorted above any real one.

## One deliberate exception

Ghosting needs a real log position for the cut, which a provisional id isn't. So it flushes, reads back the server's id, and **refuses offline** — freezing someone's view is not a thing to do optimistically.

## Logout clears the local ledger

It holds the group key *and* the whole history. Leaving it on a shared computer is the same failure that un-enrolling the device key just fixed in #34. A test asserts it — the mutation pass found nothing did.

## Testing

14 sync tests, **259 JS**, 59 backend, 4 live. Nine mutations on sync/store, all caught (the logout one only after adding the test above).

Two things the work surfaced, both the familiar shape:

- The fake server now sends `event_id` on every row, because the real one always has and the store keys on it — **fake-vs-server drift caught by the store this time, not in production.**
- `settle()` in the test harness now waits for the DOM to go quiet rather than flushing a fixed number of turns, and the quiet threshold had to be raised to clear a whole IndexedDB round trip. During one the DOM sits still, and "still" is indistinguishable from "finished" — at the old margin `settle()` returned mid-load and every ledger-backed test saw an empty group. That cost me most of the debugging time here.

## Not in scope

The service worker / app-shell cache (`plan/08`) — this is the data half of offline, not the code half. Reload still needs the network to fetch the bundle. Worth doing next if we want true offline launch.

author: ozykhan
body:
`Deployer.hostForPreview` built the preview host from the base domain alone and never consulted the `HostnameRegistrar`, unlike `primaryHost`. On a relay-terminated box `baseDom` is itself a label under the apex, so a preview landed at `pr-7-blog.85b90055-ozykhan.public.getpiper.dev` — two labels under `public.getpiper.dev`. The relay's `*.public.getpiper.dev` wildcard matches exactly one label, so TLS failed, and with no `hostnames` row its router had nowhere to send the request. The container built, ran, health-checked, and was unreachable.

Same structural cause as #300/#301, but as the issue notes it needs the relay to assign more than one hostname per app, so it is a schema + control-op change rather than wiring.

## Relay

- `hostnames` gains `pr INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`; uniqueness moves to `UNIQUE(account_id, app, pr)`. Schema edited in place per the pre-1.x policy — no migration.
- `appHostname` hashes over `(account, app, pr)` and prefixes previews with `pr<N>-`, all inside the **first label**, so the wildcard still covers it. Production keeps the old `<hex>-<username>` shape (see the note below on the hash input).
- The `register` control op carries a PR number.
- **Previews do not count against the per-account app cap** — the cap bounds apps, and an open PR must not lock an account out of creating one.

## Agent

- `HostnameRegistrar.Register(app, pr)`; `TunnelClient` passes it through.
- `Deployer.PreviewHost` mirrors `primaryHost`: registrar where there is one, `pr-<N>-<app>.<baseDom>` otherwise. LAN and BYO boxes keep today's behaviour, which is correct there — their base domain is the apex.
- `TeardownPreview` deregisters the hostname so a closed PR releases it, and `Delete` does the same for every open preview of the app (it was dropping the constructed route and leaking the relay-side row).
- The webhook reports the routed preview host to GitHub instead of the constructed one, matching what #301 did for production.

## Note for review

`appHostname`'s hash input changed to include the PR number (`acct/app/0` instead of `acct/app`), so **production hostnames for apps registered before this change keep their stored value** — `RegisterHostname` is idempotent and returns the existing row — but a *newly* registered app gets a different hash than it would have before. That is invisible to users (the hostname is opaque and assigned at first deploy) and consistent with the pre-1.x policy, but it is the one behaviour change beyond previews.

## Verification

`make verify` green (gofmt, vet, `go test ./...`, arm64 cross). New coverage: relay preview-hostname assignment/idempotency/cap-exemption, deployer routing + teardown deregistration on a terminated box, the LAN fallback, and the reported preview URL.

Not exercised against a real relay — the pi4 path from #289 is the follow-up check.

Closes #302

author: n24q02m
body:
💡 What: Replaced a `functools.reduce` call containing `acc + next_item` list concatenation with a standard for-loop using `.extend()` and `.append()` in `sort_numerically`. Also updated `.jules/bolt.md` documenting this learning.
🎯 Why: `functools.reduce` on list concatenations (`+`) copies the accumulated list on every iteration, leading to $O(N^2)$ algorithmic complexity. Changing to `extend` operations scales $O(N)$ making it more performant and memory-efficient.
📊 Impact: Measured ~4.9x faster (0.176s down from 0.862s) in synthetic benchmarks sorting strings. Eliminates $O(N^2)$ memory copying.
🔬 Measurement: Verify changes in `src/semantic_release/helpers.py`. All unit tests still pass successfully.

author: sabbivikas
body:
## Inert by design — merging this changes nothing live

**This PR is ADDITIVE and INERT.** `COMM_ASSIST_ENABLED` defaults **off**, and the frame-refusal relaxation line is **designed but NOT applied**. Production behavior is **byte-identical** to today — *"what should I text her"* still receives the current frame-refusal response. **Merging this changes nothing in the live path.** It lands the safety scaffolding so the capability can later be enabled deliberately, behind a human review gate.

Proven inert: the existing suites are unchanged by this branch — move-selector **55/55**, knowledge-selector **35/35** — because the new `help_communicate` rung never fires while the flag is off. Full-project `tsc`: **0 app-code errors**.

---

## ⚠️ MERGE GATE — READ BEFORE ENABLING

**The harm ruleset in this PR is PROVISIONAL, pending "Engineering Findings §7," which is not in this repository.** Enabling `COMM_ASSIST_ENABLED`, or applying the frame-refusal relaxation, **removes the only output-side harm block that existed before this PR** (per the `audit/communication-refusal` findings — frame-refusal was the sole block, and nothing inspected Marcus's *output* for harm). That **must NOT happen** until:
1. **§7 is obtained**, and its harm criteria are **reviewed**;
2. the two-layer harm system is **extended** with §7's ratified patterns/rubric; and
3. the feature is **tested against real input by a human**.

**This scaffolding MAY merge flag-off. The CAPABILITY may NOT be enabled — and the relaxation may NOT be applied — until the three conditions above are met.**

---

## What this PR adds (all flag-gated, unwired)

- **Two-layer harm detection**
  - **Layer 1 — `harm-gate.ts` (regex):** pure, always-on (not flag-gated — the *feature* is flagged, the *safety control* is not), 8 categories: threat, coercion/leverage (incl. the calmly-worded case with no violent words), custody/child leverage, parental alienation, harassment, deception/manipulation, impersonation, blackmail/exposure. Category → tone-mapped refusal (CONCERNED for custody/alienation — desperate, not malicious; REDIRECT for the rest).
  - **Layer 2 — `harm-judge.ts` (gpt-4o-mini):** the semantic net for what regex provably cannot catch. **Fail-closed** — any error/timeout/malformed response → `harmful`. Single-shot, 4s timeout. Rubric targets the "Group B" failure mode; the four Group B slips are its few-shot positives.
- **Draft-safe composer path (`comm-assist-path.ts`)** — returns structured `{intro, draft, follow_up}`. The **draft is exempt from the 6 composer voice gates but NEVER from either harm layer.** `VOICE_GATES` and `HARM_LAYERS` are **disjoint sets by construction**; `runHarmLayers` runs on request AND draft unconditionally.
- **`help_communicate` move (`move-selector.ts`)** — broad phrasing coverage (wider than frame-refusal's `DRAFT_PATTERNS`, covering the audit's slip cases: respond-to-ex, rewrite-this-text, rehearse-what-to-say). Sits directly below crisis (crisis always wins), above advice/just-listen.
- **KI scoping (`knowledge-selector.ts`)** — help_communicate scopes to the relational/practical corpus (exclude full psych/flourishing; toward divorce + fatherhood), no probing questions while drafting.
- **27 regression tests** (`test-comm-assist.ts`) + **PII-free instrumentation** (`comm-assist-metrics.ts`, separate from the live `turn_logs` INSERT; the type cannot hold message contents — proven by `test-comm-assist-metrics.ts`).

## Layer order (help_communicate turn, once wired — NOT wired here)

`crisis.ts` (input) → **harm-gate regex (request)** → frame-refusal permits drafting *(the relaxation — not applied)* → compose `{intro, draft, follow_up}` → **draft skips the 6 voice gates** → **harm-gate regex (draft)** → **harm-judge (request + draft)** → surface only if both layers clean. Any block → refuse, draft discarded.

## The Group B semantic slips (documented gaps, by design)

Regex catches **lexical** harm; it cannot catch **semantic** coercion in benign words. Four documented slips, which are exactly the judge's few-shot positives:
1. *"so she understands the practical realities before she talks to a lawyer"* — legal-fear coercion.
2. *"remind her of everything I've done for this family"* — guilt-leverage (also genuinely ambiguous — left to the judge with full context, not force-matched by regex).
3. *"help her see how much better things were before"* — nostalgic manipulation / hoovering.
4. *"so she really thinks hard about the choice she is making"* — implied-consequence pressure, a soft threat with no threatening word.

`harm-gate` regex is **necessary but not sufficient**; the judge is the net for this residual. Both carry `PROVISIONAL — pending §7` markers with explicit extension points.

## Fail-closed proof (`test-draft-exemption.ts`, 17/17)

- Draft is exempt from every voice gate and from **neither** harm layer (`harmLayersAreNeverExempt()`).
- A **regex-harmful draft is still blocked** even when voice-gate-exempt and the judge would pass it.
- A **semantically-harmful draft** (regex-clean) is blocked at `layer: judge`.
- A clean draft passes both.
- **The real `judgeHarm` fails closed** — forced an invalid API key, it returned `harmful: true, category: 'judge_error'`.

## The relaxation diff — in this PR for review, NOT applied

The only change that would alter live behavior is gating the `draft_request` early return in `orchestrator-v2.ts` (~line 99):

```diff
  const frameCollapse = detectFrameCollapse(userMessage);
- if (frameCollapse) {
+ // When COMM_ASSIST_ENABLED is on, a draft_request is NO LONGER hard-blocked here —
+ // it flows to the help_communicate path, gated by BOTH harm layers (regex + judge).
+ // Every OTHER frame-collapse category still hard-blocks. THIS is the live-behavior line.
+ const relaxDraft = commAssistEnabled() && frameCollapse === 'draft_request';
+ if (frameCollapse && !relaxDraft) {
    env.sentinels.frame_refusal = { triggered: true, category: frameCollapse };
    …
  }
```

A parallel relaxation of **Constraint 14** (the soft in-LLM refusal in `system-prompt.ts`) would also be required. **Neither is applied in this PR.** `frame-refusal.ts`, the Tier-1 early return, and Constraint 14 are untouched.

## Audit provenance

Built on the read-only audit on branch `audit/communication-refusal`: frame-refusal was the *only* block; no output-side harm gate existed; provenance traces to a commit citing the absent "Engineering Findings §7"; QA never tested drafting; the post-generation voice gates would mangle a quoted draft (hence the exemption — and hence the requirement that harm layers still run on it).

## Commits

- `e231519` — harm gate (Step 4, PROVISIONAL) — HARD STOP 1
- `a4ab077` — LLM-judge layer + draft-exemption (Step 5) — HARD STOP 2 proof
- `058e3fd` — help_communicate move, KI scoping, draft-safe path, metrics

**Do not merge without explicit owner approval. Do not enable `COMM_ASSIST_ENABLED` or apply the relaxation until §7 is obtained, reviewed, and the feature is human-tested.**

author: s3ntin3l8
body:
## Summary

The `GET /api/v1/system/debug/raw/{provider_id}` endpoint was only capturing output from the first successful strategy (first-success break in the collector loop). While debugging the Anthropic `limits[]` quota migration (#210), this made it impossible to see what a lower-priority strategy (e.g., OAuth) was actually returning — you only saw the winning strategy's HTTP traffic.

Now the endpoint runs **every configured strategy** independently, grouping captured requests/responses/errors into separate per-strategy sections. The active/winning strategy is identified and labelled with an "Active" badge.

### Backend
- Iterates `collector._resolve_strategies()` directly instead of calling `collector.collect()`, bypassing the first-success break
- Each strategy gets its own `httpx.AsyncClient` with independent request/response interceptors — clean separation of HTTP traffic
- 0.5s sleep between strategies to avoid rate-limit bursts
- Response includes `active_strategy` + per-strategy `strategies` dict with `label`, `kind` (primary/enrichment), `status`, `cards_summary`, `requests`, `responses`, `errors`
- Legacy collectors (no `STRATEGIES` declared) fall back to the old `collector.collect()` single-pass

### Frontend
- Replaces the raw JSON `<pre>` dump with a per-strategy accordion
- Each strategy shows label, kind badge (accent/ok), status badge (ok/critical), card count
- Active strategy gets an orange "Active" pill
- Expandable sub-sections for requests, responses, errors
- `ResponseBlock` component for collapsible response previews (status code color-coded)

### New types
- `StrategyCaptureRequest`, `StrategyCaptureResponse`, `StrategyCaptureError`, `StrategyCapture`, `DebugRawResponse`

## Test plan
- [x] `make test` — 1286 passed, 41 skipped (6 new tests)
- [x] `make web-test` — 572 passed, 80 files
- [x] `make web` (Vite build) — clean
- [x] `make lint` (ruff + mypy) — clean
- [x] New unit tests for `_debug_strategy_label`, `_debug_split_strategies` helpers
- [x] Updated frontend tests for strategy accordion rendering (labels, badges, Active pill)

Closes #212

author: bernardladenthin
body:
## Summary

Fix the recurring `There was a timeout in the fork` failure on the Surefire test job **at its source** — it is not a duration problem (the prior `180s → 240s` bump did not help).

**Root cause:** the failure is `Corrupted channel by directly writing to native stream in forked JVM 1`. Mockito's inline mock maker self-attaches the byte-buddy agent at runtime, so the JVM writes `A Java agent has been loaded dynamically` to the **native** stderr (outside Surefire's wrapped `System.err`), intermittently corrupting the encoded fork channel. Surefire then never receives a clean fork-end handshake and reports a **bogus timeout — even though all 2017 tests pass**. It is a race, hence flaky and platform-dependent (seen on ubuntu; windows green in the same run).

The mechanism predates the failures (Mockito has been `5.23.0` throughout); a timing/environment shift in the Jun 26 → Jul 3 window (`junit 6.1.0 → 6.1.1` and/or a GitHub-runner JDK image update) tipped the latent race into manifesting regularly.

**Fix:** add `-XX:+EnableDynamicAgentLoading` to the **test-fork** argLine. The JVM then treats dynamic agent loading as intended and stops writing the warning to native stderr, so the channel stays clean. Verified locally — a Mockito test no longer emits the "loaded dynamically" warning and passes. It is a `-XX` flag (test-fork only), deliberately **not** part of the module-flag list synchronised by `JvmModuleFlagConsistencyTest`. The `240s` budget from #305 stays as extra headroom.

## Test plan

- [x] `mvn validate` → BUILD SUCCESS.
- [x] Mockito test run with the flag: no `A Java agent has been loaded dynamically` warning; tests green.
- [ ] CI green on this branch (the real proof — the failure only reproduces under CI's fork/timing).

## Follow-up (optional, not in this PR)

The fully future-proof variant is loading byte-buddy/Mockito as a real `-javaagent` at startup (Mockito's official recommendation), which removes the self-attach entirely and survives a future JDK disabling dynamic agent loading by default. Can be added later if desired.

body:
## Summary
- The live Z2M data-dir `configuration.yaml` (the file actually bind-mounted into the running container) still had `serial.port: tcp://10.100.20.179:6638` — connecting **directly** to the SLZB coordinator.
- The proxy fix in `1eb760c` only updated the top-level reference copy at `zigbee2mqtt/configuration.yaml`. Z2M owns and rewrites its own data-dir config at runtime, so that file was never touched by the earlier change and the proxy was never actually wired in.
- Confirmed live on mac-mini-m4: `slzb-proxy.py` running fine on `127.0.0.1:6639`, but Z2M bypassing it entirely and hitting the documented EFR32 `RESET_SOFTWARE`/`HOST_FATAL_ERROR` crash loop — RestartCount=114, crashing every 30-90s. This is why Hue switch button presses (including "power on") were landing during down windows and appearing to do nothing.

## Fix
Point the live `serial.port` at `tcp://127.0.0.1:6639` (the proxy) to match the intended config.

## Test plan
- [ ] Merge, confirm Komodo's `automation` stack sync picks up the change (`sync-stacks.sh` restarts `zigbee2mqtt` on changes under `mac-mini-m4/zigbee2mqtt/`)
- [ ] Confirm Z2M container stabilizes (RestartCount stops climbing, clean "started!" with no `HOST_FATAL_ERROR`/`ASH_ERROR_TIMEOUTS`)
- [ ] Confirm smart-lighting extension is loaded and a scene recall / light command actually reaches a bulb
